953.answer: The Legislature of the State fixes the salaries and allowances by law.

954.question: Does each House of the Legislature of a State have a separate secretarial staff?
954.answer: Yes, each House of the Legislature of a State has a separate secretarial staff.

955.question: Who has a separate secretarial staff in the Legislature of a State?
955.answer: Each House of the Legislature of a State has a separate secretarial staff.

956.question: Who can regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of the secretarial staff of the House or Houses of the Legislature of a State?
956.answer: The Legislature of a State can regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of the secretarial staff.

957.question: Who can regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of the secretarial staff?

958.question: What does every member of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State have to do before taking his seat?
958.answer: Every member of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State has to make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before the Governor, or some person appointed by him.

959.question: Who does every member of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State make and subscribe an oath or affirmation to before taking his seat?
959.answer: Every member of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State has to make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before the Governor, or some person appointed by him.

960.question: How are all questions at any sitting of a House of the Legislature of a State determined?
960.answer: All questions at any sitting of a House of the Legislature of a State are determined by a majority of votes of the members present and voting, other than the Speaker or Chairman, or person acting as such.

961.question: Who determines all questions at any sitting of a House of the Legislature of a State?
961.answer: All questions are determined by a majority of votes of the members present and voting, other than the Speaker or Chairman, or person acting as such.

962.question: Can the Speaker or Chairman vote in the first instance?
962.answer: No, the Speaker or Chairman, or person acting as such, shall not vote in the first instance.

963.question: Is the Speaker or Chairman, or person acting as such, allowed to vote in the first instance?

964.question: What power does a House of the Legislature of a State have according to the Constitution of India?
964.answer: A House of the Legislature of a State has the power to act notwithstanding any vacancy in the membership thereof, and any proceedings in the Legislature of a State shall be valid even if it is discovered subsequently that some person who was not entitled so to do sat or voted or otherwise took part in the proceedings.

965.question: What happens if a person who is not entitled to do so, participates in the proceedings of the Legislature of a State in India?
965.answer: Even if it is discovered subsequently that some person who was not entitled so to do sat or voted or otherwise took part in the proceedings, any proceedings in the Legislature of a State shall be valid according to the Constitution of India.

966.question: What constitutes a quorum for a meeting of a House of the Legislature of a State in India?
966.answer: Until the Legislature of the State by law otherwise provides, the quorum to constitute a meeting of a House of the Legislature of a State shall be ten members or one-tenth of the total number of members of the House, whichever is greater.

967.question: What is the minimum number of members required for a quorum in a meeting of a House of the Legislature of a State in India, unless the Legislature of the State by law otherwise provides?
967.answer: The quorum to constitute a meeting of a House of the Legislature of a State is ten members or one-tenth of the total number of members of the House, whichever is greater.

968.question: What is the duty of the Speaker or Chairman when there is no quorum during a meeting of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State?
968.answer: If at any time during a meeting of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State there is no quorum, it is the duty of the Speaker or Chairman, or person acting as such, either to adjourn the House or to suspend the meeting until there is a quorum.

969.question: What should the Speaker or Chairman do if there is no quorum during a meeting of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State?
969.answer: The Speaker or Chairman, or person acting as such, should either adjourn the House or suspend the meeting until there is a quorum.

970.question: What is the provision for a person who is a member of both Houses of the Legislature of a State according to the Constitution of India?
970.answer: No person shall be a member of both Houses of the Legislature of a State and provision shall be made by the Legislature of the State by law for the vacation by a person who is chosen a member of both Houses of his seat in one house or the other.

971.question: What happens according to the law if a person is chosen as a member of both Houses of the Legislature of a State in India?
971.answer: No person shall be a member of both Houses of the Legislature of a State and provision shall be made by the Legislature of the State by law for the vacation by a person who is chosen a member of both Houses of his seat in one house or the other.

972.question: What happens if a person is a member of the Legislatures of two or more States specified in the First Schedule?
972.answer: If a person is chosen a member of the Legislatures of two or more such States, then, at the expiration of such period as may be specified in rules made by the President, that person's seat in the Legislatures of all such States shall become vacant, unless he has previously resigned his seat in the Legislatures of all but one of the States.

973.question: What happens to the seats of a person who is chosen a member of the Legislatures of two or more States specified in the First Schedule and doesn't resign from all but one state within a specified period?
973.answer: At the expiration of such period as may be specified in rules made by the President, that person's seat in the Legislatures of all such States shall become vacant.

974.question: When does a member of a House of the Legislature of a State become disqualified?
974.answer: A member of a House of the Legislature of a State becomes disqualified if he/she becomes subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in clause (1) or clause (2) of article 191, or he/she resigns his seat by writing under his hand addressed to the speaker or the Chairman.

975.question: What happens if a member of a House of the Legislature of a State becomes subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in clause (1) or clause (2) of article 191, or he/she resigns his seat by writing under his hand addressed to the speaker or the Chairman?
975.answer: A member of a House of the Legislature of a State becomes disqualified.

976.question: What happens when a resignation is accepted by the Speaker or the Chairman?
976.answer: The seat of the person resigning shall thereupon become vacant.

977.question: What occurs when the seat of the person resigning becomes vacant?
977.answer: It means that the resignation has been accepted by the Speaker or the Chairman.

978.question: What happens if the Speaker or Chairman believes a resignation is not voluntary or genuine?
978.answer: They shall not accept the resignation.

979.question: What action does the Speaker or Chairman take if they believe a resignation is not voluntary or genuine?
979.answer: They shall not accept the resignation.

980.question: What actions can be taken if a member of a House of the Legislature is absent without permission for sixty days?
980.answer: The House may declare his seat vacant.

981.question: What can the House do if a member has been absent without permission for sixty days?
981.answer: The House may declare his seat vacant.

982.question: What are some disqualifications for membership to the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council of a State?
982.answer: Holding an office of profit under the Government of India or any State, being of unsound mind as declared by a competent court, being an undischarged insolvent, not being a citizen of India, voluntarily acquiring the citizenship of a foreign State, or being disqualified by or under any law made by Parliament.

983.question: What do holding an office of profit under the Government of India or any State, being of unsound mind as declared by a competent court, being an undischarged insolvent, not being a citizen of India, voluntarily acquiring the citizenship of a foreign State, or being disqualified by or under any law made by Parliament indicate?
983.answer: These are some disqualifications for membership to the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council of a State.

984.question: What does not count as holding an office of profit under the Government of India or any State for the purposes of disqualification?
984.answer: Being a Minister either for the Union or for such State does not count as holding an office of profit.

985.question: Who is not considered as holding an office of profit under the Government of India or any State?
985.answer: A Minister either for the Union or for such State is not considered as holding an office of profit.

986.question: Who makes the final decision if a question arises about a member of a House of the Legislature of a State becoming subject to disqualifications?

987.question: Who is responsible for making the final decision in case of a disqualification dispute involving a member of a State's House of the Legislature?

988.question: What does the Governor need to obtain before making any decision on such disqualification questions?
988.answer: The opinion of the Election Commission

989.question: Whose opinion does the Governor need to obtain before making any decision on disqualification questions?

990.question: What is the penalty for a person sitting or voting as a member of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State before complying with the requirements of article 188, or when not qualified or disqualified?
990.answer: A penalty of five hundred rupees for each day on which he so sits or votes

991.question: What is the daily penalty for a person who sits or votes as a member of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State before satisfying article 188's requirements or when not qualified or disqualified?

992.question: What freedoms are granted to the members of the Legislature of every State?
992.answer: There shall be freedom of speech in the Legislature of every State

993.question: Where is the freedom of speech granted according to the constitution?
993.answer: The freedom of speech is granted in the Legislature of every State.

994.question: What are members of the Legislature of a State immune to in respect of anything said or any vote given by them in the Legislature or any committee thereof?
994.answer: They are not liable to any proceedings in any court

995.question: What happens to the members of the Legislature of a State in respect to any proceedings in any court for anything said or any vote given by them in the Legislature or any committee thereof?

996.question: What are the powers, privileges and immunities of a House of the Legislature of a State?
996.answer: The powers, privileges and immunities of a House of the Legislature of a State, and of its members and committees, shall be such as may from time to time be defined by the Legislature by law. Until so defined, they shall be those of that House and of its members and committees immediately before the coming into force of section 26 of the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978.

997.question: When do the powers, privileges and immunities of a House of the Legislature of a State, and of its members and committees come into force?
997.answer: The powers, privileges and immunities come into force immediately before the coming into force of section 26 of the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, until they are defined by the Legislature by law.

998.question: What rights do people have according to the Constitution in relation to the House of the Legislature of a State?
998.answer: Persons who by virtue of this Constitution have the right to speak in, and otherwise to take part in the proceedings of, a House of the Legislature of a State or any committee thereof.

999.question: Who has the right to speak in, and otherwise to take part in the proceedings of, a House of the Legislature of a State or any committee thereof according to the Constitution?
999.answer: Persons who by virtue of this Constitution have these rights.

1000.question: What are the entitlements of members of the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council of a State?
1000.answer: Members of the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council of a State shall be entitled to receive such salaries and allowances as may from time to time be determined, by the Legislature of the State by law.

1001.question: Who are the ones entitled to receive salaries and allowances as determined by the Legislature of the State by law?
1001.answer: Members of the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council of a State are entitled to receive such salaries and allowances.

1002.question: Where can a Bill originate in the State Legislature?
1002.answer: A Bill may originate in either House of the Legislature of a State which has a Legislative Council.

1003.question: In which house of a state's legislature, that has a Legislative Council, can a bill originate?
1003.answer: A Bill may originate in either House of the Legislature of a State.

1004.question: What happens to a Bill in a State Legislature with a Legislative Council?
1004.answer: A Bill shall not be deemed to have been passed by the Houses of the Legislature of a State having a Legislative Council unless it has been agreed to by both Houses, either without amendment or with such amendments only as are agreed to by both Houses.

1005.question: What is required for a Bill to be passed by the Houses of the Legislature of a State having a Legislative Council?
1005.answer: A Bill shall not be deemed to have been passed by the Houses of the Legislature of a State having a Legislative Council unless it has been agreed to by both Houses, either without amendment or with such amendments only as are agreed to by both Houses.

1006.question: What happens to a Bill pending in the Legislature of a State in case of prorogation?
1006.answer: A Bill pending in the Legislature of a State shall not lapse by reason of the prorogation.

1007.question: Does a Bill pending in the Legislature of a State lapse by reason of the prorogation?
1007.answer: No, a Bill pending in the Legislature of a State does not lapse by reason of the prorogation.

1008.question: What happens to a Bill pending in the Legislative Council of a State which has not been passed by the Legislative Assembly on a dissolution of the Assembly?

1009.question: Does a Bill pending in the Legislative Council of a State lapse if it has not been passed by the Legislative Assembly upon a dissolution of the Assembly?
1009.answer: No, the Bill shall not lapse.

1010.question: What happens to a Bill pending in the Legislative Assembly of a State, or which having been passed by the Legislative Assembly is pending in the Legislative Council, on a dissolution of the Assembly?

1011.question: What is the status of a Bill that was pending in the Legislative Assembly of a State or having been passed by the Legislative Assembly is pending in the Legislative Council, after the Assembly has been dissolved?

1012.question: What can the Legislative Assembly do if a Bill is rejected by the Legislative Council or if the Council does not pass the Bill within three months?
1012.answer: The Legislative Assembly may pass the Bill again in the same or in any subsequent session with or without such amendments, if any, as have been made, suggested or agreed to by the Legislative Council and then transmit the Bill as so passed to the Legislative Council.

1013.question: What happens if the Legislative Assembly passes a Bill again in the same or in any subsequent session with or without such amendments, if any, as have been made, suggested or agreed to by the Legislative Council and then transmit the Bill as so passed to the Legislative Council?
1013.answer: The Bill is considered to be rejected by the Legislative Council or the Council has not passed the Bill within three months.

1014.question: What happens if a Bill passed for the second time by the Legislative Assembly is rejected by the Council or if the Council does not pass the Bill within one month?
1014.answer: The Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by the Houses of the Legislature of the State in the form in which it was passed by the Legislative Assembly for the second time with such amendments, if any, as have been made or suggested by the Legislative Council and agreed to by the Legislative Assembly.

1015.question: What is deemed to occur if a Bill, having been passed for the second time by the Legislative Assembly, is either rejected by the Council or not passed by the Council within one month?
1015.answer: The Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by the Houses of the Legislature of the State in the form in which it was passed by the Legislative Assembly for the second time with such amendments, if any, as have been made or suggested by the Legislative Council and agreed to by the Legislative Assembly.

1016.question: Where can a Money Bill not be introduced?
1016.answer: A Money Bill shall not be introduced in a Legislative Council.

1017.question: In which legislative body shall a Money Bill not be introduced?

1018.question: What happens after a Money Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly?
1018.answer: After a Money Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly of a State having a Legislative Council, it shall be transmitted to the Legislative Council for its recommendations.

1019.question: What happens to a Money Bill after it has been passed by the Legislative Assembly of a State that has a Legislative Council?
1019.answer: After a Money Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly, it is transmitted to the Legislative Council for its recommendations.

1020.question: What is the time period within which the Legislative Council should return the Money Bill with recommendations?
1020.answer: The Legislative Council shall within a period of fourteen days from the date of its receipt of the Bill return the Bill to the Legislative Assembly with its recommendations.

1021.question: What should the Legislative Council do within a period of fourteen days from the date of its receipt of the Money Bill?
1021.answer: The Legislative Council shall return the Money Bill to the Legislative Assembly with its recommendations.

1022.question: What happens if the Legislative Assembly does not accept any of the recommendations of the Legislative Council?
1022.answer: If the Legislative Assembly does not accept any of the recommendations of the Legislative Council, the Money Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form in which it was passed by the Legislative Assembly without any of the amendments recommended by the Legislative Council.

1023.question: What is deemed to have happened if the Legislative Assembly passes a Money Bill without accepting any of the amendments recommended by the Legislative Council?
1023.answer: If the Legislative Assembly does not accept any of the recommendations of the Legislative Council, the Money Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form in which it was passed by the Legislative Assembly.

1024.question: What happens if a Money Bill is not returned to the Legislative Assembly within fourteen days?
1024.answer: If a Money Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly and transmitted to the Legislative Council for its recommendations is not returned to the Legislative Assembly within the said period of fourteen days, it shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses at the expiration of the said period in the form in which it was passed by the Legislative Assembly.

1025.question: What is the consequence of a Money Bill, passed by the Legislative Assembly and sent to the Legislative Council for recommendations, not being returned within fourteen days?
1025.answer: If a Money Bill is not returned to the Legislative Assembly within fourteen days, it is deemed to have been passed by both Houses at the expiration of the said period in the form in which it was passed by the Legislative Assembly.

1026.question: What is deemed to be a Money Bill?
1026.answer: A Bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with all or any of the following matters, namely: the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax; the regulation of the borrowing of money or the giving of any guarantee by the State, or the amendment.

1027.question: What provisions must a bill contain to be considered a Money Bill, including its relationship with taxation and state borrowing?
1027.answer: A Bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with all or any of the following matters, namely: the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax; the regulation of the borrowing of money or the giving of any guarantee by the State, or the amendment.

1028.question: What is a Money Bill not deemed to be because of?
1028.answer: A Bill is not deemed to be a Money Bill by reason only that it provides for the imposition of fines or other pecuniary penalties, or for the demand or payment of fees for licenses or fees for services rendered, or by reason that it provides for the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax by any local authority or body for local purposes.

1029.question: What provisions do not make a Bill a Money Bill?
1029.answer: A Bill providing for the imposition of fines or other pecuniary penalties, or for the demand or payment of fees for licenses or fees for services rendered, or providing for the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax by any local authority or body for local purposes, does not make it a Money Bill.

1030.question: Who has the final decision on whether a Bill introduced in the Legislature of a State is a Money Bill or not?
1030.answer: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of such State has the final decision.

1031.question: Who has the final decision on whether a Bill introduced in the Legislative Assembly of a State is a Money Bill or not?
1031.answer: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of such State has the final decision.

1032.question: What is endorsed on every Money Bill when it is transmitted to the Legislative Council?
1032.answer: The certificate of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly signed by him that it is a Money Bill is endorsed.

1033.question: What is the certificate endorsed on every Money Bill when it is transmitted to the Legislative Council?
1033.answer: It is the certificate of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly signed by him that it is a Money Bill.

1034.question: What happens when a Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly of a State?
1034.answer: When a Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly of a State or, in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, has been passed by both Houses of the Legislature of the State, it shall be presented to the Governor and the Governor shall declare either that he assents to the Bill or that he withholds assent therefrom or that he reserves the Bill.

1035.question: What does the Governor do after a Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly of a State, or in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, has been passed by both Houses of the Legislature of the State?
1035.answer: After a Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly of a State or, in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, has been passed by both Houses of the Legislature of the State, it is presented to the Governor. The Governor then declares either that he assents to the Bill, that he withholds assent therefrom, or that he reserves the Bill.

1036.question: What can a Governor do if a Bill is presented to him for assent?
1036.answer: The Governor may return the Bill if it is not a Money Bill together with a message requesting that the House or Houses will reconsider the Bill or any specified provisions thereof and, in particular, will consider the desirability of introducing any such amendments as he may recommend in his message.

1037.question: What action can the Governor take when presented with a Bill that is not a Money Bill?
1037.answer: The Governor may return the Bill together with a message requesting that the House or Houses will reconsider the Bill or any specified provisions thereof and, in particular, will consider the desirability of introducing any such amendments as he may recommend in his message.

1038.question: What happens when a Bill is returned to the House or Houses by the Governor?
1038.answer: When a Bill is so returned, the House or Houses shall reconsider the Bill accordingly, and if the Bill is passed again by the House or Houses with or without amendment and presented to the Governor for assent, the Governor shall not withhold assent therefrom.

1039.question: What will the House or Houses do if a Bill is returned by the Governor, and what happens if the Bill is passed again and presented to the Governor for assent?
1039.answer: When a Bill is so returned, the House or Houses shall reconsider the Bill accordingly, and if the Bill is passed again by the House or Houses with or without amendment and presented to the Governor for assent, the Governor shall not withhold assent therefrom.

1040.question: What is the Governor not allowed to assent to?
1040.answer: The Governor shall not assent to, but shall reserve for the consideration of the President, any Bill which in the opinion of the Governor would, if it became law, so derogate from the powers of the High Court as to endanger the position which that Court is by this Constitution designed to fill.

1041.question: What should the Governor do if he believes that a Bill would derogate from the powers of the High Court and endanger its position as designed by the Constitution?
1041.answer: The Governor shall not assent to such a Bill, but shall reserve it for the consideration of the President.

1042.question: What happens when a Bill is reserved by a Governor for the consideration of the President?
1042.answer: When a Bill is reserved by a Governor for the consideration of the President, the President shall declare either that he assents to the Bill or that he withholds assent therefrom.

1043.question: What will the President do when a Bill is reserved by a Governor for his consideration?
1043.answer: The President shall declare either that he assents to the Bill or that he withholds assent therefrom.

1044.question: What can the President do if the Bill is not a Money Bill?
1044.answer: The President may direct the Governor to return the Bill to the House or, as the case may be, the Houses of the Legislature of the State together with such a message as is mentioned in the first proviso to article 200.

1045.question: What action may the President take with the Governor and the Houses of the Legislature of the State when a Bill is not a Money Bill, according to the first proviso to article 200?
1045.answer: The President may direct the Governor to return the Bill to the House or, as the case may be, the Houses of the Legislature of the State together with such a message as is mentioned in the first proviso to article 200.

1046.question: What happens if the Bill is returned by the Governor to the House or Houses?
1046.answer: The House or Houses shall reconsider it accordingly within a period of six months from the date of receipt of such message and, if it is again passed by the House or Houses with or without amendment, it shall be presented again to the President for his consideration.

1047.question: What is the procedure if a Bill is reconsidered and again passed by the House or Houses after being returned by the Governor?
1047.answer: If a Bill is again passed by the House or Houses with or without amendment after being returned by the Governor, it shall be presented again to the President for his consideration within a period of six months from the date of receipt of such message.

1048.question: What is the Governor's role in financial matters?
1048.answer: In respect of every financial year, the Governor shall cause to be laid before the House or Houses a financial statement.

1049.question: Who is responsible for laying a financial statement before the House or Houses every financial year?
1049.answer: The Governor is responsible for laying a financial statement before the House or Houses every financial year.

1050.question: What is the 'annual financial statement' as referred to in this text?
1050.answer: The 'annual financial statement' is a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the State for that year.

1051.question: What is the statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the State for that year referred to as?
1051.answer: The statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the State for that year is referred to as the 'annual financial statement'.

1052.question: What should the estimates of expenditure in the annual financial statement show separately?
1052.answer: The estimates should show separately the sums required to meet expenditure charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State and the sums required to meet other expenditure proposed to be made from the Consolidated Fund of the State.

1053.question: What should the sums required to meet expenditure charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State and the sums required to meet other expenditure proposed to be made from the Consolidated Fund of the State be shown separately in?
1053.answer: The sums should be shown separately in the estimates of expenditure in the annual financial statement.

1054.question: What expenditure is charged on the Consolidated Fund of each State?
1054.answer: The expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of each State includes the emoluments and allowances of the Governor and other expenditure related to his office, the salaries and allowances of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, debt charges for which the State is liable and other expenditure relating to the raising of loans and the service and redemption of debt, expenditure in respect of the salaries and allowances of Judges of any High Court, any sums required to satisfy any judgment, decree or award of any court or arbitral tribunal, and any other expenditure declared by this Constitution, or by the Legislature of the State by law, to be so charged.

1055.question: What does the expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of each State include?
1055.answer: The expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of each State includes the emoluments and allowances of the Governor and other expenditure related to his office, the salaries and allowances of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, debt charges for which the State is liable and other expenditure relating to the raising of loans and the service and redemption of debt, expenditure in respect of the salaries and allowances of Judges of any High Court, any sums required to satisfy any judgment, decree or award of any court or arbitral tribunal, and any other expenditure declared by this Constitution, or by the Legislature of the State by law, to be so charged.

1056.question: What is the procedure in the Legislature with respect to estimates?
1056.answer: The procedure in the Legislature with respect to estimates is that so much of the estimates as relates to expenditure charged upon the Consolidated Fund of a State shall not be submitted to the vote of the Legislative Assembly, but nothing in this clause shall be construed as preventing the discussion in the Legislature of any of those estimates. So much of the said estimates as relates to other expenditure shall be submitted to the Legislature for approval.

1057.question: What part of the estimates is not submitted to the vote of the Legislative Assembly and what part is submitted for approval?
1057.answer: So much of the estimates as relates to expenditure charged upon the Consolidated Fund of a State shall not be submitted to the vote of the Legislative Assembly, however, this doesn't prevent the discussion of any of those estimates in the Legislature. The part of the estimates that relates to other expenditure is submitted to the Legislature for approval.

1058.question: Who has the power to assent or refuse to assent to any demand for a grant?

1059.question: What entity has the authority to assent or not assent to demands for a grant?

1060.question: Who recommendation is required for a demand for a grant to be made?

1061.question: Who needs to give a recommendation for a demand for a grant to be made?

1062.question: What is introduced after the grants have been made by the Assembly?
1062.answer: A Bill to provide for the appropriation out of the Consolidated Fund of the State

1063.question: What is introduced after the Assembly grants have been made?
1063.answer: A Bill to provide for the appropriation out of the Consolidated Fund of the State

1064.question: Who has the final decision as to whether an amendment is admissible?

1065.question: What role does the person presiding have in the admittance of an amendment?
1065.answer: They have the final decision as to whether an amendment is admissible.

1066.question: Under what conditions can money be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of the State?
1066.answer: No money shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of the State except under appropriation made by law passed in accordance with the provisions of this article

1067.question: What is the requirement for withdrawing money from the Consolidated Fund of the State?
1067.answer: The requirement for withdrawing money from the Consolidated Fund of the State is that no money shall be withdrawn except under appropriation made by law passed in accordance with the provisions of the relevant article.

1068.question: Under what circumstances can the Governor authorise expenditure for a particular service for the current financial year?
1068.answer: If the amount authorised by any law made in accordance with the provisions of article 204 to be expended for a particular service for the current financial year is found to be insufficient for the purposes of that year or when a need has arisen during the current financial year for supplementary or additional expenditure upon some new service not contemplated in the annual financial statement for that year

1069.question: What does article 204 imply for the Governor's ability to authorize expenditure for a particular service for the current financial year?
1069.answer: Article 204 allows the Governor to authorise expenditure for a particular service for the current financial year in cases where the amount authorised by any law is found to be insufficient for the purposes of that year, or when a need has arisen during the current financial year for supplementary or additional expenditure upon some new service not contemplated in the annual financial statement for that year.

1070.question: What happens when the expenditure for a service exceeds the granted amount in a financial year?
1070.answer: A statement showing the estimated amount of that expenditure is to be laid before the House or the Houses of the Legislature of the State. Alternatively, a demand for such excess is to be presented to the Legislative Assembly of the State.

1071.question: What is the procedure when the estimated amount of expenditure for a service exceeds the granted amount in a financial year?
1071.answer: A statement showing the estimated amount of that expenditure is to be laid before the House or the Houses of the Legislature of the State. Alternatively, a demand for such excess is to be presented to the Legislative Assembly of the State.

1072.question: Which articles have effect in relation to such statement and expenditure or demand and also to any law to be made authorising the appropriation of moneys?
1072.answer: Articles 202, 203 and 204 have effect in relation to such statement, expenditure or demand.

1073.question: What do Articles 202, 203 and 204 relate to?
1073.answer: Articles 202, 203 and 204 have effect in relation to a statement, expenditure or demand, and also to any law to be made authorising the appropriation of moneys.

1074.question: What is the power of the Legislative Assembly of a State according to the constitution of India?
1074.answer: The Legislative Assembly of a State has the power to make any grant in advance in respect of the estimated expenditure for a part of any financial year, to make a grant for meeting an unexpected demand upon the resources of the State, and to make an exceptional grant which forms no part of the current service of any financial year.

1075.question: What does the Legislative Assembly of a State do in terms of financial grants, according to the constitution of India?
1075.answer: The Legislative Assembly of a State has the power to make any grant in advance in respect of the estimated expenditure for a part of any financial year, to make a grant for meeting an unexpected demand upon the resources of the State, and to make an exceptional grant which forms no part of the current service of any financial year.

1076.question: What can the Legislature of the State authorise by law?
1076.answer: The Legislature of the State can authorise by law the withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of the State for the purposes.

1077.question: What can the withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of the State for the purposes be authorised by?
1077.answer: The withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of the State for the purposes can be authorised by the Legislature of the State law.

1078.question: What is the effect of articles 203 and 204 in relation to grants?
1078.answer: The provisions of articles 203 and 204 shall have effect in relation to the making of any grant and to any law to be made under that clause as they have effect in relation to the making of a grant with regard to any expenditure mentioned in the annual financial statement and the law to be made for the authorisation of appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State to meet such expenditure.

1079.question: How do the provisions of articles 203 and 204 affect the making of any grant and any law to be made under that clause, especially in relation to the annual financial statement and the authorisation of appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State?
1079.answer: Articles 203 and 204 have the same effect on the making of any grant and any law to be made under that clause as they do on the making of a grant for any expenditure mentioned in the annual financial statement and the law made for the authorisation of appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State to meet such expenditure.

1080.question: What are the special provisions about financial Bills?
1080.answer: A Bill or amendment making provision for any of the matters specified in sub-clauses (a) to (f) of clause (1) of article 199 shall not be introduced or moved except on the recommendation of the Governor, and a Bill making such provision shall not be introduced in a Legislative Council. However, no recommendation shall be required for the moving of an amendment making provision for the reduction or abolition of any tax.

1081.question: What are the rules for introducing or moving a Bill or amendment that makes provision for any of the matters specified in sub-clauses (a) to (f) of clause (1) of article 199? What about for the reduction or abolition of any tax?
1081.answer: A Bill or amendment making provision for any of the matters specified in sub-clauses (a) to (f) of clause (1) of article 199 cannot be introduced or moved except on the recommendation of the Governor, and such a Bill cannot be introduced in a Legislative Council. However, no recommendation is required for the moving of an amendment making provision for the reduction or abolition of any tax.

1082.question: What conditions must be met for a Bill involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of a State to be passed?
1082.answer: A Bill which, if enacted and brought into operation, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of a State shall not be passed by a House of the Legislature of the State unless the Governor has recommended to that House the consideration of the Bill.

1083.question: What is the process for a Bill, which if enacted would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of a State, to be passed by a House of the Legislature of the State?
1083.answer: The Bill shall not be passed unless the Governor has recommended to that House the consideration of the Bill.

1084.question: What does article 208 of the constitution provide for?
1084.answer: Article 208 provides that a House of the Legislature of a State may make rules for regulating, subject to the provisions of this Constitution, its procedure and the conduct of its business. Until rules are made under this clause, the existing rules of procedure and standing orders remain in force.

1085.question: Which article of the constitution states that a House of the Legislature of a State may make rules for regulating its procedure and the conduct of its business, and that until rules are made under this clause, the existing rules of procedure and standing orders remain in force?
1085.answer: This is provided in Article 208 of the constitution.

1086.question: Who can modify the effect of the Constitution on the Legislature of the State?
1086.answer: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly or the Chairman of the Legislative Council

1087.question: What roles have the power to modify the effect of the Constitution on the Legislature of the State?
1087.answer: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly or the Chairman of the Legislative Council

1088.question: Who can make rules for procedure with respect to communications between the two Houses in a State with a Legislative Council?
1088.answer: The Governor, after consultation with the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and the Chairman of the Legislative Council

1089.question: Who consults with the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and the Chairman of the Legislative Council to make rules for procedure with respect to communications between the two Houses in a State with a Legislative Council?

1090.question: Who can regulate the procedure of financial business in the Legislature of the State?

1091.question: Who has the authority to regulate the procedure of financial business in a State?

1092.question: In case of inconsistency between any law and any rule or standing order, which prevails?
1092.answer: The provision of any law prevails

1093.question: Which prevails in case of inconsistency between any law and any rule or standing order?
1093.answer: The provision of any law prevails

1094.question: What languages can be used in the transaction of business in the Legislature of a State?
1094.answer: The official language or languages of the State, Hindi, or English

1095.question: What languages, including State's official language, Hindi and English, can be used for conducting business in the State Legislature?
1095.answer: The official language or languages of the State, Hindi, or English

1096.question: Who can permit a member to address the House in his mother-tongue if he cannot adequately express himself in the official languages?
1096.answer: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, Chairman of the Legislative Council, or person acting as such

1097.question: Who is responsible for permitting a member to address the House in his mother-tongue if he cannot adequately express himself in the official languages?
1097.answer: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, Chairman of the Legislative Council, or person acting as such

1098.question: What happens after the expiration of a period of fifteen years from the commencement of this Constitution?
1098.answer: This article shall have effect as if the words 'or in English' were omitted therefrom.

1099.question: What is the effect of the article after a period of fifteen years from the commencement of this Constitution?
1099.answer: After fifteen years from the commencement of this Constitution, the article shall have effect as if the words 'or in English' were omitted therefrom.

1100.question: What is the exception for the Legislatures of the States of Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura?
1100.answer: This clause shall have effect as if for the words 'fifteen years' occurring therein, the words 'twenty-five years' were substituted.

1101.question: What is the effect of the clause for the Legislatures of the States of Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura?
1101.answer: This clause shall have effect as if for the words 'fifteen years' occurring therein, the words 'twenty-five years' were substituted.

1102.question: What is the exception for the Legislatures of the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Goa and Mizoram?
1102.answer: This clause shall have effect as if for the words 'fifteen years' occurring therein, the words 'forty years' were substituted.

1103.question: What happens to the clause related to the Legislatures of the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Goa and Mizoram if the words 'forty years' were substituted for 'fifteen years'?
1103.answer: This clause shall have effect as the exception.

1104.question: What restriction is placed on discussion in the Legislature?
1104.answer: No discussion shall take place in the Legislature of a State with respect to the conduct of any Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of his duties.

1105.question: What is the conduct that is not allowed to be discussed in the Legislature of a State?
1105.answer: The conduct of any Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of his duties is not allowed to be discussed in the Legislature of a State.

1106.question: Can the validity of any proceedings in the Legislature of a State be questioned?
1106.answer: The validity of any proceedings in the Legislature of a State shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure.

1107.question: On what grounds can the validity of any proceedings in the Legislature of a State not be called into question?
1107.answer: The validity of any proceedings in the Legislature of a State shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure.

1108.question: Can an officer or member of the Legislature of a State be subject to the jurisdiction of any court in respect of the exercise of their powers?
1108.answer: No officer or member of the Legislature of a State in whom powers are vested by or under this Constitution for regulating procedure or the conduct of business, or for maintaining order, in the Legislature shall be subject to the jurisdiction of any court in respect of the exercise by him of those powers.

1109.question: Who is not subject to the jurisdiction of any court in respect of the exercise of their powers, as vested by or under the Constitution for regulating procedure, conducting business, or maintaining order in the Legislature of a State?
1109.answer: No officer or member of the Legislature of a State is subject to the jurisdiction of any court in respect of the exercise of those powers.

1110.question: What is the power of the Governor during the recess of the Legislature?
1110.answer: If at any time, except when the Legislative Assembly of a State is in session, or where there is a Legislative Council in a State, except when both Houses of the Legislature are in session, the Governor is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action, he may promulgate such Ordinances as the circumstances appear to him to require.

1111.question: When can the Governor promulgate Ordinances?
1111.answer: The Governor can promulgate Ordinances when the Legislative Assembly of a State is not in session or where there is a Legislative Council in a State, except when both Houses of the Legislature are not in session, if he is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action.

1112.question: Under what conditions can an Ordinance not be promulgated without instructions from the President?
1112.answer: (a) a Bill containing the same provisions would under this Constitution have required the previous sanction of the President for the introduction thereof into the Legislature; (b) he would have deemed it necessary to reserve a Bill containing the same provisions for the consideration of the President; (c) an Act of the Legislature of the State containing the same provisions would under this Constitution have been invalid unless, having been reserved for the consideration of the President, it had received the assent of the President.

1113.question: What are the conditions in the constitution that would require an Ordinance to have the President's sanction or to be reserved for the President's consideration before promulgation?
1113.answer: The conditions include: (a) a Bill containing the same provisions would under this Constitution have required the previous sanction of the President for the introduction thereof into the Legislature; (b) he would have deemed it necessary to reserve a Bill containing the same provisions for the consideration of the President; (c) an Act of the Legislature of the State containing the same provisions would under this Constitution have been invalid unless, having been reserved for the consideration of the President, it had received the assent of the President.

1114.question: What force does an Ordinance promulgated under this article have?
1114.answer: An Ordinance promulgated under this article shall have the same force and effect as an Act of the Legislature of the State assented to by the Governor.

1115.question: What is the equivalence of an Ordinance promulgated under a certain article in terms of legislative force and effect?
1115.answer: It is equivalent to an Act of the Legislature of the State assented to by the Governor.

1116.question: What happens to an Ordinance once it is laid before the Legislative Assembly of the State?
1116.answer: It shall cease to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of the Legislature, or if before the expiration of that period a resolution disapproving it is passed by the Legislative Assembly and agreed to by the Legislative Council, if any, upon the passing of the resolution or, as the case may be, on the resolution being agreed to by the Council.

1117.question: When does an Ordinance laid before the Legislative Assembly of the State cease to operate? What happens if a resolution disapproving it is passed by the Legislative Assembly and agreed to by the Legislative Council?
1117.answer: An Ordinance shall cease to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of the Legislature. If before the expiration of that period a resolution disapproving it is passed by the Legislative Assembly and agreed to by the Legislative Council, if any, it ceases to operate upon the passing of the resolution or, as the case may be, on the resolution being agreed to by the Council.

1118.question: Can an Ordinance be withdrawn?
1118.answer: An Ordinance may be withdrawn at any time by the Governor.

1119.question: Who has the authority to withdraw an Ordinance at any time?
1119.answer: The Governor has the authority to withdraw an Ordinance at any time.

1120.question: When is an Ordinance under this article void?
1120.answer: If and so far as an Ordinance under this article makes any provision which would not be valid if enacted in an Act of the Legislature of the State assented to by the Governor, it shall be void.

1121.question: What happens if an Ordinance under this article makes any provision which would not be valid if enacted in an Act of the Legislature of the State assented to by the Governor?

1122.question: What is the role of an Ordinance promulgated in the Concurrent List?
1122.answer: It is deemed to be an Act of the Legislature of the State which has been reserved for the consideration of the President and assented to by him.

1123.question: What is the status of an Ordinance promulgated in the Concurrent List after it has been reserved for the consideration of the President and assented to by him?
1123.answer: It is deemed to be an Act of the Legislature of the State.

1124.question: What is the structure of High Courts according to the Constitution of India?
1124.answer: Every High Court shall consist of a Chief Justice and such other Judges as the President may from time to time deem it necessary to appoint.

1125.question: Who makes the decision to appoint judges to the High Courts in India, and what does the court composition consist of?
1125.answer: The President of India has the power to appoint judges as he deems necessary. The High Court consists of a Chief Justice and other judges appointed by the President.

1126.question: What is the age limit for a Judge of a High Court?
1126.answer: The age limit for a Judge of a High Court is sixty-two years.

1127.question: What position has an age limit of sixty-two years?
1127.answer: A Judge of a High Court has an age limit of sixty-two years.

1128.question: What are the conditions for resignation or removal of a Judge of a High Court?
1128.answer: A Judge may resign by writing under his hand addressed to the President. A Judge may be removed from his office by the President in the manner provided in clause (4) of article 124 for the removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court.

1129.question: How can a Judge of a High Court resign or be removed from his office?
1129.answer: A Judge may resign by writing under his hand addressed to the President. He may be removed from his office by the President in the manner provided in clause (4) of article 124 for the removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court.

1130.question: What is the qualification for appointment as a Judge of a High Court?
1130.answer: A person shall not be qualified for appointment as a Judge of a High Court unless he is a citizen of India and has for at least ten years held a judicial office in the territory.

1131.question: What does a person need to be a citizen of and what judicial position must they have held for at least ten years to qualify for appointment as a Judge of a High Court?
1131.answer: A person needs to be a citizen of India and have held a judicial office in the territory for at least ten years to qualify for appointment as a Judge of a High Court.

1132.question: What is included in computing the period during which a person has held judicial office in the territory of India?
1132.answer: There shall be included any period, after he has held any judicial office, during which the person has been an advocate of a High Court or has held the office of a member of a tribunal or any post, under the Union or a State, requiring special knowledge of law

1133.question: What does it mean for a person to have held a judicial office in the territory of India, considering their professional history?
1133.answer: It means that not only the period during which they directly held a judicial office is included, but also any period after that during which they have been an advocate of a High Court, held the office of a member of a tribunal, or any post under the Union or a State that requires special knowledge of law.

1134.question: What is included in computing the period during which a person has been an advocate of a High Court?
1134.answer: There shall be included any period during which the person has held judicial office or the office of a member of a tribunal or any post, under the Union or a State, requiring special knowledge of law after he became an advocate

1135.question: What should be included in the period during which a person has been an advocate of a High Court, if the person has held a judicial office or the office of a member of a tribunal or any post under the Union or a State requiring special knowledge of law?
1135.answer: There shall be included any period during which the person has held judicial office or the office of a member of a tribunal or any post, under the Union or a State, requiring special knowledge of law after he became an advocate

1136.question: What is included in computing the period during which a person has held judicial office in the territory of India or been an advocate of a High Court, before the commencement of this Constitution?
1136.answer: There shall be included any period before the commencement of this Constitution during which he has held judicial office in any area which was comprised before the fifteenth day of August, 1947, within India as defined by the Government of India Act, 1935, or has been an advocate of any High Court in any such area, as the case may be

1137.question: What does it mean for a person to have held judicial office in the territory of India or been an advocate of a High Court, before the commencement of this Constitution?
1137.answer: It means that there shall be included any period before the commencement of this Constitution during which he has held judicial office in any area which was comprised before the fifteenth day of August, 1947, within India as defined by the Government of India Act, 1935, or has been an advocate of any High Court in any such area, as the case may be.

1138.question: Who decides any question that arises as to the age of a Judge of a High Court?
1138.answer: The question shall be decided by the President after consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the decision of the President shall be final

1139.question: Who does the President consult with before deciding any question about the age of a High Court Judge and whose decision is final?
1139.answer: The President consults with the Chief Justice of India before deciding any question about the age of a High Court Judge and the President's decision is final.

1140.question: Which provisions of article 124 apply in relation to a High Court?
1140.answer: The provisions of clauses (4) and (5) of article 124 shall apply in relation to a High Court as they apply in relation to the Supreme Court with the substitution of references to the High Court for references to the Supreme Court

1141.question: To which court do the provisions of clauses (4) and (5) of article 124 apply, with the substitution of references to the High Court for references to the Supreme Court?
1141.answer: The provisions of clauses (4) and (5) of article 124 apply to the High Court.

1142.question: What must a judge do before entering his office according to the Constitution of India?
1142.answer: A judge must make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before the Governor of the State, or some person appointed in that behalf by him, according to the form set out for the purpose in the Third Schedule.

1143.question: Who must a judge make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before and according to what schedule in the Constitution of India prior to entering office?
1143.answer: A judge must make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before the Governor of the State, or some person appointed in that behalf by him, according to the form set out for the purpose in the Third Schedule.

1144.question: What restrictions are placed on a person after holding office as a permanent judge of a High Court in India?
1144.answer: No person who has held office as a permanent Judge of a High Court is allowed to plead or act in any court or before any authority in India except the Supreme Court and the other High Courts.

1145.question: Where can a person who has held office as a permanent Judge of a High Court in India plead or act?
1145.answer: A person who has held office as a permanent Judge of a High Court in India can only plead or act in the Supreme Court and the other High Courts.

1146.question: What does the term 'High Court' exclude according to the Constitution of India?
1146.answer: The term 'High Court' does not include a High Court for a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule as it existed before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956.

1147.question: Which High Court is excluded from the term 'High Court' according to the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 in India?
1147.answer: A High Court for a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule as it existed before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 is excluded from the term 'High Court'.

1148.question: Who determines the salaries of the Judges of each High Court in India?
1148.answer: The salaries of the Judges of each High Court are determined by Parliament by law.

1149.question: Who is responsible for determining the salaries of the Judges of each High Court by law in India?
1149.answer: Parliament is responsible for determining the salaries of the Judges of each High Court in India.

1150.question: What allowances and rights are Judges entitled to?
1150.answer: Every Judge is entitled to such allowances and to such rights in respect of leave of absence and pension as may from time to time be determined by or under law made by Parliament.

1151.question: Who is entitled to allowances, leave of absence, and pension as determined by or under law made by Parliament?
1151.answer: Every Judge is entitled to these allowances and rights.

1152.question: Can the allowances of a Judge or his rights in respect of leave of absence or pension be varied after his appointment?
1152.answer: Neither the allowances of a Judge nor his rights in respect of leave of absence or pension can be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.

1153.question: Can either the allowances of a Judge or his rights in respect of leave of absence or pension be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment?
1153.answer: No, neither the allowances of a Judge nor his rights in respect of leave of absence or pension can be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.

1154.question: Who can transfer a Judge from one High Court to another?
1154.answer: The President, on the recommendation of the National Judicial Appointments Commission, can transfer a Judge from one High Court to any other High Court.

1155.question: Who recommends the transfer of a Judge from one High Court to another to the President?
1155.answer: The National Judicial Appointments Commission recommends the transfer of a Judge from one High Court to another to the President.

1156.question: Who determines the compensatory allowance of a Chief Justice when not determined by law?

1157.question: Who is responsible for determining the compensatory allowance of a Chief Justice when not determined by law?

1158.question: Who performs the duties of the Chief Justice of a High Court when the office is vacant or the Chief Justice is unable to perform his duties?
1158.answer: One of the other Judges of the Court as the President may appoint

1159.question: Who does the President appoint to perform the duties of the Chief Justice of a High Court when the office is vacant or the Chief Justice is unable to perform his duties?
1159.answer: One of the other Judges of the Court

1160.question: Under what conditions can the President increase the number of Judges in a High Court?
1160.answer: If there is a temporary increase in the business of a High Court or because of arrears of work therein

1161.question: Why might the President increase the number of Judges in a High Court?
1161.answer: The President can increase the number of Judges in a High Court if there is a temporary increase in the business of a High Court or because of arrears of work therein.

1162.question: For how long can a person be appointed as an additional Judge of a High Court?
1162.answer: For a period not exceeding two years

1163.question: What is the maximum duration for which a person can be appointed as an additional Judge of a High Court?
1163.answer: For a period not exceeding two years

1164.question: What is the age limit for a person appointed as an additional or acting Judge of a High Court?

1165.question: What is the maximum age for a person to be appointed as an additional or acting Judge of a High Court?

1166.question: Who can request the appointment of a retired Judge at the sittings of High Courts?
1166.answer: The National Judicial Appointments Commission on a reference made by the Chief Justice of a High Court

1167.question: Who can make a reference to the National Judicial Appointments Commission for the appointment of a retired judge at the sittings of High Courts?
1167.answer: The Chief Justice of a High Court

1168.question: What allowances is a person entitled to when requested to act as a High Court Judge according to this text?
1168.answer: The person is entitled to such allowances as the President may by order determine.

1169.question: Who determines the allowances for a person requested to act as a High Court Judge?

1170.question: Does a person requested to act as a High Court Judge have to consent to do so?
1170.answer: No, the person does not have to consent to act as a High Court Judge.

1171.question: Does a person required to act as a High Court Judge have the freedom to decline?
1171.answer: Yes, the person can decline to act as a High Court Judge.

1172.question: What powers do existing High Courts have according to this text?
1172.answer: Existing High Courts have the jurisdiction of, and the law administered in, any existing High Court, and the respective powers of the Judges thereof in relation to the administration of justice in the Court, including any power to make rules of Court and to regulate the sittings of the Court and of members thereof sitting alone or in Division Courts.

1173.question: What does the jurisdiction and law administered by existing High Courts include, along with the powers of the Judges in relation to the administration of justice?
1173.answer: Existing High Courts have the jurisdiction of, and the law administered in, any existing High Court, and the respective powers of the Judges thereof in relation to the administration of justice in the Court, including any power to make rules of Court and to regulate the sittings of the Court and of members thereof sitting alone or in Division Courts.

1174.question: Are there any restrictions on the original jurisdiction of High Courts with respect to revenue matters?
1174.answer: Any restriction to which the exercise of original jurisdiction by any of the High Courts with respect to any matter concerning the revenue or concerning any act ordered or done in the collection thereof was subject immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall no longer apply to the exercise of such jurisdiction.

1175.question: What happened to the restrictions that were imposed on the original jurisdiction of the High Courts with respect to revenue matters or acts ordered or done in the collection thereof prior to the commencement of this Constitution?
1175.answer: Any restriction to which the exercise of original jurisdiction by any of the High Courts with respect to any matter concerning the revenue or concerning any act ordered or done in the collection thereof was subject immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall no longer apply to the exercise of such jurisdiction.

1176.question: What power do High Courts have in relation to issuing writs?
1176.answer: Every High Court shall have power, throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction, to issue to any person or authority, including in appropriate cases, any Government, within those territories directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, or any of them, for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by Part III and for any other purpose.

1177.question: What does the enforcement of rights conferred by Part III entail and who has the power to issue directions, orders, or writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari within their territories?
1177.answer: Every High Court has the power to enforce any of the rights conferred by Part III and to issue to any person or authority, including in appropriate cases, any Government, within their territories directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari.

1178.question: Who can exercise the power to issue directions, orders or writs to any Government, authority or person?
1178.answer: Any High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the territories within which the cause of action, wholly or in part, arises for the exercise of such power.

1179.question: Who can exercise the power to issue directions, orders or writs to any government, authority or person within the territories where the cause of action arises, wholly or in part?
1179.answer: Any High Court exercising jurisdiction can exercise such power.

1180.question: What must a party do to make an application to the High Court for the vacation of an interim order?
1180.answer: The party must furnish a copy of such application to the party in whose favour such order has been made or the counsel of such party.

1181.question: Who must a party furnish a copy of their application to when applying to the High Court for the vacation of an interim order?
1181.answer: The party must furnish a copy of such application to the party in whose favour such order has been made or the counsel of such party.

1182.question: When will the High Court dispose of the application for the vacation of an interim order?
1182.answer: The High Court shall dispose of the application within a period of two weeks from the date on which it is received or from the date on which the copy of such application is so furnished, whichever is later.

1183.question: What is the timeframe within which the High Court should dispose of an application for the vacation of an interim order?
1183.answer: The High Court should dispose of the application within a period of two weeks from the date on which it is received or from the date on which the copy of such application is so furnished, whichever is later.

1184.question: What happens if the application for the vacation of an interim order is not disposed of within the stipulated time?
1184.answer: The interim order shall, on the expiry of that period, or, as the case may be, the expiry of the said next day, stand vacated.

1185.question: What happens to the interim order when the stipulated period, or the said next day expires, and the application for its vacation hasn't been disposed of?
1185.answer: The interim order shall stand vacated.

1186.question: Does the power conferred on a High Court by this article derogate the power conferred on the Supreme Court by clause (2) of article 32?
1186.answer: No, the power conferred on a High Court by this article shall not be in derogation of the power conferred on the Supreme Court by clause (2) of article 32.

1187.question: Does the power conferred on a High Court by a certain article stand in derogation of the power given to the Supreme Court by clause (2) of article 32?

1188.question: What was repealed by the Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977, s. 8?
1188.answer: The Constitutional validity of Central laws not to be considered in proceedings under article 226 was repealed.

1189.question: Which amendment repealed the constitutional validity of Central laws not to be considered in proceedings under article 226?

1190.question: Who has the power of superintendence over all courts?
1190.answer: The High Court has the power of superintendence over all courts.

1191.question: What entity has the power of superintendence over all courts?

1192.question: What can the High Court do according to the provided text?
1192.answer: The High Court can call for returns from such courts, make and issue general rules, prescribe forms for regulating the practice and proceedings of such courts, prescribe forms in which books, entries and accounts shall be kept by the officers of any such courts, and settle tables of fees to be allowed to the sheriff and all clerks and officers of such courts and to attorneys, advocates and pleaders practising therein.

1193.question: What are the responsibilities and powers of the High Court such as regulating practices and proceedings, prescribing forms, and settling tables of fees?
1193.answer: The High Court can call for returns from such courts, make and issue general rules, prescribe forms for regulating the practice and proceedings of such courts, prescribe forms in which books, entries and accounts shall be kept by the officers of any such courts, and settle tables of fees to be allowed to the sheriff and all clerks and officers of such courts and to attorneys, advocates and pleaders practising therein.

1194.question: What conditions must rules, forms, or tables settled by the High Court meet?
1194.answer: Any rules made, forms prescribed or tables settled under clause (2) or clause (3) shall not be inconsistent with the provision of any law for the time being in force, and shall require the previous approval of the Governor.

1195.question: What is the consistency and approval requirement for any rules made, forms prescribed, or tables settled under clause (2) or clause (3) by the High Court?
1195.answer: They shall not be inconsistent with the provision of any law for the time being in force, and shall require the previous approval of the Governor.

1196.question: What is the High Court not deemed to confer on?
1196.answer: The High Court is not deemed to confer on powers of superintendence over any court or tribunal constituted by or under any law relating to the Armed Forces.

1197.question: What is the High Court not allowed to superintend over according to law?
1197.answer: The High Court is not allowed to superintend over any court or tribunal constituted by or under any law relating to the Armed Forces.

1198.question: When can a case be transferred to the High Court?
1198.answer: A case can be transferred to the High Court if it is satisfied that a case pending in a court subordinate to it involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of this Constitution the determination of which is necessary for the disposal of the case.

1199.question: Under what conditions is a case pending in a court subordinate to the High Court transferred to it?
1199.answer: A case is transferred to the High Court if it involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution, the determination of which is necessary for the disposal of the case.

1200.question: What can the High Court do after withdrawing a case?
1200.answer: After withdrawing a case, the High Court can either dispose of the case itself, or determine the said question of law and return the case to the court from which the case has been so withdrawn together with a copy of its judgment on such question. The said court shall on receipt thereof proceed to dispose of the case in conformity with such judgment.

1201.question: What happens when the High Court disposes of a case itself or determines the said question of law, after withdrawing a case?
1201.answer: When the High Court disposes of a case itself after withdrawing it, or determines the said question of law, it can return the case to the court from which the case has been so withdrawn together with a copy of its judgment on such question. The said court shall on receipt thereof proceed to dispose of the case in conformity with such judgment.

1202.question: Who appoints the officers and servants of a High Court?
1202.answer: The Chief Justice of the Court or such other Judge or officer of the Court as he may direct.

1203.question: Who has the authority to direct the appointment of officers and servants in a High Court?
1203.answer: The Chief Justice of the Court

1204.question: Under what condition can a person not already attached to the Court be appointed to any office connected with the Court?
1204.answer: The Governor of the State may by rule require that in such cases as may be specified in the rule no person not already attached to the Court shall be appointed to any office connected with the Court save after consultation with the State Public Service Commission.

1205.question: What rule may the Governor of the State implement regarding the appointment of individuals not already attached to the Court to any office connected with the Court?
1205.answer: The Governor of the State may by rule require that in such cases as may be specified in the rule no person not already attached to the Court shall be appointed to any office connected with the Court save after consultation with the State Public Service Commission.

1206.question: Who prescribes the conditions of service of officers and servants of a High Court?
1206.answer: The conditions of service of officers and servants of a High Court shall be such as may be prescribed by rules made by the Chief Justice of the Court or by some other Judge or officer of the Court authorised by the Chief Justice.

1207.question: Who is authorized to make rules prescribing the conditions of service for officers and servants of a High Court?
1207.answer: The Chief Justice of the Court or some other Judge or officer of the Court authorised by the Chief Justice is authorized to make rules prescribing the conditions of service for officers and servants of a High Court.

1208.question: What does the administrative expenses of a High Court include?
1208.answer: The administrative expenses of a High Court include all salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of the officers and servants of the Court.

1209.question: What do the salaries, allowances, and pensions payable to or in respect of the officers and servants of the Court refer to in the context of High Court expenses?
1209.answer: The salaries, allowances, and pensions payable to or in respect of the officers and servants of the Court refer to the administrative expenses of a High Court.

1210.question: What is charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State?
1210.answer: The administrative expenses of a High Court, including all salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of the officers and servants of the Court, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State.

1211.question: What are the administrative expenses of a High Court, including all salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of the officers and servants of the Court, charged upon?
1211.answer: The administrative expenses of a High Court are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State.
