1212.question: Who can extend the jurisdiction of a High Court to, or exclude the jurisdiction of a High Court from, any Union territory?
1212.answer: Parliament may by law extend the jurisdiction of a High Court to, or exclude the jurisdiction of a High Court from, any Union territory.

1213.question: Who has the power to by law extend or exclude a High Court's jurisdiction over Union territories?

1214.question: Who is referred to in place of the Governor in relation to any rules, forms or tables for subordinate courts in a Union territory?
1214.answer: The reference in article 227 to the Governor shall, in relation to any rules, forms or tables for subordinate courts in that territory, be construed as a reference to the President.

1215.question: Who does the reference in article 227 pertain to in relation to any rules, forms or tables for subordinate courts in a union territory?
1215.answer: The reference in article 227 pertains to the President.

1216.question: Who can establish a common High Court for two or more States or Union territories?

1217.question: Who has the authority to establish a common High Court for two or more States or Union territories?

1218.question: In article 227, who is referred to as the Governor in relation to rules for subordinate courts?
1218.answer: The Governor of the State in which the subordinate courts are situated

1219.question: Who is referred to as the Governor of the State in which the subordinate courts are situated, in article 227?

1220.question: How are the references in articles 219 and 229 construed?
1220.answer: As a reference to the State in which the High Court has its principal seat

1221.question: What does the reference in articles 219 and 229 refer to?
1221.answer: The State in which the High Court has its principal seat

1222.question: What happens if the principal seat of the High Court is in a Union territory?
1222.answer: The references in articles 219 and 229 to the Governor, Public Service Commission, Legislature and Consolidated Fund of the State are construed as references to the President, Union Public Service Commission, Parliament and Consolidated Fund of India.

1223.question: What are the references in articles 219 and 229 construed as if the principal seat of the High Court is in a Union territory?
1223.answer: The references are construed as references to the President, Union Public Service Commission, Parliament and Consolidated Fund of India.

1224.question: Who is responsible for the appointment, posting and promotion of district judges in any State?
1224.answer: The Governor of the State in consultation with the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to such State

1225.question: Who does the Governor of the State consult with for the appointment, posting and promotion of district judges in their State?
1225.answer: The High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to such State

1226.question: Who is eligible to be appointed a district judge?
1226.answer: A person not already in the service of the Union or of the State who has been an advocate or a pleader for not less than seven years and is recommended by the High Court for appointment.

1227.question: What are the qualifications and requirements for a person not in the service of the Union or of the State to be recommended by the High Court for appointment as a district judge?
1227.answer: They must have been an advocate or a pleader for not less than seven years.

1228.question: What does article 233A validate?
1228.answer: The appointments of, and judgments, etc., delivered by, certain district judges

1229.question: Which article validates the appointments of, and judgments, etc., delivered by, certain district judges?

1230.question: When was the Constitution (Twentieth Amendment) Act commenced?

1231.question: What significant constitutional act commenced in 1966?

1232.question: What will be deemed illegal or void according to the Constitution (Twentieth Amendment) Act, 1966?
1232.answer: Any appointment, posting, promotion or transfer made at any time before the commencement of the Act, otherwise than in accordance with the provisions of article 233 or article 235

1233.question: What is considered illegal or void under the Constitution (Twentieth Amendment) Act, 1966, in terms of appointments, postings, promotions, or transfers made prior to the commencement of the Act?
1233.answer: Any appointment, posting, promotion or transfer made at any time before the commencement of the Act, otherwise than in accordance with the provisions of article 233 or article 235

1234.question: What will not be deemed illegal or invalid according to the Constitution (Twentieth Amendment) Act, 1966?
1234.answer: No jurisdiction exercised, no judgment, decree, sentence or order passed or made, and no other act or proceeding done or taken, before the commencement of the Act by, or before, any person appointed, posted, promoted or transferred as a district judge in any State otherwise than in accordance with the provisions of article 233 or article 235

1235.question: What activities performed by a district judge in any State, before the commencement of the Constitution (Twentieth Amendment) Act, 1966, will not be deemed illegal or invalid?
1235.answer: No jurisdiction exercised, no judgment, decree, sentence or order passed or made, and no other act or proceeding done or taken, before the commencement of the Act by, or before, any person appointed, posted, promoted or transferred as a district judge in any State otherwise than in accordance with the provisions of article 233 or article 235

1236.question: Who makes the appointments of persons other than district judges to the judicial service of a State?

1237.question: Who is responsible for appointing persons other than district judges to the judicial service in a state?

1238.question: Who has control over district courts and courts subordinate thereto?

1239.question: What entity has control over district courts and courts subordinate thereto?

1240.question: What rights does article 235 of the Constitution not take away from a person belonging to the judicial service of a State?
1240.answer: Any right of appeal which he may have under the law regulating the conditions of his service

1241.question: Under article 235 of the Constitution, what is a right that a person belonging to the judicial service of a State retains?
1241.answer: Any right of appeal which he may have under the law regulating the conditions of his service

1242.question: What does the expression 'district judge' include according to the Constitution of India?
1242.answer: The expression 'district judge' includes judge of a city civil court, additional district judge, joint district judge, assistant district judge, chief judge of a small cause court, chief presidency magistrate, additional chief presidency magistrate, sessions judge, additional sessions judge and assistant sessions Judge.

1243.question: Who are the roles included under the term 'district judge' according to the Constitution of India?
1243.answer: The term 'district judge' includes judge of a city civil court, additional district judge, joint district judge, assistant district judge, chief judge of a small cause court, chief presidency magistrate, additional chief presidency magistrate, sessions judge, additional sessions judge and assistant sessions Judge.

1244.question: What is meant by 'judicial service' as per the Indian Constitution?
1244.answer: 'Judicial service' means a service consisting exclusively of persons intended to fill the post of district judge and other civil judicial posts inferior to the post of district judge.

1245.question: What posts does the 'judicial service' consist of according to the Indian Constitution?
1245.answer: 'Judicial service' consists of persons intended to fill the post of district judge and other civil judicial posts inferior to the post of district judge.

1246.question: Who has the authority to apply the provisions of the Chapter to certain class or classes of magistrates?
1246.answer: The Governor has the authority to apply the provisions of the Chapter to certain class or classes of magistrates.

1247.question: Who applies the provisions of the Chapter to certain class or classes of magistrates?

1248.question: Who administers every Union territory as per the Indian Constitution?
1248.answer: Every Union territory shall be administered by the President acting, to such extent as he thinks fit, through an administrator to be appointed by him with such designation as he may specify.

1249.question: Who appoints the administrator for a Union territory and how much control do they have as per the Indian Constitution?
1249.answer: The President appoints the administrator for a Union territory and he can act to such extent as he thinks fit.

1250.question: Can the President appoint the Governor of a State as the administrator of an adjoining Union territory?
1250.answer: Yes, the President may appoint the Governor of a State as the administrator of an adjoining Union territory.

1251.question: Is it possible for the Governor of a State to be appointed as the administrator of an adjoining Union territory by the President?
1251.answer: Yes, the President may appoint the Governor of a State as the administrator of an adjoining Union territory.

1252.question: Who can create a body to function as a Legislature for the Union territory?

1253.question: What entity has the power to create a body to function as a Legislature for the Union territory?

1254.question: What name is given to the Union territory of Delhi after the commencement of the Constitution (Sixty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1991?

1255.question: What was Delhi called after the Constitution (Sixty-ninth Amendment) Act, 1991 came into effect?

1257.question: What is the position of the person who is appointed as the administrator of the National Capital Territory of Delhi?

1259.question: What does the National Capital Territory have in terms of a governing body?

1260.question: How are the seats in the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory filled?
1260.answer: By members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies

1261.question: What is the method for selecting members for the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory?
1261.answer: Members are chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies

1262.question: Who regulates the number of seats in the Legislative Assembly, the number of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes, and the division of the National Capital Territory into territorial constituencies?

1263.question: What entity is responsible for regulating the number of seats in the Legislative Assembly, the number of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes, and the division of the National Capital Territory into territorial constituencies?

1265.question: Which articles of the constitution apply to both the National Capital Territory, its Legislative Assembly and the members thereof, as well as a State, its Legislative Assembly and the members thereof?

1266.question: What power does the Legislative Assembly have according to the Constitution?
1266.answer: The Legislative Assembly has power to make laws for the whole or any part of the National Capital Territory with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the State List or in the Concurrent List in so far as any such matter is applicable to Union territories except matters with respect to Entries 1, 2 and 18 of the State List and Entries 64, 65 and 66 of that List in so far as they relate to the said Entries 1, 2 and 18.

1267.question: Which entries in the State List and Concurrent List is the Legislative Assembly not allowed to make laws for according to the Constitution?
1267.answer: The Legislative Assembly is not allowed to make laws for Entries 1, 2 and 18 of the State List and Entries 64, 65 and 66 of that List in so far as they relate to the said Entries 1, 2 and 18.

1268.question: What happens if a provision of a law made by the Legislative Assembly is repugnant to a provision of a law made by Parliament?
1268.answer: If any provision of a law made by the Legislative Assembly with respect to any matter is repugnant to any provision of a law made by Parliament with respect to that matter, whether passed before or after the law made by the Legislative Assembly, or of an earlier law, other than a law made by the Legislative Assembly, then, in either case, the law made by Parliament, or, as the case may be, such earlier law, shall prevail and the law made by the Legislative Assembly shall, to the extent of the repugnancy, be void.

1269.question: What is the consequence when a law made by the Legislative Assembly is in conflict with a law made by the Parliament, or an earlier law?
1269.answer: If any provision of a law made by the Legislative Assembly with respect to any matter is repugnant to any provision of a law made by Parliament with respect to that matter, whether passed before or after the law made by the Legislative Assembly, or of an earlier law, other than a law made by the Legislative Assembly, then, in either case, the law made by Parliament, or, as the case may be, such earlier law, shall prevail and the law made by the Legislative Assembly shall, to the extent of the repugnancy, be void.

1270.question: What can Parliament do at any time with respect to the same matter?
1270.answer: Parliament can enact at any time any law with respect to the same matter including a law adding to, amending, varying or repealing the law so made by the Legislative Assembly.

1271.question: What actions can Parliament take with respect to a law made by the Legislative Assembly at any time?
1271.answer: Parliament can enact any law related to the same matter, including adding to, amending, varying or repealing the law.

1272.question: What is the role of the Council of Ministers?
1272.answer: The Council of Ministers, consisting of not more than ten per cent. of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly, with the Chief Minister at the head, aids and advises the Lieutenant Governor in the exercise of his functions in relation to matters with respect to which the Legislative Assembly has power to make laws.

1273.question: Who aids and advises the Lieutenant Governor in the exercise of his functions in relation to matters with respect to which the Legislative Assembly has power to make laws?
1273.answer: The Council of Ministers, consisting of not more than ten per cent. of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly, with the Chief Minister at the head, aids and advises the Lieutenant Governor in the exercise of his functions.

1274.question: Who has the power to make laws?

1275.question: What is the role of The Legislative Assembly?
1275.answer: The Legislative Assembly has the power to make laws

1276.question: In case of a difference of opinion between the Lieutenant Governor and his Ministers, to whom is the matter referred?

1277.question: Who is the matter referred to in case of a difference of opinion between the Lieutenant Governor and his Ministers?

1279.question: Who does the President appoint for the position of Chief Minister?

1280.question: Who are the Ministers appointed by?
1280.answer: The President on the advice of the Chief Minister

1281.question: Who advises the President on the appointment of Ministers?

1282.question: To whom are the Council of Ministers collectively responsible?

1283.question: Who is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly?

1284.question: What can Parliament do according to Clause 7a?
1284.answer: Parliament may, by law, make provisions for giving effect to, or supplementing the provisions contained in the foregoing clauses and for all matters incidental or consequential thereto.

1285.question: What does Clause 7a allow the Parliament to do by law?
1285.answer: Clause 7a allows Parliament to make provisions for giving effect to, or supplementing the provisions contained in the foregoing clauses and for all matters incidental or consequential thereto.

1286.question: What does the provision of article 239B apply to?
1286.answer: The National Capital Territory, the Lieutenant Governor and the Legislative Assembly

1287.question: Which article provision applies to the National Capital Territory, the Lieutenant Governor and the Legislative Assembly?

1288.question: What happens in case of failure of constitutional machinery?
1288.answer: The President, on receipt of a report from the Lieutenant

1289.question: Who takes action upon the report from the Lieutenant in case of failure of constitutional machinery?

1290.question: Under what circumstances can the President suspend the operation of any provision of article 239AA?
1290.answer: The President can suspend the operation of any provision of article 239AA if a situation has arisen in which the administration of the National Capital Territory cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of article 239AA or of any law made in pursuance of that article, or that for the proper administration of the National Capital Territory it is necessary or expedient so to do.

1291.question: When can the operation of any provision of article 239AA be suspended by the President for the administration of the National Capital Territory?
1291.answer: The operation of any provision of article 239AA can be suspended by the President if a situation has arisen in which the administration of the National Capital Territory cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of article 239AA or of any law made in pursuance of that article, or that for the proper administration of the National Capital Territory it is necessary or expedient so to do.

1292.question: What power does the administrator have during the recess of Legislature in the Union territory of Puducherry?
1292.answer: If the administrator is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action, he may promulgate such Ordinances as the circumstances appear to him to require, except after obtaining instructions from the President.

1293.question: What action can the administrator take in the Union territory of Puducherry during the recess of Legislature when immediate action is necessary, and what approval is required for this?
1293.answer: The administrator can promulgate such Ordinances as the circumstances appear to him to require, but he must obtain instructions from the President.

1294.question: What is the condition for an Ordinance promulgated under this article to be deemed an Act of the Legislature?
1294.answer: An Ordinance promulgated under this article in pursuance of instructions from the President shall be deemed to be an Act of the Legislature of the Union territory which has been duly enacted after complying with the provisions in that behalf contained in any such law.

1295.question: What is deemed to be an Act of the Legislature of the Union territory under this article?
1295.answer: An Ordinance promulgated in pursuance of instructions from the President is deemed to be an Act of the Legislature of the Union territory which has been duly enacted after complying with the provisions in that behalf contained in any such law.

1296.question: When is the administrator not allowed to promulgate any Ordinance?
1296.answer: The administrator shall not promulgate any Ordinance during the period of such dissolution or suspension of the Legislature.

1297.question: What is the administrator not allowed to do during the period of dissolution or suspension of the Legislature?
1297.answer: The administrator is not allowed to promulgate any Ordinance.

1298.question: What happens to an Ordinance according to clause 1 of article 239A?
1298.answer: The Ordinance shall be laid before the Legislature of the Union territory and shall cease to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of the Legislature or if, before the expiration of that period, a resolution disapproving it is passed by the Legislature, upon the passing of the resolution. It may also be withdrawn at any time by the administrator after obtaining instructions from the President.

1299.question: What happens to an Ordinance laid before the Legislature of the Union territory according to clause 1 of article 239A, and when does it cease to operate?
1299.answer: The Ordinance shall cease to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of the Legislature or if, before the expiration of that period, a resolution disapproving it is passed by the Legislature, upon the passing of the resolution. It may also be withdrawn at any time by the administrator after obtaining instructions from the President.

1300.question: What happens if an Ordinance under article 239A makes a provision that would not be valid if enacted in an Act of the Legislature of the Union territory?

1301.question: What is the consequence if an Ordinance under article 239A makes a provision that would not be valid if enacted in an Act of the Legislature of the Union territory?

1302.question: Under article 240, for which Union territories may the President make regulations?
1302.answer: The President may make regulations for the Union territories of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu, and Puducherry.

1303.question: Which article allows the President to make regulations for the Union territories of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu, and Puducherry?

1304.question: What is the provision related to the creation of a body under article 239A for the Union territory of Puducherry?
1304.answer: When any body is created under article 239A to function as a Legislature for the Union territory of Puducherry, the President shall not make any regulation for the peace, progress and good government of that Union territory with effect from the date appointed for the first meeting of the Legislature.

1305.question: What happens when a body is created under article 239A to function as a Legislature for the Union territory of Puducherry?
1305.answer: The President shall not make any regulation for the peace, progress and good government of that Union territory with effect from the date appointed for the first meeting of the Legislature.

1306.question: What can the President do if the body functioning as a Legislature for the Union territory of Puducherry is dissolved or remains suspended?
1306.answer: The President may, during the period of such dissolution or suspension, make regulations for the peace, progress and good government of that Union territory.

1307.question: What can the President do for the peace, progress and good government of the Union territory of Puducherry during the period of its Legislature's dissolution or suspension?
1307.answer: The President may make regulations during the period of such dissolution or suspension.

1308.question: Can any regulation made by the President under article 240 repeal or amend any Act made by Parliament or any other law?
1308.answer: Yes, any regulation so made may repeal or amend any Act made by Parliament or any other law.

1309.question: Can a regulation made under article 240 repeal or amend any Act made by Parliament or any other law?
1309.answer: Yes, any regulation made by the President under article 240 can repeal or amend any Act made by Parliament or any other law.

1310.question: What is the power of the President in the Union territory?
1310.answer: The President can promulgate laws that are for the time being applicable to the Union territory and these laws will have the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament which applies to that territory.

1311.question: What kind of laws can the President promulgate for the Union territory and what is their effect?
1311.answer: The President can promulgate laws that are for the time being applicable to the Union territory. These laws will have the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament which applies to that territory.

1312.question: What can Parliament constitute for a Union territory?
1312.answer: Parliament may by law constitute a High Court for a Union territory or declare any court in any such territory to be a High Court for all or any of the purposes of the Constitution.

1313.question: What can Parliament do by law for a High Court in a Union territory or any court in such territory in terms of the Constitution?
1313.answer: Parliament may by law constitute a High Court for a Union territory or declare any court in any such territory to be a High Court for all or any of the purposes of the Constitution.

1314.question: What provisions apply to the High Court in a Union territory?
1314.answer: The provisions of Chapter V of Part VI apply in relation to every High Court in a Union territory, subject to modifications or exceptions as Parliament may provide.

1315.question: Which chapter and part of the law applies to the High Court in a Union territory, and who may provide modifications or exceptions to it?
1315.answer: Chapter V of Part VI applies to the High Court in a Union territory, and modifications or exceptions may be provided by the Parliament.

1316.question: What is the jurisdiction of a High Court in a Union territory?
1316.answer: Subject to the provisions of the Constitution and any law of the appropriate Legislature, a High Court exercising jurisdiction immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, in relation to any Union territory shall continue to exercise such jurisdiction in relation to that territory after such commencement.

1317.question: What happens to the jurisdiction of a High Court in a Union territory after the commencement of the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956?
1317.answer: Subject to the provisions of the Constitution and any law of the appropriate Legislature, a High Court exercising jurisdiction immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, in relation to any Union territory shall continue to exercise such jurisdiction in relation to that territory after such commencement.

1318.question: What power does Parliament have in regards to the jurisdiction of a High Court for a State in relation to Union territory?
1318.answer: Parliament has the power to extend or exclude the jurisdiction of a High Court for a State to, or from, any Union territory or part thereof.

1319.question: What can Parliament do in terms of extending or excluding the jurisdiction of a High Court for a State to, or from, any Union territory or part thereof?
1319.answer: Parliament has the power to extend or exclude the jurisdiction of a High Court for a State in relation to Union territory.

1320.question: What does the term 'district' mean in Part IX of the constitution?
1320.answer: In Part IX of the constitution, 'district' means a district in a State.

1321.question: What is the term used in Part IX of the constitution to refer to a district in a State?
1321.answer: The term used in Part IX of the constitution to refer to a district in a State is 'district'.

1322.question: What does 'Gram Sabha' refer to in the constitution?
1322.answer: 'Gram Sabha' means a body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of Panchayat at the village level.

1323.question: What is the body called that consists of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of Panchayat at the village level?

1324.question: What is the 'intermediate level' as specified in the constitution?
1324.answer: 'Intermediate level' means a level between the village and district levels specified by the Governor of a State by public notification to be the intermediate level for the purposes of this Part.

1325.question: Who specifies the 'intermediate level' between the village and district levels in a state and how is it announced?
1325.answer: The 'Intermediate level' is specified by the Governor of a state and it is announced by public notification.

1326.question: What is the definition of 'Panchayat' in the constitution?
1326.answer: 'Panchayat' means an institution as specified in the constitution.

1327.question: What does the term 'Panchayat' refer to in the constitution?
1327.answer: 'Panchayat' refers to an institution as specified in the constitution.

1328.question: What is the meaning of 'Panchayat area'?
1328.answer: The territorial area of a Panchayat

1329.question: What is the term used to describe the territorial area of a Panchayat?

1330.question: What does 'Population' refer to?
1330.answer: The population as ascertained at the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published

1331.question: What does 'the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published' refer to?

1332.question: How is a 'village' defined?
1332.answer: A village specified by the Governor by public notification to be a village for the purposes of this Part and includes a group of villages so specified

1333.question: Who specifies a location to be a 'village' and how is it publicly notified?
1333.answer: The Governor specifies a location to be a 'village' by public notification.

1334.question: What powers does a Gram Sabha have?
1334.answer: A Gram Sabha may exercise such powers and perform such functions at the village level as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide

1335.question: Who provides the laws that determine the powers and functions a Gram Sabha can exercise at the village level?

1336.question: Where will Panchayats be constituted?
1336.answer: Panchayats shall be constituted in every State, at the village, intermediate and district levels in accordance with the provisions of this Part

1337.question: At what levels and in which locations will Panchayats be constituted in accordance with the provisions of this Part?
1337.answer: Panchayats will be constituted in every State, at the village, intermediate, and district levels.

1338.question: When may Panchayats at the intermediate level not be constituted?
1338.answer: Panchayats at the intermediate level may not be constituted in a State having a population not exceeding twenty lakhs

1339.question: Under what condition may a state not constitute Panchayats at the intermediate level?
1339.answer: A state may not constitute Panchayats at the intermediate level if its population does not exceed twenty lakhs.

1340.question: Who can make provisions with respect to the composition of Panchayats?
1340.answer: The Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions with respect to the composition of Panchayats

1341.question: Who has the authority to make laws regarding the composition of Panchayats?

1342.question: How are the seats in a Panchayat filled?
1342.answer: All the seats in a Panchayat shall be filled by persons chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the Panchayat area

1343.question: Who fills the seats in a Panchayat and from where are they chosen?
1343.answer: All the seats in a Panchayat are filled by persons chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the Panchayat area.

1344.question: What is the role of the Chairpersons of the Panchayats at the intermediate level?
1344.answer: The Chairpersons of the Panchayats at the intermediate level are part of the Panchayats at the district level.

1345.question: Who are part of the Panchayats at the district level?
1345.answer: The Chairpersons of the Panchayats at the intermediate level are part of the Panchayats at the district level.

1346.question: Who are the members of the House of the People and the members of the Legislative Assembly representing?
1346.answer: They are representing constituencies which comprise wholly or partly a Panchayat area at a level other than the village level.

1347.question: Who represents constituencies which comprise wholly or partly a Panchayat area at a level other than the village level?
1347.answer: The members of the House of the People and the members of the Legislative Assembly.

1348.question: Where are the members of the Council of States and the members of the Legislative Council of the State registered as electors within?
1348.answer: They are registered as electors within a Panchayat area at the intermediate level, in Panchayat at the intermediate level, and a Panchayat area at the district level, in Panchayat at the district level.

1349.question: Where are individuals registered as electors within a Panchayat area at the intermediate level, in Panchayat at the intermediate level, and a Panchayat area at the district level, in Panchayat at the district level?
1349.answer: The members of the Council of States and the members of the Legislative Council of the State are registered as electors within these areas.

1350.question: Who has the right to vote in the meetings of the Panchayats?
1350.answer: The Chairperson of a Panchayat and other members of a Panchayat whether or not chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the Panchayat area.

1351.question: Who are the individuals, whether or not chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the Panchayat area, that can vote in the Panchayat meetings?
1351.answer: The Chairperson of a Panchayat and other members of a Panchayat

1352.question: How is the Chairperson of a Panchayat at the village level elected?
1352.answer: The Chairperson of a panchayat at the village level is elected in such manner as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide.

1353.question: Who provides the law for the manner in which the Chairperson of a panchayat at the village level is elected?
1353.answer: The Legislature of a State provides the law for the manner in which the Chairperson of a panchayat at the village level is elected.

1354.question: How is the Chairperson of a Panchayat at the intermediate or district level elected?
1354.answer: The Chairperson of a Panchayat at the intermediate level or district level is elected by, and from amongst, the elected members thereof.

1355.question: Who elects the Chairperson of a Panchayat at the intermediate or district level?
1355.answer: The Chairperson of a Panchayat at the intermediate level or district level is elected by the elected members thereof.

1356.question: What is the reservation policy for seats in every Panchayat?
1356.answer: Seats in every Panchayat shall be reserved for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, in proportion to the total number of seats to be filled by direct election in that Panchayat as the population of the Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes in that Panchayat area bears to the total population of that area.

1357.question: Who are the seats in every Panchayat reserved for and how is the proportion determined?
1357.answer: Seats in every Panchayat are reserved for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes. The proportion is determined by the population of the Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes in that Panchayat area relative to the total population of that area.

1358.question: What is the reservation policy for women in every Panchayat?
1358.answer: Not less than one-third of the total number of seats reserved shall be reserved for women.

1359.question: What is the minimum percentage of seats reserved for women in every Panchayat?
1359.answer: One-third of the total number of seats are reserved for women in every Panchayat.

1360.question: What percentage of the total number of seats to be filled by direct election in every Panchayat is reserved for women?

1361.question: What is the minimum quota for women in the total number of seats to be filled by direct election in every Panchayat?

1362.question: How are the seats reserved for women in Panchayats allotted?
1362.answer: By rotation to different constituencies in a Panchayat

1363.question: What is the method used to allot the seats reserved for women in Panchayats?
1363.answer: By rotation to different constituencies in a Panchayat

1364.question: Who are the offices of the Chairpersons in the Panchayats at the village or any other level reserved for?
1364.answer: The Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and women

1365.question: For whom are the offices of the Chairpersons in the Panchayats at the village or any other level reserved?
1365.answer: The Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and women

1366.question: What is the method of allotting the number of offices reserved under this clause?
1366.answer: By rotation to different Panchayats at each level

1367.question: What is the procedure for allotting the number of offices reserved under a specific clause to different Panchayats at each level?

1368.question: When does the reservation of seats and the reservation of offices of Chairpersons cease to have effect?
1368.answer: On the expiration of the period specified in article 334

1369.question: What happens on the expiration of the period specified in article 334?
1369.answer: The reservation of seats and the reservation of offices of Chairpersons cease to have effect.

1370.question: Can the Legislature of a State make any provision for reservation of seats in any Panchayat or offices of Chairpersons in favour of backward class of citizens?

1371.question: Is it possible for the Legislature of a State to make a provision for reservation of seats in any Panchayat or offices of Chairpersons in favour of backward class of citizens?

1372.question: What is the duration of Panchayats according to 243E?
1372.answer: Every Panchayat, unless sooner dissolved under any law for the time being in force, shall continue

1373.question: Does a Panchayat continue unless sooner dissolved under any law for the time being in force, according to 243E?
1373.answer: Yes, according to 243E, every Panchayat shall continue unless sooner dissolved under any law for the time being in force.

1374.question: How long does a Panchayat continue from its first meeting?

1375.question: What is the tenure of a Panchayat from its first meeting?

1376.question: Can an amendment of any law cause the dissolution of a Panchayat?

1377.question: Does the amendment of any law lead to the dissolution of a Panchayat?

1378.question: When should an election to constitute a Panchayat be completed?
1378.answer: Before the expiry of its duration specified in clause (1) or before the expiration of a period of six months from the date of its dissolution

1379.question: What is the time period before which an election to constitute a Panchayat should be completed after its dissolution or before the expiry of its duration specified in clause (1)?
1379.answer: Before the expiration of a period of six months

1380.question: What happens if the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued is less than six months?
1380.answer: It shall not be necessary to hold any election under this clause for constituting the Panchayat for such period.

1381.question: What happens when it is not necessary to hold any election for constituting the Panchayat for a certain period?
1381.answer: This happens if the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued is less than six months.

1382.question: What is the duration for a Panchayat constituted upon the dissolution of a Panchayat?
1382.answer: It shall continue only for the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued under clause (1) had it not been so dissolved.

1383.question: What happens to the duration of a new Panchayat that is formed after the dissolution of the previous Panchayat?
1383.answer: It shall continue only for the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued under clause (1) had it not been so dissolved.

1384.question: What are the disqualifications for being a member of a Panchayat?
1384.answer: A person shall be disqualified if he is so disqualified by or under any law for the purposes of elections to the Legislature of the State concerned, and if he is disqualified by or under any law made by the Legislature of the State.

1385.question: Under what circumstances would a person be disqualified from being a member of a Panchayat according to the law made by the Legislature of the State?
1385.answer: A person would be disqualified if he is disqualified by or under any law for the purposes of elections to the Legislature of the State concerned.

1386.question: Can a person less than twenty-five years of age be a member of a Panchayat?
1386.answer: No person shall be disqualified on the ground that he is less than twenty-five years of age, if he has attained the age of twenty-one years.

1387.question: What is the minimum age for a person to become a member of a Panchayat?
1387.answer: A person needs to have attained the age of twenty-one years to become a member of a Panchayat.

1388.question: What happens if a question arises as to whether a member of a Panchayat has become subject to any of the disqualifications?
1388.answer: The question shall be referred for the decision of such authority and in such manner as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide.

1389.question: In case of a dispute regarding a Panchayat member's disqualification, where and how should the matter be resolved?
1389.answer: The question shall be referred for the decision of such authority and in such manner as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide.

1390.question: What powers can a State legislature endow the Panchayats with by law?
1390.answer: The powers and authority necessary to function as institutions of self-government. This may include provisions for the devolution of powers and responsibilities, preparation of plans for economic development and social justice, and implementation of such schemes.

1391.question: What does the devolution of powers and responsibilities, preparation of plans for economic development and social justice, and implementation of such schemes refer to in the context of State legislature and Panchayats?
1391.answer: These refer to the powers that a State legislature can endow the Panchayats with by law, necessary for them to function as institutions of self-government.

1392.question: What financial powers can a State legislature grant the Panchayats?
1392.answer: The State legislature can authorise a Panchayat to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees, assign such taxes collected by the State Government to a Panchayat, provide grants-in-aid to the Panchayats from the Consolidated Fund of the State, and provide for constitution of Funds for crediting all moneys received by or on behalf of the Panchayats.

1393.question: What can a State legislature authorise a Panchayat to do in terms of financial matters?
1393.answer: The State legislature can authorise a Panchayat to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees, assign such taxes collected by the State Government to a Panchayat, provide grants-in-aid to the Panchayats from the Consolidated Fund of the State, and provide for constitution of Funds for crediting all moneys received by or on behalf of the Panchayats.

1394.question: What is the role of the Finance Commission according to the Constitution?
1394.answer: The Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor of a State to review the financial position of the Panchayats and to make recommendations on the principles which should govern the distribution between the State and the Panchayats of the net proceeds of the taxes, duties, tolls and fees leviable by the State.

1395.question: Who constitutes the Finance Commission and what are its responsibilities regarding the financial position of the Panchayats and the distribution of the net proceeds of the taxes, duties, tolls and fees leviable by the State?
1395.answer: The Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor of a State to review the financial position of the Panchayats and to make recommendations on the principles which should govern the distribution between the State and the Panchayats of the net proceeds of the taxes, duties, tolls and fees leviable by the State.

1396.question: What is one of the roles of the Finance Commission in relation to Panchayats according to the Constitution of India?
1396.answer: They are responsible for the allocation between the Panchayats at all levels of their respective shares of such proceeds, the determination of the taxes, duties, tolls and fees which may be assigned to, or appropriated by, the Panchayats, the grants-in-aid to the Panchayats from the Consolidated Fund of the State, and measures needed to improve the financial position of the Panchayats.

1397.question: What responsibilities does the Finance Commission have regarding the allocation of shares, determination of taxes, duties, tolls and fees, the grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of the State, and measures to improve the financial position for Panchayats at all levels according to the Constitution of India?
1397.answer: These are some of the roles of the Finance Commission in relation to Panchayats according to the Constitution of India.

1398.question: What is the role of the State Election Commission in relation to Panchayats?
1398.answer: The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to the Panchayats is vested in a State Election Commission.

1399.question: Who is vested with the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to the Panchayats?

1400.question: Who appoints the State Election Commissioner?
1400.answer: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor.

1401.question: Who is appointed by the Governor for the role of State Election Commissioner?
1401.answer: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor.

1402.question: What provisions may the Legislature of a State make with respect to Panchayats?
1402.answer: The Legislature of a State may make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by the Panchayats and the auditing of such accounts.

1403.question: What may the Legislature of a State make provisions for in relation to the Panchayats?
1403.answer: The Legislature of a State may make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by the Panchayats and the auditing of such accounts.

1404.question: Can the State Election Commissioner be removed from his office?
1404.answer: The State Election Commissioner can be removed from his office, but only in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of a High Court.

1405.question: On what grounds and in what manner can the State Election Commissioner be removed from his office?
1405.answer: The State Election Commissioner can be removed from his office only in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of a High Court.

1406.question: What is the Governor of a State required to do when requested by the State Election Commission?
1406.answer: The Governor of a State shall make available to the State Election Commission such staff as may be necessary for the discharge of the functions conferred on the State Election Commission by clause (1).

1407.question: What is the Governor of a State obliged to provide to the State Election Commission according to clause (1)?
1407.answer: The Governor of a State is required to make available such staff as may be necessary for the discharge of the functions conferred on the State Election Commission.

1408.question: What power does the legislature of a State have in relation to elections to the Panchayats?
1408.answer: The Legislature of a State may, by law, make provision with respect to all matters relating to, or in connection with, elections to the Panchayats.

1409.question: What can the Legislature of a State do with respect to all matters relating to, or in connection with, elections to the Panchayats?
1409.answer: The Legislature of a State has the power to make provision by law.

1410.question: How do the provisions of Part 243L apply to Union territories?
1410.answer: The provisions of this Part shall apply to the Union territories and shall, in their application to a Union territory, have effect as if the references to the Governor of a State were references to the Administrator of the Union territory appointed under article 239 and references to the Legislature or the legislative Assembly of a State were references, in relation to a Union territory having a Legislative Assembly, to that Legislative Assembly.

1411.question: How do the references to the Governor of a State and the Legislature or the legislative Assembly of a State change when the provisions of Part 243L are applied to a Union territory?
1411.answer: When the provisions of Part 243L are applied to a Union territory, the references to the Governor of a State become references to the Administrator of the Union territory appointed under article 239 and references to the Legislature or the legislative Assembly of a State become references, in relation to a Union territory having a Legislative Assembly, to that Legislative Assembly.

1412.question: What areas does Part 243M not apply to?
1412.answer: This Part shall not apply to the Scheduled Areas referred to in clause (1), and the tribal areas referred to in clause (2), of article 244, the States of Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram, the hill areas in the State of Manipur for which District Councils exist under any law for the time being in force, and the hill areas of the District of Darjeeling in the State of West Bengal for which Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council exists under any law for the time being in force.

1413.question: Which specific regions and states does this law not apply to, as described in its Part 243M?
1413.answer: Part 243M does not apply to the Scheduled Areas referred to in clause (1), and the tribal areas referred to in clause (2), of article 244, the States of Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram, the hill areas in the State of Manipur for which District Councils exist under any law for the time being in force, and the hill areas of the District of Darjeeling in the State of West Bengal for which Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council exists under any law for the time being in force.

1414.question: What does article 243D relate to?
1414.answer: Reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes.

1415.question: Which article relates to the reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes?

1416.question: Does article 243D apply to the State of Arunachal Pradesh?

1417.question: Is there a state to which article 243D does not apply?

1418.question: What power does the Legislature of a State referred to in sub-clause (a) of clause (2) have according to the Constitution?
1418.answer: It may, by law, extend this part to that State, except the areas, if any, referred to in clause (1), if the Legislative Assembly of that State passes a resolution to that effect by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting.

1419.question: What is the process for a State Legislature referred to in sub-clause (a) of clause (2) to extend a part to that State according to the Constitution?
1419.answer: The Legislature may, by law, extend this part to that State, except the areas, if any, referred to in clause (1), if the Legislative Assembly of that State passes a resolution to that effect by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting.

1420.question: Can Parliament extend the provisions of this Part to the Scheduled Areas and the tribal areas referred to in clause (1)?
1420.answer: Yes, subject to such exceptions and modifications as may be specified in such law.

1421.question: What conditions must be met for Parliament to extend the provisions of this Part to the Scheduled Areas and the tribal areas referred to in clause (1)?
1421.answer: The conditions must be subject to such exceptions and modifications as may be specified in such law.

1422.question: What is the effect of any law relating to Panchayats in force in a State immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992?
1422.answer: Any provision of any law relating to Panchayats in force in a State immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992, which is inconsistent with the provisions of this Part, shall continue to be in force until amended or repealed by a competent Legislature or other competent authority or until the expiration of one year from such commencement, whichever is earlier.

1423.question: What happens to the provisions of any law relating to Panchayats in force in a State immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992, if they are inconsistent with the provisions of this Part?
1423.answer: Any such provision shall continue to be in force until amended or repealed by a competent Legislature or other competent authority or until the expiration of one year from such commencement, whichever is earlier.

1424.question: What happens to Panchayats existing immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992?
1424.answer: All the Panchayats existing immediately before such commencement shall continue till the expiration of their duration, unless sooner dissolved by a resolution passed to that effect by the Legislative Assembly of that State or, in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, by each House of the Legislature of that State.

1425.question: What will happen to the Panchayats that were in existence immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992, and under what conditions can they be dissolved?
1425.answer: All the Panchayats existing immediately before such commencement will continue till the expiration of their duration, unless sooner dissolved by a resolution passed to that effect by the Legislative Assembly of that State or, in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, by each House of the Legislature of that State.

1426.question: What does section 243-O of the Constitution state?
1426.answer: It bars interference by courts in electoral matters.

1427.question: Which section of the Constitution bars interference by courts in electoral matters?

1428.question: What is the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies?
1428.answer: The validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies, made or purporting to be made under article 243K, shall not be called in question in any court.

1429.question: Can the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies, made or purporting to be made under article 243K, be called into question in any court?
1429.answer: No, the validity of such a law shall not be called in question in any court.

1430.question: Can an election to any Panchayat be called in question?
1430.answer: No election to any Panchayat shall be called in question except by an election petition presented to such authority and in such manner as is provided for by or under any law made by the Legislature of a State.

1431.question: How can an election to a Panchayat be legally questioned?
1431.answer: An election to any Panchayat can be legally questioned by an election petition presented to such authority and in such manner as is provided for by or under any law made by the Legislature of a State.

1432.question: What is a 'Committee' in the context of Part IXA THE MUNICIPALITIES?
1432.answer: A 'Committee' means a Committee constituted under article 243S.

1433.question: Under which article is a 'Committee' constituted in the context of Part IXA THE MUNICIPALITIES?

1434.question: What is a 'Metropolitan area' according to Part IXA THE MUNICIPALITIES?
1434.answer: A 'Metropolitan area' means an area having a population of ten lakhs or more, comprised in one or more districts and consisting of two or more Municipalities or Panchayats or other contiguous areas, specified by the Governor by public notification to be a Metropolitan area for the purposes of this Part.

1435.question: What is the population requirement and structural composition for an area to be designated as a 'Metropolitan area' under Part IXA THE MUNICIPALITIES?
1435.answer: An area must have a population of ten lakhs or more, and must be comprised in one or more districts, consisting of two or more Municipalities or Panchayats or other contiguous areas to be designated as a 'Metropolitan area' under Part IXA THE MUNICIPALITIES.

1436.question: How is 'Municipality' defined in Part IXA THE MUNICIPALITIES?
1436.answer: 'Municipality' means an institution of self-government constituted under article 243Q.

1437.question: Under which article is a 'Municipality', as an institution of self-government, constituted?

1438.question: What does 'Panchayat' mean in the context of Part IXA THE MUNICIPALITIES?
1438.answer: 'Panchayat' means a Panchayat constituted under article 243B.

1439.question: Under which article is a 'Panchayat' constituted in the context of Part IXA THE MUNICIPALITIES?

1440.question: What does 'population' refer to in Part IXA THE MUNICIPALITIES?
1440.answer: 'Population' means the population as ascertained at the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published.

1441.question: What is the meaning of 'population' as per the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published in Part IXA THE MUNICIPALITIES?
1441.answer: 'Population' refers to the population as ascertained at the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published.

1442.question: What will be constituted in every state according to Constitution of Municipalities?
1442.answer: There shall be constituted in every State a Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area, a Municipal Council for a smaller urban area, and a Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area, in accordance with the provisions of this Part.

1443.question: What kind of municipal bodies will be constituted in every State for transitional areas, smaller urban areas, and larger urban areas according to the Constitution?
1443.answer: A Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area, a Municipal Council for a smaller urban area, and a Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area will be constituted in every State according to the Constitution.

1444.question: What does 'a transitional area', 'a smaller urban area' or 'a larger urban area' mean in the context of this article?
1444.answer: These terms refer to areas that the Governor may specify by public notification, considering factors such as population, population density, revenue generated for local administration, percentage of employment in non-agricultural activities, economic importance or other factors deemed fit.

1445.question: What factors does the Governor consider when specifying areas as 'a transitional area', 'a smaller urban area' or 'a larger urban area'?
1445.answer: The Governor may consider factors such as population, population density, revenue generated for local administration, percentage of employment in non-agricultural activities, economic importance or other factors deemed fit.

1446.question: How are the seats in a Municipality filled according to the article?
1446.answer: All the seats in a Municipality are filled by persons chosen by direct election from the territorial constituencies in the Municipal area. Each Municipal area is divided into territorial constituencies known as wards.

1447.question: What are the wards in a Municipal area and how are they filled?
1447.answer: The wards in a Municipal area are territorial constituencies into which each Municipal area is divided. All the seats in these wards are filled by persons chosen by direct election.

1448.question: What can the Legislature of a State provide in the representation in a Municipality?
1448.answer: The Legislature of a State may provide for the representation in a Municipality of people with special knowledge or experience in Municipal administration, members of the House of the People and the Legislative Assembly of the State representing constituencies in the Municipal area, members of the Council of States and the Legislative Council of the State registered as electors within the Municipal area, and the Chairpersons of the Committees constituted under clause (5) of article 243S.

1449.question: Who may the Legislature of a State provide for the representation in a Municipality?
1449.answer: The Legislature of a State may provide for the representation in a Municipality of people with special knowledge or experience in Municipal administration, members of the House of the People and the Legislative Assembly of the State representing constituencies in the Municipal area, members of the Council of States and the Legislative Council of the State registered as electors within the Municipal area, and the Chairpersons of the Committees constituted under clause (5) of article 243S.

1450.question: What is the provision regarding the election of the Chairperson of a Municipality?
1450.answer: The Legislature of a State may by law provide the manner of election of the Chairperson of a Municipality.

1451.question: Who is responsible for providing the manner of election of the Chairperson of a Municipality?
1451.answer: The Legislature of a State is responsible for providing the manner of election of the Chairperson of a Municipality.

1452.question: What is the requirement for the constitution of Wards Committees?
1452.answer: Wards Committees, consisting of one or more wards, should be constituted within the territorial area of a Municipality having a population of three lakhs or more.

1453.question: What is the population requirement for a Municipality to constitute Wards Committees consisting of one or more wards?
1453.answer: A Municipality should have a population of three lakhs or more to constitute Wards Committees consisting of one or more wards.

1454.question: What provisions can the Legislature of a State make regarding a Wards Committee?
1454.answer: The Legislature of a State can make provisions regarding the composition and the territorial area of a Wards Committee and the manner in which the seats in a Wards Committee shall be filled.

1455.question: What aspects of a Wards Committee can the Legislature of a State make provisions about?
1455.answer: The Legislature of a State can make provisions about the composition, the territorial area, and the manner in which the seats in a Wards Committee shall be filled.

1456.question: Who can be a member of a Wards Committee?
1456.answer: A member of a Municipality representing a ward within the territorial area of the Wards Committee shall be a member of that Committee.

1457.question: Who is a member of a Wards Committee within the territorial area they represent in a Municipality?
1457.answer: A member of a Municipality representing a ward within that territorial area is a member of the Wards Committee.

1458.question: Who can be the Chairperson of a Wards Committee?
1458.answer: If a Wards Committee consists of one ward, the member representing that ward in the Municipality; or if it consists of two or more wards, one of the members representing such wards in the Municipality elected by the members of the Wards Committee, shall be the Chairperson of that Committee.

1459.question: Who can be elected as the Chairperson of a Wards Committee if it consists of two or more wards?
1459.answer: One of the members representing such wards in the Municipality elected by the members of the Wards Committee can be the Chairperson of that Committee.

1460.question: What is the provision for reservation of seats in a Municipality for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
1460.answer: Seats shall be reserved for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes in every Municipality and the number of seats so reserved shall bear the same proportion to the total number of seats to be filled by direct election in that Municipality as the population of the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes in the Municipal area bears to the total population of that area. These seats may be allotted by rotation to different constituencies in a Municipality.

1461.question: How are the seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in a Municipality determined and allocated?
1461.answer: Seats shall be reserved for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes in every Municipality and the number of seats so reserved shall bear the same proportion to the total number of seats to be filled by direct election in that Municipality as the population of the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes in the Municipal area bears to the total population of that area. These seats may be allotted by rotation to different constituencies in a Municipality.

1462.question: What is the provision for reservation of seats for women in a Municipality?
1462.answer: Not less than one-third of the total number of seats reserved shall be reserved for women belonging to the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes. Also, not less than one-third (including the number of seats reserved for women belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes) of the total number of seats to be filled by direct election in every Municipality shall be reserved for women and these seats may be allotted by rotation to different constituencies in a Municipality.

1463.question: What is the minimum proportion of seats reserved for women in a Municipality, and how are these seats distributed among the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and general category?
1463.answer: Not less than one-third of the total number of seats reserved shall be reserved for women belonging to the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes. Furthermore, not less than one-third (including the number of seats reserved for women belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes) of the total number of seats to be filled by direct election in every Municipality shall be reserved for women. These seats may be allotted by rotation to different constituencies in a Municipality.

1464.question: Who can the Legislature of a State reserve seats for?
1464.answer: The Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and women

1465.question: For whom can the Legislature of a State reserve seats?
1465.answer: The Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and women

1466.question: When does the reservation of seats under clauses (1) and (2) and the reservation of offices of Chairpersons cease to have effect?
1466.answer: On the expiration of the period specified in article 334

1467.question: What happens on the expiration of the period specified in article 334?
1467.answer: The reservation of seats under clauses (1) and (2) and the reservation of offices of Chairpersons cease to have effect

1468.question: Can the Legislature of a State make any provision for reservation of seats in a Municipality or offices of Chairpersons in the Municipalities?
1468.answer: Yes, especially in favour of backward class of citizens.

1469.question: Can the Legislature of a State make provisions for reservation of seats in a Municipality or offices of Chairpersons in the Municipalities in favour of backward class of citizens?

1470.question: For how long does every Municipality continue unless sooner dissolved under any law?
1470.answer: Five years from the date appointed for its first meeting

1471.question: What does the date appointed for the first meeting of a Municipality signify?
1471.answer: It signifies the start of a five-year tenure unless the Municipality is sooner dissolved under any law

1472.question: Can an amendment of any law dissolve a Municipality?
1472.answer: No, no amendment of any law for the time being in force shall have the effect of causing dissolution of a Municipality at any level.

1473.question: What effect does an amendment of any law for the time being in force have on the dissolution of a Municipality at any level?
1473.answer: No amendment of any law for the time being in force shall have the effect of causing dissolution of a Municipality at any level.

1474.question: When should an election to constitute a Municipality be completed?
1474.answer: Before the expiry of its duration specified in clause (1), and before the expiration of a period of six months from the date of its dissolution.

1475.question: What is the timeline for completing a municipality election after its dissolution and before the expiry of its duration specified in clause (1)?
1475.answer: The election should be completed before the expiration of a period of six months from the date of its dissolution.

1476.question: For how long does a Municipality constituted upon the dissolution of a Municipality before the expiration of its duration continue?
1476.answer: Only for the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Municipality would have continued under clause (1) had it not been so dissolved.

1477.question: If a Municipality is dissolved before the expiration of its duration, for how long does the newly constituted Municipality continue?
1477.answer: Only for the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Municipality would have continued under clause (1) had it not been so dissolved.

1478.question: What disqualifies a person from being a member of a Municipality according to the Constitution of India?
1478.answer: A person can be disqualified from being a member of a Municipality if he is disqualified by any law in force for the purposes of elections to the Legislature of the State concerned, or if he is disqualified by any law made by the Legislature of the State. However, no person shall be disqualified on the ground that he is less than twenty-five years of age, if he has attained the age of twenty-one years.

1479.question: Under what conditions can a person be disqualified from being a member of a Municipality according to the Constitution of India, and what is the minimum age requirement?
1479.answer: A person can be disqualified from being a member of a Municipality if he is disqualified by any law in force for the purposes of elections to the Legislature of the State concerned, or if he is disqualified by any law made by the Legislature of the State. The minimum age requirement is twenty-one years.

1480.question: Who decides if a member of a Municipality has become subject to any of the disqualifications?
1480.answer: If any question arises as to whether a member of a Municipality has become subject to any of the disqualifications, the question shall be referred for the decision of such authority and in such manner as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide.

1481.question: What happens if a question arises regarding a member of a Municipality becoming subject to disqualifications?
1481.answer: The question is referred for the decision of an authority and in a manner as provided by the law of the State's Legislature.

1482.question: What are the powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities according to the Constitution of India?
1482.answer: The Legislature of a State may endow the Municipalities with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as institutions of self-government. This may include the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice, the performance of functions and the implementation of schemes as may be entrusted to them, including those related to the matters listed in the Twelfth Schedule.

1483.question: Who endows the Municipalities with their powers and authorities, and what functions might they be entrusted with according to the Constitution of India?
1483.answer: The Legislature of a State endows the Municipalities with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as institutions of self-government. This can include the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice, the performance of functions and the implementation of schemes as may be entrusted to them, including those related to the matters listed in the Twelfth Schedule.

1484.question: What are the powers to impose taxes by, and Funds of, the Municipalities?
1484.answer: The Legislature of a State may, by law, authorise a Municipality to levy, collect and appropriate such taxes, duties, tolls and fees in accordance with such procedure and subject to such limits.

1485.question: Who authorizes a Municipality to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls, and fees, and under what conditions?
1485.answer: The Legislature of a State authorises a Municipality to levy, collect and appropriate such taxes, duties, tolls and fees in accordance with such procedure and subject to such limits.

1486.question: What is the purpose of the Finance Commission constituted under article 243-I?
1486.answer: The Finance Commission reviews the financial position of the Municipalities and makes recommendations to the Governor on the distribution of proceeds, determination of taxes, duties, tolls and fees, grants-in-aid to the Municipalities, measures needed to improve their financial position, and any other matter referred by the Governor in the interests of sound finance of the Municipalities.

1487.question: Who reviews the financial position of the Municipalities and makes recommendations on the distribution of proceeds, determination of taxes, duties, tolls and fees, grants-in-aid to the Municipalities, measures needed to improve their financial position, and any other matter referred by the Governor in the interests of sound finance of the Municipalities?
1487.answer: The Finance Commission constituted under article 243-I is responsible for this task.

1488.question: What does the Governor do with the recommendations made by the Commission under article 243Y?
1488.answer: The Governor shall cause every recommendation made by the Commission, together with an explanatory memorandum as to the action taken thereon, to be laid before the Legislature of the State.

1489.question: What is the procedure followed by the Governor after receiving recommendations from the Commission under article 243Y?
1489.answer: The Governor shall cause every recommendation made by the Commission, together with an explanatory memorandum as to the action taken thereon, to be laid before the Legislature of the State.

1490.question: What provision can the Legislature of a State make with respect to Municipalities according to article 243Z?
1490.answer: The Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by the Municipalities and the auditing of such accounts.

1491.question: What can the Legislature of a State do by law with respect to the maintenance and auditing of accounts by the Municipalities, as per a certain article?
1491.answer: According to article 243Z, the Legislature of a State may make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by the Municipalities and the auditing of such accounts.

1492.question: What is the role of the superintendence in relation to Elections to the Municipalities in article 243ZA?
1492.answer: The superintendence has the direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for the Municipalities.

1493.question: Who has the direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for the Municipalities as per Article 243ZA?
1493.answer: The superintendence has the direction and control.

1494.question: Who is responsible for the conduct of all elections to the Municipalities?
1494.answer: The State Election Commission referred to in article 243K.

1495.question: Which entity is referred to in article 243K and is responsible for the conduct of all elections to the Municipalities?

1496.question: Who can make provision with respect to all matters relating to elections to the Municipalities?

1497.question: What entity is responsible for making provisions with respect to all matters relating to elections to the Municipalities?

1498.question: Do the provisions of this Part apply to Union territories?
1498.answer: Yes, the provisions of this Part apply to the Union territories.

1499.question: To what regions do the provisions of this Part apply?
1499.answer: The provisions of this Part apply to the Union territories.

1500.question: Who are referred to as the Governor of a State and the Legislature or the Legislative Assembly of a State in the context of a Union territory?
1500.answer: The Administrator of the Union territory and the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory.

1501.question: What are the Administrator of the Union territory and the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory referred to in the context of a State?
1501.answer: They are referred to as the Governor of a State and the Legislature or the Legislative Assembly of a State.

1502.question: Who may direct that the provisions of this Part apply to any Union territory or part thereof?

1503.question: Who has the authority to direct that the provisions of a Part apply to any Union territory or part thereof?

1504.question: Does this Part apply to the Scheduled Areas and the tribal areas referred to in clause (1), and the tribal areas referred to in clause (2), of article 244?
1504.answer: No, this Part does not apply to those areas.

1505.question: Which areas does this Part not apply to?
1505.answer: This Part does not apply to the Scheduled Areas and the tribal areas referred to in clause (1), and the tribal areas referred to in clause (2), of article 244.

1506.question: What is not affected by this Part?
1506.answer: The functions and powers of the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council.

1507.question: Which body's functions and powers are not affected by this Part?

1508.question: Can Parliament extend the provisions of this Part to the Scheduled Areas and the tribal areas?
1508.answer: Yes, Parliament can extend the provisions of this Part to the Scheduled Areas and the tribal areas.

1509.question: Who has the authority to extend the provisions of this Part to the Scheduled Areas and the tribal areas?
1509.answer: Parliament has the authority to extend the provisions of this Part to the Scheduled Areas and the tribal areas.

1510.question: What is the purpose of the District Planning Committee?
1510.answer: The purpose of a District Planning Committee is to consolidate the plans prepared by the Panchayats and the Municipalities in the district and to prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole.

1511.question: What does a District Planning Committee do with the plans prepared by the Panchayats and the Municipalities in the district?
1511.answer: A District Planning Committee consolidates the plans prepared by the Panchayats and the Municipalities in the district and prepares a draft development plan for the district as a whole.

1512.question: What is the minimum proportion of the District Planning Committee's members that should be elected from the Panchayat and Municipalities?
1512.answer: Not less than four-fifths of the total number of members of the District Planning Committee shall be elected by, and from amongst, the elected members of the Panchayat at the district level and of the Municipalities in the district.
