1513.question: Who elects not less than four-fifths of the total number of members of the District Planning Committee?
1513.answer: Four-fifths of the total number of members of the District Planning Committee are elected by, and from amongst, the elected members of the Panchayat at the district level and of the Municipalities in the district.

1514.question: What should the District Planning Committee consider when preparing the draft development plan?
1514.answer: The District Planning Committee should consider matters of common interest between the Panchayats and the Municipalities including spatial planning, sharing of water and other physical and natural resources, the integrated development of infrastructure and environmental conservation. They should also consider the extent and type of available resources, whether financial or otherwise.

1515.question: What should the District Planning Committee consider in terms of resources and development, including matters of common interest between the Panchayats and the Municipalities, when preparing the draft development plan?
1515.answer: The District Planning Committee should consider spatial planning, sharing of water and other physical and natural resources, the integrated development of infrastructure and environmental conservation. They should also consider the extent and type of available resources, whether financial or otherwise.

1516.question: Who does the District Planning Committee consult?
1516.answer: The District Planning Committee consults such institutions and organisations as the Governor may, by order, specify.

1517.question: Who specifies the institutions and organisations that the District Planning Committee consults?
1517.answer: The Governor specifies the institutions and organisations that the District Planning Committee consults.

1518.question: What happens to the development plan once it's recommended by the District Planning Committee?
1518.answer: The Chairperson of every District Planning Committee shall forward the development plan, as recommended by such Committee, to the Government of the State.

1519.question: Who forwards the development plan recommended by the District Planning Committee to the Government of the State?
1519.answer: The Chairperson of every District Planning Committee forwards the development plan.

1520.question: What is the purpose of the Metropolitan Planning Committee?
1520.answer: The purpose of the Metropolitan Planning Committee is to prepare a draft development plan for the Metropolitan area as a whole.

1521.question: Which committee is responsible for preparing a draft development plan for the Metropolitan area as a whole?
1521.answer: The Metropolitan Planning Committee is responsible for preparing a draft development plan for the Metropolitan area as a whole.

1522.question: What is the minimum proportion of Committee members that should be elected from the municipalities and panchayats?

1523.question: What proportion of Committee members should be elected from the municipalities and panchayats?

1524.question: What is the role of the Metropolitan Planning Committee in preparing the draft development plan?
1524.answer: It is to regard to the plans prepared by the Municipalities and the Panchayats, matters of common interest, the overall objectives and priorities set by the Government of India and the State, investments likely to be made and other available resources. They are also to consult such institutions and organisations as specified by the Governor.

1525.question: What factors does the Metropolitan Planning Committee consider when preparing the draft development plan, and who are they required to consult?
1525.answer: The Metropolitan Planning Committee considers the plans prepared by the Municipalities and the Panchayats, matters of common interest, the overall objectives and priorities set by the Government of India and the State, investments likely to be made and other available resources. They are required to consult such institutions and organisations as specified by the Governor.

1526.question: Who should the Chairperson of every Metropolitan Planning Committee forward the development plan to?

1527.question: Who does the development plan of every Metropolitan Planning Committee get forwarded to by the Chairperson?

1528.question: What are the functions that can be assigned to the Metropolitan Planning Committees?
1528.answer: Functions relating to planning and coordination for the Metropolitan area

1529.question: To whom can the functions relating to planning and coordination for the Metropolitan area be assigned?
1529.answer: The functions can be assigned to the Metropolitan Planning Committees

1530.question: How should the Chairpersons of such Committees be chosen?
1530.answer: The manner in which the Chairpersons of such Committees shall be chosen is not specified in the provided text.

1531.question: Is the method of selecting the Chairpersons of such Committees specified in the provided text?
1531.answer: No, the manner in which the Chairpersons of such Committees shall be chosen is not specified in the provided text.

1532.question: What happens to municipalities in force inconsistent with the Constitution (Seventy-fourth Amendment) Act, 1992?
1532.answer: They continue to be in force until amended or repealed by a competent Legislature or other competent authority or until the expiration of one year from such commencement, whichever is earlier.

1533.question: How long do municipalities inconsistent with the Constitution (Seventy-fourth Amendment) Act, 1992 continue to be in force?
1533.answer: They continue to be in force until amended or repealed by a competent Legislature or other competent authority or until the expiration of one year from such commencement, whichever is earlier.

1534.question: What is the provision for municipalities existing before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-fourth Amendment) Act, 1992?
1534.answer: All the Municipalities existing immediately before such commencement shall continue till the expiration of their duration, unless sooner dissolved by a resolution passed to that effect by the Legislative Assembly of that State or, in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, by each House of the Legislature of that State.

1535.question: What happens to the Municipalities that existed immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-fourth Amendment) Act, 1992?
1535.answer: All the Municipalities existing immediately before such commencement shall continue till the expiration of their duration, unless sooner dissolved by a resolution passed to that effect by the Legislative Assembly of that State or, in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, by each House of the Legislature of that State.

1536.question: What does article 243ZG state about the interference by courts in electoral matters?
1536.answer: It states that the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies, made or purporting to be made under article 243ZA shall not be called in question in any court. Also, no election to any Municipality shall be called in question except by an election petition presented to such authority and in such manner as is provided for by or under any law made by the Legislature of a State.

1537.question: What does Article 243ZG state about the validity of laws relating to delimitation of constituencies and the questioning of elections in any municipality?
1537.answer: Article 243ZG states that the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies, made or purporting to be made under article 243ZA shall not be called in question in any court. Also, no election to any Municipality shall be called in question except by an election petition presented to such authority and in such manner as is provided for by or under any law made by the Legislature of a State.

1538.question: What does 'authorised person' mean in the context of Part IX-B THE CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES?
1538.answer: An 'authorised person' refers to a person referred to as such in Article 243-ZQ.

1539.question: Who is referred to as the 'authorised person' in Article 243-ZQ?
1539.answer: The 'authorised person' in Article 243-ZQ is a term used in the context of Part IX-B THE CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES.

1540.question: What is the definition of 'board' in the context of co-operative societies?
1540.answer: A 'board' refers to the board of directors or the governing body of a co-operative society, by whatever name called, to which the direction and control of the management of the affairs of a society is entrusted to.

1541.question: To whom is the direction and control of the management of the affairs of a co-operative society entrusted?
1541.answer: The direction and control of the management of the affairs of a co-operative society is entrusted to the 'board' or the board of directors or the governing body, by whatever name called.

1542.question: What is a 'co-operative society' as defined in the Constitution?
1542.answer: A 'co-operative society' is a society registered or deemed to be registered under any law relating to co-operative societies for the time being in force in any State.

1543.question: Under which law should a society be registered or deemed to be registered for it to be considered a 'co-operative society'?
1543.answer: A society should be registered or deemed to be registered under any law relating to co-operative societies for the time being in force in any State to be considered a 'co-operative society'.

1544.question: What is a 'multi-State co-operative society'?
1544.answer: A 'multi-State co-operative society' is a society with objects not confined to one State and registered.

1545.question: What type of society has objects not confined to one State and is registered?
1545.answer: A 'multi-State co-operative society' is a society with objects not confined to one State and registered.

1546.question: What does 'officer bearer' mean in the context of a co-operative society?
1546.answer: An 'officer bearer' refers to a President, Vice-President, Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Secretary or Treasurer of a co-operative society and includes any other person to be elected by the board of any co-operative society.

1547.question: Who does the term 'officer bearer' include in a co-operative society?
1547.answer: An 'officer bearer' refers to a President, Vice-President, Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Secretary or Treasurer of a co-operative society and includes any other person to be elected by the board of any co-operative society.

1548.question: Who is the 'Registrar' as mentioned in the text?
1548.answer: The 'Registrar' refers to the Central Registrar appointed by the Central Government in relation to the multi-State co-operative societies and the Registrar for co-operative societies appointed by the State Government under the law made by the Legislature of a State in relation to co-operative societies.

1549.question: Who appoints the Central Registrar and the Registrar for co-operative societies, as per the law made by the Legislature of a State in relation to co-operative societies?
1549.answer: The Central Registrar is appointed by the Central Government and the Registrar for co-operative societies is appointed by the State Government.

1550.question: What is a 'State Act'?
1550.answer: A 'State Act' means any law made by the Legislature of a State.

1551.question: Who makes any law referred to as a 'State Act'?
1551.answer: The Legislature of a State makes any law referred to as a 'State Act'.

1552.question: What is a 'State level co-operative society'?
1552.answer: A 'State level co-operative society' is a co-operative society having its area of operation extending to the whole of a State and defined as such in any law made by the Legislature of a State.

1553.question: What is the area of operation for a 'State level co-operative society' and how is it defined?
1553.answer: The area of operation for a 'State level co-operative society' extends to the whole of a State and it is defined as such in any law made by the Legislature of a State.

1554.question: What does the legislation 243-ZI state?
1554.answer: Legislation 243-ZI states that the Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions with respect to the incorporation, regulation and winding up of co-operative societies based on the principles of voluntary formation, democratic member-control, member-economic participation and autonomous functioning.

1555.question: Which legislation states that a State's Legislature may make provisions for the incorporation, regulation, and winding up of co-operative societies based on voluntary formation, democratic member-control, member-economic participation, and autonomous functioning?

1556.question: What is the maximum number of directors a co-operative society can have according to the legislation?
1556.answer: According to the legislation, the maximum number of directors of a co-operative society shall not exceed twenty-one.

1557.question: According to the legislation, how many directors can a co-operative society have at maximum?
1557.answer: A co-operative society can have a maximum of twenty-one directors according to the legislation.

1558.question: What reservations does the law provide for on the board of a co-operative society?
1558.answer: The law provides for the reservation of one seat for the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes and two seats for women on the board of every co-operative society consisting of individuals as members and having members from such class or category of persons.

1559.question: How many seats are reserved for the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes and for women on the board of a co-operative society consisting of individuals as members and having members from such class or category of persons?
1559.answer: One seat is reserved for the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes and two seats are reserved for women.

1560.question: What is the term of office for the elected members of the board and its office bearers in a co-operative society?
1560.answer: The term of office of elected members of the board and its office bearers in a co-operative society is five years from the date of election.

1561.question: How long is the term of office for elected members of the board and its office bearers in a co-operative society from the date of election?
1561.answer: The term of office is five years.

1562.question: What happens when there is a casual vacancy on the board?
1562.answer: The board may fill a casual vacancy on the board by nomination out of the same class of members in respect of which the casual vacancy has arisen, if the term of office of the board is less than half of its original term.

1563.question: How can the board fill a casual vacancy if the term of office of the board is less than half of its original term?
1563.answer: The board may fill a casual vacancy on the board by nomination out of the same class of members in respect of which the casual vacancy has arisen.

1564.question: Who can be co-opted as members of the board?
1564.answer: The Legislature of a State shall, by law, make provisions for co-option of persons to be members of the board having experience in the field of banking, management, finance or specialisation in any other field relating to the objects and activities undertaken by the co-operative society.

1565.question: What qualifications or experience should a person have to be co-opted as a member of the board of a co-operative society, according to the provisions made by the Legislature of a State?
1565.answer: A person should have experience in the field of banking, management, finance or specialisation in any other field relating to the objects and activities undertaken by the co-operative society.

1566.question: What is the maximum number of co-opted members allowed on the board?
1566.answer: The number of such co-opted members shall not exceed two in addition to twenty-one directors.

1567.question: How many directors are there on the board, in addition to the maximum of two co-opted members?
1567.answer: There are twenty-one directors on the board in addition to the maximum of two co-opted members.

1568.question: Do co-opted members have the right to vote?
1568.answer: Co-opted members shall not have the right to vote in any election of the co-operative society in their capacity as such member or to be eligible to be elected as office bearers of the board.

1569.question: Can co-opted members be eligible to be elected as office bearers of the board or vote in any election of the co-operative society?
1569.answer: No, co-opted members do not have the right to vote in any election of the co-operative society or to be eligible to be elected as office bearers of the board in their capacity as such member.

1570.question: Who oversees the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections to a co-operative society?
1570.answer: The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to a co-operative society shall vest in such an authority or body, as may be provided by the Legislature of a State, by law.

1571.question: Where does the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to a co-operative society vest?
1571.answer: The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to a co-operative society vests in such an authority or body, as may be provided by the Legislature of a State, by law.

1572.question: When should the election of a board be conducted?
1572.answer: The election of a board shall be conducted before the expiry of the term of the board so as to ensure that the newly elected members of the board assume office immediately on the expiry of the office of members of the outgoing board.

1573.question: What is the purpose of conducting the election of a board before the expiry of the term of the current board?
1573.answer: The purpose of conducting the election of a board before the expiry of the term of the current board is to ensure that the newly elected members of the board assume office immediately on the expiry of the office of members of the outgoing board.

1574.question: What are the conditions under which a board may be superseded or kept under suspension?
1574.answer: The board may be superseded or kept under suspension in case of its persistent default; negligence in the performance of its duties; the board has committed any act prejudicial to the interests of the co-operative society or its members; there is stalemate in the constitution or functions of the board; or the authority or body as provided by the Legislature of a State, by law, under clause (2) of Article 243-ZK, has failed to conduct elections in accordance with the provisions of the State Act.

1575.question: What could cause the persistent default, negligence in duties, committing acts prejudicial to the interests of the co-operative society or its members, stalemate in the constitution or functions of the board, or failure to conduct elections in accordance with the provisions of the State Act under clause (2) of Article 243-ZK by the authority or body as provided by the Legislature of a State?
1575.answer: These could lead to the board being superseded or kept under suspension.

1576.question: Under what conditions can the board of a co-operative society not be superseded or kept under suspension?
1576.answer: The board of any such co-operative society shall not be superseded or kept under suspension where there is no Government shareholding or loan or financial assistance or any guarantee by the Government.

1577.question: What prevents the board of a co-operative society from being superseded or kept under suspension?
1577.answer: The board of a co-operative society cannot be superseded or kept under suspension if there is no Government shareholding, loan, financial assistance, or any form of guarantee by the Government.

1578.question: What provisions apply in case of a co-operative society carrying on the business of banking?
1578.answer: In case of a co-operative society carrying on the business of banking, the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (10 of 1949) shall also apply.

1579.question: What law is applicable to a co-operative society conducting banking business?
1579.answer: The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (10 of 1949) is applicable to a co-operative society conducting banking business.

1580.question: What happens in case of supersession of a board?
1580.answer: In case of supersession of a board, the administrator appointed to manage the affairs of such co-operative society shall arrange for conduct of elections within the period specified in clause (1) and handover the management to be elected board.

1581.question: Who arranges for the conduct of elections and hands over the management to the elected board when a board is superseded?
1581.answer: The administrator appointed to manage the affairs of such co-operative society arranges for the conduct of elections and hands over the management when a board is superseded.

1582.question: Who can make provisions for the conditions of service of the administrator?
1582.answer: The Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions for the conditions of service of the administrator.

1583.question: Who has the authority, by law, to define the conditions of service for an administrator?

1584.question: Who is responsible for the auditing of co-operative society's accounts?
1584.answer: An auditor or auditing firms appointed by the general body of the co-operative society are responsible for the auditing of the co-operative society's accounts.

1585.question: Who appoints the auditor or auditing firms responsible for the auditing of the co-operative society's accounts?
1585.answer: The auditor or auditing firms are appointed by the general body of the co-operative society.

1586.question: Who determines the minimum qualifications and experience of auditors and auditing firms for co-operative societies?
1586.answer: The Legislature of a State lays down the minimum qualifications and experience of auditors and auditing firms.

1587.question: Who lays down the minimum qualifications and experience of auditors and auditing firms for co-operative societies?
1587.answer: The Legislature of a State determines the minimum qualifications and experience of auditors and auditing firms.

1588.question: When should the accounts of every co-operative society be audited?
1588.answer: The accounts of every co-operative society should be audited within six months of the close of the financial year to which such accounts relate.

1589.question: What should be done within six months of the close of the financial year for every co-operative society?
1589.answer: The accounts of every co-operative society should be audited.

1590.question: What is the timeline for the convening of the annual general body meeting of every co-operative society?
1590.answer: The annual general body meeting of every co-operative society should be convened within a period of six months of close of the financial year.

1591.question: Within what period should the annual general body meeting of every co-operative society be convened after the close of the financial year?
1591.answer: The annual general body meeting of every co-operative society should be convened within a period of six months of close of the financial year.

1592.question: What kind of access does a member of a co-operative society have according to the law?
1592.answer: A member of a co-operative society has access to the books, information and accounts of the co-operative society kept in regular transaction of its business with such member.

1593.question: What does a member of a co-operative society have access to in regular transaction of its business?
1593.answer: A member of a co-operative society has access to the books, information and accounts of the co-operative society.

1594.question: What provisions can the Legislature of a State make to ensure the participation of members in the management of the co-operative society?
1594.answer: The Legislature of a State can make provisions to ensure the participation of members in the management of the co-operative society providing minimum requirement of attending meetings by the members and utilising the minimum level of services.

1595.question: What provisions can a State Legislature make to ensure member participation in co-operative society management?
1595.answer: A State Legislature can ensure member participation in co-operative society management by stipulating a minimum requirement for meeting attendance and service utilization.

1596.question: What kind of education can the Legislature of a State provide for its members?
1596.answer: The Legislature of a State can provide for co-operative education and training for its members.

1597.question: Who can provide co-operative education and training for its members?
1597.answer: The Legislature of a State can provide co-operative education and training for its members.

1598.question: When should every co-operative society file returns?
1598.answer: Within six months of the close of every financial year.

1599.question: What is the deadline for a co-operative society to file returns after the close of a financial year?

1600.question: What should the return of a co-operative society include?
1600.answer: Annual report of its activities, its audited statement of accounts, plan for surplus disposal, list of amendments to the bye-laws, declaration regarding date of holding of its general body meeting and conduct of elections when due, and any other information required by the Registrar.

1601.question: What does the annual report of a co-operative society, its audited statement of accounts, plan for surplus disposal, list of amendments to the bye-laws, declaration regarding date of holding of its general body meeting and conduct of elections when due, and any other information required by the Registrar refer to?
1601.answer: These refer to the return of a co-operative society.

1602.question: Who can make provisions for the offences relating to the co-operative societies and penalties for such offences?

1603.question: Who has the authority to make provisions for the offences relating to co-operative societies and penalties for such offences?

1604.question: What acts or omissions are considered as offences under the law made by the Legislature of a State?
1604.answer: Making a false return or furnishing false information, not furnishing any information required, disobeying any summons, requisition or lawful written order issued under the provisions of the State Act, failing to pay to a co-operative society amount deducted from its employee within a specified period, failing to handover custody of books, accounts, documents, records, cash, security and other property belonging to a co-operative society to an authorised person.

1605.question: What are the consequences of making a false return, not providing necessary information, disobeying summons or lawful orders, failing to pay a co-operative society within a specified time, or not handing over custody of books, accounts, and other properties to an authorised person?
1605.answer: These acts or omissions are considered as offences under the law made by the Legislature of a State.

1606.question: What does 243-ZR state about the application of provisions to multi-State co-operative societies?
1606.answer: 243-ZR states that the provisions of this Part apply to the multi-State co-operative societies, with the modification that any reference to 'Legislature of a State', 'State Act' or 'State Government' should be construed as a reference to 'Parliament', 'Central Act' or 'the Central Government' respectively.

1607.question: What does 243-ZR specify should be the interpretation of 'Legislature of a State', 'State Act' or 'State Government' in the context of multi-State co-operative societies?
1607.answer: 243-ZR specifies that in the context of multi-State co-operative societies, any reference to 'Legislature of a State', 'State Act' or 'State Government' should be construed as a reference to 'Parliament', 'Central Act' or 'the Central Government' respectively.

1608.question: What does 243-ZS state about the application to Union territories?
1608.answer: 243-ZS states that the provisions of this Part apply to the Union territories. In their application to a Union territory without a Legislative Assembly, references to the Legislature of a State should be a reference to the administrator thereof appointed under Article 239. In relation to a Union territory having a Legislative Assembly, it is to that Legislative Assembly. However, the President may direct that the provisions of this Part shall not apply to any Union territory or Part thereof as specified in a notification in the Official Gazette.

1609.question: What does 243-ZS specify in regards to its application to Union territories without a Legislative Assembly, Union territories with a Legislative Assembly, and the President's power to exempt certain Union territories?
1609.answer: 243-ZS states that the provisions of this Part apply to the Union territories. In their application to a Union territory without a Legislative Assembly, references to the Legislature of a State should be a reference to the administrator thereof appointed under Article 239. In relation to a Union territory having a Legislative Assembly, it is to that Legislative Assembly. However, the President may direct that the provisions of this Part shall not apply to any Union territory or Part thereof as specified in a notification in the Official Gazette.

1610.question: What does 243-ZT state about the continuance of existing laws?
1610.answer: 243-ZT states that any provision of any law relating to co-operative societies in force in a State immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Ninety-seventh Amendment) Act, 2011, which is inconsistent with the provisions of this Part, shall continue to be in force until amended or repealed by a competent Legislature or other competent authority or until the expiration of one year from such commencement, whichever is less.

1611.question: What does 243-ZT specify about the duration and conditions under which a law relating to co-operative societies can remain in force after the commencement of the Constitution (Ninety-seventh Amendment) Act, 2011?
1611.answer: 243-ZT states that any provision of any law relating to co-operative societies in force in a State immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Ninety-seventh Amendment) Act, 2011, which is inconsistent with the provisions of this Part, shall continue to be in force until amended or repealed by a competent Legislature or other competent authority or until the expiration of one year from such commencement, whichever is less.

1612.question: What does Article 244 state about the administration of Scheduled Areas and tribal areas?
1612.answer: Article 244 states that the provisions of the Fifth Schedule shall apply to the administration and control of the Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in any State other than the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. The provisions of the Sixth Schedule shall apply to the administration of the tribal areas in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

1613.question: Which Schedule applies to the administration and control of the Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in any State other than the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram according to Article 244? And which Schedule applies to the administration of the tribal areas in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram?
1613.answer: According to Article 244, the provisions of the Fifth Schedule apply to the administration and control of the Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in any State other than the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. The provisions of the Sixth Schedule apply to the administration of the tribal areas in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

1614.question: What can the Parliament form within the State of Assam according to the constitution?
1614.answer: An autonomous State comprising all or any of the tribal areas specified in Part I of the table appended to paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule.

1615.question: Which part of the constitution specifies that an autonomous state can be formed in Assam, comprising all or any of the tribal areas?
1615.answer: Part I of the table appended to paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule.

1616.question: What can be created for the autonomous State?
1616.answer: A body, whether elected or partly nominated and partly elected, to function as a Legislature for the autonomous State, or a Council of Ministers, or both.

1617.question: What is the function of a body, whether elected or partly nominated and partly elected, in the autonomous State?
1617.answer: The body can function as a Legislature for the autonomous State, a Council of Ministers, or both.

1618.question: What matters can the law specify in relation to the autonomous State?
1618.answer: The matters enumerated in the State List or the Concurrent List with respect to which the Legislature of the autonomous State shall have power to make laws, the matters with respect to which the executive power of the autonomous State shall extend, any tax levied by the State of Assam that should be assigned to the autonomous State, any reference to a State in the constitution should include the autonomous State, and make any necessary supplemental, incidental and consequential provisions.

1619.question: What does the State List or the Concurrent List enumerate, what does the executive power of the autonomous State extend to, what tax is levied by the State of Assam that should be assigned to the autonomous State, what does any reference to a State in the constitution include, and what kind of provisions should be made?
1619.answer: The law specifies these matters in relation to the autonomous State. The State List or the Concurrent List enumerates the matters to which the Legislature of the autonomous State has the power to make laws. The executive power of the autonomous State extends to these matters. The tax that should be assigned to the autonomous State is the one levied by the State of Assam. Any reference to a State in the constitution includes the autonomous State, and any necessary supplemental, incidental, and consequential provisions should be made.

1620.question: What is required for an amendment of any such law to have effect?
1620.answer: The amendment must be passed in each House of Parliament by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

1621.question: What is the procedure for an amendment to pass in each House of Parliament?
1621.answer: The amendment must be passed by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

1622.question: Is such a law considered an amendment of the constitution?
1622.answer: No, it shall not be deemed to be an amendment of the constitution.

1623.question: Can a law be deemed as an amendment of the constitution?
1623.answer: No, it shall not be deemed to be an amendment of the constitution.

1624.question: What is the purpose of Article 368?
1624.answer: Article 368 provides the process to amend the Constitution.

1625.question: Which article provides the process to amend the Constitution?

1626.question: What is the extent of laws made by Parliament and by the Legislatures of States according to Article 245?
1626.answer: According to Article 245, Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India, and the Legislature of a State may make laws for the whole or any part of the State.

1627.question: Which article states that the Parliament can make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India, and the Legislature of a State may make laws for the whole or any part of the State?

1628.question: What is the subject-matter of laws made by Parliament and by the Legislatures of States according to Article 246?
1628.answer: According to Article 246, Parliament has exclusive power to make laws with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the Union List. Both Parliament and the Legislature of any State have power to make laws with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the Concurrent List. The Legislature of any State has exclusive power to make laws for such State or any part thereof with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the State List.

1629.question: Which entity has the exclusive power to make laws with respect to the matters enumerated in the Union List, and who has the power to make laws with respect to the matters enumerated in the Concurrent List and State List according to Article 246?
1629.answer: According to Article 246, Parliament has exclusive power to make laws with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the Union List. Both Parliament and the Legislature of any State have power to make laws with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the Concurrent List. The Legislature of any State has exclusive power to make laws for such State or any part thereof with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the State List.

1630.question: What power does Parliament have under Article 246A?
1630.answer: Under Article 246A, Parliament and the Legislature of every State have power to make laws with respect to goods and services tax imposed by the Union or by such State.

1631.question: Which article gives Parliament and the Legislature of every State the power to make laws with respect to goods and services tax imposed by the Union or by such State?
1631.answer: Article 246A gives Parliament and the Legislature of every State this power.

1632.question: Who has the exclusive power to make laws with respect to goods and services tax where the supply of goods, or of services, or both takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce?

1633.question: Which body has the power to make laws regarding the goods and services tax in the context of inter-State trade or commerce?

1634.question: When do the provisions of this article, in respect of goods and services tax referred to in clause (5) of article 279A, take effect?
1634.answer: From the date recommended by the Goods and Services Tax Council

1635.question: What determines the date when the provisions of this article, in respect of goods and services tax referred to in clause (5) of article 279A, take effect?
1635.answer: The date recommended by the Goods and Services Tax Council

1636.question: What can Parliament provide for, notwithstanding anything in this Chapter?
1636.answer: The establishment of any additional courts for the better administration of laws made by Parliament or of any existing laws with respect to a matter enumerated in the Union List

1637.question: What does the establishment of any additional courts for the better administration of laws made by Parliament or of any existing laws with respect to a matter enumerated in the Union List refer to?
1637.answer: It refers to what Parliament can provide for, notwithstanding anything in this Chapter.

1638.question: What is the Parliament's power according to article 248?
1638.answer: Parliament has exclusive power to make any law with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Concurrent List or State List, including the power of making any law imposing a tax not mentioned in either of those Lists

1639.question: Which body has exclusive power to make any law with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Concurrent List or State List, and can impose a tax not mentioned in either of those Lists, according to the constitution?

1640.question: Under what conditions can the Parliament legislate with respect to goods and services tax provided under article 246A or a matter in the State List in the national interest?
1640.answer: If the Council of States has declared by resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting that it is necessary or expedient in the national interest that Parliament should make laws with respect to any matter enumerated in the State List specified in the resolution

1641.question: What is the necessary procedure for the Parliament to make laws with respect to any matter enumerated in the State List specified in the resolution?
1641.answer: The Council of States has to declare by resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting that it is necessary or expedient in the national interest.

1642.question: For how long does a resolution passed under clause (1) remain in force?
1642.answer: For such period not exceeding one year as may be specified therein

1643.question: What is the maximum duration that a resolution under clause (1) can remain in force if specified?

1644.question: What happens to a resolution passed in the manner provided in clause (1)?
1644.answer: Such resolution shall continue in force for a further period of one year from the date on which under this clause it would otherwise have ceased to be in force.

1645.question: How long will a resolution passed in the manner provided in clause (1) continue in force from the date on which it would otherwise have ceased to be in force?
1645.answer: Such resolution shall continue in force for a further period of one year.

1646.question: What happens to a law made by Parliament under clause (1) after the resolution has ceased to be in force?
1646.answer: It shall, to the extent of the incompetency, cease to have effect on the expiration of a period of six months after the resolution has ceased to be in force, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before the expiration of the said period.

1647.question: What is the duration for a law made by Parliament under clause (1) to cease to have effect after the resolution has ceased to be in force and what are the exceptions to it?
1647.answer: The law shall cease to have effect on the expiration of a period of six months after the resolution has ceased to be in force, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before the expiration of the said period.

1648.question: What power does Parliament have during a Proclamation of Emergency according to article 250?
1648.answer: Parliament shall, while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, have power to make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the State List.

1649.question: What authority is granted to Parliament in regards to making laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the State List during a Proclamation of Emergency?
1649.answer: According to article 250, during a Proclamation of Emergency, Parliament has the power to make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India.

1650.question: What happens to a law made by Parliament during a Proclamation of Emergency after it has ceased to operate?
1650.answer: It shall, to the extent of the incompetency, cease to have effect on the expiration of a period of six months after the Proclamation has ceased to operate, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before the expiration of the said period.

1651.question: When does a law made by Parliament during a Proclamation of Emergency cease to have effect after the Proclamation has ceased to operate?
1651.answer: It ceases to have effect on the expiration of a period of six months after the Proclamation has ceased to operate, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before the expiration of the said period.

1652.question: What is stated in article 251 regarding the inconsistency between laws made by Parliament and the Legislatures of States?
1652.answer: Nothing in articles 249 and 250 shall restrict the power of the Legislature of a State to make any law which under this Constitution it has power to make, but if any provision of a law made by the Legislature of a State is repugnant to any provision of a law made by Parliament which Parliament has under either of the said articles power to make, the law made by Parliament, whether passed before or after the law made by the Legislature of a State, shall prevail.

1653.question: What happens if a law made by the Legislature of a State is repugnant to a law made by Parliament under either of articles 249 and 250?
1653.answer: If a law made by the Legislature of a State is repugnant to a law made by Parliament, which Parliament has under either of the articles 249 and 250 the power to make, the law made by Parliament shall prevail, regardless of whether it was passed before or after the law made by the State Legislature. This is stated in article 251.

1654.question: What happens when a law made by the Legislature of a State is repugnant to a law made by Parliament?
1654.answer: The law made by Parliament shall prevail, and the law made by the Legislature of the State shall be inoperative to the extent of the repugnancy, but only as long as the law made by Parliament continues to have effect.

1655.question: What is the effect of a law made by Parliament on a conflicting law made by the Legislature of a State?
1655.answer: If a law made by the Legislature of a State is repugnant to a law made by Parliament, the law made by Parliament shall prevail, and the law made by the State Legislature will be inoperative to the extent of the repugnancy. However, this applies only as long as the law made by Parliament is in effect.

1656.question: What is the power of Parliament to legislate for two or more States by consent and adoption of such legislation by any other State?
1656.answer: If it appears desirable to the Legislatures of two or more States that any matter should be regulated by Parliament by law, and if resolutions to that effect are passed by all the Houses of the Legislatures of those States, Parliament can pass an act for regulating that matter. Any Act so passed shall apply to such States and to any other State which adopts it afterwards by resolution passed by the House or, where there are two Houses, by each of the Houses of the Legislature of that State.

1657.question: How can Parliament pass an act that regulates a matter for two or more States and how can other States adopt this act?
1657.answer: If it appears desirable to the Legislatures of two or more States that any matter should be regulated by Parliament by law, and if resolutions to that effect are passed by all the Houses of the Legislatures of those States, Parliament can pass an act for regulating that matter. Any Act so passed shall apply to such States and to any other State which adopts it afterwards by resolution passed by the House or, where there are two Houses, by each of the Houses of the Legislature of that State.

1658.question: Can an Act passed by Parliament be amended or repealed by an Act of the Legislature of that State?
1658.answer: No, any Act passed by Parliament can be amended or repealed by an Act of Parliament passed or adopted in like manner but shall not, as respects any State to which it applies, be amended or repealed by an Act of the Legislature of that State.

1659.question: Who has the authority to amend or repeal an Act passed by Parliament?
1659.answer: Any Act passed by Parliament can be amended or repealed by an Act of Parliament passed or adopted in like manner, not by an Act of the Legislature of any State.

1660.question: Does Parliament have the power to make any law for implementing any treaty, agreement or convention with any other country?
1660.answer: Yes, Parliament has the power to make any law for the whole or any part of the territory of India for implementing any treaty, agreement or convention with any other country or any decision made at any international conference, association or other body.

1661.question: Who has the power to make any law for the whole or any part of the territory of India for implementing any treaty, agreement or convention with any other country or any decision made at any international conference, association or other body?
1661.answer: Parliament has the power to make any law for implementing any treaty, agreement or convention with any other country.

1662.question: What happens in case of inconsistency between laws made by Parliament and laws made by the Legislatures of States?
1662.answer: If any provision of a law made by the Legislature of a State is repugnant to any provision of a law made by Parliament which Parliament is competent to enact, the law made by Parliament shall prevail and the law made by the State Legislature shall, to the extent of repugnancy, be void.

1663.question: Which law prevails when there is a contradiction between a law made by Parliament and a law made by the Legislature of a State, and what happens to the contradicting state law?
1663.answer: If any provision of a law made by the Legislature of a State is repugnant to any provision of a law made by Parliament which Parliament is competent to enact, the law made by Parliament shall prevail and the law made by the State Legislature shall, to the extent of repugnancy, be void.

1664.question: What happens when a state law conflicts with a law made by Parliament or an existing law, according to the Concurrent List?
1664.answer: The law made by Parliament, whether passed before or after the law made by the state, shall prevail and the state law shall be void to the extent of the repugnancy.

1665.question: Which law prevails when there is a conflict between a state law and a law made by Parliament, and what happens to the state law?
1665.answer: The law made by Parliament, whether passed before or after the law made by the state, shall prevail and the state law shall be void to the extent of the repugnancy.

1666.question: What occurs if a law made by the Legislature of a State repugnant to the provisions of an earlier law by Parliament or an existing law has been reserved for the consideration of the President and has received his assent?
1666.answer: The law so made by the Legislature of such State shall prevail in that State.

1667.question: What happens when a law made by the Legislature of a State, which contradicts an earlier law by Parliament or an existing law, receives the President's assent after being reserved for his consideration?
1667.answer: The law so made by the Legislature of such State shall prevail in that State.

1668.question: Can Parliament make any law with respect to the same matter including a law adding to, amending, varying or repealing the law so made by the Legislature of the State?
1668.answer: Yes, Parliament can enact at any time any law with respect to the same matter including a law adding to, amending, varying or repealing the law so made by the Legislature of the State.

1669.question: Is it possible for Parliament to enact at any time any law with respect to the same matter including a law adding to, amending, varying or repealing the law so made by the Legislature of the State?
1669.answer: Yes, Parliament can make any law with respect to the same matter including a law adding to, amending, varying or repealing the law so made by the Legislature of the State.

1670.question: What are the requirements for an Act of Parliament or of the Legislature of a State to be regarded as valid, even if some recommendation or previous sanction required by the Constitution was not given?
1670.answer: The Act will be valid if assent to that Act was given by the Governor or the President, depending on who the recommendation required was from.

1671.question: In the absence of some recommendation or previous sanction required by the Constitution, under what circumstances can an Act of Parliament or of the Legislature of a State be regarded as valid?
1671.answer: The Act can be regarded as valid if assent to that Act was given by the Governor or the President, depending on who the recommendation required was from.

1672.question: What is the obligation of States and the Union according to Section 256?
1672.answer: The executive power of every State shall be so exercised as to ensure compliance with the laws made by Parliament and any existing laws.

1673.question: How should the executive power of every State be exercised according to the laws made by Parliament and any existing laws?
1673.answer: According to Section 256, the executive power of every State should be exercised so as to ensure compliance with the laws made by Parliament and any existing laws.

1674.question: What is the main provision of Article 257 of the Indian Constitution?
1674.answer: The executive power of every State shall be so exercised as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union, and the Union has the power to give directions to a State as may appear to the Government of India to be necessary.

1675.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution states that the executive power of every State should not impede the exercise of the Union's executive power, and that the Union can give directions to a State as necessary?

1676.question: What power does the Union have regarding the construction and maintenance of means of communication?
1676.answer: The executive power of the Union extends to the giving of directions to a State as to the construction and maintenance of means of communication declared in the direction to be of national or military importance.

1677.question: To what extent does the executive power of the Union reach in terms of giving directions to a State for the construction and maintenance of means of communication of national or military importance?
1677.answer: The executive power of the Union extends to the giving of directions to a State as to the construction and maintenance of means of communication declared in the direction to be of national or military importance.

1678.question: What is the Union's power in relation to the protection of railways within a State?
1678.answer: The executive power of the Union extends to the giving of directions to a State as to the measures to be taken for the protection of the railways within the State.

1679.question: What does the executive power of the Union extend to in regards to the protection of the railways within a State?
1679.answer: The executive power of the Union extends to the giving of directions to a State as to the measures to be taken for the protection of the railways within the State.

1680.question: What happens if costs are incurred in excess while carrying out a direction given to a State?
1680.answer: If costs have been incurred in excess of those which would have been incurred in the discharge of the normal duties of the State, there shall be paid by the Government of India to the State such sum as may be agreed, or, in default of agreement, as may be determined by an arbitrator appointed by the Chief Justice of India.

1681.question: Who pays the state if costs have been incurred in excess of those which would have been incurred in the discharge of the normal duties of the State, and how is the sum determined?
1681.answer: The Government of India shall pay the State such sum as may be agreed. If there is no agreement, it will be determined by an arbitrator appointed by the Chief Justice of India.

1682.question: What does the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 33 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979) repeal?
1682.answer: The Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 33 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979) repeals the Assistance to States by deployment of armed forces or other forces of the Union.

1683.question: What is repealed by The Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 33 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979)?
1683.answer: The Assistance to States by deployment of armed forces or other forces of the Union is repealed by The Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 33 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979).

1684.question: What power does the President have according to article 258 of the Constitution of India?
1684.answer: According to article 258 of the Constitution of India, the President may, with the consent of the Government of a State, entrust either conditionally or unconditionally to that Government or to its officers functions in relation to any matter to which the executive power of the Union extends.

1685.question: What is the function of the Government of a State according to article 258 of the Constitution of India, assuming the President has given consent?
1685.answer: According to article 258 of the Constitution of India, if the President gives consent, the Government of a State or its officers can be entrusted with functions in relation to any matter to which the executive power of the Union extends, either conditionally or unconditionally.

1686.question: What happens when powers and duties have been conferred or imposed upon a State or officers or authorities thereof under article 258?
1686.answer: Under article 258, if powers and duties have been conferred or imposed upon a State or officers or authorities thereof, the Government of India shall pay the State such sum as may be agreed, or, in default of agreement, as may be determined by an arbitrator appointed by the Chief Justice of India, in respect of any extra costs of administration incurred by the State in connection with the exercise of those powers and duties.

1687.question: What happens in terms of financial compensation when the Government of India confers or imposes powers and duties upon a State, its officers, or authorities under Article 258?
1687.answer: The Government of India shall pay the State such sum as may be agreed upon, or, in default of agreement, as may be determined by an arbitrator appointed by the Chief Justice of India, in respect of any extra costs of administration incurred by the State in connection with the exercise of those powers and duties.

1688.question: What power does the Governor of a State have according to article 258A?
1688.answer: According to article 258A, the Governor of a State may, with the consent of the Government of India, entrust either conditionally or unconditionally to that Government or to its officers functions in relation to any matter to which the executive power of the State extends.

1689.question: Which article allows the Governor of a State to entrust either conditionally or unconditionally to the Government of India or to its officers functions in relation to any matter to which the executive power of the State extends, with the consent of the Government of India?
1689.answer: Article 258A allows the Governor of a State to entrust these functions.

1690.question: What does the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch. repeal?
1690.answer: The Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch. repeals the Armed Forces in States in Part B of the First Schedule.

1691.question: What is repealed by the Armed Forces in States in Part B of the First Schedule?
1691.answer: The Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch.

1692.question: What jurisdiction does the Union have in relation to territories outside India according to article 260?
1692.answer: According to article 260, the Government of the Union has jurisdiction in relation to territories outside India.

1693.question: Which article states that the Government of the Union has jurisdiction in relation to territories outside India?
1693.answer: Article 260 states that the Government of the Union has jurisdiction in relation to territories outside India.

1694.question: What can the government of India undertake with the agreement of any territory not part of India?
1694.answer: The government of India can undertake any executive, legislative or judicial functions vested in the Government of such territory.

1695.question: What functions can the government of India undertake in a territory not part of India, with their agreement?
1695.answer: The government of India can undertake any executive, legislative or judicial functions vested in the Government of such territory.

1696.question: What is given full faith and credit throughout the territory of India?
1696.answer: Public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and of every State are given full faith and credit throughout the territory of India.

1697.question: What are public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and of every State given throughout the territory of India?
1697.answer: Public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and of every State are given full faith and credit throughout the territory of India.

1698.question: What is the capability of final judgments or orders delivered by civil courts in any part of the territory of India?
1698.answer: Final judgments or orders delivered by civil courts in any part of the territory of India shall be capable of execution anywhere within that territory according to law.

1699.question: Where can final judgments or orders delivered by civil courts in any part of the territory of India be executed?
1699.answer: Final judgments or orders delivered by civil courts in any part of the territory of India can be executed anywhere within that territory according to law.

1700.question: What provision may the Parliament make with respect to disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers or river valleys?
1700.answer: Parliament may by law provide for the adjudication of any dispute or complaint with respect to the use, distribution or control of the waters of, or in, any inter-State river or river valley.

1701.question: What can the Parliament do by law in terms of adjudication of any dispute or complaint concerning the use, distribution, or control of the waters of any inter-State river or river valley?
1701.answer: With respect to disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers or river valleys, the Parliament may make provisions by law for their adjudication.

1702.question: What restriction can Parliament place on the Supreme Court or any other court with respect to certain disputes?
1702.answer: Parliament may by law provide that neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall exercise jurisdiction in respect of any such dispute or complaint as is referred to in clause (1).

1703.question: What provision can be made by Parliament to prevent the Supreme Court or any other court from exercising jurisdiction in respect of certain disputes or complaints?
1703.answer: Parliament may by law provide that neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall exercise jurisdiction in respect of any such dispute or complaint as is referred to in clause (1).

1704.question: What is the duty of the Council established if it appears to the President that the public interests would be served?
1704.answer: The Council is charged with the duty of inquiring into and advising upon disputes which may have arisen between States; and investigating and discussing subjects in which some or all of the States, or the Union and one or more of the States, have a common interest.

1705.question: What are the responsibilities of the Council when disputes arise between States or when subjects of common interest between some or all States and the Union come up?
1705.answer: The Council is charged with the duty of inquiring into and advising upon such disputes and investigating and discussing such subjects, especially if it appears to the President that the public interests would be served by its establishment.

1706.question: What does the 'Finance Commission' refer to in this document?
1706.answer: A Finance Commission constituted under article 280.

1707.question: Under which article is the 'Finance Commission' constituted as mentioned in this document?

1708.question: Under what conditions can a tax be levied or collected according to this text?
1708.answer: A tax can be levied or collected only by the authority of law.

1709.question: Who has the authority to levy or collect a tax according to this text?
1709.answer: Only the authority of law can levy or collect a tax.

1710.question: What forms the 'Consolidated Fund of India' according to this document?
1710.answer: All revenues received by the Government of India, all loans raised by that Government by the issue of treasury bills, loans or ways and means advances and all moneys received by that Government in repayment of loans.

1711.question: What does the Government of India include in the 'Consolidated Fund of India'?
1711.answer: All revenues received by the Government of India, all loans raised by that Government by the issue of treasury bills, loans or ways and means advances and all moneys received by that Government in repayment of loans.

1712.question: What forms the 'Consolidated Fund of the State' according to this document?
1712.answer: All revenues received by the Government of a State, all loans raised by that Government by the issue of treasury bills, loans or ways and means advances and all moneys received by that Government in repayment of loans.

1713.question: What does 'All revenues received by the Government of a State, all loans raised by that Government by the issue of treasury bills, loans or ways and means advances and all moneys received by that Government in repayment of loans' constitute according to this document?
1713.answer: It forms the 'Consolidated Fund of the State'.

1714.question: Where should all other public moneys received by or on behalf of the Government of India or the Government of a State be credited?
1714.answer: They should be credited to the public account of India or the public account of the State, as the case may be.

1715.question: Where should the public moneys received by or on behalf of the Government of India or the Government of a State be credited?
1715.answer: They should be credited to the public account of India or the public account of the State, depending on whether the money was received on behalf of the Government of India or the Government of a State.

1716.question: Under what conditions can moneys be appropriated from the Consolidated Fund of India or the Consolidated Fund of a State?
1716.answer: No moneys can be appropriated except in accordance with law and for the purposes and in the manner provided in this Constitution.

1717.question: What is required for moneys to be appropriated from the Consolidated Fund of India or the Consolidated Fund of a State?
1717.answer: No moneys can be appropriated except in accordance with law and for the purposes and in the manner provided in this Constitution.

1718.question: What is the purpose of the Contingency Fund of India?
1718.answer: The Contingency Fund of India is established to enable advances to be made by the President for the purposes of meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation of such expenditure by Parliament.

1719.question: Who is enabled to make advances for meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament through the Contingency Fund of India?
1719.answer: The President is enabled to make advances for meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament through the Contingency Fund of India.

1720.question: Who has the disposal of the Contingency Fund of the State?
1720.answer: The Contingency Fund of the State is placed at the disposal of the Governor of the State.

1721.question: Who is the Contingency Fund of the State placed at the disposal of?
1721.answer: The Contingency Fund of the State is placed at the disposal of the Governor of the State.

1722.question: What is the purpose of the Contingency Fund of the State?
1722.answer: The Contingency Fund of the State is established to enable advances to be made by the Governor for the purposes of meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation of such expenditure by the Legislature of the State.

1723.question: Who is enabled to make advances for meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by the Legislature from the Contingency Fund of the State?
1723.answer: The Governor is enabled to make advances for meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by the Legislature from the Contingency Fund of the State.

1724.question: Who collects stamp duties levied by the Government of India?
1724.answer: Stamp duties levied by the Government of India are collected by the Government of India within any Union territory, and by the States within which such duties are respectively leviable.

1725.question: Who collects stamp duties within any Union territory and within the States where such duties are leviable in India?
1725.answer: Stamp duties levied by the Government of India are collected by the Government of India within any Union territory, and by the States within which such duties are respectively leviable.

1726.question: Do the proceeds of any such duty leviable within any State form part of the Consolidated Fund of India?
1726.answer: No, the proceeds in any financial year of any such duty leviable within any State shall not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India, but shall be assigned to that State.

1727.question: Where are the proceeds in any financial year of any such duty leviable within any State assigned to?
1727.answer: The proceeds in any financial year of any such duty leviable within any State are assigned to that State, not the Consolidated Fund of India.

1728.question: Who levies and collects taxes on the sale or purchase of goods and taxes on the consignment of goods?
1728.answer: Taxes on the sale or purchase of goods and taxes on the consignment of goods are levied and collected by the Government of India.

1729.question: Who is responsible for levying and collecting taxes on the sale or purchase and consignment of goods in India?
1729.answer: The Government of India is responsible for levying and collecting taxes on the sale or purchase and consignment of goods.

1730.question: To whom are these taxes assigned?
1730.answer: These taxes are assigned and shall be deemed to have been assigned to the States.

1731.question: Who are the taxes deemed to have been assigned to?
1731.answer: The taxes are deemed to have been assigned to the States.

1732.question: What does the expression 'taxes on the sale or purchase of goods' mean?
1732.answer: Taxes on sale or purchase of goods other than newspapers, where such sale or purchase takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce.

1733.question: What does the phrase 'sale or purchase takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce' apply to, excluding newspapers?
1733.answer: This phrase applies to the taxes on the sale or purchase of goods.

1734.question: What does the expression 'taxes on the consignment of goods' mean?
1734.answer: Taxes on the consignment of goods (whether the consignment is to the person making it or to any other person), where such consignment takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce.

1735.question: When does the term 'taxes on the consignment of goods' apply?
1735.answer: The term 'taxes on the consignment of goods' applies when such consignment takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce, whether the consignment is to the person making it or to any other person.

1736.question: What happens to the net proceeds of any such tax in a financial year?
1736.answer: They do not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India, but shall be assigned to the States within which that tax is leviable in that year, and shall be distributed among those States in accordance with such principles of distribution as may be formulated by Parliament by law.

1737.question: Where do the net proceeds of any such tax in a financial year go and how are they distributed?
1737.answer: They do not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India, but shall be assigned to the States within which that tax is leviable in that year, and shall be distributed among those States in accordance with such principles of distribution as may be formulated by Parliament by law.

1738.question: Who can formulate principles for determining when a sale or purchase of, or consignment of, goods takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce?
1738.answer: Parliament may by law formulate these principles.

1739.question: Who has the authority to formulate laws for determining when a sale or purchase of, or consignment of, goods takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce?
1739.answer: Parliament has the authority to formulate these principles.

1740.question: Who levies and collects the goods and services tax on supplies in the course of inter-State trade or commerce?

1741.question: Which entity is responsible for levying and collecting the goods and services tax on supplies in the course of inter-State trade or commerce?

1742.question: What happens to the amount apportioned to a State under clause (1)?
1742.answer: It shall not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India.

1743.question: Does the amount apportioned to a State under clause (1) form part of the Consolidated Fund of India?
1743.answer: No, it does not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India.

1744.question: What happens to the tax levied by a State under article 246A?
1744.answer: The tax levied by a State under article 246A, if used for payment of the tax, shall not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Consolidated Fund of the State.

1745.question: Does the tax levied by a State under article 246A form part of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Consolidated Fund of the State if used for payment of the tax?
1745.answer: No, the tax levied by a State under article 246A, if used for payment of the tax, does not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Consolidated Fund of the State.

1746.question: What is the role of the Parliament regarding the principles for determining the place of supply?
1746.answer: Parliament may, by law, formulate the principles for determining the place of supply, and when a supply of goods, or of services, or both takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce.

1747.question: Who has the authority to formulate the principles for determining the place of supply, particularly in the context of inter-State trade or commerce?
1747.answer: The Parliament has the authority to formulate the principles for determining the place of supply in the context of inter-State trade or commerce.

1748.question: What happens to the taxes and duties referred to in the Union List?
1748.answer: All taxes and duties referred to in the Union List, except those specified, shall be levied and collected by the Government of India and shall be distributed between the Union and the States in the manner provided in clause (2).

1749.question: Who levies and collects all taxes and duties referred to in the Union List, and how are they distributed?
1749.answer: All taxes and duties referred to in the Union List, except those specified, are levied and collected by the Government of India and are distributed between the Union and the States in the manner provided in clause (2).

1750.question: How is the tax collected by the Union under clause (1) of article 246A distributed?
1750.answer: The tax collected by the Union under clause (1) of article 246A shall also be distributed between the Union and the States in the manner provided in clause (2).

1751.question: How is the tax collected under clause (1) of article 246A, which is gathered by the Union, distributed between the Union and the States?
1751.answer: The tax is distributed in the manner provided in clause (2) of the same article.

1752.question: What happens to the tax levied and collected by the Union under clause (2) of article 246A and article 269A?
1752.answer: The tax levied and collected by the Union under clause (2) of article 246A and article 269A, which has been used for payment of the tax levied by the Union under clause (1) of article 246A, and the amount apportioned to the Union under clause (1) of article 269A, shall also be distributed between the Union and the States in the manner provided in clause (2).

1753.question: What is the distribution of the tax levied and collected by the Union under clause (2) of article 246A and article 269A, that has been used for payment of the tax levied by the Union under clause (1) of article 246A, and the amount apportioned to the Union under clause (1) of article 269A?
1753.answer: The tax and the apportioned amount shall be distributed between the Union and the States in the manner provided in clause (2).

1754.question: What does 'prescribed' mean in this article?
1754.answer: In this article, 'prescribed' typically refers to a rule or guideline that has been officially put forth or stipulated.

1755.question: What is the meaning of 'prescribed' when it refers to a rule or guideline that has been officially put forth or stipulated in an article?
1755.answer: In this context, 'prescribed' typically means that the rule or guideline has been officially put forth or stipulated.

1756.question: Who can prescribe an order before and after a Finance Commission has been constituted?

1757.question: Who has the authority to prescribe an order before and after a Finance Commission has been constituted?

1758.question: Can Parliament increase any of the duties or taxes referred to in articles 269 and 270?
1758.answer: Yes, Parliament may at any time increase any of the duties or taxes referred to in those articles except the goods and services tax.

1759.question: Can Parliament increase the goods and services tax referred to in articles 269 and 270?
1759.answer: No, Parliament cannot increase the goods and services tax, but they may increase any other duties or taxes referred to in those articles.

1760.question: What happens to the whole proceeds of any such surcharge?
1760.answer: The whole proceeds of any such surcharge shall form part of the Consolidated Fund of India.

1761.question: What does the whole proceeds of any such surcharge form part of?
1761.answer: The whole proceeds of any such surcharge form part of the Consolidated Fund of India.

1762.question: What is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India in each year as grants-in-aid of the revenues of certain states?
1762.answer: There shall be charged sums as may be prescribed in lieu of assignment of any share of the net proceeds in each year of export duty on jute and jute products.

1763.question: What is prescribed to be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India in lieu of assignment of any share of the net proceeds in each year of export duty on jute and jute products?
1763.answer: Grants-in-aid of the revenues of certain states are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India each year.

1764.question: How long will the sums continue to be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
1764.answer: The sums will continue to be charged so long as any export duty on jute or jute products continues to be levied by the Government of India or until the expiration of ten years from the commencement of this Constitution whichever is earlier.

1765.question: Until when will the sums continue to be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India if any export duty on jute or jute products continues to be levied by the Government of India?
