1765.answer: The sums will continue to be charged until the expiration of ten years from the commencement of this Constitution whichever is earlier.

1766.question: What is required for Bills affecting taxation in which States are interested?
1766.answer: Prior recommendation of President is required.

1767.question: What is required for a bill affecting taxation to be considered, especially when states are interested?
1767.answer: Prior recommendation of President is required.

1768.question: In what circumstances can a bill affecting the principles of money distribution to States be introduced in the Parliament?
1768.answer: A bill that affects the principles on which money is distributable to States can be introduced or moved in either House of Parliament only on the recommendation of the President.

1769.question: Who needs to recommend a bill for it to be introduced in either House of Parliament if it affects the principles on which money is distributable to States?
1769.answer: The President needs to recommend such a bill.

1770.question: What does the expression “tax or duty in which States are interested” mean according to this article?
1770.answer: The expression “tax or duty in which States are interested” means either a tax or duty the whole or part of the net proceeds whereof are assigned to any State, or a tax or duty by reference to the net proceeds whereof sums are for the time being payable out of the Consolidated Fund of India to any State.

1771.question: What could be the potential meanings of a 'tax or duty in which States are interested' if it refers to a tax or duty where the net proceeds are either assigned to any State or sums are payable out of the Consolidated Fund of India to any State?
1771.answer: The expression “tax or duty in which States are interested” means either a tax or duty the whole or part of the net proceeds whereof are assigned to any State, or a tax or duty by reference to the net proceeds whereof sums are for the time being payable out of the Consolidated Fund of India to any State.

1772.question: What sums are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India each year?
1772.answer: Sums that Parliament may by law provide are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India each year as grants-in-aid of the revenues of such States as Parliament may determine to be in need of assistance.

1773.question: What determines the sums charged on the Consolidated Fund of India each year and how is it allocated?
1773.answer: The sums charged on the Consolidated Fund of India each year are determined by what the Parliament may by law provide. These sums are allocated as grants-in-aid of the revenues of such States as Parliament may determine to be in need of assistance.

1774.question: What is the purpose of the grants-in-aid of the revenues of a State paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India?
1774.answer: The grants-in-aid of the revenues of a State paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India are meant to enable that State to meet the costs of such schemes of development as may be undertaken by the State with the approval of the Government of India for the purpose of promoting the welfare of the Scheduled Tribes in that State or raising the level of administration of the Scheduled Areas therein to that of the administration of the rest of the areas of that State.

1775.question: What are the grants-in-aid of the revenues of a State paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India meant for?
1775.answer: The grants-in-aid of the revenues of a State paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India are meant to enable that State to meet the costs of such schemes of development as may be undertaken by the State with the approval of the Government of India for the purpose of promoting the welfare of the Scheduled Tribes in that State or raising the level of administration of the Scheduled Areas therein to that of the administration of the rest of the areas of that State.

1776.question: What specific provisions are made for the State of Assam?
1776.answer: There shall be paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India as grants-in-aid of the revenues of the State of Assam sums, capital and recurring, equivalent to the average excess of expenditure over the revenues during the two years immediately preceding the commencement of this Constitution in respect of the administration of the tribal areas specified in Part I of the table appended.

1777.question: What is the purpose of the funds paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India to the State of Assam?
1777.answer: The funds paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India to the State of Assam are intended as grants-in-aid of the revenues, capital and recurring, equivalent to the average excess of expenditure over the revenues during the two years immediately preceding the commencement of this Constitution in respect of the administration of the tribal areas specified in Part I of the table appended.

1778.question: Who approves the schemes of development undertaken by the State for raising the level of administration?

1779.question: What entity is responsible for approving the schemes of development undertaken by the State for raising the level of administration?

1780.question: To whom shall the sums payable under clause (a) of the second proviso to clause (1) be paid if the autonomous State comprises all the tribal areas?

1781.question: Who will receive the sums payable under clause (a) of the second proviso to clause (1) if it comprises all the tribal areas?

1782.question: If the autonomous State comprises only some of the tribal areas, how will the sums payable be apportioned?
1782.answer: Between the State of Assam and the autonomous State as the President may, by order, specify

1783.question: Who decides how the sums payable will be apportioned between the State of Assam and the autonomous State if the autonomous State comprises only some of the tribal areas?
1783.answer: The President, by order, specifies this

1784.question: What shall be paid out of the Consolidated Fund of India as grants-in-aid of the revenues of the autonomous State?
1784.answer: Sums, capital and recurring, equivalent to the costs of such schemes of development as may be undertaken by the autonomous State with the approval of the Government of India

1785.question: What are the sums, capital and recurring, equivalent to the costs of such schemes of development as may be undertaken by the autonomous State with the approval of the Government of India paid out of?
1785.answer: The Consolidated Fund of India as grants-in-aid of the revenues of the autonomous State

1786.question: Who has the power to make orders until provision is made by Parliament under clause (1)?

1787.question: Who can make orders until provision is made by Parliament under clause (1)?

1788.question: After a Finance Commission has been constituted, when can the President make an order under this clause?
1788.answer: After considering the recommendations of the Finance Commission

1789.question: What does the President consider before making an order under the clause after a Finance Commission has been constituted?
1789.answer: The President considers the recommendations of the Finance Commission

1790.question: What does article 276 relate to?
1790.answer: Taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments

1791.question: Which article relates to taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments?

1792.question: Who can pass a law relating to taxes for the benefit of the State or of a municipality, district board, local board or other local authority?

1793.question: What is the role of the Legislature of a State in relation to taxes for the benefit of the State or of a municipality, district board, local board or other local authority?
1793.answer: They can pass a law relating to taxes

1794.question: What is the maximum amount payable in respect of any one person to the State or to any one municipality, district board, local board or other local authority in the State by way of taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments?
1794.answer: Two thousand and five hundred rupees per annum.

1795.question: What is the annual tax limit that can be paid by any one person to the State or to any one municipality, district board, local board or other local authority in the State on professions, trades, callings and employments?
1795.answer: Two thousand and five hundred rupees

1796.question: Does the power of the Legislature of a State to make laws regarding taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments limit the power of Parliament to make laws with respect to taxes on income accruing from or arising out of these professions, trades, callings and employments?
1796.answer: No, it does not limit the power of Parliament in any way.

1797.question: Does the power of the Legislature of a State to make laws regarding taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments limit the power of Parliament in any way?
1797.answer: No, it does not limit the power of Parliament in any way.

1798.question: What can continue to be levied and applied to the same purposes despite being mentioned in the Union List?
1798.answer: Any taxes, duties, cesses or fees which were being lawfully levied by the Government of any State or by any municipality or other local authority or body for the purposes of the State, municipality, district or other local area before the commencement of this Constitution.

1799.question: Before the commencement of the constitution, who was lawfully levying taxes, duties, cesses or fees for the purposes of the State, municipality, district or other local area?
1799.answer: The Government of any State or any municipality or other local authority or body

1800.question: What is the meaning of 'net proceeds' in the context of tax or duty?
1800.answer: Net proceeds in relation to any tax or duty means the proceeds thereof reduced by the cost of collection.

1801.question: What is reduced by the cost of collection in relation to any tax or duty?
1801.answer: The net proceeds are reduced by the cost of collection in relation to any tax or duty.

1802.question: Who is responsible for ascertaining and certifying the net proceeds of any tax or duty, or of any part of any tax or duty, in or attributable to any area?
1802.answer: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

1803.question: What is the role of The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India in relation to taxes and duties?
1803.answer: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India is responsible for ascertaining and certifying the net proceeds of any tax or duty, or of any part of any tax or duty, in or attributable to any area.

1804.question: Who is responsible for providing the manner in which the proceeds of any duty or tax are calculated?

1805.question: What role is responsible for providing the manner in which the proceeds of any duty or tax are calculated?

1806.question: What is the President required to constitute within sixty days from the date of commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016?
1806.answer: The Goods and Services Tax Council

1807.question: What was constituted by the President within sixty days from the date of commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016?
1807.answer: The Goods and Services Tax Council

1808.question: Who are the members of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
1808.answer: The Union Finance Minister (Chairperson), the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance (Member), and the Minister in charge of Finance or Taxation or any other Minister nominated by each State Government (Members)

1809.question: Who holds the positions of Chairperson and Member in the Goods and Services Tax Council?
1809.answer: The Union Finance Minister holds the position of Chairperson and the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance and the Minister in charge of Finance or Taxation or any other Minister nominated by each State Government hold the positions of Members.

1810.question: Who chooses the Vice-Chairperson of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
1810.answer: The Members of the Goods and Services Tax Council referred to in sub-clause (c) of clause (2)

1811.question: Who are referred to in sub-clause (c) of clause (2) of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
1811.answer: The Members who choose the Vice-Chairperson of the Goods and Services Tax Council

1812.question: What is one of the responsibilities of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
1812.answer: To make recommendations to the Union and the States on various aspects related to the goods and services tax

1813.question: Who is responsible for making recommendations to the Union and the States on various aspects related to the goods and services tax?
1813.answer: The Goods and Services Tax Council

1814.question: What is the Goods and Services Tax Council responsible for?
1814.answer: The Goods and Services Tax Council is responsible for deciding matters related to the goods and services tax, including the date on which the tax will be levied on certain items such as petroleum crude, high speed diesel, motor spirit, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel. The Council is guided by the need for a harmonised structure of goods and services tax and the development of a harmonised national market for goods and services.

1815.question: What does the Goods and Services Tax Council decide and what is it guided by?
1815.answer: The Goods and Services Tax Council decides on matters related to the goods and services tax, including the date on which the tax will be levied on certain items such as petroleum crude, high speed diesel, motor spirit, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel. It is guided by the need for a harmonised structure of goods and services tax and the development of a harmonised national market for goods and services.

1816.question: What constitutes a quorum at the Goods and Services Tax Council meetings?
1816.answer: One-half of the total number of Members of the Goods and Services Tax Council constitutes the quorum at its meetings.

1817.question: What is the number of members that constitutes a quorum at the Goods and Services Tax Council meetings?
1817.answer: One-half of the total number of Members of the Goods and Services Tax Council.

1818.question: How are decisions made at the Goods and Services Tax Council?
1818.answer: Every decision of the Goods and Services Tax Council is taken at a meeting, by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting. The vote of the Central Government has a weightage of one-third of the total votes cast, while the votes of all the State Governments taken together have a weightage of two-thirds of the total votes cast.

1819.question: What is the required majority for a decision to be taken at a Goods and Services Tax Council meeting and how are the votes weighted between the Central Government and the State Governments?
1819.answer: A decision at a Goods and Services Tax Council meeting is taken by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting. The Central Government's vote has a weightage of one-third of the total votes cast, while the votes of all the State Governments taken together have a weightage of two-thirds of the total votes cast.

1820.question: What happens if there is a vacancy or defect in the constitution of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
1820.answer: No act or proceedings of the Goods and Services Tax Council is invalid merely by reason of any vacancy in, or any defect in, the constitution of the Council, any defect in the appointment of a person as a Member of the Council, or any procedural irregularity of the Council not affecting the merits of the case.

1821.question: Is any act or proceedings of the Goods and Services Tax Council invalidated by any vacancy in, or any defect in, the constitution of the Council, any defect in the appointment of a person as a Member of the Council, or any procedural irregularity of the Council not affecting the merits of the case?
1821.answer: No, no act or proceedings of the Goods and Services Tax Council is invalid merely by reason of any of these issues.

1822.question: Who can adjudicate disputes between the Government of India and one or more States?

1823.question: Who adjudicates disputes between the Government of India and one or more States?

1824.question: Who can adjudicate disputes between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more other States on the other side?

1825.question: Who is responsible for adjudicating disputes between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more other States on the other side?

1826.question: Who can adjudicate disputes between two or more States?

1827.question: What is the role of The Council in the event of disputes between two or more States?
1827.answer: The Council can adjudicate disputes between two or more States.

1830.question: How frequently is the Finance Commission constituted?
1830.answer: Within two years from the commencement of the Constitution and thereafter at the expiration of every fifth year or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary

1831.question: When is the Finance Commission constituted after the commencement of the Constitution?
1831.answer: Within two years from the commencement of the Constitution and thereafter at the expiration of every fifth year or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary

1832.question: Who determines the qualifications for appointment as members of the Finance Commission?

1833.question: Who is responsible for determining the qualifications for appointment as members of the Finance Commission?

1834.question: What is the duty of the Finance Commission?
1834.answer: To make recommendations to the President on the distribution of taxes, principles governing grants-in-aid, measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State, and any other matter referred by the President in the interests of sound finance.

1835.question: What responsibilities does the Finance Commission have in relation to the President, distribution of taxes, grants-in-aid, and the Consolidated Fund of a State?
1835.answer: The Finance Commission's duty is to make recommendations to the President on the distribution of taxes, principles governing grants-in-aid, measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State, and any other matter referred by the President in the interests of sound finance.

1836.question: Who determines the procedure of the Finance Commission?

1837.question: Who determines its own procedure in the Finance Commission?

1838.question: Who provides the Commission with powers in the performance of their functions?

1839.question: Who does the Parliament provide powers to in the performance of their functions?

1840.question: What action is to be taken by the President with regards to the recommendations of the Finance Commission?
1840.answer: The President shall cause every recommendation made by the Finance Commission under the provisions of this Constitution together with an explanatory memorandum as to the action taken thereon to be laid before each House of Parliament.

1841.question: What is the procedure for the President to follow regarding the recommendations made by the Finance Commission under the provisions of the Constitution?
1841.answer: The President shall cause every recommendation made by the Finance Commission under the provisions of this Constitution together with an explanatory memorandum as to the action taken thereon to be laid before each House of Parliament.

1842.question: Who can make grants for any public purpose according to section 282 of the constitution?
1842.answer: The Union or a State may make any grants for any public purpose.

1843.question: According to section 282 of the constitution, who may make grants for any public purpose?

1844.question: What does section 283 of the constitution stipulate about the custody of the Consolidated Funds, Contingency Funds and moneys credited to the public accounts?
1844.answer: The custody of the Consolidated Fund of India and the Contingency Fund of India, the payment of moneys into such Funds, the withdrawal of moneys therefrom, the custody of public moneys other than those credited to such Funds received by or on behalf of the Government of India, their payment into the public account of India and the withdrawal of moneys from such account and all other matters connected with or ancillary to matters aforesaid shall be regulated by law made by Parliament, and, until provision in that behalf is so made, shall be regulated by rules made by the President.

1845.question: Who regulates the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India and the Contingency Fund of India, the payment of moneys into such Funds, the withdrawal of moneys therefrom, the custody of public moneys other than those credited to such Funds received by or on behalf of the Government of India, their payment into the public account of India and the withdrawal of moneys from such account and all other matters connected with or ancillary to matters aforesaid until provision in that behalf is so made?
1845.answer: These matters are regulated by law made by Parliament, and, until provision in that behalf is so made, they are regulated by rules made by the President, as stipulated by section 283 of the constitution.

1846.question: What does section 283(2) of the constitution stipulate about the custody of the Consolidated Fund of a State and the Contingency Fund of a State?
1846.answer: The custody of the Consolidated Fund of a State and the Contingency Fund of a State, the payment of moneys into such Funds, the withdrawal of moneys therefrom, the custody of public moneys other than those credited to such Funds received by or on behalf of the Government of the State, their payment into the public account of the State and the withdrawal of moneys from such account and all other matters connected with or ancillary to matters aforesaid shall be regulated by law made by the Legislature of the State, and, until provision in that behalf is so made, shall be regulated by rules made by the Governor of the State.

1847.question: What does the law made by the Legislature of a State or the rules made by the Governor of the State regulate in terms of the custody of the Consolidated Fund of a State and the Contingency Fund of a State, the payment of moneys into such Funds, the withdrawal of moneys therefrom, the custody of public moneys other than those credited to such Funds received by or on behalf of the Government of the State, their payment into the public account of the State and the withdrawal of moneys from such account and all other matters connected with or ancillary to matters aforesaid?
1847.answer: This is stipulated in section 283(2) of the constitution.

1848.question: What happens to moneys received by public servants and courts in India?
1848.answer: These moneys shall be paid into the public account of India or the public account of the State.

1849.question: Where are moneys received by public servants and courts in India paid into?
1849.answer: These moneys shall be paid into the public account of India or the public account of the State.

1850.question: What is the rule regarding taxation of the property of the Union in India?
1850.answer: The property of the Union is exempt from all taxes imposed by a State or by any authority within a State, unless Parliament provides otherwise by law.

1851.question: Is the property of the Union in India exempt from all taxes imposed by a State or any authority within the State, and under what condition could this change?
1851.answer: Yes, the property of the Union is exempt from all taxes imposed by a State or any authority within a State, unless Parliament provides otherwise by law.

1852.question: Can a State impose a tax on the supply of goods or services that takes place outside the State or during import/export?
1852.answer: No, a State cannot impose a tax on the supply of goods or services that takes place outside the State or during import/export.

1853.question: Is it permissible for a State to impose a tax on the supply of goods or services that are provided outside the State or during import/export?
1853.answer: No, it is not permissible for a State to impose such a tax.

1854.question: Are there any restrictions on the imposition of tax on the sale or purchase of goods in India?
1854.answer: Yes, no law of a State shall impose, or authorise the imposition of, a tax on the supply of goods or services where such supply takes place outside the State or in the course of import or export of the goods or services.

1855.question: Can a state law in India impose a tax on the supply of goods or services when such supply takes place outside the State or during the import or export of the goods or services?
1855.answer: No, no law of a State shall impose, or authorise the imposition of, a tax on the supply of goods or services where such supply takes place outside the State or in the course of import or export of the goods or services.

1856.question: What is the rule regarding taxation on the consumption or sale of electricity in India?
1856.answer: Unless otherwise provided by Parliament by law, no law of a State shall impose or authorise the imposition of a tax on the consumption or sale of electricity.

1857.question: Who has the authority to impose a tax on the consumption or sale of electricity in India?
1857.answer: Unless otherwise provided by Parliament by law, no law of a State shall impose or authorise the imposition of a tax on the consumption or sale of electricity.

1858.question: What is the law regarding the consumption of electricity by the Government of India?
1858.answer: Any law imposing, or authorising the imposition of, a tax on the sale of electricity shall secure that the price of electricity sold to the Government of India for consumption by that Government, or to any such railway company for consumption in the construction, maintenance or operation of any railway, shall be less by the amount of the tax than the price charged to other consumers.

1859.question: What is the stipulation of any law imposing a tax on the sale of electricity in relation to the price of electricity sold to the Government of India or any railway company?
1859.answer: The law ensures that the price of electricity sold to the Government of India for its consumption, or to any railway company for use in construction, maintenance or operation of any railway, shall be less by the amount of the tax than the price charged to other consumers.

1860.question: What is the exemption from taxation by States in respect of water or electricity in certain cases according to the Constitution of India?
1860.answer: No law of a State in force immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall impose, or authorise the imposition of, a tax in respect of any water or electricity stored, generated, consumed, distributed or sold by any authority established by any existing law or any law made by Parliament for regulating or developing any inter-State river or river valley. However, the Legislature of a State may by law impose such tax, but no such law shall have any effect unless it has, after having been reserved for the consideration of the President, received his assent.

1861.question: What does the Constitution of India state regarding the imposition of tax on water or electricity by a State's law in force before the commencement of the Constitution?
1861.answer: The Constitution of India states that no law of a State in force immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall impose, or authorise the imposition of, a tax in respect of any water or electricity stored, generated, consumed, distributed or sold by any authority established by any existing law or any law made by Parliament for regulating or developing any inter-State river or river valley. However, the Legislature of a State may by law impose such tax, but no such law shall have any effect unless it has, after having been reserved for the consideration of the President, received his assent.

1862.question: What does the expression 'law of a State in force' include?
1862.answer: The expression 'law of a State in force' includes a law of a State passed or made before the commencement of the Constitution and not previously repealed, notwithstanding that it or parts of it may not be then in operation either at all or in particular areas.

1863.question: What does a law of a State passed or made before the commencement of the Constitution and not previously repealed, notwithstanding that it or parts of it may not be then in operation either at all or in particular areas, refer to?
1863.answer: This refers to the expression 'law of a State in force'.

1864.question: What needs to be obtained before making any rule or order under the law regarding the fixation of tax rates?
1864.answer: The previous consent of the President.

1865.question: Whose consent is required to be obtained before making any rule or order under the law regarding the fixation of tax rates?
1865.answer: The previous consent of the President.

1866.question: Is the property and income of a State exempt from Union taxation?
1866.answer: Yes, the property and income of a State shall be exempt from Union taxation.

1867.question: Is the property and income of a State subject to Union taxation?
1867.answer: No, the property and income of a State are not subject to Union taxation.

1868.question: Can the Union impose any tax on a state's trade or business?
1868.answer: Yes, the Union can impose, or authorise the imposition of, any tax to such extent, if any, as Parliament may by law provide in respect of a trade or business of any kind carried on by, or on behalf of, the Government of a State.

1869.question: Who authorizes the imposition of any tax on a state's trade or business and to what extent?
1869.answer: The Union can impose, or authorise the imposition of, any tax to such extent, if any, as Parliament may by law provide in respect of a trade or business of any kind carried on by, or on behalf of, the Government of a State.

1870.question: What is the exception to the Union imposing tax on a state's trade or business?
1870.answer: The exception is any trade or business, or to any class of trade or business, which Parliament may by law declare to be incidental to the ordinary functions of Government.

1871.question: What does Parliament declare to be incidental to the ordinary functions of Government that exempts it from the Union imposing tax on a state's trade or business?
1871.answer: Any trade or business, or to any class of trade or business is declared by Parliament to be incidental to the ordinary functions of Government, which is the exception to the Union imposing tax.

1872.question: What factors determine if the expenses of a court or Commission, or pension are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India or the Consolidated Fund of a State?
1872.answer: It depends on whether the court or Commission serves any of the separate needs of a State or the Union, or if the person has served wholly or in part in connection with the affairs of a State or the Union.

1873.question: What determines whether the expenses of a court, Commission, or pension are charged on the Consolidated Fund of a State or the Consolidated Fund of India?
1873.answer: If the court or Commission serves any of the separate needs of a State or the Union, or if the person has served wholly or in part in connection with the affairs of a State or the Union, it determines whether the expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of a State or the Consolidated Fund of India.

1874.question: Who determines the contribution in respect of the expenses or pension in case of a disagreement?
1874.answer: An arbitrator appointed by the Chief Justice of India

1875.question: Who appoints the arbitrator that determines the contribution in respect of the expenses or pension in case of a disagreement?

1876.question: What is the annual payment to the Travancore Devaswom Fund from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala?
1876.answer: Forty-six lakhs and fifty thousand rupees

1877.question: Which fund receives an annual payment of forty-six lakhs and fifty thousand rupees from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala?

1878.question: What is the annual payment to the Devaswom Fund from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Tamil Nadu?
1878.answer: Thirteen lakhs and fifty thousand rupees

1879.question: Which fund receives an annual payment of thirteen lakhs and fifty thousand rupees from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Tamil Nadu?

1880.question: Who has the power to borrow upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of India?
1880.answer: The executive power of the Union

1881.question: Who can borrow upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of India?
1881.answer: The executive power of the Union

1882.question: Who sets the limits for borrowing upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of India?

1883.question: What entity is responsible for setting the limits for borrowing upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of India?

1884.question: Who has the power to borrow within the territory of India upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of the State?
1884.answer: The executive power of a State

1885.question: Who has the authority to borrow on the security of the Consolidated Fund of the State within the territory of India?
1885.answer: The executive power of a State

1886.question: Who sets the limits for borrowing upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of the State?

1887.question: What body is responsible for setting the limits for borrowing upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of a State?

1888.question: Can the Government of India make loans to any State?
1888.answer: Yes, subject to conditions laid down by or under any law made by Parliament

1889.question: Under what conditions can the Government of India make loans to any State?
1889.answer: The Government of India can make loans to any State subject to conditions laid down by or under any law made by Parliament

1890.question: Can a State raise any loan without the consent of the Government of India?
1890.answer: No, a State may not raise any loan without the consent of the Government of India if there is still outstanding any part of a loan which has been made to the State by the Government of India or by its predecessor Government.

1891.question: If there is still outstanding any part of a loan which has been made to a State by the Government of India or by its predecessor Government, can the State raise any loan without the consent of the Government of India?
1891.answer: No, a State may not raise any loan without the consent of the Government of India in such circumstances.

1892.question: What happens to the property and assets vested in His Majesty for the purposes of the Government of the Dominion of India and each Governor’s Province at the commencement of this Constitution?
1892.answer: All property and assets which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution were vested in His Majesty for the purposes of the Government of the Dominion of India and each Governor’s Province shall vest respectively in the Union and the corresponding State.

1893.question: Where did all the property and assets vested in His Majesty for the purposes of the Government of the Dominion of India and each Governor’s Province vest after the commencement of the Constitution?
1893.answer: All property and assets which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution were vested in His Majesty for the purposes of the Government of the Dominion of India and each Governor’s Province vested respectively in the Union and the corresponding State.

1894.question: What happens to the rights, liabilities, and obligations of the Government of the Dominion of India and each Governor's Province at the commencement of this Constitution?
1894.answer: All rights, liabilities and obligations of the Government of the Dominion of India and of the Government of each Governor's Province, whether arising out of any contract or otherwise, shall be the rights, liabilities and obligations respectively of the Government of India and the Government of each corresponding State.

1895.question: Who assumes the rights, liabilities and obligations of the Government of the Dominion of India and of the Government of each Governor's Province, whether arising out of any contract or otherwise, at the commencement of the Constitution?
1895.answer: The rights, liabilities and obligations respectively of the Government of India and the Government of each corresponding State.

1896.question: What happens to the property and assets vested in any Indian State corresponding to a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule?
1896.answer: They shall vest in the Union, if the purposes for which such property and assets were held immediately before such commencement will thereafter be purposes of the Union relating to any of the matters enumerated in the Union List.

1897.question: Who does the property and assets vested in any Indian State corresponding to a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule vest in if the purposes for which such property and assets were held immediately before such commencement will thereafter be purposes of the Union relating to any of the matters enumerated in the Union List?
1897.answer: They shall vest in the Union

1898.question: What happens to the rights, liabilities and obligations of the Government of any Indian State corresponding to a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule?
1898.answer: They shall be the rights, liabilities and obligations of the Government of India, if the purposes for which such rights were acquired or liabilities or obligations were incurred before such commencement will thereafter be purposes of the Government of India relating to any of the matters enumerated in the Union List.

1899.question: Who assumes the rights, liabilities and obligations of the Government of an Indian State corresponding to a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule, if the purposes for which such rights were acquired or liabilities or obligations were incurred before such commencement will thereafter be purposes of the Government of India relating to any of the matters enumerated in the Union List?
1899.answer: They shall be the rights, liabilities and obligations of the Government of India.

1900.question: Who is the successor of the Government of each State specified in Part B of the First Schedule?
1900.answer: The Government of each State specified in Part B of the First Schedule shall be the successor of the Government of the corresponding Indian State as regards all property and assets and all rights, liabilities and obligations.

1901.question: Who shall the Government of the corresponding Indian State as regards all property and assets and all rights, liabilities and obligations succeed?
1901.answer: The Government of each State specified in Part B of the First Schedule is the successor of the Government of the corresponding Indian State as regards all property and assets and all rights, liabilities and obligations.

1902.question: What happens to any property in the territory of India which would have accrued to His Majesty or the Ruler of an Indian State by escheat or lapse, or as bona vacantia for want of a rightful owner?
1902.answer: It shall, if it is property situate in a State, vest in such State, and shall, in any other case, vest in the Union.

1903.question: Where does property in the territory of India, which would have accrued to His Majesty or the Ruler of an Indian State by escheat or lapse, or as bona vacantia for want of a rightful owner, vest if it is property situated in a State or in any other case?
1903.answer: It shall, if it is property situate in a State, vest in such State, and shall, in any other case, vest in the Union.

1904.question: What does Article 297 of the Indian Constitution state?
1904.answer: Article 297 states that all lands, minerals and other things of value within the territorial waters, the continental shelf, or the exclusive economic zone of India shall vest in the Union and be held for the purposes of the Union. Also, all other resources of the exclusive economic zone of India shall vest in the Union and be held for the purposes of the Union.

1905.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution declares that all lands, minerals and other things of value within the territorial waters, the continental shelf, or the exclusive economic zone of India shall vest in the Union and be held for the purposes of the Union?
1905.answer: Article 297 of the Indian Constitution states this.

1906.question: What is the executive power of the Union and each State in relation to trade according to Article 298 of the Indian Constitution?
1906.answer: According to Article 298, the executive power of the Union and of each State extends to carrying on any trade or business and to the acquisition, holding and disposal of property and the making of contracts for any purpose. However, the executive power of the Union is subject to legislation by the State in matters that Parliament cannot make laws about. Similarly, the executive power of each State is subject to legislation by Parliament in matters that the State Legislature cannot make laws about.

1907.question: What does Article 298 of the Indian Constitution say about the extent of executive power of the Union and each State, and how it's affected by legislation from the respective State or the Parliament?
1907.answer: According to Article 298, the executive power of the Union and of each State extends to carrying on any trade or business and to the acquisition, holding and disposal of property and the making of contracts for any purpose. However, the executive power of the Union is subject to legislation by the State in matters that Parliament cannot make laws about. Similarly, the executive power of each State is subject to legislation by Parliament in matters that the State Legislature cannot make laws about.

1908.question: How are contracts made in the exercise of the executive power of the Union or a State expressed according to Article 299 of the Indian Constitution?
1908.answer: According to Article 299, all contracts made in the exercise of the executive power of the Union or of a State shall be expressed to be made by.

1909.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution stipulates that all contracts made in the exercise of the executive power of the Union or of a State shall be expressed to be made by?

1910.question: Who are the expressions 'Ruler' and 'Indian State' referred to as per the constitution?
1910.answer: In the given article, the expressions 'Ruler' and 'Indian State' have the same meanings as in article 363.

1911.question: According to which article do the expressions 'Ruler' and 'Indian State' have the same meanings as in a given article in the Constitution?

1912.question: Who can execute contracts and property assurances according to this constitution?
1912.answer: The President or the Governor can execute contracts and property assurances, by authorizing certain persons to do so in a manner they direct.

1913.question: Who is authorized to execute contracts and property assurances, and who do they delegate to carry out this task according to the constitution?
1913.answer: The President or the Governor are authorized to execute contracts and property assurances, and they delegate this task to certain persons they direct.

1914.question: Are the President or the Governor personally liable for any contract or assurance made or executed for the purposes of this Constitution?
1914.answer: No, neither the President nor the Governor shall be personally liable in respect of any contract or assurance made or executed for the purposes of this Constitution.

1915.question: Who is not personally liable in respect of any contract or assurance made or executed for the purposes of the Constitution?
1915.answer: Neither the President nor the Governor are personally liable.

1916.question: Who can sue the Government of India?
1916.answer: The Government of India may be sued by the name of the Union of India.

1917.question: Under what name can someone sue the Government of India?
1917.answer: Someone can sue the Government of India under the name of the Union of India.

1918.question: Under what circumstances can a State Government be sued?
1918.answer: The Government of a State may be sued by the name of the State and may be sued in relation to their respective affairs in the like cases as the Dominion of India and the corresponding Provinces or the corresponding Indian States might have sued if this Constitution had not been enacted.

1919.question: Who can sue the Government of a State and in what circumstances, according to the constitution?
1919.answer: The Government of a State may be sued by the name of the State and may be sued in relation to their respective affairs in the like cases as the Dominion of India and the corresponding Provinces or the corresponding Indian States might have sued if this Constitution had not been enacted.

1920.question: What happens to legal proceedings at the commencement of this Constitution where the Dominion of India is a party?
1920.answer: If any legal proceedings are pending to which the Dominion of India is a party, the Union of India shall be deemed to be substituted for the Dominion in those proceedings.

1921.question: Who shall be deemed substituted for the Dominion of India in any legal proceedings pending at the commencement of this Constitution where the Dominion of India is a party?
1921.answer: The Union of India shall be deemed to be substituted for the Dominion in those proceedings.

1922.question: What is the right to property under this Constitution?
1922.answer: No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

1923.question: Under what conditions can a person be deprived of his property according to this Constitution?
1923.answer: A person can be deprived of his property only by authority of law.

1924.question: What is the status of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India?
1924.answer: Trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free, subject to the other provisions of this Part.

1925.question: What are the conditions under which trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India operate?
1925.answer: Trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India operate freely, subject to the other provisions of this Part.

1926.question: Who has the power to impose restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse?
1926.answer: Parliament may by law impose such restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse.

1927.question: Who may by law impose restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse?
1927.answer: Parliament has the power to impose restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse.

1928.question: Under what conditions can restrictions be imposed on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse?
1928.answer: Restrictions can be imposed if required in the public interest.

1929.question: Under what circumstances can restrictions be imposed on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse?
1929.answer: If it is required in the public interest.

1930.question: Can Parliament or the Legislature of a State give preference to one State over another in terms of trade and commerce?
1930.answer: No, neither Parliament nor the Legislature of a State shall have power to make any law giving preference to one State over another, or making any discrimination between one State and another, in terms of trade and commerce.

1931.question: Does the Parliament or the Legislature of a State have the power to make a law that gives preference to one State over another, or make any discrimination between one State and another, in terms of trade and commerce?
1931.answer: No, neither Parliament nor the Legislature of a State has the power to make any law that gives preference to one State over another, or make any discrimination between one State and another, in terms of trade and commerce.

1932.question: What exception allows Parliament to give preference or make discrimination between states?
1932.answer: Parliament can make any law giving preference or making discrimination between states if it is declared by such law that it is necessary to do so for the purpose of dealing with a situation arising from scarcity of goods in any part of the territory of India.

1933.question: Under what circumstances can the Parliament make a law giving preference or making discrimination between states?
1933.answer: Parliament can make such a law when it is necessary to deal with a situation arising from scarcity of goods in any part of the territory of India.

1934.question: Can a State impose taxes on goods imported from other States or the Union territories?
1934.answer: Yes, the Legislature of a State may by law impose on goods imported from other States or the Union territories any tax to which similar goods manufactured or produced in that State are subject.

1935.question: What type of tax can the Legislature of a State impose on goods imported from other States or the Union territories?
1935.answer: The Legislature of a State may impose any tax to which similar goods manufactured or produced in that State are subject.

1936.question: Can a State impose restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse?
1936.answer: Yes, a State can impose such reasonable restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse with or within that State as may be required in the public interest.

1937.question: What conditions allow a State to impose restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse?
1937.answer: A State can impose such restrictions if they are reasonable and required in the public interest.

1938.question: What does Article 305 of the Indian Constitution state?
1938.answer: Article 305 states that nothing in articles 301 and 303 shall affect the provisions of any existing law unless the President orders otherwise. Also, nothing in article 301 shall affect the operation of any law made before the commencement of the Constitution (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1955, or prevent Parliament or the Legislature of a State from making any law relating to the matters referred in sub-clause (ii) of clause (6) of article 19.

1939.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution states that nothing in articles 301 and 303 shall affect the provisions of any existing law unless the President orders otherwise, and nothing in article 301 shall affect the operation of any law made before the commencement of the Constitution (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1955, or prevent Parliament or the Legislature of a State from making any law relating to the matters referred in sub-clause (ii) of clause (6) of article 19?
1939.answer: Article 305 of the Indian Constitution states this.

1940.question: What is the purpose of Article 307 of the Indian Constitution?
1940.answer: Article 307 allows Parliament to appoint an authority for carrying out the purposes of articles 301, 302, 303 and 304. It can confer on the appointed authority any powers and duties it considers necessary.

1941.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution permits the Parliament to appoint an authority for executing the purposes of articles 301, 302, 303, and 304, and to confer on them any necessary powers and duties?
1941.answer: Article 307 of the Indian Constitution allows the Parliament to do this.

1942.question: What does Article 308 of the Indian Constitution clarify?
1942.answer: Article 308 clarifies that in the context of this Part of the Constitution, the expression 'State' does not include the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

1943.question: Which state is not included in the expression 'State' according to Article 308 of the Indian Constitution?
1943.answer: The State of Jammu and Kashmir is not included in the expression 'State' according to Article 308 of the Indian Constitution.

1944.question: What does Article 309 of the Indian Constitution state?
1944.answer: Article 309 states that, subject to the provisions of the Constitution, Acts of the appropriate Legislature may regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or any State.

1945.question: What does the Indian Constitution allow the appropriate Legislature to regulate in regards to persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or any State?
1945.answer: Article 309 of the Indian Constitution allows the appropriate Legislature to regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of these persons.

1946.question: Who makes the rules regulating the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to services and posts?

1947.question: What entity is responsible for making the rules regulating the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to services and posts?

1948.question: Who holds office during the pleasure of the President?
1948.answer: Every person who is a member of a defence service or of a civil service of the Union or of an all-India service or holds any post connected with defence or any civil post under the Union

1949.question: Who are the people that are members of a defence service or of a civil service of the Union or of an all-India service or hold any post connected with defence or any civil post under the Union?
1949.answer: Every person who holds office during the pleasure of the President

1950.question: Who holds office during the pleasure of the Governor of the State?
1950.answer: Every person who is a member of a civil service of a State or holds any civil post under a State

1951.question: Who is Every person who is a member of a civil service of a State or holds any civil post under a State?
1951.answer: They are the ones who hold office during the pleasure of the Governor of the State

1952.question: Can a contract provide for the payment of compensation to a person appointed under this Constitution?
1952.answer: Yes, if the President or the Governor deems it necessary in order to secure the services of a person having special qualifications

1953.question: Who can deem it necessary for a contract to provide for the payment of compensation to a person appointed under the Constitution, in order to secure the services of a person having special qualifications?

1954.question: Who cannot be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate?
1954.answer: No person who is a member of a civil service of the Union or an all-India service or a civil service of a State or holds a civil post under the Union or a State

1955.question: What positions does a person hold if they cannot be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate?
1955.answer: A member of a civil service of the Union or an all-India service or a civil service of a State or holds a civil post under the Union or a State

1956.question: What conditions need to be met before a person can be dismissed, removed, or reduced in rank?
1956.answer: Such a person can only be dismissed, removed, or reduced in rank after an inquiry in which he has been informed of the charges against him and given a reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of those charges. However, if it is proposed to impose a penalty on him after such inquiry, it may be imposed on the basis of the evidence adduced during the inquiry and it is not necessary to give such person any opportunity of making a representation on the penalty proposed.

1957.question: What is the process for dismissing, removing, or reducing a person's rank and what opportunity should be given to such a person during this process?
1957.answer: The process involves an inquiry where the person is informed of the charges against him and given a reasonable opportunity to be heard in respect to those charges. If a penalty is proposed after the inquiry, it can be imposed based on the evidence presented during the inquiry. The person does not need to be given another opportunity to make a representation on the proposed penalty.

1958.question: Are there any exceptions to the requirements for dismissal, removal, or reduction in rank?
1958.answer: Yes, the requirements do not apply if a person is dismissed or removed or reduced in rank on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge; where the authority empowered to dismiss or remove a person or to reduce him in rank is satisfied that for some reason, it is not reasonably practicable to hold such inquiry; or where the President or the Governor, as the case may be, is satisfied that in the interest of the security of the State it is not expedient to hold such inquiry.

1959.question: Under what circumstances do the requirements for dismissal, removal, or reduction in rank not apply?
1959.answer: The requirements do not apply if a person is dismissed or removed or reduced in rank on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge; where the authority empowered to dismiss or remove a person or to reduce him in rank is satisfied that for some reason, it is not reasonably practicable to hold such inquiry; or where the President or the Governor, as the case may be, is satisfied that in the interest of the security of the State it is not expedient to hold such inquiry.

1960.question: Who decides if it is reasonably practicable to hold an inquiry in respect of dismissal, removal, or reduction in rank?
1960.answer: The decision on whether it is reasonably practicable to hold such an inquiry lies with the authority empowered to dismiss or remove such person or to reduce him in rank.

1961.question: Who has the power to decide if an inquiry can be held when it comes to the dismissal, removal, or reduction in rank of a person?
1961.answer: The authority empowered to dismiss or remove such person or to reduce him in rank has the power to decide if an inquiry can be held.

1962.question: Under what conditions can Parliament create an All-India service?
1962.answer: Parliament can create an All-India service if the Council of States has declared by resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting that it is necessary or expedient in the national interest to do so.

1963.question: What needs to happen for Parliament to create an All-India service in the national interest?
1963.answer: The Council of States has to declare by resolution, supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting, that it is necessary or expedient to do so.

1964.question: What services are deemed to be created by Parliament at the commencement of the Constitution?
1964.answer: The Indian Administrative Service and the Indian Police Service

1965.question: Which services were created by Parliament at the commencement of the Constitution in India?
1965.answer: The Indian Administrative Service and the Indian Police Service

1966.question: What is not included in the all-India judicial service?
1966.answer: Any post inferior to that of a district judge as defined in article 236

1967.question: What is defined as inferior to the post of a district judge in the all-India judicial service according to article 236?
1967.answer: Any post that is not included in the all-India judicial service

1968.question: What does the law providing for the creation of the all-India judicial service may contain?
1968.answer: Such provisions for the amendment of Chapter VI of Part VI as may be necessary for giving effect to the provisions of that law

1969.question: What may be necessary for giving effect to the law providing for the creation of the all-India judicial service?
1969.answer: Such provisions for the amendment of Chapter VI of Part VI

1970.question: What power does the Parliament have in varying or revoking conditions of service of officers of certain services?
1970.answer: Parliament may by law vary or revoke, whether prospectively or retrospectively, the conditions of services as respects remuneration, leave and pension and the rights as respects disciplinary matters of persons who have been appointed by the Secretary of State or Secretary of State in Council to a civil service of the Crown in India before the commencement of this Constitution

1971.question: Who can vary or revoke the conditions of services such as remuneration, leave, pension and disciplinary matters of persons appointed by the Secretary of State or Secretary of State in Council to a civil service of the Crown in India before the commencement of the Constitution?
1971.answer: The Parliament has the power to vary or revoke these conditions of service.

1972.question: Who can the Parliament vary or revoke the conditions of service for?
1972.answer: Persons who, having been appointed by the Secretary of State or Secretary of State in Council to a civil service of the Crown in India before the commencement of this Constitution, continue to serve under the Government of India or of a State in any service or post; and persons who, having been appointed by the Secretary of State or Secretary of State in Council to a civil service of the Crown in India before the commencement of this Constitution, retired or otherwise ceased to be in service at any time before the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-eighth Amendment) Act, 1972

1973.question: Who were the persons appointed by the Secretary of State or Secretary of State in Council to a civil service of the Crown in India before the commencement of this Constitution and continued to serve or retired before the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-eighth Amendment) Act, 1972?
1973.answer: The Parliament can vary or revoke the conditions of service for these persons.

1974.question: What does the Constitution of India state about the empowerment of Parliament to vary or revoke conditions of service?
1974.answer: The Constitution of India states that nothing in sub-clause (a) or sub-clause (b) shall be construed as empowering Parliament to vary or revoke, after his appointment to such post, the conditions of his service to his disadvantage except in so far as such conditions of service are applicable to him by reason of his being a person appointed by the Secretary of State or Secretary of State in Council to a civil service of the Crown in India.

1975.question: What does sub-clause (a) and sub-clause (b) of the Constitution of India state about the power of Parliament to vary or revoke the conditions of service after a person's appointment, particularly to his disadvantage?
1975.answer: The Constitution of India states that nothing in sub-clause (a) or sub-clause (b) shall be construed as empowering Parliament to vary or revoke, after his appointment to such post, the conditions of his service to his disadvantage except in so far as such conditions of service are applicable to him by reason of his being a person appointed by the Secretary of State or Secretary of State in Council to a civil service of the Crown in India.

1976.question: What is the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court or any other court in disputes according to the Constitution of India?
1976.answer: The Constitution of India states that neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall have jurisdiction in any dispute arising out of any provision of, or any endorsement on, any covenant, agreement or other similar instrument which was entered into or executed by any person referred to in clause (1), or arising out of any letter issued to such person, in relation to his appointment to any civil service of the Crown in India or his continuance in service under the Government of the Dominion of India or a Province thereof.

1977.question: What does the Constitution of India state about the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts in disputes arising from provisions, endorsements, covenants, agreements or similar instruments entered into by any person referenced in clause (1), or from any letter issued to such person in relation to his appointment to any civil service of the Crown in India or his continuance in service under the Government of the Dominion of India or a Province thereof?
1977.answer: The Constitution of India states that neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall have jurisdiction in any such dispute.

1978.question: What is stated in the transitional provisions of the Constitution of India?
1978.answer: The transitional provisions of the Constitution of India state that until other provision is made in this behalf under this Constitution, all the laws in force immediately before the commencement of this Constitution and applicable to any public service or any post which continues to exist after the commencement of this Constitution, as an all-India service or as se

1979.question: What do the laws in force immediately before the commencement of the Constitution of India apply to according to the transitional provisions of the Constitution?
1979.answer: According to the transitional provisions of the Constitution of India, the laws in force immediately before the commencement of the Constitution apply to any public service or any post which continues to exist after the commencement of this Constitution, as an all-India service.

1980.question: What is the effect of the provisions of a certain article according to the Constitution of India?
1980.answer: The Constitution of India states that the provisions of this article shall have effect notwithstanding anything in article 314 as originally enacted or in any other provision of this Constitution.

1981.question: What does the Constitution of India state about the effect of the provisions of a certain article, especially in relation to article 314 and other provisions of the Constitution?
1981.answer: The Constitution of India states that the provisions of this article shall have effect notwithstanding anything in article 314 as originally enacted or in any other provision of this Constitution.

1982.question: What does the Constitution of India's Chapter II cover?

1983.question: Which chapter of the Constitution of India covers Public Service Commissions?

1984.question: What is the purpose of a Public Service Commission according to the Indian Constitution?
1984.answer: The Public Service Commission serves the needs of the Union or the State as respects the particular matter in question.

1985.question: Who serves the needs of the Union or the State as respects the particular matter in question, according to the Indian Constitution?
1985.answer: The Public Service Commission serves the needs of the Union or the State in this regard.

1986.question: Can two or more states have one Public Service Commission?
1986.answer: Yes, two or more States may agree to have one Public Service Commission.

1987.question: Can two or more States agree to have one Public Service Commission?
1987.answer: Yes, two or more states can have one Public Service Commission.

1988.question: Who is responsible for appointing the Chairman and the members of the Public Service Commission?
1988.answer: The Chairman and other members of a Public Service Commission are appointed by the President in the case of the Union Commission or a Joint Commission, and by the Governor in the case of a State Commission.

1989.question: Who does the President and the Governor appoint in the case of the Union Commission or a Joint Commission and a State Commission respectively?
1989.answer: The President appoints the Chairman and other members of the Union Commission or a Joint Commission, while the Governor appoints the same for a State Commission.

1990.question: What does the Indian Constitution say about the continuation of services or posts under the Union or a State?
1990.answer: Services or posts under the Union or a State shall continue in force so far as consistent with the provisions of this Constitution.

1991.question: What does the Constitution provision regarding the continuation of services or posts under the Union or a State?
1991.answer: The Indian Constitution says that services or posts under the Union or a State shall continue in force so far as consistent with the provisions of this Constitution.

1992.question: What is the minimum years of service required for someone to be considered for appointment in the Public Service Commission?

1993.question: How many years of service are required for someone to be considered for appointment in the Public Service Commission?

1994.question: Who would perform the duties of the Chairman of the Commission in case of absence or other reasons?
1994.answer: The duties would be performed by one of the other members of the Commission as appointed by the President, in the case of the Union Commission or a Joint Commission, and the Governor of the State in the case of a State Commission.

1995.question: Who appoints the member to perform the duties of the Chairman of the Union Commission or a Joint Commission in case of absence or other reasons?
1995.answer: The President appoints one of the other members to perform the duties.

1996.question: What is the term of office for a member of a Public Service Commission?
1996.answer: Six years from the date on which he enters upon his office or until he attains, in the case of the Union Commission, the age of sixty-five years, and in the case of a State Commission or a Joint Commission, the age of sixty-two years, whichever is earlier.

1997.question: How long can a member serve in a Public Service Commission before he attains the age of sixty-five years in the Union Commission, or sixty-two years in a State Commission or a Joint Commission?
1997.answer: Six years from the date on which he enters upon his office.

1998.question: How can a member of a Public Service Commission resign his office?
1998.answer: A member of a Public Service Commission may resign his office by writing under his hand addressed, in the case of the Union Commission or a Joint Commission, to the President, and in the case of a State Commission, to the Governor of the State.

1999.question: To whom should a member of a Public Service Commission address his resignation letter if he wants to resign from the Union Commission or a Joint Commission, and to whom if he wants to resign from a State Commission?
1999.answer: A member of a Public Service Commission should address his resignation letter to the President if he wants to resign from the Union Commission or a Joint Commission, and to the Governor of the State if he wants to resign from a State Commission.

2000.question: Is a person who holds office as a member of a Public Service Commission eligible for reappointment on the expiration of his term?
2000.answer: No, a person who holds office as a member of a Public Service Commission is ineligible for reappointment on the expiration of his term.

2001.question: Can a member of a Public Service Commission be reappointed after his term expires?
2001.answer: No, a member of a Public Service Commission cannot be reappointed after his term expires.

2002.question: Who can remove the Chairman or any other member of a Public Service Commission from office?

2003.question: Who has the authority to remove the Chairman or any other member of a Public Service Commission from office?

2004.question: On what grounds can the Chairman or any other member of a Public Service Commission be removed from his office?
2004.answer: On the ground of misbehaviour after the Supreme Court has reported that the Chairman or such other member ought on any such ground to be removed.

2005.question: What should the Supreme Court report for the Chairman or any other member of a Public Service Commission to be removed from his office?
2005.answer: The Supreme Court should report that the Chairman or such other member ought to be removed on the ground of misbehaviour.

2006.question: Who can suspend from office the Chairman or any other member of the Commission?
2006.answer: The President, in the case of the Union Commission or a Joint Commission, and the Governor in the case of a State Commission

2007.question: Who has the authority to suspend the Chairman or any other member of the Union Commission or a Joint Commission, and who has the authority in the case of a State Commission?
2007.answer: The President has the authority to suspend the Chairman or any other member of the Union Commission or a Joint Commission, and the Governor has the authority in the case of a State Commission

2008.question: Under what circumstances can the President remove from office the Chairman or any other member of a Public Service Commission, disregarding clause (1)?
2008.answer: If the Chairman or such other member is adjudged an insolvent, engages during his term of office in any paid employment outside the duties of his office, or is, in the opinion of the President, unfit to continue in office by reason of infirmity of mind or body.

2009.question: What are the reasons for which the President can remove the Chairman or any other member of a Public Service Commission, disregarding clause (1)?
2009.answer: The President can remove the Chairman or such other member if they are adjudged an insolvent, if they engage during their term of office in any paid employment outside the duties of their office, or if they are, in the opinion of the President, unfit to continue in office by reason of infirmity of mind or body.

2010.question: What is considered misbehaviour for the purposes of clause (1) if the Chairman or any other member of a Public Service Commission is concerned or interested in any contract or agreement made by or on behalf of the Government of India or the Government of a State?
2010.answer: If he participates in any way in the profit thereof or in any benefit or emolument arising therefrom otherwise than as a member and in common with the other members of an incorporated company, he is deemed to be guilty of misbehaviour.

2011.question: What actions by the Chairman or any other member of a Public Service Commission related to a contract or agreement made by or on behalf of the Government of India or the Government of a State are deemed as misbehaviour?
2011.answer: If he participates in any way in the profit thereof or in any benefit or emolument arising therefrom otherwise than as a member and in common with the other members of an incorporated company, he is deemed to be guilty of misbehaviour.

2012.question: Who can determine the number of members and their conditions of service in a Union Commission?

2013.question: Who has the power to determine the number of members and their conditions of service in a Union Commission?

2014.question: Who can set the conditions of service for a State Commission?

2015.question: Who has the authority to set the conditions of service for a State Commission?

2016.question: What happens to the conditions of service of a member of a Public Service Commission after his appointment?
2016.answer: The conditions of service of a member of a Public Service Commission shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.

2017.question: Can the conditions of service of a member of a Public Service Commission be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment?
2017.answer: No, the conditions of service of a member of a Public Service Commission shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.

2018.question: What happens to the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission after ceasing to hold office?
2018.answer: The Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission shall be ineligible for further employment either under the Government of India or under the Government of a State.

2019.question: Who becomes ineligible for further employment either under the Government of India or under the Government of a State after their term ends?
2019.answer: The Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission becomes ineligible for further employment either under the Government of India or under the Government of a State after their term ends.

2020.question: What are the possible appointments for the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission after ceasing to hold office?
2020.answer: The Chairman of a State Public Service Commission shall be eligible for appointment as the Chairman or any other member of the Union Public Service Commission or as the Chairman of any other State Public Service Commission, but not for any other employment either under the Government of India or under the Government of a State.

2021.question: Can the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission be employed under the Government of India or under the Government of a State after ceasing to hold office?
2021.answer: No, the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission is not eligible for any other employment either under the Government of India or under the Government of a State after ceasing to hold office. They are only eligible for appointment as the Chairman or any other member of the Union Public Service Commission or as the Chairman of any other State Public Service Commission.

2022.question: What are the possible appointments for a member other than the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission after ceasing to hold office?
2022.answer: A member other than the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission shall be eligible for appointment as the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission or as the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission, but not for any other employment either under the Government of India or under the Government of a State.

2023.question: What roles can a member, other than the Chairman, of the Union Public Service Commission be appointed to after they cease to hold their office?
2023.answer: After ceasing to hold office, a member other than the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission is eligible to be appointed as the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission or as the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission. However, they are not eligible for any other employment either under the Government of India or under the Government of a State.

2024.question: What are the possible appointments for a member other than the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission after ceasing to hold office?
2024.answer: A member other than the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission shall be eligible for appointment as the Chairman or any other member of the Union Public Service Commission or as the Chairman of that or any other State Public Service Commission, but not for any other employment either under the Government of India or under the Government of a State.

2025.question: Can a member other than the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission be appointed as the Chairman or any other member of the Union Public Service Commission or as the Chairman of that or any other State Public Service Commission after he/she ceases to hold office?
2025.answer: Yes, a member other than the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission is eligible for such appointments after ceasing to hold office.

2026.question: Who conducts examinations for appointments to the services of the Union and the State?
