2355.question: What happens to a Proclamation that has been approved by the Council of States, but not by the House of the People within the two month period, if the House of the People is dissolved and then reconstituted?
2355.answer: The Proclamation ceases to operate at the expiration of thirty days from the date the House of the People first sits after its reconstitution, unless the Proclamation is approved by the House of the People within that period.

2356.question: When does a Proclamation cease to operate if it is approved?
2356.answer: A Proclamation that is approved ceases to operate on the expiration of a period of six months from the date of issue of the Proclamation, unless it is revoked or a resolution approving its continuance is passed by both Houses of Parliament.

2357.question: What happens to an approved Proclamation after six months from the date of issue, unless it is revoked or a resolution approving its continuance is passed by both Houses of Parliament?
2357.answer: An approved Proclamation ceases to operate.

2358.question: What is the maximum duration a Proclamation can remain in force?
2358.answer: No Proclamation can remain in force for more than three years.

2359.question: For how long can a Proclamation remain in force at most?
2359.answer: A Proclamation can remain in force for no more than three years.

2360.question: What happens if a resolution for the continuance of a Proclamation is not passed by the House of the People?
2360.answer: The Proclamation shall cease to operate at the expiration of thirty days from the date on which the House of the People first sits after its reconstitution.

2361.question: When does the Proclamation cease to operate if a resolution for its continuance is not passed by the House of the People after its reconstitution?
2361.answer: The Proclamation shall cease to operate at the expiration of thirty days from the date on which the House of the People first sits after its reconstitution.

2362.question: What is the exception for the Proclamation issued on the 11th day of May, 1987 with respect to the State of Punjab?
2362.answer: The reference in the first proviso to 'three years' shall be construed as a reference to five years.

2363.question: How is 'three years' in the first proviso of the Proclamation issued on the 11th day of May, 1987 with respect to the State of Punjab to be construed?
2363.answer: The reference in the first proviso to 'three years' shall be construed as a reference to five years.

2364.question: Under what conditions can a resolution for the continuance in force of a Proclamation be passed for any period beyond the expiration of one year?
2364.answer: A resolution can be passed if a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, in the whole of India or, as the case may be, in the whole or any part of the State, at the time of the passing of such resolution, and the Election Commission certifies that the continuance in force of the Proclamation approved under clause (3) during the period specified in such resolution is necessary on account of difficulties in holding general elections to the Legislative Assembly of the State concerned.

2365.question: What is required for a resolution to be passed for the continuance in force of a Proclamation beyond the expiration of one year, particularly in relation to the operation of a Proclamation of Emergency and the certification from the Election Commission?
2365.answer: For a resolution to be passed for the continuance in force of a Proclamation beyond the expiration of one year, a Proclamation of Emergency must be in operation in the whole of India or, as the case may be, in the whole or any part of the State at the time of the passing of such resolution. Additionally, the Election Commission must certify that the continuance in force of the Proclamation approved under clause (3) during the period specified in such resolution is necessary due to difficulties in holding general elections to the Legislative Assembly of the State concerned.

2366.question: Does clause (5) apply to the Proclamation issued on the 11th day of May, 1987 with respect to the State of Punjab?
2366.answer: No, nothing in this clause shall apply to the Proclamation issued on the 11th day of May, 1987 with respect to the State of Punjab.

2367.question: Does anything in clause (5) apply to the Proclamation issued on the 11th day of May, 1987 with respect to the State of Punjab?

2368.question: Who can the Parliament confer the power of the Legislature of the State to make laws to?
2368.answer: The Parliament can confer this power to the President.

2369.question: Who can the Parliament confer the power to make laws for the Legislature of the State?

2370.question: Can the President delegate the power conferred to him?
2370.answer: Yes, the President can delegate the power conferred to him, subject to such conditions as he may think fit to impose.

2371.question: Is it possible for the President to impose conditions on the power he delegates?
2371.answer: Yes, the President can impose such conditions as he may think fit on the power he delegates.

2372.question: Who can the President specify to have the delegated power?
2372.answer: The President can specify any other authority to have the delegated power.

2373.question: Who can have the delegated power as specified by the President?
2373.answer: Any other authority can have the delegated power as specified by the President.

2374.question: What can the President authorize when the House of the People is not in session?
2374.answer: The President can authorize expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of the State pending the sanction of such expenditure by Parliament.

2375.question: From where can the President authorize expenditure when the House of the People is not in session, pending the sanction of such expenditure by Parliament?
2375.answer: The President can authorize expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of the State.

2376.question: What happens to a law made in exercise of the power of the Legislature of the State by Parliament or the President or other authority after the Proclamation has ceased to operate?
2376.answer: The law continues in force until altered or repealed or amended by a competent Legislature or other authority.

2377.question: What is the status of a law made by the Legislature of the State, Parliament, President, or other authority after the Proclamation has ceased to operate, and until it is altered, repealed, or amended by a competent authority?

2378.question: What does article 358 state?
2378.answer: Article 358 states that during emergencies when a Proclamation of Emergency declaring that the security of India or any part of the territory thereof is threatened by war or by external aggression is in operation, nothing in article 19 shall restrict the power of the State to make any law or to take any executive action. Any law so made shall cease to have effect as soon as the Proclamation ceases to operate.

2379.question: What happens to laws made under the provisions of Article 358 when the Proclamation of Emergency ceases to operate?
2379.answer: Any law made under the provisions of Article 358 shall cease to have effect as soon as the Proclamation of Emergency ceases to operate.

2380.question: What happens when a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation?
2380.answer: When a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, any law may be made, or any executive action may be taken, under this article in relation to or in any State or Union territory in which or in any part of which the Proclamation of Emergency is not in operation, if and in so far as the security of India or any part of the territory thereof is threatened by activities in or in relation to the part of the territory of India in which the Proclamation of Emergency is in operation.

2381.question: What actions can be taken under the article when a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, and where can these actions be taken?
2381.answer: When a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, any law may be made, or any executive action may be taken, under this article in relation to or in any State or Union territory in which or in any part of which the Proclamation of Emergency is not in operation, if and in so far as the security of India or any part of the territory thereof is threatened by activities in or in relation to the part of the territory of India in which the Proclamation of Emergency is in operation.

2382.question: What does not apply according to clause 1?
2382.answer: Clause 1 does not apply to any law which does not contain a recital to the effect that such law is in relation to the Proclamation of Emergency in operation when it is made; or to any executive action taken otherwise than under a law containing such a recital.

2383.question: To what does Clause 1 not apply?
2383.answer: Clause 1 does not apply to any law which does not contain a recital to the effect that such law is in relation to the Proclamation of Emergency in operation when it is made; or to any executive action taken otherwise than under a law containing such a recital.

2384.question: What can the President do during the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III during emergencies?
2384.answer: During the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III during emergencies, the President may declare that the right to move any court for the enforcement of such of the rights as may be mentioned in the order and all proceedings pending in any court for the enforcement of the rights so mentioned shall remain suspended for the period during which the Proclamation is in force or for such shorter period as may be specified in the order.

2385.question: What power does the President have regarding the enforcement of rights mentioned in the order and all proceedings pending in any court during the period during which the Proclamation is in force or for such shorter period as may be specified in the order?
2385.answer: During the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III during emergencies, the President can declare that the right to move any court for the enforcement of such of the rights as may be mentioned in the order and all proceedings pending in any court for the enforcement of the rights so mentioned shall remain suspended.

2386.question: What happens while an order made under clause 1 mentioning any of the rights conferred by Part III is in operation?
2386.answer: While an order made under clause 1 mentioning any of the rights conferred by Part III is in operation, nothing in that Part conferring those rights shall restrict the power of the State as defined in the said Part to make any law or to take any executive action which the State would but for the provisions contained in that Part be competent to make or to take, but any law so made shall, to the extent of the incompetency, cease to have effect.

2387.question: What happens when the State, as mentioned in Part III, makes a law or takes an executive action under the operation of an order made under clause 1, which mentions any of the rights conferred by Part III?
2387.answer: While an order made under clause 1 mentioning any of the rights conferred by Part III is in operation, nothing in that Part conferring those rights shall restrict the power of the State as defined in the said Part to make any law or to take any executive action which the State would but for the provisions contained in that Part be competent to make or to take, but any law so made shall, to the extent of the incompetency, cease to have effect.

2388.question: What happens when the order ceases to operate?
2388.answer: Except as respects things done or omitted to be done before the law so ceases to have effect.

2389.question: What is the consequence of things done or omitted to be done before a law ceases to have effect?
2389.answer: When the order ceases to operate, those things are excepted.

2390.question: What is the condition for a law to be made or any executive action to be taken under this article?
2390.answer: It can be made if and in so far as the security of India or any part of the territory thereof is threatened by activities in or in relation to the part of the territory of India in which the Proclamation of Emergency is in operation.

2391.question: Under what circumstances can a law be made or an executive action be taken when the Proclamation of Emergency is in operation in a part of the territory of India?
2391.answer: A law can be made or an executive action can be taken if and in so far as the security of India or any part of the territory thereof is threatened by activities in or in relation to the part of the territory of India where the Proclamation of Emergency is in operation.

2392.question: What does clause (1A) not apply to?
2392.answer: It does not apply to any law which does not contain a recital to the effect that such law is in relation to the Proclamation of Emergency in operation when it is made; or to any executive action taken otherwise than under a law containing such a recital.

2393.question: What are the conditions under which clause (1A) does not apply?
2393.answer: Clause (1A) does not apply to any law which does not contain a recital to the effect that such law is in relation to the Proclamation of Emergency in operation when it is made; or to any executive action taken otherwise than under a law containing such a recital.

2394.question: To what extent can an order extend?
2394.answer: An order may extend to the whole or any part of the territory of India.

2395.question: Where may an order extend in India?
2395.answer: An order may extend to the whole or any part of the territory of India.

2396.question: What does the President consider for extending the order?
2396.answer: The President considers such extension to be necessary if the security of India or any part of the territory thereof is threatened by activities in or in relation to the part of the territory of India in which the Proclamation of Emergency is in operation.

2397.question: Under what circumstances does the President find it necessary to extend the Proclamation of Emergency?
2397.answer: The President considers such extension to be necessary if the security of India or any part of the territory thereof is threatened by activities in or in relation to the part of the territory of India in which the Proclamation of Emergency is in operation.

2398.question: What is the requirement for every order made under clause (1)?
2398.answer: Every order made under clause (1) shall, as soon as may be after it is made, be laid before each House of Parliament.

2399.question: Where should every order made under clause (1) be laid as soon as it is made?
2399.answer: Every order made under clause (1) should be laid before each House of Parliament.

2400.question: What is mentioned about the application of this Part to the State of Punjab?
2400.answer: It was repealed by the Constitution (Sixty-third Amendment) Act, 1989, s. 3 (w.e.f. 6-1-1990).

2401.question: Which Act repealed the application of this Part to the State of Punjab and when did it come into effect?
2401.answer: The Constitution (Sixty-third Amendment) Act, 1989, s. 3 repealed it, coming into effect on 6-1-1990.

2402.question: Under what condition can a financial emergency be proclaimed?
2402.answer: If the President is satisfied that a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or credit of India or any part of the territory thereof is threatened.

2403.question: What does it mean when the President is satisfied that a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or credit of India or any part of the territory thereof is threatened?
2403.answer: It means a financial emergency can be proclaimed.

2404.question: Who can issue a Proclamation according to clause (1)?

2405.question: According to clause (1), who has the authority to issue a Proclamation?

2406.question: How can a Proclamation issued under clause (1) be revoked or altered?

2407.question: What is the method to revoke or alter a Proclamation issued under clause (1)?

2408.question: What happens to a Proclamation if it has not been approved by resolutions of both Houses of Parliament within two months?

2409.question: What occurs if a Proclamation has not been approved by resolutions of both Houses of Parliament within two months?

2410.question: What happens to a Proclamation issued when the House of the People has been dissolved or the dissolution of the House of the People takes place during the period of two months?
2410.answer: The Proclamation shall cease to operate at the expiration of thirty days from the date on which the House of the People first sits after its reconstitution unless a resolution approving the Proclamation has been also passed by the House of the People.

2411.question: When does a Proclamation cease to operate if the House of the People has been dissolved and then reconstituted?
2411.answer: The Proclamation shall cease to operate at the expiration of thirty days from the date on which the House of the People first sits after its reconstitution unless a resolution approving the Proclamation has been also passed by the House of the People.

2412.question: During the period any such Proclamation as is mentioned in clause (1) is in operation, who has the executive authority?

2413.question: Who has the executive authority during the period any Proclamation as mentioned in clause (1) is in operation?

2414.question: What type of directions can the Union give to any State during the operation of a Proclamation?
2414.answer: Directions to observe such canons of financial propriety as may be specified in the directions, and to the giving of such other directions as the President may deem necessary and adequate for the purpose.

2415.question: What does the President specify in the directions given to a State during the operation of a Proclamation by the Union?
2415.answer: The President specifies the observance of certain canons of financial propriety and any other directions deemed necessary and adequate for the purpose.

2416.question: What provisions can be included in the directions given by the Union to a State during the operation of a Proclamation?
2416.answer: A provision requiring the reduction of salaries and allowances of all or any class of persons serving in connection with the affairs of a State, and a provision requiring all Money Bills or other Bills to be reserved for the consideration of the President.

2417.question: What does the provision requiring the reduction of salaries and allowances of all or any class of persons serving in connection with the affairs of a State, and the provision requiring all Money Bills or other Bills to be reserved for the consideration of the President pertain to in the Indian constitution?
2417.answer: These provisions can be included in the directions given by the Union to a State during the operation of a Proclamation.

2418.question: Who can issue directions for the reduction of salaries and allowances during the period any Proclamation is in operation?

2419.question: Who has the authority to issue directions for the reduction of salaries and allowances during the period any Proclamation is in operation?

2420.question: Who shall not be answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his office?
2420.answer: The President, or the Governor or Rajpramukh of a State

2421.question: What is the immunity provided to the President, or the Governor or Rajpramukh of a State in relation to the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of their office?
2421.answer: They shall not be answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of their office

2422.question: Can the conduct of the President be brought under review by any court, tribunal or body?
2422.answer: Yes, the conduct of the President may be brought under review by any court, tribunal or body appointed or designated by either House of Parliament for the investigation of a charge under article 61.

2423.question: Who has the authority to appoint or designate a court, tribunal, or body to review the conduct of the President under Article 61?
2423.answer: Either House of Parliament has the authority to appoint or designate a court, tribunal, or body to review the conduct of the President under Article 61.

2424.question: Can criminal proceedings be instituted or continued against the President, or the Governor of a State, during their term of office?

2425.question: Is it possible to institute or continue criminal proceedings against the President, or the Governor of a State, during their term of office?

2426.question: Can civil proceedings be instituted during the President's or Governor's term of office in any court in respect of any act done by him in his personal capacity?
2426.answer: No, not until the expiration of two months next after notice in writing has been delivered to the President or the Governor, or left at his office stating the nature of the proceedings.

2427.question: When can civil proceedings be instituted against the President or Governor in respect of any act done by him in his personal capacity?
2427.answer: Civil proceedings can be instituted after the expiration of two months next after notice in writing has been delivered to the President or the Governor, or left at his office stating the nature of the proceedings.

2428.question: Can the President or the Governor of a State be arrested or imprisoned during his term of office?

2429.question: Is it possible for the President or the Governor of a State to be arrested or imprisoned during their term of office?

2430.question: What is the protection for publication of proceedings of Parliament and State Legislatures?
2430.answer: No person shall be liable to any proceedings, civil or criminal, in any court in respect of the publication in a newspaper of a substantially true report of any proceedings of either House of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly, or, as the case may be, either House of the Legislature, of a State, unless the publication is proved to have been made with malice.

2431.question: What happens if a person publishes a substantially true report of any proceedings of the Parliament or the State Legislature in a newspaper without malice?
2431.answer: No person shall be liable to any proceedings, civil or criminal, in any court in respect of the publication in a newspaper of a substantially true report of any proceedings of either House of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly, or, as the case may be, either House of the Legislature, of a State, unless the publication is proved to have been made with malice.

2432.question: Does the protection for publication of proceedings apply to reports broadcast by wireless telegraphy?
2432.answer: Yes, clause (1) shall apply in relation to reports or matters broadcast by means of wireless telegraphy as part of any programme or service provided by means of a broadcasting station.

2433.question: Does clause (1) apply to reports or matters broadcast by wireless telegraphy as part of any programme or service provided by a broadcasting station?
2433.answer: Yes, the protection for publication of proceedings does apply to these reports broadcast by wireless telegraphy.

2434.question: Does the protection for publication of proceedings apply to secret sittings of the House of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly?
2434.answer: No, the protection does not apply to the publication of any report of the proceedings of a secret sitting of either House of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly.

2435.question: Does the protection apply to the publication of any report of the proceedings of a secret sitting of either House of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly?
2435.answer: No, the protection does not apply.

2436.question: What does 'newspaper' include in this context?
2436.answer: In this article, 'newspaper' includes a news agency report containing material for publication in a newspaper.

2437.question: What is the meaning of 'newspaper' in the context of this article?
2437.answer: 'Newspaper' in the context of this article refers to a news agency report containing material for publication in a newspaper.

2438.question: What is the disqualification for appointment on remunerative political post?
2438.answer: A member of a House belonging to any political party who is disqualified for being a member of the House under paragraph 2 of the Tenth Schedule shall also be disqualified to hold any remunerative political post for duration of the period commencing from the date of his disqualification till the date on which the term of his office as such member would expire or till the date on which he contests an election to a House and is declared elected, whichever is earlier.

2439.question: What happens to a member of a House belonging to any political party who is disqualified for being a member of the House under paragraph 2 of the Tenth Schedule?
2439.answer: That member is also disqualified to hold any remunerative political post for duration of the period commencing from the date of his disqualification till the date on which the term of his office as such member would expire or till the date on which he contests an election to a House and is declared elected, whichever is earlier.

2440.question: What is the meaning of 'House' for the purposes of the article on disqualification for appointment on remunerative political post?
2440.answer: The expression 'House' has the meaning assigned to it in clause (a) of paragraph 1 of the Tenth Schedule.

2441.question: Where is the meaning of the term 'House' for the article on disqualification for appointment on remunerative political post assigned?
2441.answer: The meaning of 'House' is assigned in clause (a) of paragraph 1 of the Tenth Schedule.

2442.question: What does the expression 'remunerative political post' refer to?
2442.answer: A 'remunerative political post' refers to any office under the Government of India or the Government of a State where the salary or remuneration for such office is paid out of the public revenue of the Government of India or the Government of the State. It can also refer to an office under a body, whether incorporated or not, which is wholly or partially owned by the Government of India or the Government of State, and the salary or remuneration for such office is paid by such body. This does not apply if the salary or remuneration paid is compensatory in nature.

2443.question: What types of offices can be considered as 'remunerative political posts' and under what conditions are they not considered as such?
2443.answer: 'Remunerative political post' can be any office under the Government of India or the Government of a State where the salary or remuneration for such office is paid out of the public revenue of the Government of India or the Government of the State. It can also be an office under a body, whether incorporated or not, which is wholly or partially owned by the Government of India or the Government of State, and the salary or remuneration for such office is paid by such body. However, this does not apply if the salary or remuneration paid is compensatory in nature.

2444.question: What is the implication of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, s. 2 on the rights and privileges of Rulers of Indian States?
2444.answer: The Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, s. 2 has repealed the rights and privileges of Rulers of Indian States.

2445.question: What has the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, s. 2 done to the rights and privileges of Rulers of Indian States?
2445.answer: The Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, s. 2 has repealed the rights and privileges of Rulers of Indian States.

2446.question: What is the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court or any other court in relation to disputes arising out of certain treaties, agreements, etc.?
2446.answer: Neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall have jurisdiction in any dispute arising out of any provision of a treaty, agreement, covenant, engagement, sanad or other similar instrument which was entered into or executed before the commencement of the Constitution by any Ruler of an Indian State and to which the Government of the Dominion of India or any of its predecessor Governments was a party and which has or has been continued in operation after such commencement.

2447.question: Who has jurisdiction over disputes arising from provisions of a treaty, agreement, covenant, engagement, sanad, or similar instrument entered into or executed before the commencement of the Constitution by a Ruler of an Indian State to which the Government of the Dominion of India or any of its predecessor Governments was a party and which has or has been continued in operation after such commencement?
2447.answer: Neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall have jurisdiction in any such dispute.

2448.question: What does 'Indian State' mean in the context of the Constitution?
2448.answer: 'Indian State' refers to any territory recognised before the commencement of the Constitution by His Majesty or the Government of the Dominion of India as being such a State.

2449.question: What does a territory recognised before the commencement of the Constitution by His Majesty or the Government of the Dominion of India as being such a State refer to?
2449.answer: This refers to the 'Indian State' in the context of the Constitution.

2450.question: Who is included in the term 'Ruler' as per the Constitution?
2450.answer: 'Ruler' includes the Prince, Chief or other person recognised before the commencement of the Constitution by His Majesty or the Government of the Dominion of India.

2451.question: Who were the Prince, Chief or other person recognized by His Majesty or the Government of the Dominion of India before the commencement of the Constitution referred to as?
2451.answer: They were referred to as 'Ruler' as per the Constitution.

2452.question: What happens to the recognition of the Rulers of Indian States according to section 363A?
2452.answer: According to section 363A, the Prince, Chief or other person who was recognized by the President as the Ruler of an Indian State before the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, ceases to be recognized as such Ruler or the successor of such Ruler from such commencement.

2453.question: Who ceases to be recognized as the Ruler of an Indian State from the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971 according to section 363A?
2453.answer: The Prince, Chief or other person who was recognized by the President as the Ruler of an Indian State before the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, ceases to be recognized as such Ruler or the successor of such Ruler from such commencement.

2454.question: What changes were made to the privy purses as per the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971?
2454.answer: With the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, privy purse was abolished. All rights, liabilities and obligations in respect of privy purse were extinguished. The Ruler or, as the case may be, the successor of such Ruler, or any other person shall not be paid any sum as privy purse.

2455.question: What happened to the privy purse after the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971?
2455.answer: The privy purse was abolished after the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971. All rights, liabilities and obligations in respect of privy purse were extinguished. No sum as privy purse was to be paid to the Ruler, their successor, or any other person.

2456.question: What powers does the President have regarding major ports and aerodromes according to section 364 of the Indian Constitution?
2456.answer: According to section 364, the President may direct that any law made by Parliament or by the Legislature of a State shall not apply to any major port or aerodrome or shall apply thereto subject to exceptions or modifications. The President may also direct that any existing law shall cease to have effect in any major port or aerodrome except as respects things done or omitted to be done before the said date.

2457.question: What does section 364 of the Indian Constitution state about the President's ability to direct the application of laws to major ports and aerodromes?
2457.answer: Section 364 of the Indian Constitution states that the President may direct that any law made by Parliament or by the Legislature of a State shall not apply to any major port or aerodrome or shall apply thereto subject to exceptions or modifications. Additionally, the President may direct that any existing law shall cease to have effect in any major port or aerodrome except as respects things done or omitted to be done before the said date.

2458.question: What is the definition of a 'major port' according to section 364 of the Indian Constitution?
2458.answer: As per section 364 of the Indian Constitution, a 'major port' means a port declared to be a major port by or under any law made by Parliament or any existing law and includes all areas for the time being included within the same.

2459.question: According to the Indian Constitution, what criteria does a port need to meet to be declared a 'major port' under section 364?
2459.answer: To be declared a 'major port' under section 364 of the Indian Constitution, a port must be declared to be a major port by or under any law made by Parliament or any existing law and should include all areas for the time being included within the same.

2460.question: What is the definition of 'aerodrome' in this context?
2460.answer: Aerodrome is defined for the purposes of the enactments relating to airways, aircraft and air navigation.

2461.question: For what purposes is 'aerodrome' defined in the context of airways, aircraft and air navigation?
2461.answer: Aerodrome is defined for the purposes of the enactments relating to airways, aircraft and air navigation.

2462.question: What does 'agricultural income' mean in this constitution?
2462.answer: Agricultural income means agricultural income as defined for the purposes of the enactments relating to Indian income-tax.

2463.question: In which enactments is the definition of 'agricultural income' used for the purposes of this constitution?
2463.answer: The definition of 'agricultural income' is used in the enactments relating to Indian income-tax.

2464.question: Who is referred to as 'an Anglo-Indian' in this constitution?
2464.answer: An Anglo-Indian means a person whose father or any of whose other male progenitors in the male line is or was of European descent but who is domiciled within the territory of India and is or was born within such territory of parents habitually resident therein and not established there for temporary purposes only.

2465.question: What does it mean to be a person whose father or any of whose other male progenitors in the male line is or was of European descent but who is domiciled within the territory of India and is or was born within such territory of parents habitually resident therein and not established there for temporary purposes only?
2465.answer: This describes 'an Anglo-Indian' in the constitution.

2466.question: What is the definition of 'article' in this context?
2466.answer: Article means an article of this Constitution.

2467.question: In what context does 'article' refer to an article of the Constitution?
2467.answer: The term 'article' refers to an article of the Constitution in this context.

2468.question: What is the meaning of 'borrow' in this context?
2468.answer: Borrow includes the raising of money by the grant of annuities, and 'loan' shall be construed accordingly.

2469.question: What does the term 'borrow' include in the context of finance and how should 'loan' be construed?
2469.answer: Borrow includes the raising of money by the grant of annuities, and 'loan' shall be construed accordingly.

2470.question: What does 'clause' mean in this constitution?
2470.answer: Clause means a clause of the article in which the expression occurs.

2471.question: In the context of a constitution, where does the expression 'clause' occur?
2471.answer: The expression 'clause' occurs in a clause of the article.

2472.question: What does 'corporation tax' mean in this constitution?
2472.answer: Corporation tax means any tax on income, so far as that tax is payable by companies and is a tax in the case of which the following conditions are fulfilled: it is not chargeable in respect of agricultural income; no deduction in respect of the tax paid by companies is, by any enactments which may apply to the tax, authorised to be made from dividends payable by the companies to individuals; and no provision exists for taking the tax.

2473.question: In this constitution, which tax that is payable by companies, is not chargeable in respect of agricultural income, has no deduction authorized from dividends payable to the companies to individuals, and has no provision for taking the tax?

2474.question: What is the meaning of 'corresponding Province', 'corresponding Indian State' or 'corresponding State'?
2474.answer: In cases of doubt such Province, Indian State or State as may be determined by the President to be the corresponding Province, the corresponding Indian State or the corresponding State, as the case may be, for the particular purpose in question

2475.question: Who determines what is the 'corresponding Province', 'corresponding Indian State' or 'corresponding State' in cases of doubt?
2475.answer: The President determines what is the 'corresponding Province', 'corresponding Indian State' or 'corresponding State' in cases of doubt.

2476.question: What is included in the term 'debt'?
2476.answer: Any liability in respect of any obligation to repay capital sums by way of annuities and any liability under any guarantee

2477.question: What does a liability in respect of any obligation to repay capital sums by way of annuities and any liability under any guarantee refer to?

2478.question: What does 'estate duty' refer to?
2478.answer: A duty to be assessed on or by reference to the principal value, ascertained in accordance with such rules as may be prescribed by or under laws made by Parliament or the Legislature of a State relating to the duty, of all property passing upon death or deemed, under the provisions of the said laws, so to pass

2479.question: What is the duty assessed on or by reference to the principal value of all property passing upon death or deemed to pass under the provisions of laws made by Parliament or the Legislature of a State?
2479.answer: This is referred to as 'estate duty'.

2480.question: What is the definition of 'existing law'?
2480.answer: Any law, Ordinance, order, bye-law, rule or regulation passed or made before the commencement of this Constitution by any Legislature, authority or person having power to make such a law, Ordinance, order, bye-law, rule or regulation

2481.question: What entities can pass or make an 'existing law' before the commencement of a Constitution?
2481.answer: Any Legislature, authority or person having power to make such a law, Ordinance, order, bye-law, rule or regulation

2482.question: What does the term 'Federal Court' refer to?
2482.answer: The Federal Court constituted under the Government of India Act, 1935

2483.question: Under which act was the Federal Court constituted?
2483.answer: The Federal Court was constituted under the Government of India Act, 1935

2484.question: What is included in the term 'goods'?

2485.question: What does the term for 'all materials, commodities, and articles' refer to?
2485.answer: The term for 'all materials, commodities, and articles' refers to 'goods'.

2486.question: What is 'goods and services tax'?
2486.answer: Any tax on supply of goods, or services or both except taxes on the supply of the alcoholic liquor for human consumption

2487.question: What is a tax on the supply of goods, or services or both except taxes on the supply of the alcoholic liquor for human consumption called?

2488.question: What does 'guarantee' include?
2488.answer: Any obligation undertaken before the commencement of this Constitution to make payments in the event of the profits of an undertaking falling short of a specified amount

2489.question: What term refers to any obligation undertaken before the commencement of a constitution to make payments in the event of the profits of an undertaking falling short of a specified amount?

2490.question: What does 'High Court' refer to?
2490.answer: Any Court which is deemed for the purposes of this Constitution to be a High Court

2491.question: What is a court that is deemed for the purposes of a Constitution referred to as?

2492.question: What is the definition of a 'High Court' in this context?
2492.answer: A 'High Court' refers to any Court in the territory of India constituted or reconstituted under this Constitution as a High Court, and any other Court in the territory of India which may be declared by Parliament by law to be a High Court for all or any of the purposes of this Constitution.

2493.question: Which courts are referred to as 'High Courts' under the Indian Constitution?
2493.answer: A 'High Court' refers to any Court in the territory of India constituted or reconstituted under this Constitution as a High Court, and any other Court in the territory of India which may be declared by Parliament by law to be a High Court for all or any of the purposes of this Constitution.

2494.question: What does 'Indian State' mean?
2494.answer: An 'Indian State' means any territory which the Government of the Dominion of India recognised as such a State.

2495.question: Which entity recognises a territory as an 'Indian State'?
2495.answer: The Government of the Dominion of India recognises a territory as an 'Indian State'.

2496.question: What does 'Part' refer to?
2496.answer: A 'Part' refers to a Part of this Constitution.

2497.question: What is a 'Part' in the context of the Constitution?
2497.answer: A 'Part' refers to a Part of this Constitution.

2498.question: What is the definition of a 'pension' in this context?
2498.answer: A 'pension' means a pension, whether contributory or not, of any kind whatsoever payable to or in respect of any person, and includes retired pay so payable; a gratuity so payable and any sum or sums so payable by way of the return, with or without interest thereon or any other addition thereto, of subscriptions to a provident fund.

2499.question: What does a 'pension' include, whether it's contributory or not?
2499.answer: A 'pension' includes any kind of pension payable to or in respect of any person, retired pay so payable, a gratuity so payable, and any sum or sums payable by way of the return, with or without interest thereon or any other addition thereto, of subscriptions to a provident fund.

2500.question: What does 'Proclamation of Emergency' refer to?
2500.answer: A 'Proclamation of Emergency' refers to a Proclamation issued under clause (1) of article 352.

2501.question: Under which clause and article is a 'Proclamation of Emergency' issued?
2501.answer: A 'Proclamation of Emergency' is issued under clause (1) of article 352.

2502.question: What is a 'public notification'?
2502.answer: A 'public notification' means a notification in the Gazette of India, or, as the case may be, the Official Gazette of a State.

2503.question: What does it mean when a notification is in the Gazette of India or the Official Gazette of a State?
2503.answer: When a notification is in the Gazette of India or the Official Gazette of a State, it is referred to as a 'public notification'.

2504.question: What is the definition of a 'railway'?
2504.answer: A 'railway' does not include a tramway wholly within a municipal area, or any other line of communication wholly situate in one State and declared by Parliament by law not to be a railway.

2505.question: What does the term 'railway' not include according to Parliament law?
2505.answer: A 'railway' does not include a tramway wholly within a municipal area, or any other line of communication wholly situate in one State and declared by Parliament by law not to be a railway.

2506.question: What does 'Ruler' mean in this context?
2506.answer: A 'Ruler' means the Prince, Chief or other person who, at any time before the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, was recognised by the President as the Ruler of an Indian State or any person who, at any time before such commencement, was recognised by the President as the successor of such Ruler.

2507.question: Who is recognized by the President as the Ruler of an Indian State before the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971?
2507.answer: The Prince, Chief or other person who, at any time before the commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, was recognised by the President as the Ruler of an Indian State is referred to as 'Ruler' in this context.

2508.question: What does 'Schedule' mean?
2508.answer: A 'Schedule' means a Schedule to this Constitution.

2509.question: What does a Schedule to this Constitution refer to?
2509.answer: A Schedule to this Constitution refers to a 'Schedule'.

2510.question: What are 'Scheduled Castes'?
2510.answer: Scheduled Castes' means such castes, races or tribes or parts of or groups within such castes, races or tribes as are deemed under article 341 to be Scheduled Castes for the purposes of this Constitution.

2511.question: Which article deems certain castes, races or tribes or parts of or groups within such castes, races or tribes to be Scheduled Castes for the purposes of the Constitution?

2512.question: What are 'Scheduled Tribes'?
2512.answer: Scheduled Tribes' means such tribes or tribal communities or parts of or groups within such tribes or tribal communities.

2513.question: What is the term for such tribes or tribal communities or parts of or groups within such tribes or tribal communities?
2513.answer: The term for such tribes or tribal communities or parts of or groups within such tribes or tribal communities is 'Scheduled Tribes'.

2514.question: What does the term 'Scheduled Tribes' refer to as per article 342 of the constitution?
2514.answer: Scheduled Tribes are those that are deemed under article 342 for the purposes of the Constitution.

2515.question: Under which article of the Constitution are the Scheduled Tribes deemed for its purposes?
2515.answer: The Scheduled Tribes are deemed under article 342 of the Constitution for its purposes.

2516.question: What does 'securities' include according to the constitutional definition?

2517.question: What is included in the term 'securities' according to the constitutional definition?
2517.answer: Stock is included in the term 'securities'.

2518.question: What is the definition of 'Services' in the constitution?

2519.question: What does the term 'Services' defined as anything other than goods refer to in a legal context?
2519.answer: In the constitution, 'Services' is defined as anything other than goods.

2520.question: What does the term 'State' refer to in articles 246A, 268, 269, 269A and article 279A?
2520.answer: 'State' with reference to these articles includes a Union territory with Legislature.

2521.question: Which territories does the term 'State' include in the context of articles 246A, 268, 269, 269A and article 279A?
2521.answer: The term 'State' includes a Union territory with Legislature.

2522.question: What does 'socially and educationally backward classes' mean as per the constitution?
2522.answer: It means such backward classes as are so deemed under article 342A for the purposes of this Constitution.

2523.question: Which article of the constitution deems certain classes as 'socially and educationally backward' for the purposes of the Constitution?
2523.answer: Article 342A of the Constitution deems certain classes as 'socially and educationally backward'.

2524.question: What is the meaning of 'sub-clause' in the constitution?
2524.answer: 'Sub-clause' means a sub-clause of the clause in which the expression occurs.

2525.question: What does 'sub-clause' refer to when used in a clause?
2525.answer: 'Sub-clause' refers to a sub-clause of the clause in which the expression occurs.

2526.question: What is included in the term 'taxation' as per the constitution?
2526.answer: 'Taxation' includes the imposition of any tax or impost, whether general or local or special, and 'tax' shall be construed accordingly.

2527.question: What does the term 'taxation' include according to its constitutional definition?
2527.answer: 'Taxation' includes the imposition of any tax or impost, whether general or local or special, and 'tax' shall be construed accordingly.

2528.question: What does 'tax on income' include?
2528.answer: 'Tax on income' includes a tax in the nature of an excess profits tax.

2529.question: What is an example of a tax that 'tax on income' might include?
2529.answer: An example of a tax that 'tax on income' might include is a tax in the nature of an excess profits tax.

2530.question: What is included in 'tax on the sale or purchase of goods'?
2530.answer: It includes a tax on the transfer of property in goods for cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration, a tax on the delivery of goods on hire-purchase or any system of payment by installments, a tax on the transfer of the right to use any goods for any purpose for cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration, a tax on the supply of goods by any unincorporated association or body of persons to a member thereof for cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration, a tax on the supply, by way of or as part of any service or in any other manner whatsoever, of goods, being food or any other article for human consumption or any drink, where such supply or service, is for cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration. Such transfer, delivery or supply of any goods shall be deemed to be a sale of those goods by the person making the transfer.

2531.question: What does the tax on the transfer of property in goods for cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration, a tax on the delivery of goods on hire-purchase or any system of payment by installments, a tax on the transfer of the right to use any goods for any purpose for cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration, a tax on the supply of goods by any unincorporated association or body of persons to a member thereof for cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration, a tax on the supply, by way of or as part of any service or in any other manner whatsoever, of goods, being food or any other article for human consumption or any drink, where such supply or service, is for cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration, refer to?
2531.answer: It refers to 'tax on the sale or purchase of goods'. Such transfer, delivery or supply of any goods shall be deemed to be a sale of those goods by the person making the transfer.

2532.question: What does 'Union territory' refer to?
2532.answer: Any Union territory specified in the First Schedule and includes any other territory comprised within the territory of India but not specified in that Schedule.

2533.question: What is included in the term 'Union territory' according to the First Schedule in the territory of India?
2533.answer: Any Union territory specified in the First Schedule and includes any other territory comprised within the territory of India but not specified in that Schedule.

2534.question: What document is used for the interpretation of the Constitution?

2535.question: What is the purpose of The General Clauses Act, 1897?
2535.answer: It is used for the interpretation of the Constitution.

2536.question: What does the term 'foreign State' refer to in the context of this Constitution?

2537.question: In the context of this Constitution, which country is not considered a 'foreign State'?

2538.question: What power does the Parliament have regarding the Constitution?
2538.answer: Parliament may in exercise of its constituent power amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of this Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in this article.

2539.question: What can the Parliament do to the Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in the Constitution's article?
2539.answer: Parliament may in exercise of its constituent power amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of this Constitution.

2540.question: How can an amendment of the Constitution be initiated?
2540.answer: An amendment of this Constitution may be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill for the purpose in either House of Parliament, and when the Bill is passed in each House by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting, it shall be presented to the President who shall give his assent.

2541.question: What happens after a Bill to amend the Constitution is passed in each House of Parliament by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting?
2541.answer: After the Bill is passed in each House of Parliament, it is presented to the President who shall give his assent.

2542.question: What happens if an amendment seeks to make changes in certain articles or chapters of the constitution?
2542.answer: The amendment requires to be ratified by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States by resolutions to that effect passed by those Legislatures before the Bill making provision for such amendment is presented to the President for assent.

2543.question: What is the process for an amendment that seeks to change certain articles or chapters of the constitution before it is presented to the President for assent?
2543.answer: The amendment requires to be ratified by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States by resolutions to that effect passed by those Legislatures.

2544.question: Does article 13 apply to any amendment made under this article?
2544.answer: No, nothing in article 13 shall apply to any amendment made under this article.

2545.question: Does anything in article 13 apply to any amendment made under the same article?
2545.answer: No, nothing in article 13 shall apply to any amendment made under this article.

2546.question: Can amendments of the Constitution be called into question in any court?
2546.answer: No, no amendment of the Constitution shall be called in question in any court on any ground.

2547.question: Is there any ground on which an amendment of the Constitution can be called into question in court?
2547.answer: No, no amendment of the Constitution shall be called in question in any court on any ground.

2548.question: Is there any limitation on the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution?
2548.answer: No, there is no limitation whatever on the constituent power of Parliament to amend by way of addition, variation or repeal the provisions of this Constitution under this article.

2549.question: Does the constituent power of Parliament to amend by way of addition, variation or repeal the provisions of the Constitution under this article have any limitations?
2549.answer: No, there is no limitation whatever on the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution.

2550.question: What was the verdict of the court in the case of Minerva Mills Ltd. and Others Vs. Union of India and Others?
2550.answer: This section has been declared invalid by the Supreme Court in Minerva Mills Ltd. and Others Vs. Union of India and Others.

2551.question: Which section was declared invalid by the Supreme Court in the case of Minerva Mills Ltd. and Others Vs. Union of India and Others?
2551.answer: The verdict of the court was that this section has been declared invalid.

2552.question: What is the temporary power given to Parliament under section 369?
2552.answer: Parliament has the temporary power to make laws with respect to certain matters in the State List as if they were matters in the Concurrent List for a period of five years from the commencement of this Constitution.

2553.question: What does the Constitution allow Parliament to do for a period of five years from its commencement, in relation to the State List and the Concurrent List?
2553.answer: Under section 369, Parliament is given the temporary power to make laws with respect to certain matters in the State List as if they were matters in the Concurrent List.

2554.question: What matters can laws be made about according to the text?
2554.answer: Trade and commerce within a State, production, supply and distribution of cotton and woollen textiles, raw cotton, cotton seed, paper, food-stuffs, cattle fodder, coal, iron, steel and mica.

2555.question: According to the text, can laws be made about the trade and commerce within a State, production, supply and distribution of cotton and woollen textiles, raw cotton, cotton seed, paper, food-stuffs, cattle fodder, coal, iron, steel and mica?
2555.answer: Yes, laws can be made about these matters.

2556.question: What does clause (b) refer to?
2556.answer: Offences against laws with respect to any of the matters mentioned in clause (a), jurisdiction and powers of all courts except the Supreme Court with respect to any of those matters, and fees in respect of any of those matters but not including fees taken in any court.

2557.question: What does the reference to 'offences against laws with respect to any of the matters mentioned in clause (a), jurisdiction and powers of all courts except the Supreme Court with respect to any of those matters, and fees in respect of any of those matters but not including fees taken in any court' correspond to in the context?

2558.question: What happens to a law made by Parliament that it would not have been competent to make without the provisions of this article?
2558.answer: It shall cease to have effect on the expiration of the said period, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before the expiration thereof.

2559.question: What happens to a law made by Parliament, which was not competent to make without the provisions of a certain article, after the expiration of the said period?
2559.answer: It shall cease to have effect, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before the expiration thereof.

2560.question: What are the temporary provisions with respect to the State of Jammu and Kashmir?
2560.answer: The provisions of article 238 shall not apply in relation to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

2561.question: Which article's provisions do not apply in relation to the State of Jammu and Kashmir?
2561.answer: The provisions of article 238 do not apply in relation to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

2562.question: What modification was made to article 370 on the 17th day of November, 1952?
2562.answer: The said art. 370 shall be operative with the modification that for the Explanation in cl. (1) thereof, the following Explanation is substituted.

2563.question: What was the modification made to the Explanation in clause (1) of article 370?
2563.answer: The following Explanation was substituted for the original one on the 17th day of November, 1952.

2564.question: What is the power of Parliament to make laws for the said State limited to?
2564.answer: The power of Parliament to make laws for the said State is limited to those matters in the Union List and the Concurrent List which, in consultation with the Government of the State, are declared by the President to correspond to matters specified in the Instrument of Accession governing the accession of the State to the Dominion of India as the matters with respect to which the Dominion Legislature may make laws for that State; and such other matters in the said Lists as, with the concurrence of the Government of the State, the President may by order specify.

2565.question: What matters are the Parliament's ability to make laws for a state limited to, and who must agree to these matters?
2565.answer: The Parliament's ability to make laws for a state are limited to matters in the Union List and the Concurrent List. These matters must be declared by the President to correspond to matters specified in the Instrument of Accession governing the state's accession to the Dominion of India. The President may also specify other matters in the said Lists, but this requires the concurrence of the State Government.

2566.question: What does the Government of the State mean for the purposes of this article?
2566.answer: For the purposes of this article, the Government of the State means the person for the time being recognised by the President as the Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir acting on the advice of the Council of Ministers for the time being in office under the Maharaja’s Proclamation dated the fifth day of March, 1948.

2567.question: Who is considered as the Government of the State in the context of the Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir acting on the advice of the Council of Ministers under the Maharaja’s Proclamation dated the fifth day of March, 1948?
2567.answer: For the purposes of this article, the Government of the State is the person for the time being recognised by the President as the Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir.

2568.question: Which provisions of the Constitution apply in relation to that State?
2568.answer: The provisions of article 1 and of this article shall apply in relation to that State; such of the other provisions of this Constitution shall apply in relation to that State subject to such exceptions and modifications as the President may by order specify.

2569.question: What articles of the Constitution apply to a specific State and what modifications can be made?
2569.answer: The articles of the Constitution that apply to a specific State are article 1 and the article in question. The other provisions of the Constitution may also apply, subject to exceptions and modifications that the President may specify by order.

2570.question: Under what conditions can an order which relates to the matters specified in the Instrument of Accession of the State be issued?
2570.answer: An order which relates to the matters specified in the Instrument of Accession of the State can be issued only in consultation with the Government of the State.

2571.question: Who must be consulted before issuing an order which relates to the matters specified in the Instrument of Accession of the State?
2571.answer: The Government of the State must be consulted before issuing such an order.

2572.question: Under what conditions can an order which relates to matters other than those referred to in the last preceding proviso be issued?
2572.answer: An order which relates to matters other than those referred to in the last preceding proviso can be issued only with the concurrence of that Government.

2573.question: What is required for an order relating to matters other than those referred to in the last preceding proviso to be issued?
2573.answer: Only with the concurrence of that Government can such an order be issued.

2574.question: What does the Constituent Assembly do before convening the framing of the Constitution of the State?
2574.answer: The Constituent Assembly places it before such Assembly for such decision as it may take thereon.

2575.question: What does the Constituent Assembly do with the Constitution of the State before it is framed?
2575.answer: The Constituent Assembly places it before such Assembly for such decision as it may take thereon.

2576.question: Under what conditions may the President declare that an article shall cease to be operative or be operative only with exceptions and modifications?
2576.answer: The President may declare this after the recommendation of the Constituent Assembly of the State referred to in clause (2).

2577.question: Who must recommend for the President to declare that an article shall cease to be operative or be operative only with exceptions and modifications?
2577.answer: The Constituent Assembly of the State referred to in clause (2) must recommend.

2578.question: What special provisions does the President have with respect to the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat?
2578.answer: The President may provide for any special responsibility of the Governor for the establishment of separate development boards, the equitable allocation of funds for developmental expenditure, and an equitable arrangement providing adequate facilities for technical education and vocational training and employment opportunities.

2579.question: What responsibilities can the President assign to the Governor for the states of Maharashtra and Gujarat?
2579.answer: The President can assign the Governor special responsibilities, including the establishment of separate development boards, the equitable allocation of funds for developmental expenditure, and an equitable arrangement providing adequate facilities for technical education and vocational training and employment opportunities.

2580.question: What are the special provisions with respect to the State of Nagaland?
2580.answer: No Act of Parliament in respect of religious or social practices of the Nagas, Naga customary law and procedure, and administration of civil and criminal justice.

2581.question: What does the Act of Parliament not regulate in the State of Nagaland?
2581.answer: Religious or social practices of the Nagas, Naga customary law and procedure, and administration of civil and criminal justice.

2582.question: What applies to the State of Nagaland according to Naga customary law?
2582.answer: Ownership and transfer of land and its resources apply to the State of Nagaland according to Naga customary law.

2583.question: According to Naga customary law, what applies to the ownership and transfer of land and its resources?
2583.answer: It applies to the State of Nagaland.

2584.question: What responsibility does the Governor of Nagaland have with respect to law and order?
2584.answer: The Governor of Nagaland has special responsibility with respect to law and order in the State of Nagaland, particularly during periods of internal disturbances.

2585.question: Who has special responsibility with respect to law and order in the State of Nagaland, particularly during periods of internal disturbances?
2585.answer: The Governor of Nagaland has special responsibility with respect to law and order in the State of Nagaland, particularly during periods of internal disturbances.

2586.question: What is the role of the Governor's discretion in the exercise of his duties?
2586.answer: The Governor's discretion is final in determining whether a matter is one in which he is required to act in the exercise of his individual judgment. The validity of anything done by the Governor cannot be questioned on the grounds of his discretion.

2587.question: Is the Governor's discretion final in determining whether a matter requires his individual judgment and can the validity of anything done by the Governor be questioned on the grounds of his discretion?
2587.answer: Yes, the Governor's discretion is final in determining whether a matter is one in which he is required to act in the exercise of his individual judgment. No, the validity of anything done by the Governor cannot be questioned on the grounds of his discretion.

2588.question: Under what conditions can the Governor of Nagaland cease to have special responsibility with respect to law and order?
2588.answer: The President can order the Governor of Nagaland to cease having special responsibility with respect to law and order if he is satisfied, based on a report from the Governor or otherwise, that it is no longer necessary.

2589.question: Who has the power to order the Governor of Nagaland to cease having special responsibility for law and order, and under what circumstances?
2589.answer: The President has the power to order the Governor of Nagaland to cease having special responsibility for law and order, specifically when he is satisfied, based on a report from the Governor or otherwise, that it is no longer necessary.

2590.question: What should the Governor of Nagaland ensure when making his recommendation with respect to any demand for a grant?
2590.answer: The Governor of Nagaland should ensure that any money provided by the Government of India out of the Consolidated Fund of India for any specific service or purpose is included in the demand for a grant relating to that service or purpose and not in any other demand.

2591.question: What should the Governor of Nagaland ensure about the money provided by the Government of India from the Consolidated Fund of India for any specific service or purpose?
2591.answer: The Governor of Nagaland should ensure that this money is included in the demand for a grant relating to that service or purpose and not in any other demand when making his recommendation.

2592.question: What is the regional council for the Tuensang district composed of?
2592.answer: The regional council for the Tuensang district is composed of thirty-five members.

2593.question: How many members are there in the regional council for the Tuensang district?
2593.answer: There are thirty-five members in the regional council for the Tuensang district.

2594.question: Who shall be the Chairman of the regional council for the Tuensang district?
2594.answer: The Deputy Commissioner of the Tuensang district shall be the Chairman ex officio of the regional council.

2595.question: Who is the Chairman ex officio of the regional council for the Tuensang district?
2595.answer: The Deputy Commissioner of the Tuensang district is the Chairman ex officio of the regional council.

2596.question: Who elects the Vice-Chairman of the regional council?
2596.answer: The Vice-Chairman of the regional council is elected by the members thereof from amongst themselves.

2597.question: Who are the Vice-Chairman of the regional council elected by?
2597.answer: The Vice-Chairman of the regional council is elected by the members thereof from amongst themselves.

2598.question: What does the Governor provide rules for in relation to the regional council?
2598.answer: The Governor provides rules for the composition of the council, qualifications for members, term of office, salaries and allowances, procedure and conduct of business, appointment of officers and staff and their conditions of service, and any other matters necessary for the constitution and proper functioning of the council.

2599.question: What aspects does the Governor's rules for the regional council cover?
2599.answer: The Governor's rules for the regional council cover the composition of the council, qualifications for members, term of office, salaries and allowances, procedure and conduct of business, appointment of officers and staff and their conditions of service, and any other matters necessary for the constitution and proper functioning of the council.

2600.question: Who will administer the Tuensang district for a period of ten years from the date of the formation of the State of Nagaland?
2600.answer: The Governor will administer the Tuensang district for a period of ten years from the date of the formation of the State of Nagaland.

2601.question: Who will administer the Tuensang district for a period of ten years from the date of the formation of the State of Nagaland?

2602.question: Who decides the allocation of money provided by the Government of India to the Government of Nagaland?
2602.answer: The Governor, in his discretion, arranges for an equitable allocation of that money between the Tuensang district and the rest of the State.

2603.question: Who arranges for an equitable allocation of the money provided by the Government of India between the Tuensang district and the rest of the State of Nagaland?
2603.answer: The Governor, in his discretion, decides the allocation of that money.

2604.question: Under what conditions does an Act of the Legislature of Nagaland apply to Tuensang district?
2604.answer: No Act of the Legislature of Nagaland shall apply to Tuensang district unless the Governor, on the recommendation of the regional council, by public notification so directs.

2605.question: Who needs to direct that an Act of the Legislature of Nagaland applies to Tuensang district and under what recommendation?
2605.answer: The Governor needs to direct it on the recommendation of the regional council.

2606.question: What modifications can be made to the application of the act in the Tuensang district?
2606.answer: The act may be subject to exceptions or modifications as the Governor may specify on the recommendation of the regional council.

2607.question: Who can specify exceptions or modifications to the act in the Tuensang district and on whose recommendation?
2607.answer: The Governor can specify exceptions or modifications to the act on the recommendation of the regional council.

2608.question: Who can make regulations for the Tuensang district?
2608.answer: The Governor can make regulations for the Tuensang district.

2609.question: For which district can the Governor make regulations?
2609.answer: The Governor can make regulations for the Tuensang district.

2610.question: Who shall be appointed Minister for Tuensang affairs?
2610.answer: One of the members representing the Tuensang district in the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland shall be appointed Minister for Tuensang affairs by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.

2611.question: Who appoints the Minister for Tuensang affairs and who is eligible for this position?
2611.answer: The Governor appoints one of the members representing the Tuensang district in the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland as the Minister for Tuensang affairs on the advice of the Chief Minister.

2612.question: Who has final say on all matters relating to the Tuensang district?
2612.answer: The final decision on all matters relating to the Tuensang district shall be made by the Governor in his discretion.

2613.question: Who makes the final decision on all matters relating to the Tuensang district?
2613.answer: The Governor in his discretion has final say on all matters relating to the Tuensang district.

2614.question: In articles 54 and 55 and clause (4) of article 80, who do the references to the elected members of the Legislative Assembly of a State include?
2614.answer: The references include the members or member of the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland elected by the regional council established under this article.

2615.question: Who are the members or member of the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland elected by the regional council established under this article referred to in articles 54 and 55 and clause (4) of article 80?
2615.answer: The references are to the elected members of the Legislative Assembly of a State.

2616.question: What is the effect of clause (1) in article 170 in relation to the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland?
2616.answer: Clause (1) shall have effect as if for the word 'sixty', the word 'forty-six' had been substituted.

2617.question: What is substituted for the word 'sixty' in clause (1) of article 170 in relation to the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland?
2617.answer: The word 'forty-six' is substituted for the word 'sixty'.

2618.question: What does the reference to direct election from territorial constituencies in the state in the said clause of article 170 include?
2618.answer: It includes election by the members of the regional council.

2619.question: What does the election by the members of the regional council refer to in the context of direct election from territorial constituencies in the state as per the clause of article 170?
2619.answer: It refers to the reference to direct election from territorial constituencies in the state in the said clause of article 170.

2620.question: What does the President have the authority to do if difficulties arise in implementing the provisions of this article?
2620.answer: The President may by order do anything (including any adaptation or modification of any other article) which appears to him to be necessary for the purpose of removing that difficulty.

2621.question: What can the President do by order when he identifies a necessity to remove a difficulty in implementing the provisions of an article?
2621.answer: The President may do anything (including any adaptation or modification of any other article) which appears to him to be necessary for the purpose of removing that difficulty.

2622.question: What is the time limit for the President to make such an order?
2622.answer: No such order shall be made after the expiration of three years from the date of the formation of the State of Nagaland.

2623.question: When does the time limit for the President to make such an order expire in relation to the formation of the State of Nagaland?
2623.answer: The time limit for the President to make such an order expires three years after the date of the formation of the State of Nagaland.

2624.question: What special provision is given with respect to the State of Assam?
2624.answer: The President may, by order made with respect to the State of Assam, provide for the constitution and functions of a committee of the Legislative Assembly of the State consisting of members of that Assembly elected from the tribal areas specified in Part I of the table appended to paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule.

2625.question: What can the President provide for the State of Assam by order made with respect to it?
2625.answer: The President can provide for the constitution and functions of a committee of the Legislative Assembly of the State consisting of members of that Assembly elected from the tribal areas specified in Part I of the table appended to paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule.

2626.question: What special provision is given with respect to the State of Manipur?
2626.answer: The President may, by order made with respect to the State of Manipur, provide for the constitution and functions of a committee of the Legislative Assembly of the State consisting of members of that Assembly elected from the Hill Areas of that State.

2627.question: What can the President do with respect to the constitution and functions of a committee of the Legislative Assembly of Manipur?
2627.answer: The President may, by order made with respect to the State of Manipur, provide for the constitution and functions of a committee of the Legislative Assembly of the State consisting of members of that Assembly elected from the Hill Areas of that State.

2628.question: What does the Governor do annually or when required by the President?
2628.answer: The Governor makes a report to the President regarding the administration of the Hill Areas in the State of Manipur.

2629.question: To whom does the Governor of Manipur report about the administration of the Hill Areas in the State, annually or when required?
2629.answer: The Governor of Manipur makes a report to the President.

2630.question: What power does the Union have regarding the Hill Areas?
2630.answer: The executive power of the Union extends to giving directions to the State as to the administration of the said areas.
