2631.question: To whom does the Union's executive power extend in the administration of the Hill Areas?
2631.answer: The Union's executive power extends to giving directions to the State.

2632.question: What does the term 'Hill Areas' refer to?
2632.answer: The term 'Hill Areas' refers to areas that the President may, by order, declare to be Hill areas.

2633.question: Who has the authority to declare areas as 'Hill Areas'?
2633.answer: The President has the authority to declare areas as 'Hill Areas'.

2634.question: What can the President provide for the State of Andhra Pradesh?
2634.answer: The President can provide for equitable opportunities and facilities for the people belonging to different parts of the State in terms of public employment and education.

2635.question: What can the President do to ensure equitable opportunities and facilities for the people belonging to different parts of a State in terms of public employment and education?
2635.answer: The President can provide for the State of Andhra Pradesh.

2636.question: What can an order made under clause (1) specify for the State of Andhra Pradesh?
2636.answer: The order can require the State Government to organise any class or classes of posts in a civil service or any class or classes of civil posts under the State into different local cadres for different parts of the State. It can also specify the local area for direct recruitment to posts in any local cadre under the State Government, for direct recruitment to posts in any cadre under any local authority within the State, and for the purposes of admission to any University within the State or to any other educational institution which is subject to the control of the State Government.

2637.question: What does the order requiring the State Government of Andhra Pradesh to organise any class or classes of posts in a civil service or any class or classes of civil posts under the State into different local cadres for different parts of the State, and specifying the local area for direct recruitment to posts in any local cadre under the State Government, for direct recruitment to posts in any cadre under any local authority within the State, and for the purposes of admission to any University within the State or to any other educational institution which is subject to the control of the State Government, made under clause (1)?
2637.answer: This order can be made under clause (1).

2638.question: What is the preference or reservation given to in the matter of direct recruitment?
2638.answer: Preference or reservation is given to candidates who have resided or studied for any period specified in the order in the local area in respect of such cadre.

2639.question: Who are the candidates given preference or reservation in the matter of direct recruitment?
2639.answer: Candidates who have resided or studied for any period specified in the order in the local area in respect of such cadre are given preference or reservation.

2640.question: What can the President provide for the constitution of in the State of Andhra Pradesh?
2640.answer: The President may provide for the constitution of an Administrative Tribunal.

2641.question: Who may provide for the constitution of an Administrative Tribunal in the State of Andhra Pradesh?

2642.question: What jurisdiction, powers, and authority can the Administrative Tribunal exercise?
2642.answer: The Administrative Tribunal can exercise any jurisdiction, power and authority which immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 1973, was exercisable by any court (other than the Supreme Court) or by any tribunal or other authority.

2643.question: What jurisdiction, power and authority was exercisable by any court (other than the Supreme Court) or by any tribunal or other authority immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 1973?
2643.answer: The jurisdiction, power and authority that was exercisable by any court (other than the Supreme Court) or by any tribunal or other authority immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 1973, can now be exercised by the Administrative Tribunal.

2644.question: What matters does the jurisdiction of the Administrative Tribunal for the State of Andhra Pradesh cover?
2644.answer: The jurisdiction of the Administrative Tribunal covers appointment, allotment or promotion to certain classes of posts in any civil service of the State, seniority of persons appointed, allotted or promoted to such classes of posts, and other conditions of service of persons appointed, allotted or promoted to such classes of posts.

2645.question: What does the appointment, allotment or promotion to certain classes of posts in any civil service of the State, seniority of persons appointed, allotted or promoted to such classes of posts, and other conditions of service of persons appointed, allotted or promoted to such classes of posts pertain to?
2645.answer: These matters pertain to the jurisdiction of the Administrative Tribunal for the State of Andhra Pradesh.

2646.question: What is the preference or reservation given to in the matter of admission to any such University or other educational institution?
2646.answer: Preference or reservation is given to candidates who have resided or studied for any period specified in the order in the local area in respect of such University or other educational institution.

2647.question: Who is given preference or reservation in the matter of admission to any University or other educational institution?
2647.answer: Candidates who have resided or studied for any period specified in the order in the local area in respect of such University or other educational institution are given preference or reservation.

2648.question: What can an order made under clause (3) of The Constitution of India authorize the Administrative Tribunal to do?
2648.answer: The order can authorise the Administrative Tribunal to receive representations for the redress of grievances relating to any matter within its jurisdiction as the President may specify in the order and to make such orders thereon as the Administrative Tribunal deems fit.

2649.question: What does the order authorize the Administrative Tribunal to do, according to clause (3) of The Constitution of India, when it comes to grievances within its jurisdiction?
2649.answer: The order authorizes the Administrative Tribunal to receive representations for the redress of grievances relating to any matter within its jurisdiction as the President may specify in the order and to make such orders thereon as the Administrative Tribunal deems fit.

2650.question: What provisions can an order made under clause (3) contain regarding the powers and authorities of the Administrative Tribunal?
2650.answer: The order can contain provisions with respect to the powers and authorities and procedure of the Administrative Tribunal, including provisions with respect to the powers of the Administrative Tribunal to punish for contempt of itself, as the President may deem necessary.

2651.question: What provisions with respect to the powers, authorities and procedure of the Administrative Tribunal can be included in an order made under clause (3), as deemed necessary by the President?
2651.answer: An order made under clause (3) can contain provisions regarding the powers and authorities of the Administrative Tribunal, including its ability to punish for contempt of itself.

2652.question: What can an order made under clause (3) provide for in regards to the transfer of proceedings?
2652.answer: The order can provide for the transfer to the Administrative Tribunal of such classes of proceedings, being proceedings relating to matters within its jurisdiction and pending before any court (other than the Supreme Court) or tribunal or other authority immediately before the commencement of such order.

2653.question: Where can proceedings be transferred to under an order made under clause (3)?
2653.answer: The proceedings can be transferred to the Administrative Tribunal.

2654.question: When does the Order of the Administrative Tribunal become effective?
2654.answer: The Order of the Administrative Tribunal finally disposing of any case shall become effective upon its confirmation by the State Government or on the expiry of three months from the date on which the order is made, whichever is earlier.

2655.question: What happens to the Order of the Administrative Tribunal after its confirmation by the State Government or after three months have passed since its creation?
2655.answer: The Order of the Administrative Tribunal finally disposing of any case becomes effective.

2656.question: What can the State Government do before the order of the Administrative Tribunal becomes effective?
2656.answer: The State Government may, by special order made in writing and for reasons to be specified therein, modify or annul any order of the Administrative Tribunal before it becomes effective.

2657.question: How can the State Government modify or annul an order of the Administrative Tribunal before it becomes effective?
2657.answer: The State Government may do so by making a special order in writing, and specifying the reasons therein.

2658.question: What happens to a special order made by the State Government under the proviso to clause (5)?
2658.answer: Every special order made by the State Government under the proviso to clause (5) shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made.

2659.question: What is the procedure for a special order made by the State Government under the proviso to clause (5) after it is made?
2659.answer: Every special order made by the State Government under the proviso to clause (5) shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made.

2660.question: Who does not have any powers of superintendence over the Administrative Tribunal?
2660.answer: The High Court for the State

2661.question: Which court does not have any powers of superintendence over the Administrative Tribunal?
2661.answer: The High Court for the State

2662.question: Who declared cl. (5) of art. 371D along with the proviso to be unconstitutional and void?

2663.question: Which institution declared cl. (5) of art. 371D along with the proviso to be unconstitutional and void?

2664.question: Who can abolish the Administrative Tribunal?

2665.question: Who has the power to abolish the Administrative Tribunal?

2666.question: What can the President do if he is satisfied that the continued existence of the Administrative Tribunal is not necessary?
2666.answer: The President may by order abolish the Administrative Tribunal and make such provisions in such order as he may deem fit for the transfer and disposal of cases pending before the Tribunal immediately before such abolition.

2667.question: What process does the President follow to abolish the Administrative Tribunal and how are the pending cases handled?
2667.answer: The President may by order abolish the Administrative Tribunal and make provisions in the order for the transfer and disposal of cases pending before the Tribunal immediately before its abolition, as he deems fit.

2668.question: What is not deemed to be illegal or void merely on the ground that the appointment, posting, promotion or transfer of such person was not made in accordance with any law, then in force?
2668.answer: No appointment, posting, promotion or transfer of any person made before the 1st day of November, 1956, to any post under the Government of, or any local authority within, the State of Hyderabad as it existed before that date; or made before the commencement of the Constitution (Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 1973, to any post under the Government of, or any local or other authority within, the State of Andhra Pradesh; and no action taken or thing done by or before any person referred to in sub-clause (a).

2669.question: What appointments, postings, promotions or transfers are not considered illegal or void, even if they were not made in accordance with any law in force at the time, specifically before November 1, 1956, in the State of Hyderabad and before the commencement of the Constitution (Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 1973, in the State of Andhra Pradesh?
2669.answer: The appointments, postings, promotions or transfers that are not considered illegal or void, even if they were not made in accordance with any law in force at the time, specifically are those made before the 1st day of November, 1956, to any post under the Government of, or any local authority within, the State of Hyderabad as it existed before that date; or made before the commencement of the Constitution (Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 1973, to any post under the Government of, or any local or other authority within, the State of Andhra Pradesh. This also includes any action taken or thing done by or before any person referred to in these cases.

2670.question: What does article 371E provide for in Andhra Pradesh?
2670.answer: Article 371E provides that the Parliament may by law provide for the establishment of a University in the State of Andhra Pradesh.

2671.question: What does the Parliament have the authority to establish in the State of Andhra Pradesh according to Article 371E?
2671.answer: According to Article 371E, the Parliament has the authority to provide for the establishment of a University in the State of Andhra Pradesh.

2672.question: What special provisions are made for the State of Sikkim according to article 371F?
2672.answer: Article 371F provides special provisions for the State of Sikkim including: the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim shall consist of not less than thirty members; the assembly formed as a result of the elections held in Sikkim in April, 1974 with thirty-two members shall be deemed to be the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim under the Constitution; the period of five years in clause (1) of article 172 shall be construed as references to a period of four years for the Assembly of Sikkim; and until other provisions are made by Parliament by law, there shall be allotted to the State of Sikkim one seat in the House of the People.

2673.question: What does Article 371F state about the legislative assembly of Sikkim, the period of years in clause (1) of article 172 for the Assembly of Sikkim, and the number of seats allotted to Sikkim in the House of People?
2673.answer: Article 371F provides special provisions for the State of Sikkim including: the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim shall consist of not less than thirty members; the assembly formed as a result of the elections held in Sikkim in April, 1974 with thirty-two members shall be deemed to be the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim under the Constitution; the period of five years in clause (1) of article 172 shall be construed as references to a period of four years for the Assembly of Sikkim; and until other provisions are made by Parliament by law, there shall be allotted to the State of Sikkim one seat in the House of the People.

2674.question: What is the minimum number of members for the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim according to article 371F?
2674.answer: The minimum number of members for the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim is thirty according to article 371F.

2675.question: How many members does article 371F state as the minimum for the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim?
2675.answer: Article 371F states that the minimum number of members for the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim is thirty.

2676.question: When is the period of four years for the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim deemed to commence from?
2676.answer: The period of four years for the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim is deemed to commence from the appointed day.

2677.question: From what day is the period of four years for the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim deemed to commence?

2678.question: What is provided for the State of Sikkim in terms of representation in the House of People according to article 371F?
2678.answer: According to article 371F, until other provisions are made by Parliament by law, there shall be allotted to the State of Sikkim one seat in the House of the People.

2679.question: Which article states that until other provisions are made by Parliament by law, there shall be allotted to the State of Sikkim one seat in the House of the People?

2680.question: What is the parliamentary constituency for Sikkim?
2680.answer: The parliamentary constituency for Sikkim is formed from one parliamentary constituency.

2681.question: How many parliamentary constituencies form the parliamentary constituency for Sikkim?
2681.answer: One parliamentary constituency forms the parliamentary constituency for Sikkim.

2682.question: How is the representative of the State of Sikkim in the House of the People elected?
2682.answer: The representative of the State of Sikkim in the House of the People is elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim.

2683.question: Who elects the representative of the State of Sikkim in the House of the People?
2683.answer: The representative of the State of Sikkim in the House of the People is elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim.

2684.question: What responsibility does the Parliament have regarding Sikkim's Legislative Assembly?
2684.answer: Parliament may make provision for the number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim which may be filled by candidates belonging to different sections of the population, and for the delimitation of the assembly constituencies from which candidates belonging to such sections alone may stand for election.

2685.question: What provision can the Parliament make for the number of seats and delimitation of assembly constituencies in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim?
2685.answer: Parliament may make provision for the number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim which may be filled by candidates belonging to different sections of the population, and for the delimitation of the assembly constituencies from which candidates belonging to such sections alone may stand for election.

2686.question: What is the special responsibility of the Governor of Sikkim?
2686.answer: The Governor of Sikkim has special responsibility for peace and for an equitable arrangement for ensuring the social and economic advancement of different sections of the population of Sikkim.

2687.question: Who has the special responsibility for peace and for an equitable arrangement for ensuring the social and economic advancement of different sections of the population of Sikkim?
2687.answer: The Governor of Sikkim has this special responsibility.

2688.question: What happens to the property and assets vested in the Government of Sikkim after the appointed day?
2688.answer: All property and assets vested in the Government of Sikkim before the appointed day shall, as from the appointed day, vest in the Government of the State of Sikkim.

2689.question: Where do all property and assets vested in the Government of Sikkim before the appointed day go after the appointed day?
2689.answer: After the appointed day, all property and assets vested in the Government of Sikkim before the appointed day vest in the Government of the State of Sikkim.

2690.question: What happens to the High Court of Sikkim after the appointed day?
2690.answer: The High Court functioning immediately before the appointed day in the territories comprised in the State of Sikkim shall, on and from the appointed day, be deemed to be the High Court for the State of Sikkim.

2691.question: Which court is deemed to be the High Court for the State of Sikkim on and from the appointed day?
2691.answer: The High Court functioning immediately before the appointed day in the territories comprised in the State of Sikkim.

2692.question: What happens to all courts of civil, criminal and revenue jurisdiction, all authorities and all officers in Sikkim after the appointed day?
2692.answer: All courts of civil, criminal and revenue jurisdiction, all authorities and all officers, judicial, executive and ministerial, throughout the territory of the State of Sikkim shall continue on and from the appointed day.

2693.question: What is the fate of all courts of civil, criminal and revenue jurisdiction, all authorities and all officers, judicial, executive and ministerial, throughout the territory of the State of Sikkim on and from the appointed day?
2693.answer: They shall continue functioning as they were.

2694.question: What happens to the laws in force before the appointed day in the territories comprised in the State of Sikkim?
2694.answer: They continue to be in force therein until amended or repealed by a competent Legislature or other competent authority.

2695.question: Until when do the laws in force before the appointed day continue to be in effect in the territories comprised in the State of Sikkim?
2695.answer: They continue to be in force therein until amended or repealed by a competent Legislature or other competent authority.

2696.question: Who can make adaptations and modifications of laws in relation to the administration of the State of Sikkim?
2696.answer: The President may make such adaptations and modifications of the law, whether by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient.

2697.question: Who has the authority to make necessary or expedient adaptations and modifications of the law, whether by way of repeal or amendment?
2697.answer: The President may make such adaptations and modifications of the law in relation to the administration of the State of Sikkim.

2698.question: Can the adaptations or modifications made by the president be questioned in any court of law?
2698.answer: No, any such adaptation or modification shall not be questioned in any court of law.

2699.question: Can the adaptations or modifications made by the president be questioned in any court of law?
2699.answer: No, any such adaptation or modification shall not be questioned in any court of law.

2700.question: Do the Supreme Court or any other court have jurisdiction in respect of any dispute or matter arising out of any treaty, agreement, engagement or other similar instrument relating to Sikkim?
2700.answer: No, neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall have jurisdiction in respect of any such dispute or matter.

2701.question: Is it true that neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall have jurisdiction in respect of any dispute or matter arising out of any treaty, agreement, engagement or other similar instrument relating to Sikkim?

2702.question: What can the President do if any difficulty arises in giving effect to any of the foregoing provisions of this article?
2702.answer: The President may, by order, do anything which appears to him to be necessary for the purpose of removing that difficulty.

2703.question: What can the President do to remove a difficulty that arises in giving effect to any of the provisions of an article?
2703.answer: The President may, by order, do anything which appears to him to be necessary for the purpose of removing that difficulty.

2704.question: What can the President do with any enactment which is in force in a State in India?
2704.answer: The President may, by public notification, extend with such restrictions or modifications as he thinks fit to the State of Sikkim any enactment which is in force in a State in India at the date of the notification.

2705.question: How can the President extend any enactment which is in force in a State in India to the State of Sikkim?
2705.answer: The President may, by public notification, extend with such restrictions or modifications as he thinks fit to the State of Sikkim any enactment which is in force in a State in India at the date of the notification.

2706.question: When can no such order be made according to the text?
2706.answer: After the expiry of two years from the appointed day

2707.question: What event happens after the expiry of two years from the appointed day that affects the making of an order?
2707.answer: No such order can be made

2708.question: What is deemed valid in relation to the State of Sikkim or the territories comprised therein?
2708.answer: All things done and all actions taken during the period commencing on the appointed day and ending immediately before the date on which the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975, receives the assent of the President

2709.question: What is considered valid during the period commencing on the appointed day and ending immediately before the date on which the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975, receives the assent of the President?
2709.answer: All things done and all actions taken in relation to the State of Sikkim or the territories comprised therein are deemed valid

2710.question: What does not apply to the State of Mizoram unless the Legislative Assembly of the State of Mizoram decides?
2710.answer: No Act of Parliament in respect of religious or social practices of the Mizos, Mizo customary law and procedure, administration of civil and criminal justice involving decisions according to Mizo customary law, ownership and transfer of land

2711.question: What is the Act of Parliament that doesn't apply to the State of Mizoram unless the Legislative Assembly of the State of Mizoram decides?
2711.answer: The Act of Parliament in respect of religious or social practices of the Mizos, Mizo customary law and procedure, administration of civil and criminal justice involving decisions according to Mizo customary law, ownership and transfer of land

2715.question: Which state in India does the Governor have special responsibility with respect to law and order?

2716.question: Who has the final decision in the exercise of his individual judgment according to the clause?

2717.question: According to the clause, who has the final decision in the exercise of individual judgment?

2718.question: What can the President do if he is satisfied that it is no longer necessary for the Governor to have special responsibility with respect to law and order in the State of Arunachal Pradesh?
2718.answer: He may by order direct that the Governor shall cease to have such responsibility with effect from such date as may be specified in the order

2719.question: What can the President do to stop the Governor's special responsibility regarding law and order in the State of Arunachal Pradesh?
2719.answer: The President may by order direct that the Governor shall cease to have such responsibility with effect from a specified date.

2720.question: How many members should the Legislative Assembly of the State of Arunachal Pradesh consist of, at minimum?

2721.question: What is the minimum number of members in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Arunachal Pradesh?

2723.question: Which state in India has a Legislative Assembly consisting of thirty members?

2724.question: What special responsibilities can the President provide for the Governor with respect to the State of Karnataka?
2724.answer: Establishment of a separate development board for Hyderabad-Karnataka region, equitable allocation of funds for developmental expenditure over the said region, and equitable opportunities and facilities for the people belonging to the said region in matters of public employment, education and vocational training.

2725.question: What does the establishment of a separate development board for Hyderabad-Karnataka region by the President for the Governor entail with respect to the State of Karnataka?
2725.answer: It entails equitable allocation of funds for developmental expenditure over the said region, and equitable opportunities and facilities for the people belonging to the said region in matters of public employment, education and vocational training.

2726.question: What can an order made under sub-clause (c) of clause (1) provide for?
2726.answer: Reservation of a proportion of seats in educational and vocational training institutions in the Hyderabad-Karnataka region for students who belong to that region by birth

2727.question: What does the reservation of a proportion of seats in educational and vocational training institutions in the Hyderabad-Karnataka region for students who belong to that region by birth, pertain to?
2727.answer: It pertains to an order made under sub-clause (c) of clause (1)

2728.question: What does the law state about identification of posts under the State Government in the Hyderabad-Karnataka region?
2728.answer: The law states that there should be identification of posts or classes of posts under the State Government and in any body or organisation under the control of the State Government in the Hyderabad-Karnataka region. There should also be reservation of a proportion of such posts for persons who belong to that region by birth or by domicile and for appointment thereto by direct recruitment or by promotion or in any other manner as may be specified in the order.

2729.question: What does the law specify regarding the reservation and appointment of posts under the State Government and in any body or organisation under its control in the Hyderabad-Karnataka region?
2729.answer: The law specifies that there should be identification of posts or classes of posts under the State Government and in any body or organisation under the control of the State Government in the Hyderabad-Karnataka region. There should also be reservation of a proportion of such posts for persons who belong to that region by birth or by domicile and for appointment thereto by direct recruitment or by promotion or in any other manner as may be specified in the order.

2730.question: What happens to laws in force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of the Constitution?
2730.answer: All the laws in force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall continue in force therein until altered or repealed or amended by a competent Legislature or other competent authority.

2731.question: What will happen to the laws in force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of the Constitution if they are not altered, repealed, or amended by a competent legislature or other competent authority?
2731.answer: All the laws in force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall continue in force therein.

2732.question: What power does the President have in terms of adapting and modifying laws?
2732.answer: The President may by order make such adaptations and modifications of such law, whether by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient, and provide that the law shall, as from such date as may be specified in the order, have effect subject to the adaptations and modifications so made.

2733.question: What can the President do by order in order to adapt, modify, repeal or amend a law, and when does this change take effect?
2733.answer: The President may by order make such adaptations and modifications of such law, whether by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient, and provide that the law shall, as from such date as may be specified in the order, have effect subject to the adaptations and modifications so made.

2734.question: What limitations are there on the President's power to adapt and modify laws?
2734.answer: The President cannot make any adaptation or modification of any law after the expiration of three years from the commencement of this Constitution. Also, the President cannot prevent any competent Legislature or other competent authority from repealing or amending any law adapted or modified by the President.

2735.question: Can the President prevent any competent Legislature or other competent authority from repealing or amending any law adapted or modified by the President, and for how long can the President make any adaptation or modification of any law after the commencement of the Constitution?
2735.answer: No, the President cannot prevent any competent Legislature or other competent authority from repealing or amending any law adapted or modified by the President. The President can make any adaptation or modification of any law only for three years from the commencement of the Constitution.

2736.question: What is included in the expression 'law in force' in this article?
2736.answer: The expression 'law in force' in this article shall include a law passed or made by a Legislature or other competent authority in the territory of India before the commencement of this Constitution.

2737.question: What does the expression 'law in force' in the article refer to when discussing laws passed or made by a Legislature or other competent authority in the territory of India before the commencement of this Constitution?
2737.answer: The expression 'law in force' in this article refers to a law that was passed or made by a Legislature or other competent authority in the territory of India prior to the start of the Constitution.

2738.question: What happens to a law that had extra-territorial effect before the commencement of the Constitution?
2738.answer: Any law passed or made by a Legislature or other competent authority in the territory of India which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution had extra-territorial effect as well as effect in the territory of India shall continue to have such extra-territorial effect, subject to any adaptations and modifications.

2739.question: What will happen to a law made by a Legislature or other competent authority in the territory of India that had extra-territorial effect immediately before the commencement of the Constitution?
2739.answer: Any such law will continue to have such extra-territorial effect, subject to any adaptations and modifications.

2740.question: What does the Constitution state about continuing any temporary law?
2740.answer: Nothing in this article shall be construed as continuing any temporary law in force beyond the date fixed for its expiration or the date on which it would have expired if this Constitution had not come into force.

2741.question: What happens to a temporary law in force beyond the date fixed for its expiration or the date on which it would have expired if the Constitution had not come into force?
2741.answer: The Constitution states that nothing in this article shall be construed as continuing any temporary law in force beyond that date.

2742.question: What happens to an Ordinance promulgated by the Governor of a Province under section 88 of the Government of India Act, 1935?
2742.answer: An Ordinance promulgated by the Governor of a Province under section 88 of the Government of India Act, 1935, and in force immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall cease to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the first meeting after such commencement of the Legislative Assembly of that State functioning under clause (1) of article 382.

2743.question: When does an Ordinance promulgated by the Governor of a Province under section 88 of the Government of India Act, 1935, cease to operate if it's in force immediately before the commencement of the Constitution?
2743.answer: The Ordinance shall cease to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the first meeting after such commencement of the Legislative Assembly of that State functioning under clause (1) of article 382.

2744.question: What is the power of the President to adapt laws according to the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956?
2744.answer: For the purposes of bringing the provisions of any law in force in India or in any part thereof, immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, into accord with the provisions of this Constitution as amended by that Act, the President may by order make such adaptations and modifications of the law, whether by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient, and provide that the law shall, as from such date as may be specified in the order, have effect subject to the adaptations and modifications so made.

2745.question: What authority does the President have to adapt and modify laws in order to align them with the Constitution as amended by the Seventh Amendment Act, 1956?
2745.answer: The President has the power to make adaptations and modifications of any law that was in force in India or in any part thereof, immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, whether by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient. The President can provide that the law shall, as from such date as may be specified in the order, have effect subject to the adaptations and modifications so made.

2746.question: Who has the power to repeal or amend any law adapted or modified by the President?
2746.answer: A competent Legislature or other competent authority

2747.question: Who can modify or repeal laws that have been adapted or changed by the President?
2747.answer: A competent Legislature or other competent authority

2748.question: Who has the power to make order in respect of persons under preventive detention in certain cases?

2749.question: Who has the authority to issue orders concerning individuals under preventive detention in certain circumstances?

2750.question: What happens to the Judges of the Federal Court after the commencement of this Constitution?
2750.answer: They become the Judges of the Supreme Court, unless they have elected otherwise.

2751.question: Who do the Judges of the Federal Court become after the commencement of the Constitution, unless they have elected otherwise?
2751.answer: They become the Judges of the Supreme Court.

2752.question: What happens to all suits, appeals and proceedings pending in the Federal Court at the commencement of this Constitution?
2752.answer: They shall stand removed to the Supreme Court.

2753.question: Where are all suits, appeals and proceedings pending in the Federal Court at the commencement of this Constitution moved to?
2753.answer: They are moved to the Supreme Court.

2754.question: What will the judgments and orders of the Federal Court have after the commencement of this Constitution?
2754.answer: They shall have the same force and effect as if they had been delivered or made by the Supreme Court.

2755.question: What force and effect will the judgments and orders of the Federal Court have after the commencement of this Constitution?
2755.answer: They shall have the same force and effect as if they had been delivered or made by the Supreme Court.

2756.question: Does anything in this Constitution operate to invalidate the exercise of jurisdiction by His Majesty?

2757.question: Does the Constitution uphold the exercise of jurisdiction by His Majesty?

2758.question: What happens to orders of His Majesty in Council made on any appeal or petition after the commencement of this Constitution?
2758.answer: Any order of His Majesty in Council made on any such appeal or petition after the commencement of this Constitution shall for all purposes have effect as if it were an order or decree made by the Supreme Court in the exercise of the jurisdiction conferred on such Court by this Constitution.

2759.question: What is the effect of any order of His Majesty in Council made on any appeal or petition after the commencement of this Constitution?
2759.answer: Any order of His Majesty in Council made on any such appeal or petition after the commencement of this Constitution shall for all purposes have effect as if it were an order or decree made by the Supreme Court in the exercise of the jurisdiction conferred on such Court by this Constitution.

2760.question: What happens to the jurisdiction of the authority functioning as the Privy Council in a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule after the commencement of this Constitution?
2760.answer: On and from the commencement of this Constitution the jurisdiction of the authority functioning as the Privy Council in a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule to entertain and dispose of appeals and petitions from or in respect of any judgment, decree or order of any court within that State shall cease, and all appeals and other proceedings pending before the said authority at such commencement shall be transferred to, and disposed of by, the Supreme Court.

2761.question: What happens to the appeals and other proceedings pending before the authority functioning as the Privy Council in a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule after the commencement of this Constitution?
2761.answer: All appeals and other proceedings pending before the said authority at such commencement shall be transferred to, and disposed of by, the Supreme Court.

2762.question: What happens to the courts, authorities and officers in the territory of India after the provisions of this Constitution?
2762.answer: All courts of civil, criminal and revenue jurisdiction, all authorities and all officers, judicial, executive and ministerial, throughout the territory of India, shall continue to exercise their respective functions subject to the provisions of this Constitution.

2763.question: What will the courts of civil, criminal and revenue jurisdiction, all authorities and all officers, judicial, executive and ministerial do after the provisions of this Constitution are implemented in the territory of India?
2763.answer: They shall continue to exercise their respective functions subject to the provisions of this Constitution.

2764.question: What happens to the Judges of a High Court in any Province holding office immediately before the commencement of this Constitution?
2764.answer: The Judges of a High Court in any Province holding office immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, become on such commencement the Judges of the High Court in the corresponding State, and shall thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for.

2765.question: What happens to the Judges of a High Court in any Province who were in office before the commencement of the Constitution, in terms of their position, salaries, allowances, leave of absence, and pension rights?
2765.answer: Unless they have elected otherwise, they become the Judges of the High Court in the corresponding State on the commencement of the Constitution, and are entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for.

2766.question: Who is eligible for appointment as Chief Justice of the High Court according to article 221?
2766.answer: Any Judge, even if he is not a citizen of India, is eligible for appointment as Chief Justice of the High Court.

2767.question: According to Article 221, is a judge eligible for appointment as Chief Justice of the High Court even if they are not a citizen of India?
2767.answer: Yes, any Judge, even if he is not a citizen of India, is eligible for appointment as Chief Justice of the High Court.

2768.question: What happens to the Judges of a High Court in any Indian State corresponding to any State specified in Part B of the First Schedule after the commencement of this Constitution?
2768.answer: Unless they have elected otherwise, they become the Judges of the High Court in the State so specified and continue to hold office until the expiration of such period as the President may by order determine.

2769.question: What happens to the Judges of a High Court in any Indian State specified in Part B of the First Schedule if they do not elect otherwise after the commencement of the Constitution?
2769.answer: They become the Judges of the High Court in the State so specified and continue to hold office until the expiration of such period as the President may by order determine.

2770.question: Does the expression 'Judge' in article 221 include an acting Judge or an additional Judge?
2770.answer: No, the expression 'Judge' does not include an acting Judge or an additional Judge.

2771.question: Does the expression 'Judge' include an acting Judge or an additional Judge?
2771.answer: No, the expression 'Judge' does not include an acting Judge or an additional Judge.

2772.question: What happens to the Auditor-General of India after the commencement of this Constitution?
2772.answer: Unless he has elected otherwise, the Auditor-General of India becomes the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and is entitled to continue to hold office until the expiration of his term of office.

2773.question: Who does the Auditor-General of India become after the commencement of the Constitution, unless he chooses otherwise? And until when can he hold the office?
2773.answer: The Auditor-General of India becomes the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and can hold office until the expiration of his term of office.

2774.question: What happens to the members of the Public Service Commission for the Dominion of India after the commencement of this Constitution?
2774.answer: Unless they have elected otherwise, they become the members of the Public Service Commission for the Union.

2775.question: Who becomes the members of the Public Service Commission for the Union after the commencement of the Constitution, if they haven't elected otherwise?
2775.answer: The members of the Public Service Commission for the Dominion of India become the members of the Public Service Commission for the Union unless they have elected otherwise.

2776.question: What happens to the members of a Public Service Commission of a Province or a Public Service Commission serving the needs of a group of Provinces before the commencement of the Constitution?
2776.answer: Unless they have elected otherwise, they become the members of the Public Service Commission for the corresponding State or the members of the Joint State Public Service Commission serving the needs of the corresponding States, and continue to hold office until the expiration of their term of office as determined under the rules which were applicable immediately before such commencement.

2777.question: What is the fate of the members of a Public Service Commission of a Province or a Public Service Commission serving the needs of a group of Provinces if they have not elected otherwise before the commencement of the Constitution?
2777.answer: They become the members of the Public Service Commission for the corresponding State or the members of the Joint State Public Service Commission serving the needs of the corresponding States, and continue to hold office until the expiration of their term of office as determined under the rules which were applicable immediately before such commencement.

2778.question: What is the duration of Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly as per the special provision?
2778.answer: Unless sooner dissolved, it will continue for a period of five years from the date referred to in section 29 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, and no longer. The expiration of the said period shall operate as a dissolution of that Legislative Assembly.

2779.question: What happens to the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly after the expiration of the five-year period from the date referred to in section 29 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
2779.answer: The expiration of the said period operates as a dissolution of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.

2780.question: What power does the President have in regards to removing difficulties in the transition from the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935, to the provisions of the Constitution?
2780.answer: The President may, for the purpose of removing any difficulties, by order direct that this Constitution shall, during such period as may be specified.

2781.question: What can the President do to remove any difficulties during a specified period while transitioning from the Government of India Act, 1935, to the Constitution?
2781.answer: The President may, for the purpose of removing any difficulties, by order direct that this Constitution shall, during such period as may be specified.

2782.question: What powers does the President have according to this text?
2782.answer: The powers conferred on the President by this article, by article 324, by clause (3) of article 367 and by article 391.

2783.question: According to this text, which articles and clauses confer powers on the President?
2783.answer: The powers conferred on the President by this article, by article 324, by clause (3) of article 367 and by article 391.

2784.question: Who can exercise the powers of the President before the commencement of the Constitution?
2784.answer: The Governor-General of the Dominion of India.

2785.question: Before the commencement of the Constitution, whose role was it to exercise the powers of the President?
2785.answer: The Governor-General of the Dominion of India.

2786.question: What is the short title of the Constitution according to Part XXII?
2786.answer: This Constitution may be called the Constitution of India.

2787.question: What does 'This Constitution may be called the Constitution of India' refer to in Part XXII?
2787.answer: It refers to the short title of the Constitution.

2788.question: When will the remaining provisions of this Constitution come into force?
2788.answer: On the twenty-sixth day of January, 1950.

2789.question: What significant event in the Constitution took place on the twenty-sixth day of January, 1950?
2789.answer: The remaining provisions of the Constitution came into force.

2790.question: What is the purpose of the authoritative text in the Hindi language?
2790.answer: The President shall cause to be published under his authority the translation of this Constitution in the Hindi language, signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, with such modifications as may be necessary to bring it in conformity with the language, style and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of Central Acts in the Hindi language, and incorporating therein all the amendments of this Constitution made before such publication.

2791.question: Who is responsible for publishing the translation of the Constitution in the Hindi language and what does it incorporate?
2791.answer: The President is responsible for publishing the translation of the Constitution in the Hindi language, ensuring it is in conformity with the language, style, and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of Central Acts in Hindi, and incorporating all the amendments made before such publication.

2792.question: Who is responsible for the translation of the Constitution and every amendment in Hindi language?
2792.answer: The President is responsible for the translation of the Constitution and every amendment in Hindi language.

2793.question: Who is responsible for translating the Constitution and all its amendments into the Hindi language?

2794.question: What is considered the authoritative text of the Constitution and its amendments?
2794.answer: The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof published under this article shall be deemed to be, for all purposes, the authoritative text thereof in the Hindi language.

2795.question: What is deemed to be the authoritative text of the Constitution and its amendments in the Hindi language?
2795.answer: The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof published under this article is considered the authoritative text in the Hindi language.

2796.question: What acts were repealed by the Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935?
2796.answer: The Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or supplementing the latter Act, but not including the Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949, are hereby repealed.

2797.question: Which acts are repealed by the Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or supplementing the latter Act, but not including the Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949?
2797.answer: The Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935 were repealed.

2798.question: What are the territories of Andhra Pradesh according to the First Schedule?
2798.answer: The territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Andhra State Act, 1953, sub-section (1) of section 3 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, the First Schedule to the Andhra Pradesh and Madras (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1959, and the Schedule to the Andhra Pradesh and Mysore (Transfer of Territory) Act, 1968, but excluding the territories specified in the Second Schedule to the Andhra Pradesh and Madras (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1959.

2799.question: Which Acts and Schedules specify the territories of Andhra Pradesh, and which territories are excluded?
2799.answer: The territories of Andhra Pradesh are specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Andhra State Act, 1953, sub-section (1) of section 3 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, the First Schedule to the Andhra Pradesh and Madras (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1959, and the Schedule to the Andhra Pradesh and Mysore (Transfer of Territory) Act, 1968. However, the territories specified in the Second Schedule to the Andhra Pradesh and Madras (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1959 are excluded.

2800.question: What are the territories of Assam according to the First Schedule?
2800.answer: The territories which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution were comprised in the Province of Assam, the Khasi States and the Assam Tribal Areas, but excluding the territories specified in the Schedule to the Assam (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1951 and the territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the State of Nagaland Act, 1962 and the territories specified in sections 5, 6 and 7 of the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971 and the territories referred to in Part I of the Second Schedule to the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015, notwithstanding anything contained in clause (a) of section 3 of the Constitution (Ninth Amendment) Act, 1960, so far as it relates to the territories referred to in Part I of the Second Schedule to the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015.

2801.question: Which territories were immediately before the commencement of this Constitution were comprised in the Province of Assam, the Khasi States, and the Assam Tribal Areas, but excluding the territories specified in the Schedule to the Assam (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1951 and the territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the State of Nagaland Act, 1962 and the territories specified in sections 5, 6 and 7 of the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971 and the territories referred to in Part I of the Second Schedule to the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015, notwithstanding anything contained in clause (a) of section 3 of the Constitution (Ninth Amendment) Act, 1960, so far as it relates to the territories referred to in Part I of the Second Schedule to the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015?
2801.answer: These are the territories of Assam according to the First Schedule.

2802.question: What territories does Bihar comprise of according to the text?
2802.answer: The territories comprised in the Province of Bihar include those specified in clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1968, but excluding the territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Bihar and West Bengal (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1956, and the territories specified in clause (b) of subsection (1) of section 3 of the first mentioned Act and the territories specified in section 3 of the Bihar Reorganisation Act, 2000.

2803.question: Which act and clause specifies the territories comprised in the Province of Bihar? And which territories are excluded according to the same?
2803.answer: The territories comprised in the Province of Bihar are specified in clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1968. The territories excluded are those specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Bihar and West Bengal (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1956, the territories specified in clause (b) of subsection (1) of section 3 of the first mentioned Act and the territories specified in section 3 of the Bihar Reorganisation Act, 2000.

2804.question: What territories are included in Gujarat according to the text?
2804.answer: The territories referred to in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Bombay Reorganisation Act, 1960.

2805.question: According to the Bombay Reorganisation Act, 1960, what territories does sub-section (1) of section 3 refer to?
2805.answer: It refers to the territories included in Gujarat.

2806.question: What territories are included in Kerala according to the text?
2806.answer: The territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

2807.question: Which Act specifies the territories included in Kerala in its sub-section (1) of section 5?

2808.question: What territories are included in Madhya Pradesh according to the text?
2808.answer: The territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 9 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the First Schedule to the Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1959, but excluding the territories specified in section 3 of the Madhya Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000.

2809.question: Which legal documents and sections specify the territories included in Madhya Pradesh?
2809.answer: The territories are specified in sub-section (1) of section 9 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the First Schedule to the Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1959, but not the territories specified in section 3 of the Madhya Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000.

2810.question: What territories are included in Tamil Nadu according to the text?
2810.answer: The territories which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution were either comprised in the Province of Madras or were being administered as if they formed part of that Province and the territories specified in section 4 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, and the Second Schedule to the Andhra Pradesh and Madras (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1959, but excluding the territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 and sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Andhra State Act, 1953 and the territories specified in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 5, section 6 and clause (d) of sub-section (1) of section 7 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the territories specified in the First Schedule to the Andhra Pradesh and Madras (Alteration of Boundaries) Act.

2811.question: Which territories were either comprised in the Province of Madras or were being administered as if they formed part of that Province before the commencement of this Constitution, and are specified in section 4 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, and the Second Schedule to the Andhra Pradesh and Madras (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1959, but excluding the territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 and sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Andhra State Act, 1953 and the territories specified in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 5, section 6 and clause (d) of sub-section (1) of section 7 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the territories specified in the First Schedule to the Andhra Pradesh and Madras (Alteration of Boundaries) Act?
2811.answer: These territories are included in Tamil Nadu.

2812.question: What territories does Odisha consist of according to the constitution of India?
2812.answer: The territories which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution were either comprised in the Province of Odisha or were being administered as if they formed part of that Province.

2813.question: Which territories were either comprised in the Province of Odisha or were being administered as if they formed part of that Province before the commencement of the Constitution of India?
2813.answer: Odisha consists of these territories according to the constitution of India.

2814.question: What territories are excluded from Punjab as per the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the Acquired Territories (Merger) Act, 1960?
2814.answer: The territories referred to in Part II of the First Schedule to the Constitution (Ninth Amendment) Act, 1960 and the territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3, section 4 and sub-section (1) of section 5 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966.

2815.question: Which territories are referred to in Part II of the First Schedule to the Constitution (Ninth Amendment) Act, 1960 and the territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3, section 4 and sub-section (1) of section 5 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966?
2815.answer: These are the territories that are excluded from Punjab as per the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the Acquired Territories (Merger) Act, 1960.

2816.question: What territories does Rajasthan consist of?
2816.answer: The territories specified in section 10 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 but excluding the territories specified in the First Schedule to the Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1959.

2817.question: Which act specifies the territories that Rajasthan consists of, and which act excludes certain territories from it?
2817.answer: The territories of Rajasthan are specified in section 10 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, but the territories specified in the First Schedule to the Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1959 are excluded.

2818.question: What territories are included in Uttar Pradesh?
2818.answer: The territories which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution were either comprised in the Province known as the United Provinces or were being administered as if they formed part of that Province, the territories specified in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1968, and the territories specified in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1979.

2819.question: Which territories immediately before the commencement of the Constitution, were either comprised in the Province known as the United Provinces or were being administered as if they formed part of that Province, and which territories are specified in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1968, and in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1979?
2819.answer: These territories are included in Uttar Pradesh.

2820.question: What territories are excluded from Uttar Pradesh?
2820.answer: The territories specified in clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1979.

2821.question: Which clause of what act specifies the territories excluded from Uttar Pradesh?
2821.answer: Clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1979 specifies the territories excluded from Uttar Pradesh.

2822.question: What territories does West Bengal comprise of?
2822.answer: The territories which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution were either comprised in the Province of West Bengal or were being administered as if they formed part of that Province and the territory of Chandernagore as defined in clause (c) of section 2 of the Chandernagore (Merger) Act, 1954 and also the territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Bihar and West Bengal (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1956 and also the territories referred to in Part III of the First Schedule but excluding the territories referred to in Part III of the Second Schedule to the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015, notwithstanding anything contained in clause (c) of section 3 of the Constitution (Ninth Amendment) Act, 1960, so far as it relates to the territories referred to in Part III of the First Schedule and the territories referred to in Part III of the Second Schedule to the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015

2823.question: Which territories were immediately before the commencement of the Constitution either comprised in the Province of West Bengal or were being administered as if they formed part of that Province, and what are the territories specified in clause (c) of section 2 of the Chandernagore (Merger) Act, 1954, sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Bihar and West Bengal (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1956, and in Part III of the First Schedule, excluding the territories referred to in Part III of the Second Schedule to the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015?
2823.answer: These territories comprise of West Bengal.

2824.question: What territory did Jammu and Kashmir comprise of before the commencement of this Constitution?
2824.answer: The territory which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution was comprised in the Indian State of Jammu and Kashmir.

2825.question: What was the territory comprised in the Indian State of Jammu and Kashmir immediately before the commencement of the Constitution?

2826.question: What territories does Nagaland comprise of?
2826.answer: The territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the State of Nagaland Act, 1962.

2828.question: What territories does Haryana comprise of?
2828.answer: The territories specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 and the territories specified in clause (a) of subsection (1) of section 4 of the Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1979, but excluding the territories specified in clause (v) of sub-section.

2829.question: Which act and sections specify the territories of Haryana?
2829.answer: The territories of Haryana are specified in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 and the territories specified in clause (a) of subsection (1) of section 4 of the Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1979.

2830.question: What territories were being administered as Chief Commissioners’ Provinces under the names of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur before the commencement of the Indian Constitution?
2830.answer: The territories which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution were being administered as if they were Chief Commissioners’ Provinces under the names of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur.

2831.question: What is the status of the territories which immediately before the commencement of the Indian Constitution were being administered as if they were Chief Commissioners’ Provinces under the names of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur?
2831.answer: These territories were being administered as Chief Commissioners’ Provinces under the names of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur before the commencement of the Indian Constitution.

2832.question: What territory was being administered as a Chief Commissioner’s Province under the name of Manipur before the commencement of the Indian Constitution?
2832.answer: The territory which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution was being administered as if it were a Chief Commissioner’s Province under the name of Manipur.

2833.question: What is the name of the territory that was administered as if it were a Chief Commissioner’s Province immediately before the commencement of the Indian Constitution?

2834.question: What territory was being administered as a Chief Commissioner’s Province under the name of Tripura before the commencement of the Indian Constitution?
2834.answer: The territory which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution was being administered as if it were a Chief Commissioner’s Province under the name of Tripura.

2835.question: What was the status of the territory known as Tripura before the commencement of the Indian Constitution?
2835.answer: It was being administered as a Chief Commissioner’s Province.

2836.question: What territories does the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015 refer to?
2836.answer: The territories referred to in Part II of the First Schedule to the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015.

2837.question: Which act refers to the territories in Part II of the First Schedule?

2838.question: What territories were comprised in Sikkim before the commencement of the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975?
2838.answer: The territories which immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975, were comprised in Sikkim.

2839.question: Which territories, immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act 1975, were included in Sikkim?
2839.answer: The territories which were included in Sikkim before the commencement of the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975 are the same territories that were comprised in Sikkim.

2840.question: What territories are specified in section 3 of the Goa, Daman and Diu Reorganisation Act, 1987?
2840.answer: The territories specified in section 3 of the Goa, Daman and Diu Reorganisation Act, 1987.

2841.question: In which section of the Goa, Daman and Diu Reorganisation Act, 1987 are the territories specified?
2841.answer: The territories are specified in section 3 of the Goa, Daman and Diu Reorganisation Act, 1987.

2842.question: What territories are specified in section 3 of the Madhya Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000?
2842.answer: The territories specified in section 3 of the Madhya Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000.

2843.question: Which Act specifies the territories in its section 3?

2844.question: What territories are specified in section 3 of the Uttar Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000?
2844.answer: The territories specified in section 3 of the Uttar Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000.

2845.question: Which section of the Uttar Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000 specifies the territories?
2845.answer: Section 3 of the Uttar Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000 specifies the territories.

2846.question: What is the territory of Delhi according to the constitution?
2846.answer: The territory which immediately before the commencement of this Constitution was comprised in the Chief Commissioner’s Province of Delhi.

2848.question: What is the territory of The Andaman and Nicobar Islands according to the constitution?

2852.answer: The territory which immediately before the eleventh day of August, 1961 was comprised in Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

2853.answer: It became the territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
