2860.question: What allowances are paid to the President and to the Governors of the States according to the constitution?
2860.answer: Such allowances as were payable respectively to the Governor-General of the Dominion of India and to the Governors of the corresponding Provinces immediately before the commencement of this Constitution.

2861.question: What allowances were payable respectively to the Governor-General of the Dominion of India and to the Governors of the corresponding Provinces immediately before the commencement of the Constitution?
2861.answer: Those allowances are now paid to the President and to the Governors of the States according to the constitution.

2862.question: What privileges are the President and the Governors of the States entitled to according to the constitution?
2862.answer: They shall be entitled to the same privileges to which the Governor General and the Governors of the corresponding Provinces were respectively entitled immediately before the commencement of this Constitution.

2863.question: Who is entitled to the same privileges as the Governor General and the Governors of the corresponding Provinces were entitled to immediately before the commencement of the Constitution?
2863.answer: The President and the Governors of the States are entitled to these privileges according to the constitution.

2864.question: What is the entitlement of a person who discharges the functions of the Governor?
2864.answer: The person shall be entitled to the same emoluments, allowances and privileges as the President or the Governor.

2865.question: Who is entitled to the same emoluments, allowances, and privileges as the President or the Governor?
2865.answer: A person who discharges the functions of the Governor is entitled to the same emoluments, allowances, and privileges as the President or the Governor.

2866.question: Who are the positions mentioned in Part C of the provisions?
2866.answer: The positions are the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the House of the People, the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, and the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, and the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council of a State.

2867.question: Which positions does the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the House of the People, the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, and the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, and the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council of a State refer to in the provisions?
2867.answer: These positions are mentioned in Part C of the provisions.

2868.question: What are the salaries and allowances of the Speaker of the House of People and the Chairman of the Council of States?
2868.answer: Their salaries and allowances are the same as what were payable to the Speaker of the Constituent Assembly of the Dominion of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution.

2869.question: Who receives the same salaries and allowances as the Speaker of the Constituent Assembly of the Dominion of India did immediately before the commencement of the Constitution?
2869.answer: The Speaker of the House of People and the Chairman of the Council of States receive the same salaries and allowances.

2870.question: What are the salaries and allowances of the Deputy Speaker of the House of the People and the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States?
2870.answer: Their salaries and allowances are the same as what were payable to the Deputy Speaker of the Constituent Assembly of the Dominion of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution.

2871.question: Who receives the same salaries and allowances as the Deputy Speaker of the Constituent Assembly of the Dominion of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution?
2871.answer: The Deputy Speaker of the House of the People and the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States receive the same salaries and allowances.

2872.question: What are the salaries and allowances of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council of a State?
2872.answer: Their salaries and allowances are the same as what were payable respectively to the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and the President and the Deputy President of the Legislative Council of the corresponding Province immediately before the commencement of this Constitution.

2873.question: What is the basis for the salaries and allowances of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council of a State?
2873.answer: Their salaries and allowances are the same as what were payable respectively to the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and the President and the Deputy President of the Legislative Council of the corresponding Province immediately before the commencement of this Constitution.

2874.question: What is the salary for the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, as per the document?
2874.answer: 10,000 rupees, but it has been updated to 1,00,000 rupees as of 2009

2875.question: What was the original salary of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court and what is it updated to as of 2009?
2875.answer: The original salary was 10,000 rupees, but it has been updated to 1,00,000 rupees as of 2009

2876.question: What is the salary for any other Judge of the Supreme Court, as per the document?
2876.answer: 9,000 rupees, but it has been updated to 90,000 rupees as of 2009

2877.question: What was the updated salary for a Supreme Court Judge in 2009, and what was it previously?
2877.answer: The updated salary for a Supreme Court Judge in 2009 was 90,000 rupees, up from the previous salary of 9,000 rupees.

2878.question: How is the salary of a Judge of the Supreme Court affected if they receive a pension or retirement gratuity?
2878.answer: Their salary is reduced by the amount of the pension or the pension equivalent of the retirement gratuity.

2879.question: What happens to the salary of a Supreme Court Judge if they are receiving a pension or retirement gratuity?
2879.answer: Their salary is reduced by the amount of the pension or the pension equivalent of the retirement gratuity.

2880.question: What are the judges of the Supreme Court entitled to, regarding their residence?
2880.answer: Every Judge of the Supreme Court is entitled to the use of an official residence without payment of rent.

2881.question: Who is entitled to the use of an official residence without payment of rent?
2881.answer: Every Judge of the Supreme Court is entitled to this.

2882.question: Who are the exceptions to the sub-paragraph (2) regarding the official residence?
2882.answer: A Judge who was holding office as the Chief Justice of the Federal Court or any other Judge of the Federal Court at the time of the commencement of this Constitution.

2883.question: What position was held by the person who is an exception to the sub-paragraph (2) regarding the official residence at the time of the commencement of the Constitution?
2883.answer: The position was held by a Judge who was the Chief Justice of the Federal Court or any other Judge of the Federal Court.

2884.question: Who is entitled to receive special pay in addition to their salary?
2884.answer: The Chief Justice or other Judge of the Supreme Court who has spent time on actual service.

2885.question: What additional benefits does the Chief Justice or other Judge of the Supreme Court receive after spending time on actual service?
2885.answer: They are entitled to receive special pay in addition to their salary.

2886.question: What allowances do Judges of the Supreme Court receive?
2886.answer: They receive reasonable allowances to reimburse for expenses incurred in travelling on duty within the territory of India.

2887.question: Who receives reasonable allowances to reimburse for expenses incurred in travelling on duty within the territory of India?
2887.answer: Judges of the Supreme Court receive these allowances.

2888.question: Who determines the travelling facilities for the Judges of the Supreme Court?
2888.answer: The President prescribes the travelling facilities.

2889.question: Who prescribes the travelling facilities for the Judges of the Supreme Court?

2890.question: What governs the rights in respect of leave of absence and pension of the Judges of the Supreme Court?
2890.answer: The provisions which, immediately before the commencement of this Constitution, were applicable to the Judges of the Federal Court.

2891.question: What were applied to the Judges of the Federal Court that now governs the rights in respect of leave of absence and pension of the Judges of the Supreme Court?
2891.answer: The provisions which, immediately before the commencement of this Constitution

2892.question: What is the salary of the Chief Justice and any other Judge of the High Court?
2892.answer: The Chief Justice receives 90,000 rupees and any other Judge receives 80,000 rupees.

2893.question: Who receives a salary of 90,000 rupees and who receives 80,000 rupees in the High Court?
2893.answer: The Chief Justice receives 90,000 rupees and any other Judge receives 80,000 rupees.

2894.question: What happens to the salary of a Judge of a High Court if they are in receipt of a pension at the time of their appointment?
2894.answer: Their salary in respect of service in the High Court shall be reduced by the amount of that pension.

2895.question: What is the effect on the salary of a High Court Judge if they are receiving a pension at the time of their appointment?
2895.answer: Their salary in respect of service in the High Court shall be reduced by the amount of that pension.

2896.question: Who will be entitled to receive an amount equivalent to the difference between their current salary and the salary they were drawing before the commencement of the Constitution?
2896.answer: Every person who was holding office as the Chief Justice of a High Court or any other Judge of a High Court and has become the Chief Justice or a Judge of the High Court in the corresponding State under clause (1) of article 376, if they were drawing a salary at a higher rate before the commencement of the Constitution.

2897.question: Who is the person that was holding office as the Chief Justice of a High Court or any other Judge of a High Court and has become the Chief Justice or a Judge of the High Court in the corresponding State under clause (1) of article 376, and was drawing a salary at a higher rate before the commencement of the Constitution?
2897.answer: This person is entitled to receive an amount equivalent to the difference between their current salary and the salary they were drawing before the commencement of the Constitution.

2898.question: Who will be entitled to receive the same amount as allowance in addition to the salary specified in sub-paragraph (1), if they were drawing an allowance before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956?
2898.answer: Any person who was holding office as the Chief Justice of the High Court of a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule and has become the Chief Justice of the High Court of a State specified in the amended Schedule by the Act.

2899.question: Who was holding office as the Chief Justice of the High Court of a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule and has become the Chief Justice of the High Court of a State specified in the amended Schedule by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, and is entitled to receive the same amount as allowance in addition to the salary if they were drawing an allowance before the commencement of the Act?

2900.question: What happens to the pension of a person in relation to their previous service if they have commuted the value thereof before their appointment?
2900.answer: It will be reduced by the amount of that portion of the pension.

2901.question: What will happen to the pension of a person who has commuted the value of their previous service before their appointment?
2901.answer: It will be reduced by the amount of that portion of the pension.

2902.question: What happens if a person has received a retirement gratuity in respect of their previous service before such appointment?
2902.answer: It will be reduced by the pension equivalent of that gratuity.

2903.question: What happens to the retirement gratuity a person has received from their previous service when they receive a pension?
2903.answer: The retirement gratuity will be reduced by the pension equivalent of that gratuity.

2904.question: What does the expression 'Chief Justice' include?
2904.answer: The expression 'Chief Justice' includes an acting Chief Justice.

2905.question: What is included in the role of an acting Chief Justice?
2905.answer: The role of an acting Chief Justice is included in the expression 'Chief Justice'.

2906.question: What is included in the term 'Judge'?
2906.answer: The term 'Judge' includes an ad hoc Judge.

2907.question: What term includes an ad hoc Judge?
2907.answer: The term 'Judge' includes an ad hoc Judge.

2908.question: What does 'actual service' include for a Judge?
2908.answer: Actual service includes time spent by a Judge on duty as a Judge or in the performance of such other functions as he may at the request of the President undertake to discharge, vacations excluding any time during which the Judge is absent on leave, and joining time on transfer from a High Court to the Supreme Court or from one High Court to another.

2909.question: What is meant by a Judge's time on duty, performance of other functions at the request of the President, vacations excluding leave time, and joining time on transfer from one court to another?
2909.answer: These terms refer to 'actual service' for a Judge.

2910.question: What is the salary of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India?
2910.answer: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India shall be paid a salary at the rate of four thousand rupees per mensem.

2911.question: Who receives a salary at the rate of four thousand rupees per mensem in India?
2911.answer: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India receives a salary at the rate of four thousand rupees per mensem.

2912.question: What additional pay is the person, who was holding office immediately before the commencement of this Constitution as Auditor-General of India, entitled to?
2912.answer: The person who was holding office immediately before the commencement of this Constitution as Auditor-General of India and has become on such commencement the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India under article 377 shall in addition to the salary specified in sub-paragraph (1) be entitled to receive as special pay an amount equivalent to the difference between the salary so specified and the salary which he was drawing as Auditor-General of India immediately before such commencement.

2913.question: Who is entitled to receive as special pay an amount equivalent to the difference between the salary so specified and the salary which he was drawing as Auditor-General of India immediately before the commencement of the Constitution?
2913.answer: The person who was holding office immediately before the commencement of this Constitution as Auditor-General of India and has become on such commencement the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India under article 377 is entitled to this additional pay.

2914.question: What governs the rights in respect of leave of absence and pension and the other conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India?
2914.answer: The rights in respect of leave of absence and pension and the other conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India shall be governed or shall continue to be governed, as the case may be, by the provisions which were applicable to the Auditor-General of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution and all references in those provisions to the Governor-General shall be construed as references to the President.

2915.question: Which provisions govern the rights in respect of leave of absence and pension and other conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, and to whom do references to the Governor-General in those provisions now refer?
2915.answer: The rights in respect of leave of absence and pension and the other conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India are governed by the provisions which were applicable to the Auditor-General of India immediately before the commencement of this Constitution. All references in those provisions to the Governor-General are now construed as references to the President.

2916.question: What is the salary of the Judges of the Supreme Court?
2916.answer: The salary of Judges of the Supreme Court has been raised to Rs.90,000 per mensem.

2917.question: What has been the recent increase in the salary of the Judges of the Supreme Court?
2917.answer: The salary of Judges of the Supreme Court has been raised to Rs.90,000 per mensem.

2918.question: What is the form of oath of office for a Minister for the Union?
2918.answer: “I, A. B., do swear in the name of God that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, that I will faithfully and conscientiously discharge my duties as a Minister for the Union and that I will do right to all manner of people in accordance with the Constitution and the law, without fear or favour, affection or ill-will.”

2919.question: Who swears, 'I, A. B., do swear in the name of God that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, that I will faithfully and conscientiously discharge my duties as a Minister for the Union and that I will do right to all manner of people in accordance with the Constitution and the law, without fear or favour, affection or ill-will'?

2920.question: What is the form of oath of secrecy for a Minister for the Union?
2920.answer: “I, A.B., do swear in the name of God that I will not directly or indirectly communicate or reveal to any person or persons any matter which shall be brought under my consideration or shall become known to me as a Minister for the Union except as may be required for the due discharge of my duties as such Minister.”

2921.question: What is the oath that states 'I, A.B., do swear in the name of God that I will not directly or indirectly communicate or reveal to any person or persons any matter which shall be brought under my consideration or shall become known to me as a Minister for the Union except as may be required for the due discharge of my duties as such Minister'?
2921.answer: It is the form of oath of secrecy for a Minister for the Union.

2922.question: What is the form of oath or affirmation to be made by a candidate for election to Parliament?
2922.answer: “I, A.B., having been nominated as a candidate to fill a seat in the Council of States (or the House of the People) do swear in the name of God that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established and that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India.”

2923.question: What does candidate A.B. swear to uphold when nominated to fill a seat in the Council of States or the House of the People in India?
2923.answer: Candidate A.B. swears to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established and to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India.

2924.question: What is the form of oath or affirmation to be made by a member of Parliament?
2924.answer: “I, A.B., having been elected (or nominated) a member of the Council of States (or the House of the People) do swear in the name of God that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India and that I will faithfully discharge the duty upon which I am about to enter.”

2925.question: What does A.B., a member of the Council of States (or the House of the People), swear to uphold and bear true faith to after being elected or nominated?
2925.answer: A.B. swears in the name of God that he will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India and faithfully discharge the duty upon which he is about to enter.

2926.question: What is the form of oath or affirmation to be made by the Judges of the Supreme Court and the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India?
2926.answer: “I, A.B., having been appointed Chief Justice (or a Judge) of the Supreme Court of India (or Comptroller and Auditor-General of India) do swear in the name of God that I will bear true faith and solemnly affirm faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, that I will duly and faithfully and to the best of my ability, knowledge and judgment perform the duties of my office without fear or favour, affection or ill-will and that I will uphold the Constitution and the laws.”

2927.question: Who is required to swear in the name of God to uphold the Constitution and laws of India, bear true faith and allegiance, uphold sovereignty and integrity, and perform their duties without fear, favour, affection or ill-will?
2927.answer: The Judges of the Supreme Court and the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India are required to make this oath or affirmation.

2928.question: What is the form of oath of office for a Minister for a State?
2928.answer: “I, A.B., do swear in the name of God that I will bear true faith solemnly affirm and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, that I will faithfully and conscientiously discharge my duties as a Minister for the State of ..........and that I will do right to all manner of people in accordance with the Constitution and the law without fear or favour, affection or ill-will.”

2929.question: What does Minister for a State swear to uphold and discharge in his oath of office?
2929.answer: The Minister for a State swears to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, faithfully and conscientiously discharge his duties as a Minister for the State, and to do right to all manner of people in accordance with the Constitution and the law without fear or favour, affection or ill-will.

2930.question: What is the form of oath of secrecy for a Minister for a State?
2930.answer: “I, A.B., do swear in the name of God that I will not directly or solemnly affirm indirectly communicate or reveal to any person or persons any matter which shall be brought under my consideration or shall become known to me as a Minister for the State of ....................except as may be required for the due discharge of my duties as such Minister.”

2931.question: What does a Minister for a State swear or affirm not to do in their oath of secrecy?
2931.answer: A Minister for a State swears or affirms not to directly or indirectly communicate or reveal to any person or persons any matter which shall be brought under their consideration or shall become known to them, except as may be required for the due discharge of their duties as such Minister.

2932.question: What is the form of oath or affirmation to be made by a candidate for election to the Legislature of a State?
2932.answer: “I, A.B., having been nominated as a candidate to fill a seat in the Legislative Assembly (or Legislative Council), do swear in the name of God that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established.

2933.question: What does A.B. swear to do in the oath taken when nominated as a candidate for the Legislative Assembly (or Legislative Council) in India?
2933.answer: A.B. swears to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established.

2934.question: What is the form of oath or affirmation to be made by a member of the Legislature of a State in India?
2934.answer: "I, A.B., having been elected (or nominated) a member of the Legislative Assembly (or Legislative Council), do swear in the name of God that solemnly affirm I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India and that I will faithfully discharge the duty upon which I am about to enter."

2935.question: Who says the oath 'I, A.B., having been elected (or nominated) a member of the Legislative Assembly (or Legislative Council), do swear in the name of God that solemnly affirm I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India and that I will faithfully discharge the duty upon which I am about to enter'?
2935.answer: A member of the Legislature of a State in India

2936.question: What is the form of oath or affirmation to be made by the Judges of a High Court in India?
2936.answer: "I, A.B., having been appointed Chief Justice (or a Judge) of the High Court at (or of) ………-….. do swear in the name of God that I will bear solemnly affirm true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, that I will duly and faithfully and to the best of my ability, knowledge and judgment perform the duties of my office without fear or favour, affection or ill-will and that I will uphold the Constitution and the laws."

2937.question: What does a Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court in India swear to uphold and perform during their oath or affirmation?
2937.answer: During their oath or affirmation, a Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court in India swears to bear solemnly affirm true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, perform the duties of their office without fear or favour, affection or ill-will and uphold the Constitution and the laws.

3000.answer: The Governor of each State having Scheduled Areas

3001.question: What is the role of the Governor of each State having Scheduled Areas in relation to the President?
3001.answer: They are responsible for making a report to the President regarding the administration of Scheduled Areas

3002.question: What is the Tribes Advisory Council?
3002.answer: The Tribes Advisory Council is a body established in each State having Scheduled Areas and, if directed by the President, also in any State having Scheduled Tribes but not Scheduled Areas. It consists of not more than twenty members, three-fourths of whom should be representatives of the Scheduled Tribes in the State's Legislative Assembly. The council's duty is to advise on matters related to the welfare and advancement of the Scheduled Tribes in the State.

3003.question: What is the composition of the Tribes Advisory Council and what are its duties?
3003.answer: The Tribes Advisory Council consists of not more than twenty members, three-fourths of whom should be representatives of the Scheduled Tribes in the State's Legislative Assembly. The council's duty is to advise on matters related to the welfare and advancement of the Scheduled Tribes in the State.

3004.question: What happens if the number of representatives of Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assembly is less than the number of seats in the Tribes Advisory Council?
3004.answer: If the number of representatives of the Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assembly of the State is less than the number of seats in the Tribes Advisory Council to be filled by such representatives, the remaining seats shall be filled by other members of those tribes.

3054.question: What is the constitution of District Councils and Regional Councils?
3054.answer: There shall be a District Council for each autonomous district consisting of not more than thirty members, of whom not more than four persons shall be nominated by the Governor and the rest shall be elected on the basis of adult suffrage. 3150.answer: Yes, the President may direct the Governor to return the law to the Bodoland Territorial Council, along with a message requesting reconsideration or amendments.

3151.question: Who can direct the Governor to return the law to the Bodoland Territorial Council along with a message requesting reconsideration or amendments?
3151.answer: The President can direct the Governor to return the law to the Bodoland Territorial Council along with a message requesting reconsideration or amendments.

3152.question: What is the time period for the Council to reconsider a returned law?
3152.answer: The Council should reconsider the law within a period of six months.

3153.question: Within what period should the Council reconsider a law that has been returned?
3153.answer: The Council should reconsider the law within a period of six months.

3154.question: What is a 'reserved forest' according to the Constitution of India?
3154.answer: A 'reserved forest' is any area which is a reserved forest under the Assam Forest Regulation, 1891, or under any other law for the time being in force in the area in question.

3155.question: Under which law or regulation is an area considered a 'reserved forest' in India?
3155.answer: An area is considered a 'reserved forest' under the Assam Forest Regulation, 1891, or under any other law for the time being in force in the area in question.

3156.question: What happens to laws made under paragraph 3 of the Constitution of India?
3156.answer: All laws made under paragraph 3 shall be submitted forthwith to the Governor and, until assented to by him, shall have no effect.

3157.question: To whom shall laws made under paragraph 3 of the Constitution of India be submitted and when do they take effect?
3157.answer: All laws made under paragraph 3 are submitted forthwith to the Governor and they take effect only after being assented to by him.

3158.question: Who can constitute village councils or courts for the trial of suits and cases in autonomous regions?
3158.answer: The Regional Council for an autonomous region in respect of areas within such region and the District Council for an autonomous district in respect of areas within the district can constitute village councils or courts for the trial of suits and cases.

3159.question: Who can constitute village councils or courts for the trial of suits and cases in areas within an autonomous region or an autonomous district?
3159.answer: The Regional Council for an autonomous region and the District Council for an autonomous district can constitute village councils or courts for the trial of suits and cases in areas within such region or district respectively.

3160.question: Who exercises the powers of a court of appeal in respect of all suits and cases triable by a village council or court?
3160.answer: The Regional Council for an autonomous region or any court constituted in that behalf by the Regional Council or, if in respect of any area within an autonomous district there is no Regional Council, the District Council for such district, or any court constituted in that behalf by the District Council, shall exercise the powers of a court of appeal.

3161.question: Who is responsible for exercising the powers of a court of appeal in an area within an autonomous district where there is no Regional Council?
3161.answer: The District Council for such district, or any court constituted in that behalf by the District Council, is responsible for exercising the powers of a court of appeal.

3162.question: Which courts have jurisdiction over the suits or cases as mentioned in the text?
3162.answer: The High Court and the Supreme Court

3163.question: What suits or cases do the High Court and the Supreme Court have jurisdiction over as mentioned in the text?
3163.answer: The suits or cases mentioned in the text

3164.question: What changes have been made to paragraph 4 in its application to the State of Assam?
3164.answer: The Sixth Schedule to the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 2003 (44 of 2003), s. 2, inserted a new subparagraph after sub-paragraph (5)

3165.question: What was inserted after sub-paragraph (5) by the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 2003 (44 of 2003), s. 2 with respect to the State of Assam?
3165.answer: A new subparagraph was inserted in paragraph 4 in its application to the State of Assam.

3166.question: What is the purpose of the amendment made to paragraph 4 in its application to the State of Assam?
3166.answer: The amendment states that nothing in this paragraph shall apply to the Bodoland Territorial Council

3167.question: Which region is specified in the amendment to paragraph 4 as being exempt from its application in the State of Assam?

3168.question: What powers does a Regional Council or District Council have according to paragraph 4?
3168.answer: They can make rules regulating the constitution of village councils and courts, the procedure to be followed by village councils or courts, the enforcement of decisions and orders of such councils and courts, and all other ancillary matters for the carrying out of the provisions

3169.question: What responsibilities do Regional Councils or District Councils have in regulating village councils and courts, according to paragraph 4?
3169.answer: They have the power to make rules regulating the constitution of village councils and courts, the procedure to be followed by village councils or courts, the enforcement of decisions and orders of such councils and courts, and all other ancillary matters for the carrying out of the provisions.

3170.question: What happens when the President, after consulting the Government of the State concerned, appoints a date in relation to an autonomous district or region?
3170.answer: The paragraph will have effect in relation to such autonomous district or region as specified in the notification

3171.question: What is the effect of the President appointing a date for an autonomous district or region after consulting with the State Government?
3171.answer: The paragraph will have effect in relation to such autonomous district or region as specified in the notification

3172.question: What was substituted for the words in sub-paragraph (1) regarding parties belonging to Scheduled Tribes?
3172.answer: The words 'not being suits and cases of the nature referred to in sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph (5) of this Schedule, which the Governor may specify in this behalf,' had been substituted.

3173.question: What words were substituted in sub-paragraph (1) for parties belonging to Scheduled Tribes?
3173.answer: The words 'not being suits and cases of the nature referred to in sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph (5) of this Schedule, which the Governor may specify in this behalf,' were substituted.

3175.question: What was the action taken on sub-paragraphs (2) and (3)?

3176.answer: The words 'the Governor may make rules regulating' had been substituted.

3177.question: What words had been substituted for 'the Governor may make rules regulating' in sub-paragraph (4)?
3177.answer: The words 'A Regional Council or District Council, as the case may be, may with the previous approval of the Governor make rules regulating' were substituted.

3178.question: What was the substituted clause for clause (a) in sub-paragraph (4)?
3178.answer: The constitution of village councils and courts, the powers to be exercised by them under this paragraph and the courts to which appeals from the decisions of village councils and courts shall lie.

3179.question: What does the clause (a) in sub-paragraph (4) regarding the constitution of village councils and courts, the powers to be exercised by them under this paragraph and the courts to which appeals from the decisions of village councils and courts shall lie, substitute?
3179.answer: It was the substituted clause for clause (a) in sub-paragraph (4).

3180.question: What was the substituted clause for clause (c) in sub-paragraph (4)?
3180.answer: The transfer of appeals and other proceedings pending before the Regional or District Council or any court constituted by such Council immediately before the date appointed by the President under sub-paragraph (5).

3181.question: What clause was 'The transfer of appeals and other proceedings pending before the Regional or District Council or any court constituted by such Council immediately before the date appointed by the President under sub-paragraph (5)' used to replace?

3182.question: What was substituted in clause (e) in sub-paragraph (4)?
3182.answer: For the words, brackets and figures 'sub-paragraphs (1) and (2)', the word, brackets and figure 'sub-paragraph (1)' had been substituted.

3183.question: What were the changes made in clause (e) in sub-paragraph (4)?
3183.answer: For the words, brackets and figures 'sub-paragraphs (1) and (2)', the word, brackets and figure 'sub-paragraph (1)' had been substituted.

3184.question: What powers can the Governor confer under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898?
3184.answer: The Governor may, for the trial of suits or cases arising out of any law in force in any autonomous district or region being a law specified in that behalf by the Governor, or for the trial of offences punishable with death, transportation for life, or imprisonment.

3185.question: Under what circumstances may the Governor confer powers for the trial of suits or cases, according to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898?
3185.answer: The Governor may confer powers for the trial of suits or cases arising out of any law in force in any autonomous district or region being a law specified in that behalf by the Governor, or for the trial of offences punishable with death, transportation for life, or imprisonment.

3186.question: What powers can the Governor confer on the District Council or the Regional Council under the Indian Penal Code?
3186.answer: The Governor can confer on the District Council or the Regional Council powers under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, or the Code of Criminal Procedure, 18981, as he deems appropriate.

3187.question: Under which codes can the Governor confer powers on the District Council or the Regional Council, according to the Indian Penal Code?
3187.answer: The Governor can confer powers under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, or the Code of Criminal Procedure, 18981.

3188.question: Can the Governor withdraw or modify any of the powers conferred on a District Council, Regional Council, court or officer?
3188.answer: Yes, the Governor may withdraw or modify any of the powers conferred on a District Council, Regional Council, court or officer.

3189.question: Who has the authority to withdraw or modify any of the powers conferred on a District Council, Regional Council, court or officer?
3189.answer: The Governor has the authority to withdraw or modify any of the powers conferred on a District Council, Regional Council, court or officer.

3190.question: Do the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 18981, apply to the trial of any suits, cases or offences in an autonomous district or in any autonomous region?
3190.answer: Except as expressly provided in this paragraph, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 18981, shall not apply to the trial of any suits, cases or offences in an autonomous district or in any autonomous region.

3191.question: Do the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 18981, apply to the trial of any suits, cases or offences in an autonomous district or in any autonomous region without any express provision?
3191.answer: No, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 18981, do not apply to the trial of any suits, cases or offences in an autonomous district or in any autonomous region without any express provision.

3192.question: What cannot be done on and from the date appointed by the President in relation to any autonomous district or autonomous region?
3192.answer: On and from the date appointed by the President, nothing contained in this paragraph shall be deemed to authorise the Governor to confer on the District Council or Regional Council or on courts constituted by the District Council any of the powers referred to in sub-paragraph (1) of this paragraph.

3193.question: What is the implication of the date appointed by the President in relation to an autonomous district or region on the powers of the District Council, Regional Council, or courts constituted by the District Council?
3193.answer: On and from the date appointed by the President, nothing contained in this paragraph shall be deemed to authorise the Governor to confer on the District Council or Regional Council or on courts constituted by the District Council any of the powers referred to in sub-paragraph (1) of this paragraph.

3194.question: What powers does the District Council for an autonomous district have?
3194.answer: The District Council for an autonomous district may establish, construct, or manage primary schools, dispensaries, markets, cattle pounds, ferries, fisheries, roads, road transport and waterways in the district.

3195.question: What establishments and services may the District Council for an autonomous district establish, construct, or manage?
3195.answer: The District Council for an autonomous district may establish, construct, or manage primary schools, dispensaries, markets, cattle pounds, ferries, fisheries, roads, road transport and waterways in the district.

3196.question: Who can make regulations for the regulation and control of primary education in the district?

3197.question: Who has the authority to make regulations for the regulation and control of primary education in the district?

3198.question: What functions may the Governor entrust to the District Council or its officers?
3198.answer: Functions in relation to agriculture, animal husbandry, community projects, cooperative societies, social welfare, village planning or any other matter to which the executive power of the State extends.

3199.question: In relation to which areas can the District Council or its officers be entrusted with functions by the Governor?
3199.answer: The Governor may entrust functions to the District Council or its officers in relation to agriculture, animal husbandry, community projects, cooperative societies, social welfare, village planning or any other matter to which the executive power of the State extends.

3200.question: What funds are constituted for each autonomous district and region?
3200.answer: A District Fund and a Regional Fund

3201.question: What are the names of the funds constituted for an autonomous district and region?
3201.answer: A District Fund and a Regional Fund

3202.question: Who may make rules for the management of the District Fund or the Regional Fund?

3203.question: What role is responsible for making rules for the management of the District Fund or the Regional Fund?

3204.question: In what form shall the accounts of the District Council or the Regional Council be kept?
3204.answer: In such form as the Comptroller and Auditor General of India may, with the approval of the President, prescribe.

3205.question: Who prescribes the form in which the accounts of the District Council or the Regional Council are to be kept?
3205.answer: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India, with the approval of the President, prescribes the form.

3206.question: Who audits the accounts of the District and Regional Councils?

3207.question: What role does The Comptroller and Auditor-General play for the District and Regional Councils?
3207.answer: The Comptroller and Auditor-General audits the accounts of the District and Regional Councils.

3208.question: Who submits the audit reports of District and Regional Councils' accounts to?

3209.question: Who receives the audit reports of District and Regional Councils' accounts?

3210.question: Who has the power to assess and collect revenue in respect of lands within an autonomous region or district?
3210.answer: The Regional Council for an autonomous region and the District Council for an autonomous district have the power to assess and collect revenue in respect of lands within such region or district.

3211.question: Who has the power to assess and collect revenue in respect of lands within an autonomous region and an autonomous district?
3211.answer: The Regional Council for an autonomous region and the District Council for an autonomous district.

3212.question: What power does the Regional Council for an autonomous region and the District Council for an autonomous district have in respect of areas within such region and district?
3212.answer: They have power to levy and collect taxes on lands and buildings, and tolls on persons resident within such areas.

3213.question: What can the Regional Council for an autonomous region and the District Council for an autonomous district do on lands and buildings, and on persons resident within such areas?
3213.answer: They have power to levy and collect taxes on lands and buildings, and tolls on persons resident within such areas.

3214.question: What taxes can the District Council for an autonomous district levy and collect within the district?
3214.answer: The District Council can levy and collect taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments; taxes on animals, vehicles and boats; taxes on the entry of goods into a market for sale therein, and tolls on passengers and goods carried in ferries; taxes for the maintenance of schools, dispensaries or roads, and taxes on entertainment and amusements.

3215.question: What are the various types of taxes that a District Council in an autonomous district can levy and collect?
3215.answer: A District Council in an autonomous district can levy and collect taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments; taxes on animals, vehicles and boats; taxes on the entry of goods into a market for sale therein, and tolls on passengers and goods carried in ferries; taxes for the maintenance of schools, dispensaries or roads, and taxes on entertainment and amusements.

3216.question: What happens to the regulations made by a Regional Council or District Council for the levy and collection of taxes?
3216.answer: These regulations shall be submitted forthwith to the Governor and, until assented to by him, shall have no effect.

3217.question: What happens to the regulations made by a Regional Council or District Council for the levy and collection of taxes before the Governor assents to them?
3217.answer: These regulations shall have no effect until assented to by the Governor.

3218.question: What are licences or leases for the purpose of prospecting for, or extraction of, minerals related to?
3218.answer: They relate to the share of the royalties accruing each year from these licences or leases.

3219.question: What do the share of royalties accruing each year from licences or leases for prospecting for, or extraction of, minerals relate to?
3219.answer: They relate to the licences or leases for the purpose of prospecting for, or extraction of, minerals.

3220.question: What happens if a dispute arises over the share of royalties to be made over to a District Council?
3220.answer: If a dispute arises, it is referred to the Governor for determination. The amount determined by the Governor is deemed to be the amount payable and the decision of the Governor is final.

3221.question: Who determines the amount payable in case of a dispute over the share of royalties to be made over to a District Council and is their decision final?
3221.answer: In case of a dispute, the amount payable is determined by the Governor and their decision is final.

3222.question: What amendment was made in Paragraph 9 in its application to the States of Tripura and Mizoram?
3222.answer: The amendment was made by the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 1988, to insert a sub-paragraph stating that the Governor may direct that the share of royalties to be made over to a District Council shall be made over to that Council within a year from the date of any agreement or determination.

3223.question: What does the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 1988, state about the share of royalties made over to a District Council in the States of Tripura and Mizoram?
3223.answer: The Sixth Schedule to the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 1988, states that the Governor may direct that the share of royalties to be made over to a District Council shall be made over to that Council within a year from the date of any agreement or determination. This amendment was made in Paragraph 9 in its application to the States of Tripura and Mizoram.

3224.question: What power does the District Council of an autonomous district have in terms of money-lending and trading?
3224.answer: The District Council can make regulations for the regulation and control of money-lending or trading within the district by persons other than Scheduled Tribes resident in the district.

3225.question: Who can the District Council regulate and control in terms of money-lending and trading within the district?
3225.answer: The District Council can regulate and control money-lending or trading by persons other than Scheduled Tribes resident in the district.

3226.question: What can such regulations for the control of money-lending and trading by non-tribals prescribe or provide for?
3226.answer: The regulations may prescribe that no one except the holder of a license shall carry on the business of money-lending, prescribe the maximum rate of interest which may be charged or recovered by a money-lender, and provide for the maintenance of accounts by money-lenders and for the inspection of such accounts.

3227.question: What can the regulations for non-tribal money-lending and trading potentially include?
3227.answer: The regulations may include that only a license holder can carry on the business, a maximum rate of interest that can be charged or recovered by a money-lender, and provisions for the maintenance and inspection of accounts by money-lenders.

3228.question: Who can carry on wholesale or retail business in any commodity according to the original regulations?
3228.answer: Only a member of the Scheduled Tribes resident in the district

3229.question: Who is allowed to carry on wholesale or retail business in any commodity according to the original regulations, if they are a resident of the district?
3229.answer: Only a member of the Scheduled Tribes

3230.question: Under what conditions can this business be carried out?
3230.answer: Under a licence issued by the District Council

3231.question: Who issues the license for carrying out this business?

3232.question: What is the requirement for making regulations under this paragraph?
3232.answer: They have to be passed by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the total membership of the District Council

3233.question: What is the voting requirement for the District Council to pass regulations under this paragraph?
3233.answer: A majority of not less than three-fourths of the total membership of the District Council is required.

3234.question: Can a license be refused to a money-lender or trader who has been doing business before the regulations were made?

3235.question: Is it possible for a money-lender or trader who has been doing business before the regulations were made to be refused a license?

3236.question: What are the changes made to paragraph 10 in its application to the States of Tripura and Mizoram?
3236.answer: The words 'by non-tribals' and 'other than Scheduled Tribes' have been omitted and clause (d) has been replaced with 'prescribe that no person resident in the district shall carry on any trade, whether wholesale or retail, except under a licence issued in that behalf by the District Council.'

3237.question: What is the replacement for clause (d) in paragraph 10 as it applies to the States of Tripura and Mizoram, and which phrases have been omitted?
3237.answer: Clause (d) has been replaced with 'prescribe that no person resident in the district shall carry on any trade, whether wholesale or retail, except under a licence issued in that behalf by the District Council.' The words 'by non-tribals' and 'other than Scheduled Tribes' have been omitted.

3238.question: What is the amendment made to paragraph 10 in its application to the State of Assam?
3238.answer: A new sub-paragraph was inserted stating that nothing in this paragraph shall apply to the Bodoland Territorial Council constituted under the proviso to sub-paragraph (3) of paragraph 2 of this Schedule.

3239.question: What does the amendment to paragraph 10 in its application to the State of Assam, regarding the Bodoland Territorial Council, state?
3239.answer: A new sub-paragraph was inserted stating that nothing in this paragraph shall apply to the Bodoland Territorial Council constituted under the proviso to sub-paragraph (3) of paragraph 2 of this Schedule.

3240.question: What happens to all regulations made under this paragraph?
3240.answer: They shall be submitted forthwith to the Governor and, until assented to by him, shall have no effect.

3241.question: To whom are all regulations made under a certain paragraph submitted and when do they take effect?
3241.answer: They are submitted forthwith to the Governor and take effect only after his assent.

3242.question: Where should all laws, rules and regulations made under this Schedule by a District Council or a Regional Council be published?
3242.answer: In the Official Gazette of the State.

3243.question: Where are all laws, rules and regulations made under the Schedule by a District Council or a Regional Council published?
3243.answer: In the Official Gazette of the State.

3244.question: What happens to the laws, rules and regulations once they are published in the Official Gazette of the State?
3244.answer: They have the force of law.

3245.question: What does it mean for the laws, rules and regulations when they are published in the Official Gazette of the State?
3245.answer: It means they have the force of law.

3246.question: Can any Act of the Legislature of the State of Assam apply to any autonomous district or autonomous region in that State?
3246.answer: No, unless the District Council for such district or having jurisdiction over such region by public notification so directs.

3247.question: What is required for an Act of the Legislature of the State of Assam to apply to any autonomous district or autonomous region in that State?
3247.answer: The District Council for such district or having jurisdiction over such region must direct so by public notification.

3248.question: What power does the Governor have regarding the application of any Act of Parliament or of the Legislature of the State of Assam?
3248.answer: The Governor may, by public notification, direct that any Act of Parliament or of the Legislature of the State of Assam shall not apply to an autonomous district or an autonomous region in that State, or shall apply to such district or region or any part thereof subject to such exceptions or modifications as he may specify in the notification.

3249.question: What action can the Governor take to modify the application of an Act of Parliament or of the Legislature of the State of Assam to an autonomous district or an autonomous region in that State?
3249.answer: The Governor may, by public notification, direct that any Act of Parliament or of the Legislature of the State of Assam shall not apply to an autonomous district or an autonomous region in that State, or shall apply to such district or region or any part thereof subject to such exceptions or modifications as he may specify in the notification.

3250.question: What amendment was made to Paragraph 12 related to its application to the State of Assam?
3250.answer: Paragraph 12 has been amended by the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 1995 (42 of 1995), s.2.

3251.question: What was the amendment made to Paragraph 12 by the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 1995 (42 of 1995), s.2?
3251.answer: The amendment was related to its application to the State of Assam.

3252.question: What change was made to paragraph 12 by the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 2003?
3252.answer: In paragraph 12, in sub-paragraph (1), in clause (a), for the words, figures and letter “matters specified in paragraph 3 or paragraph 3A of this Schedule”, the words, figures and letter “matters specified in paragraph 3 or paragraph 3A or paragraph 3B of this Schedule” shall be substituted.

3253.question: What substitution was made in paragraph 12, sub-paragraph (1), clause (a) by the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 2003?
3253.answer: For the words, figures and letter “matters specified in paragraph 3 or paragraph 3A of this Schedule”, the words, figures and letter “matters specified in paragraph 3 or paragraph 3A or paragraph 3B of this Schedule” were substituted.

3254.question: What happens if a law made by a District or Regional Council in the State of Meghalaya is repugnant to any provision of a law made by the Legislature of the State of Meghalaya?
3254.answer: The law or regulation made by the District Council or, as the case may be, the Regional Council whether made before or after the law made by the Legislature of the State of Meghalaya, shall, to the extent of repugnancy, be void and the law made by the Legislature of the State of Meghalaya shall prevail.

3255.question: What is the consequence if a law or regulation made by the District or Regional Council in Meghalaya conflicts with a law made by the Legislature of the State of Meghalaya?
3255.answer: The law or regulation made by the District Council or, as the case may be, the Regional Council, shall, to the extent of the conflict, be void and the law made by the Legislature of the State of Meghalaya shall prevail.

3256.question: What power does the President have with respect to any Act of Parliament towards an autonomous district or an autonomous region in the State of Meghalaya?
3256.answer: The President may, by notification, direct that it shall not apply to an autonomous district or an autonomous region in the State of Meghalaya, or shall apply to such district or region.

3257.question: What can the President do regarding the application of an Act of Parliament to an autonomous district or an autonomous region in the State of Meghalaya?
3257.answer: The President may, by notification, direct that it shall not apply to an autonomous district or an autonomous region in the State of Meghalaya, or shall apply to such district or region.

3258.question: What is stated in the 12AA of the Constitution of India regarding the application of Acts of Parliament and of the Legislature of the State of Tripura to the autonomous districts and regions?
3258.answer: The 12AA of the Constitution of India states that notwithstanding anything in the Constitution, no Act of the Legislature of the State of Tripura in respect of any of the matters specified in paragraph 3 of this Schedule as matters with respect to which a District Council or a Regional Council may make laws, and no Act of the Legislature of the State of Tripura prohibiting or restricting the consumption of any non-distilled alcoholic liquor shall apply to any autonomous district or autonomous region in that State unless, in either case the District Council for such district or having jurisdiction over such region by public notification so directs. The Governor may, by public notification, direct that any Act of the Legislature of the State of Tripura to which the provisions of clause (a) of this sub-paragraph do not apply, shall not apply to the autonomous district or any autonomous region in that State, or shall apply to that district or such region, or any part thereof, subject to such exceptions or modifications, as he may specify in the notification. The President may, with respect to any Act of Parliament, by notification, direct that it shall not apply to the autonomous district or an autonomous region in the State of Tripura, or shall apply to such district or region or any part thereof, subject to such exceptions or modifications as he may specify in the notification.

3259.question: What does the 12AA of the Constitution of India state about the application of Acts of the Legislature of the State of Tripura and Acts of Parliament to the autonomous districts and regions in Tripura?
3259.answer: The 12AA of the Constitution of India states that notwithstanding anything in the Constitution, no Act of the Legislature of the State of Tripura in respect of any of the matters specified in paragraph 3 of this Schedule as matters with respect to which a District Council or a Regional Council may make laws, and no Act of the Legislature of the State of Tripura prohibiting or restricting the consumption of any non-distilled alcoholic liquor shall apply to any autonomous district or autonomous region in that State unless, in either case the District Council for such district or having jurisdiction over such region by public notification so directs. The Governor may, by public notification, direct that any Act of the Legislature of the State of Tripura to which the provisions of clause (a) of this sub-paragraph do not apply, shall not apply to the autonomous district or any autonomous region in that State, or shall apply to that district or such region, or any part thereof, subject to such exceptions or modifications, as he may specify in the notification. The President may, with respect to any Act of Parliament, by notification, direct that it shall not apply to the autonomous district or an autonomous region in the State of Tripura, or shall apply to such district or region or any part thereof, subject to such exceptions or modifications as he may specify in the notification.

3260.question: Who has the authority to direct that an Act of the Legislature of the State of Tripura may not apply to any autonomous district or autonomous region?
3260.answer: The Governor has the authority to direct that an Act of the Legislature of the State of Tripura may not apply to any autonomous district or autonomous region.
