3262.question: Who can specify exceptions or modifications to any Act of Parliament in its application to the autonomous district or an autonomous region in the State of Tripura?
3262.answer: The President can specify exceptions or modifications to any Act of Parliament in its application to the autonomous district or an autonomous region in the State of Tripura.

3263.question: Who has the power to specify exceptions or modifications to any Act of Parliament as it applies to the autonomous district or an autonomous region in the State of Tripura?

3264.question: Who can decide if an Act of the Legislature of the State of Tripura applies to an autonomous district or region?
3264.answer: The District Council for such district or having jurisdiction over such region can decide if an Act of the Legislature of the State of Tripura applies to an autonomous district or region.

3265.question: Who has the authority to decide if an Act of the Legislature of the State of Tripura applies to an autonomous district or region?
3265.answer: The District Council for such district or having jurisdiction over such region.

3266.question: Who can direct that an Act of the Legislature of the State of Mizoram shall not apply to an autonomous district or an autonomous region in that State?

3267.question: Who has the authority to decide that an Act of the Legislature of the State of Mizoram doesn't apply to an autonomous district or an autonomous region in that State?

3268.question: Under what conditions does an Act of the Legislature of the State of Mizoram not apply to an autonomous district or autonomous region in that State?
3268.answer: The Act does not apply unless the District Council for such district or having jurisdiction over such region, by public notification, so directs.

3269.question: What needs to happen for an Act of the Legislature of the State of Mizoram to apply to an autonomous district or autonomous region in that State?
3269.answer: The Act will apply only if the District Council for such district or having jurisdiction over such region, by public notification, so directs.

3270.question: Who can make modifications to an Act of Parliament's application to an autonomous district or an autonomous region in the State of Mizoram?

3271.question: Who has the authority to make modifications to an Act of Parliament's application to an autonomous district or an autonomous region in the State of Mizoram?

3272.question: Can modifications or exceptions made to an Act of Parliament's application to an autonomous district or region in Mizoram have retrospective effect?

3273.question: Is it possible for modifications or exceptions made to an Act of Parliament's application to an autonomous district or region in Mizoram to have retrospective effect?

3274.question: What is specified in paragraph 3 of the Schedule?
3274.answer: It specifies matters with respect to which a District Council or a Regional Council may make laws.

3275.question: Which paragraph of the Schedule specifies the matters with respect to which a District Council or a Regional Council may make laws?
3275.answer: Paragraph 3 of the Schedule specifies this.

3276.question: What has to be done before the estimated receipts and expenditure pertaining to an autonomous district are credited to the Consolidated Fund of the State?
3276.answer: They shall be first placed before the District Council for discussion.

3277.question: What needs to be done with the estimated receipts and expenditure pertaining to an autonomous district before they are credited to the Consolidated Fund of the State?
3277.answer: They shall be first placed before the District Council for discussion.

3278.question: What can the Governor do in relation to the administration of autonomous districts and regions?
3278.answer: The Governor may appoint a Commission to examine and report on any matter relating to the administration of the autonomous districts and regions, including matters specified in certain clauses of paragraph 1 of the schedule. The Governor may also appoint a Commission to inquire into and report on the administration of autonomous districts and regions generally and on certain specific matters.

3279.question: What powers does the Governor have in terms of appointing Commissions related to the administration of autonomous districts and regions?
3279.answer: The Governor may appoint a Commission to examine and report on any matter relating to the administration of the autonomous districts and regions, including matters specified in certain clauses of paragraph 1 of the schedule. The Governor may also appoint a Commission to inquire into and report on the administration of autonomous districts and regions generally and on certain specific matters.

3280.question: What are some of the specific matters the Commission may inquire into and report on?
3280.answer: The provision of educational and medical facilities and communications in such districts and regions, the need for any new or special legislation in respect of such districts and regions, and the administration of the laws, rules and regulations made by the District and Regional Councils.

3281.question: What responsibilities do the District and Regional Councils have in terms of the administration of laws, rules and regulations, and what are some areas they may need special legislation for?
3281.answer: The District and Regional Councils are responsible for the administration of the laws, rules and regulations. They may need new or special legislation for specific matters like the provision of educational and medical facilities and communications in certain districts and regions. These matters can be inquired into and reported on by the Commission.

3282.question: What happens after the report of the Commission is completed?
3282.answer: The report of the Commission, with the recommendations of the Governor, shall be laid before the Legislature of the State by the Minister concerned together with an explanatory memorandum regarding the action proposed to be taken thereon by the Government of the State.

3283.question: What is the procedure followed by the Government of the State once the Commission's report is completed and the Governor's recommendations are received?
3283.answer: The report of the Commission, with the recommendations of the Governor, shall be laid before the Legislature of the State by the Minister concerned together with an explanatory memorandum regarding the action proposed to be taken thereon by the Government of the State.

3284.question: What role can the Governor assign to one of his Ministers in relation to the autonomous districts and regions?
3284.answer: The Governor may place one of his Ministers specially in charge of the welfare of the autonomous districts and autonomous regions in the State.

3285.question: Who may the Governor place in charge of the welfare of the autonomous districts and autonomous regions in the State?
3285.answer: The Governor may place one of his Ministers in charge of the welfare of the autonomous districts and autonomous regions in the State.

3286.question: What change was made to paragraph 14's application to Assam by the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 1995?
3286.answer: The words 'with the recommendations of the Governor with respect thereto' were omitted.

3287.question: Which words were omitted from paragraph 14's application to Assam by the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 1995?
3287.answer: The words 'with the recommendations of the Governor with respect thereto' were omitted.

3288.question: What can the Governor do if an act or resolution of a District or Regional Council is likely to endanger the safety of India or is prejudicial to public order?
3288.answer: The Governor may annul or suspend such act or resolution and take such steps as he may consider necessary, including the suspension of the Council and the assumption to himself of all or any of the powers vested in or exercisable by the Council.

3289.question: What actions can the Governor take if he finds an act or resolution of a District or Regional Council to be endangering the safety of India or prejudicial to public order?
3289.answer: The Governor may annul or suspend such act or resolution and take such steps as he may consider necessary, including the suspension of the Council and the assumption to himself of all or any of the powers vested in or exercisable by the Council.

3290.question: What happens to an order made by the Governor under sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph 15?
3290.answer: The order, along with the reasons for it, shall be laid before the Legislature of the State as soon as possible. The order will continue in force for a period of twelve months from the date it was made, unless revoked by the Legislature of the State.

3291.question: How long does an order made by the Governor under sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph 15 stay in force, and where should it be presented?
3291.answer: The order stays in force for a period of twelve months from the date it was made and should be laid before the Legislature of the State as soon as possible.

3292.question: Under what conditions can the Governor dissolve a District or a Regional Council?
3292.answer: The Governor can dissolve a District or a Regional Council on the recommendation of a Commission appointed under paragraph 14 of the Schedule.

3293.question: On whose recommendation can the Governor dissolve a District or a Regional Council?
3293.answer: The Governor can dissolve a District or a Regional Council on the recommendation of a Commission appointed under paragraph 14 of the Schedule.

3294.question: What happens after the dissolution of a District or a Regional Council?
3294.answer: The Governor may direct that a fresh general election be held immediately for the reconstitution of the Council.

3295.question: Who may direct that a fresh general election be held immediately for the reconstitution of a Council after its dissolution?

3296.question: Which paragraph was amended in its application to the states of Tripura and Mizoram in the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution Amendment Act, 1988?

3297.question: What happened to Paragraph 15 in the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution Amendment Act, 1988 in relation to the states of Tripura and Mizoram?

3298.question: What was the amendment made to paragraph 15?
3298.answer: In the opening paragraph, the words 'by the Legislature of the State' were substituted with 'by him', and the proviso was omitted.

3299.question: What changes were made in the opening paragraph of paragraph 15, specifically regarding the use of 'by the Legislature of the State' and the proviso?
3299.answer: 'By the Legislature of the State' was substituted with 'by him', and the proviso was omitted.

3300.question: Which other paragraph was amended in its application to the states of Tripura and Mizoram in the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution Amendment Act, 1988?

3301.question: In the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution Amendment Act, 1988, which paragraph's application to the states of Tripura and Mizoram was amended?

3302.question: What was the amendment made to paragraph 16?
3302.answer: In sub-paragraph (1), the words 'subject to the previous approval of the Legislature of the State' occurring in clause (b), and the second proviso were omitted. For sub-paragraph (3), a new sub-paragraph was substituted stating that every order made under sub-paragraph (1) or sub-paragraph (2) of this paragraph, along with the reasons therefor shall be laid before the Legislature of the State.

3303.question: What changes were made to sub-paragraph (1) and sub-paragraph (3) in paragraph 16?
3303.answer: In sub-paragraph (1), the words 'subject to the previous approval of the Legislature of the State' occurring in clause (b), and the second proviso were omitted. For sub-paragraph (3), a new sub-paragraph was substituted stating that every order made under sub-paragraph (1) or sub-paragraph (2) of this paragraph, along with the reasons therefor shall be laid before the Legislature of the State.

3304.question: What actions are subject to the previous approval of the Legislature of the State in the context of the administration of the area under the authority of a Council?
3304.answer: The Governor can assume the administration of the area under the authority of such Council himself or place the administration of such area under the Commission appointed under the said paragraph or any other body considered suitable by him for a period not exceeding twelve months.

3305.question: Who can assume the administration of the area under the authority of a Council and for what period of time, according to the approval of the Legislature of the State?
3305.answer: The Governor can assume the administration of the area under the authority of such Council himself or place the administration of such area under the Commission appointed under the said paragraph or any other body considered suitable by him for a period not exceeding twelve months.

3306.question: What actions can the Governor take with regard to the administration of the area in question pending the reconstitution of the Council on fresh general election?
3306.answer: When an order under clause (a) of this paragraph has been made, the Governor may take the action referred to in clause (b) of this paragraph.

3307.question: What can the Governor do when an order under clause (a) of this paragraph has been made?
3307.answer: The Governor may take the action referred to in clause (b) of this paragraph with regard to the administration of the area in question pending the reconstitution of the Council on fresh general election.

3308.question: What conditions must be met before action can be taken under clause (b) of this paragraph?
3308.answer: No action can be taken under clause (b) of this paragraph without giving the District or the Regional Council, as the case may be, an opportunity of placing its views before the Legislature of the State.

3309.question: Who must be given an opportunity to place their views before the State Legislature before action can be taken under clause (b) of this paragraph?
3309.answer: The District or the Regional Council, as the case may be, must be given an opportunity.

3310.question: What can the Governor do if the administration of an autonomous district cannot be carried out according to the provisions of this Schedule?
3310.answer: The Governor may, by public notification, assume to himself all or any of the functions or powers vested in or exercisable by the District Council or the Regional Council and declare that such functions or powers shall be exercisable by such person or authority as he may specify, for a period not exceeding six months.

3311.question: What action can the Governor take when the administration of an autonomous district is not functioning according to provisions, and for how long can this action be implemented?
3311.answer: The Governor may, by public notification, assume to himself all or any of the functions or powers vested in or exercisable by the District Council or the Regional Council and declare that such functions or powers shall be exercisable by such person or authority as he may specify, for a period not exceeding six months.

3312.question: Can the period of the Governor's assumption of powers be extended?
3312.answer: Yes, the Governor may by a further order or orders extend the operation of the initial order by a period not exceeding six months on each occasion.

3313.question: By how much can the Governor extend the operation of the initial order on each occasion?
3313.answer: The Governor may extend the operation of the initial order by a period not exceeding six months on each occasion.

3314.question: What happens to the order made under sub-paragraph (2) of this paragraph?
3314.answer: Every order made under sub-paragraph (2) of this paragraph with the reasons therefor shall be laid before the Legislature of the State and shall cease to operate at the expiration of thirty days from the date on which the State Legislature first sits after the issue of the order, unless, before the expiry of that period it has been approved by that State Legislature.

3315.question: What is the procedure and validity period for an order made under sub-paragraph (2) of a given paragraph?
3315.answer: An order made under sub-paragraph (2) of this paragraph is laid before the Legislature of the State with the reasons for it. It ceases to operate at the expiration of thirty days from the date on which the State Legislature first sits after the issue of the order, unless it has been approved by the State Legislature before that period ends.

3316.question: What can the Governor declare regarding areas within an autonomous district for the purposes of elections to the Legislative Assembly?
3316.answer: The Governor may by order declare that any area within an autonomous district in the State of Assam or Meghalaya or Tripura or Mizoram, shall not form part of any constituency to fill a seat or seats in the Assembly reserved for any such district but shall form part of a constituency to fill a seat or seats in the Assembly not so reserved to be specified in the order.

3317.question: Which states may a Governor order to declare that any area within an autonomous district shall not form part of any constituency to fill a seat or seats in the Assembly reserved for any such district but shall form part of a constituency to fill a seat or seats in the Assembly not so reserved to be specified in the order?
3317.answer: The Governor may make such an order for the autonomous districts in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, or Mizoram.

3318.question: What amendment was made to Paragraph 17 in its application to the State of Assam?
3318.answer: Paragraph 17 was amended to insert the following proviso: 'Provided that nothing in this paragraph shall apply to the Bodoland Territorial Areas District.'

3319.question: To which territorial area does the amendment to Paragraph 17 not apply in the State of Assam?
3319.answer: The amendment to Paragraph 17 does not apply to the Bodoland Territorial Areas District.

3332.question: What amendment was made to Paragraph 19 in its application to the State of Assam by the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 2003?
3332.answer: The amendment inserted a new subparagraph after sub-paragraph (3) stating that an Interim Executive Council for Bodoland Territorial Areas District in Assam shall be formed by the Governor from amongst leaders of the Bodo movement.

3333.question: Which amendment to the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 2003, led to the formation of an Interim Executive Council for Bodoland Territorial Areas District in Assam by the Governor from amongst leaders of the Bodo movement?
3333.answer: The amendment to Paragraph 19 in its application to the State of Assam by the Sixth Schedule.

3334.question: What does the 'Memorandum of Settlement' refer to?
3334.answer: The 'Memorandum of Settlement' refers to the Memorandum signed on the 10th day of February, 2003 between Government of India, Government of Assam and Bodo Liberation Tigers.

3335.question: Who signed the Memorandum on the 10th day of February, 2003?
3335.answer: The Memorandum, known as 'Memorandum of Settlement', was signed by the Government of India, Government of Assam and Bodo Liberation Tigers.

3336.question: What is the duration of the Interim Council as per the Memorandum of Settlement?
3336.answer: The duration of the Interim Council as per the Memorandum of Settlement is for a period of six months.

3337.question: For how long is the Interim Council established according to the Memorandum of Settlement?
3337.answer: The Interim Council is established for a period of six months according to the Memorandum of Settlement.

3338.question: Which areas are designated as tribal areas within the State of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram according to the Constitution of India?
3338.answer: The areas specified in Parts I, II, IIA and III of the table are respectively the tribal areas within the State of Assam, the State of Meghalaya, the State of Tripura and the State of Mizoram.

3339.question: What does the Constitution of India specify about the tribal areas in Parts I, II, IIA and III of the table within the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram?
3339.answer: The areas specified in Parts I, II, IIA and III of the table are respectively the tribal areas within the State of Assam, the State of Meghalaya, the State of Tripura and the State of Mizoram.

3340.question: How is any reference to any district in Part I, II or III of the table to be understood?
3340.answer: Any reference to any district in Part I, II or III of the table is to be construed as a reference to the territories comprised within the autonomous district of that name existing immediately before the day appointed under clause (b) of section 2 of the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971.

3341.question: What does the reference to any district in Part I, II or III of the table in the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971 refer to?
3341.answer: It is to be construed as a reference to the territories comprised within the autonomous district of that name existing immediately before the day appointed under clause (b) of section 2.

3342.question: What does the reference to the 'Tripura Tribal Areas District' in Part IIA of the table signify?
3342.answer: The reference to the 'Tripura Tribal Areas District' in Part IIA of the table is construed as a reference to the territory comprising the tribal areas specified in the First Schedule to the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council Act, 1979.

3343.question: What does the reference to the territory comprising the tribal areas specified in the First Schedule to the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council Act, 1979 signify?
3343.answer: The reference to this territory is construed as a reference to the 'Tripura Tribal Areas District' in Part IIA of the table.

3344.question: Which areas are part of the Khasi Hills District as per the Constitution of India?
3344.answer: For the purposes of certain clauses and paragraphs of the Schedule, no part of the area comprised within the municipality of Shillong shall be deemed to be within the Khasi Hills District.

3345.question: According to the Constitution of India, is the area within the municipality of Shillong considered part of the Khasi Hills District for certain clauses and paragraphs of the Schedule?
3345.answer: No, for the purposes of certain clauses and paragraphs of the Schedule, no part of the area comprised within the municipality of Shillong shall be deemed to be within the Khasi Hills District.

3346.question: What districts are specified in Part I of the table?
3346.answer: The districts specified in Part I of the table are The North Cachar Hills District, The Karbi Anglong District, and The Bodoland Territorial Area District.

3347.question: Which part of the table specifies The North Cachar Hills District, The Karbi Anglong District, and The Bodoland Territorial Area District?
3347.answer: Part I of the table specifies The North Cachar Hills District, The Karbi Anglong District, and The Bodoland Territorial Area District.

3348.question: What districts are specified in Part II of the table?
3348.answer: The districts specified in Part II of the table are Khasi Hills District, Jaintia Hills District, and The Garo Hills District.

3349.question: Which part of the table specifies Khasi Hills District, Jaintia Hills District, and The Garo Hills District?
3349.answer: Khasi Hills District, Jaintia Hills District, and The Garo Hills District are specified in Part II of the table.

3350.question: What is the Chakma District?
3350.answer: The Chakma District is a district mentioned in THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA.

3351.question: In which document is the Chakma District mentioned?
3351.answer: The Chakma District is mentioned in THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA.

3352.question: What is the Mara District?
3352.answer: The Mara District is a district mentioned in THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA.

3353.question: Where is the Mara District mentioned?
3353.answer: The Mara District is mentioned in THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA.

3354.question: What is the Lai District?
3354.answer: The Lai District is a district mentioned in THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA.

3355.question: Where is the Lai District mentioned?
3355.answer: The Lai District is mentioned in THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA.

3356.question: What happens to the Mizo District Council according to the constitution?
3356.answer: According to the constitution, the Mizo District Council shall stand dissolved and cease to exist. The Administrator of the Union territory of Mizoram may provide for the transfer of the assets, rights and liabilities of the Mizo District Council to the Union or to any other authority; the substitution of the Union or any other authority for the Mizo District Council; the transfer or re-employment of any employees of the Mizo District Council; the continuance of any laws, made by the Mizo District Council and in force immediately before its dissolution, subject to such adaptations and modifications, as the Administrator may make in this behalf, until such laws are altered, repealed or amended by a competent Legislature or other competent authority.

3357.question: What will the Administrator of the Union territory of Mizoram provide for after the dissolution of the Mizo District Council according to the constitution? What will happen to the laws made by the Mizo District Council?
3357.answer: After the dissolution of the Mizo District Council, the Administrator of the Union territory of Mizoram may provide for the transfer of the assets, rights and liabilities of the Mizo District Council to the Union or to any other authority; the substitution of the Union or any other authority for the Mizo District Council; the transfer or re-employment of any employees of the Mizo District Council. The laws made by the Mizo District Council and in force immediately before its dissolution will continue, subject to such adaptations and modifications, as the Administrator may make in this behalf, until such laws are altered, repealed or amended by a competent Legislature or other competent authority.

3358.question: What is the 'prescribed date' referred to in the constitution?
3358.answer: In the constitution, the 'prescribed date' refers to the date on which the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory of Mizoram is duly constituted under and in accordance with the provisions of the Government of Union Territories Act.

3359.question: Under and in accordance with the provisions of the Government of Union Territories Act, what does the 'prescribed date' in the constitution refer to?
3359.answer: The 'prescribed date' in the constitution refers to the date on which the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory of Mizoram is duly constituted.

3360.question: What happens to every autonomous region in the Union territory of Mizoram existing before the prescribed date according to the Constitution of India?
3360.answer: Every autonomous region existing before the prescribed date in the Union territory of Mizoram shall, on and from that date, be an autonomous district in that Union territory. The Administrator thereof may direct that necessary amendments be made to give effect to this clause.

3361.question: What is the status and who has the authority to make amendments, according to the Constitution of India, for autonomous regions in the Union territory of Mizoram that existed before a certain prescribed date?
3361.answer: Every autonomous region that existed before the prescribed date in the Union territory of Mizoram becomes an autonomous district on and from that date. The Administrator of the Union territory has the authority to make necessary amendments to give effect to this clause.

3362.question: What happens to every Regional Council of an autonomous region in the Union territory of Mizoram existing before the prescribed date?
3362.answer: Every Regional Council of an autonomous region in the Union territory of Mizoram existing immediately before the prescribed date shall, on and from that date and until a District Council is duly constituted for the corresponding new district, be deemed to be the District Council of that district.

3363.question: What is the status of the Regional Council of an autonomous region in the Union territory of Mizoram existing immediately before the prescribed date until a District Council is duly constituted for the corresponding new district?
3363.answer: Every Regional Council of an autonomous region in the Union territory of Mizoram existing immediately before the prescribed date shall, on and from that date and until a District Council is duly constituted for the corresponding new district, be deemed to be the District Council of that district.

3364.question: What is the change in paragraph 20B in the Constitution of India in its application to the State of Assam?
3364.answer: After paragraph 20B, a new paragraph 20BA has been inserted, which discusses the exercise of discretionary powers by the Governor in the discharge of his functions.

3365.question: What update was made to the Constitution of India's paragraph 20B in relation to the State of Assam?
3365.answer: After paragraph 20B, a new paragraph 20BA has been inserted, which discusses the exercise of discretionary powers by the Governor in the discharge of his functions.

3366.question: What action is to be taken after consulting the Council of Ministers and the North Cachar Hills Autonomous Council or the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council?
3366.answer: The action that the governor considers necessary in his discretion.

3367.question: After consulting the Council of Ministers and the North Cachar Hills Autonomous Council or the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council, whose discretion is it to consider the necessary action to be taken?
3367.answer: It is the governor's discretion to consider the necessary action to be taken.

3368.question: What was inserted after paragraph 20B in its application to the States of Tripura and Mizoram?
3368.answer: The following paragraph has been inserted: '20BB. Exercise of discretionary powers by the Governor in the discharge of his functions.'

3369.question: Where was the '20BB. Exercise of discretionary powers by the Governor in the discharge of his functions' paragraph inserted in its application to the States?
3369.answer: It was inserted after paragraph 20B in the States of Tripura and Mizoram.

3370.question: What action should the Governor take after consulting the Council of Ministers and the District Council or the Regional Council concerned?
3370.answer: The Governor should take such action as he considers necessary in his discretion.

3371.question: In whose discretion should the Governor take necessary action after consulting the Council of Ministers and the District Council or the Regional Council concerned?
3371.answer: The Governor should take such action in his own discretion.

3372.question: What happens to every member, whether elected or nominated, of an existing Regional Council?
3372.answer: They shall be deemed to have been elected or, as the case may be, nominated to the corresponding new District Council and shall hold office until a District Council is duly constituted for the corresponding new district under this Schedule.

3373.question: What is the status of every member of an existing Regional Council, whether elected or nominated, when a corresponding new District Council is formed under this Schedule?
3373.answer: They shall be deemed to have been elected or, as the case may be, nominated to the corresponding new District Council and shall hold office until a District Council is duly constituted for the corresponding new district.

3374.question: What happens until rules are made under sub-paragraph (7) of paragraph 2 and subparagraph (4) of paragraph 4 of this Schedule by the corresponding new District Council?
3374.answer: Until these rules are made, the rules made under the said provisions by the existing Regional Council will continue to apply.

3375.question: What will continue to apply until the rules are made under sub-paragraph (7) of paragraph 2 and subparagraph (4) of paragraph 4 of this Schedule by the new District Council?
3375.answer: The rules made under the said provisions by the existing Regional Council will continue to apply until these rules are made.

3376.question: Who has the authority to make adaptations and modifications in relation to the new District Council in the Union territory of Mizoram?
3376.answer: The Administrator of the Union territory of Mizoram

3377.question: Who holds the responsibility for making adaptations and modifications in the new District Council in Mizoram?
3377.answer: The Administrator of the Union territory of Mizoram

3378.question: What matters can the Administrator of the Union territory of Mizoram provide for?
3378.answer: The transfer in whole or in part of the assets, rights and liabilities of the existing Regional Council to the new District Council, the substitution of the new District Council for the existing one in legal proceedings, the transfer or re-employment of any employees of the existing Council to the new one, the continuance of any laws made by the existing Council subject to adaptations and modifications, and any incidental, consequential and supplementary matters considered necessary.

3379.question: What does the transfer in whole or in part of the assets, rights and liabilities of the existing Regional Council to the new District Council, the substitution of the new District Council for the existing one in legal proceedings, the transfer or re-employment of any employees of the existing Council to the new one, the continuance of any laws made by the existing Council subject to adaptations and modifications, and any incidental, consequential and supplementary matters considered necessary pertain to?
3379.answer: These matters pertain to what the Administrator of the Union territory of Mizoram can provide for.

3380.question: Who is referred to instead of the Governor and Government of the State in the application of provisions to the Union territory of Mizoram?
3380.answer: The Administrator of the Union territory

3381.question: Who applies the provisions to the Union territory of Mizoram instead of the Governor and Government of the State?
3381.answer: The Administrator of the Union territory

3382.question: What does the term 'State' refer to in the context of the Union territory of Mizoram?

3383.question: What is the term for Mizoram in the context of Indian political divisions?

3384.question: Who is responsible for the transfer or re-employment of employees from the existing Regional Council to the new District Council?
3384.answer: The Administrator of the Union territory of Mizoram

3385.question: What is the role of the Administrator of the Union territory of Mizoram in relation to the Regional Council and the new District Council?
3385.answer: He is responsible for the transfer or re-employment of employees from the existing Regional Council to the new District Council.

3386.question: What can Parliament do according to Amendment of the Schedule in the Constitution of India?
3386.answer: Parliament may from time to time by law amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any of the provisions of this Schedule and, when the Schedule is so amended, any reference to this Schedule in this Constitution shall be construed as a reference to such Schedule as so amended.

3387.question: What does it mean when any reference to the Schedule in the Constitution of India is construed as a reference to such Schedule as so amended?
3387.answer: It means that the Parliament has the power to amend the Schedule by way of addition, variation or repeal any of the provisions of this Schedule from time to time.

3388.question: Does the amendment of the Schedule count as an amendment of the Constitution?
3388.answer: No, such law as is mentioned in sub-paragraph (1) of this paragraph shall not be deemed to be an amendment of this Constitution for the purposes of article 368.

3389.question: What is not deemed to be an amendment of the Constitution under sub-paragraph (1) of this paragraph for the purposes of article 368?

4036.question: Under what conditions can a member of a House be disqualified based on defection?
4036.answer: A member can be disqualified if he voluntarily gives up his membership of the political party or if he votes or abstains from voting contrary to the direction issued by the political party without obtaining prior permission and such action has not been condoned within fifteen days.

4037.question: What does it mean if a member voluntarily gives up his membership, votes, or abstains from voting contrary to the direction issued by the political party without obtaining prior permission, and such action has not been condoned within fifteen days?
4037.answer: It means the member can be disqualified based on defection.

4038.question: How is an elected member of a House deemed to belong to a political party?
4038.answer: An elected member is deemed to belong to the political party that set him up as a candidate for election.

4039.question: How does a political party determine which elected member belongs to them?
4039.answer: The political party determines that an elected member belongs to them if they set him up as a candidate for election.

4040.question: What happens if an elected member of a House joins a political party after being elected independently?
4040.answer: The member will be disqualified for being a member of the House if he joins any political party after such election.

4041.question: What is the consequence for an independent elected member of a House who joins a political party after the election?
4041.answer: The member will be disqualified for being a member of the House.

4042.question: When can a nominated member of a House be disqualified for being a member of the House?
4042.answer: A nominated member of a House can be disqualified for being a member of the House if he joins any political party after the expiry of six months from the date on which he takes his seat.

4043.question: What happens if a nominated member of a House joins a political party after six months from the date he takes his seat?
4043.answer: If a nominated member of a House joins any political party after the expiry of six months from the date on which he takes his seat, he can be disqualified for being a member of the House.

4044.question: What happens to a person who is a member of a House at the commencement of the Constitution (Fiftysecond Amendment) Act, 1985?
4044.answer: A person who, on the commencement of the Constitution (Fiftysecond Amendment) Act, 1985, is a member of a House (whether elected or nominated as such) shall, if he was a member of political party immediately before such commencement, be deemed to have been elected as a member of such House as a candidate set up by such political party. In any other case, he is deemed to be an elected member of the House who has been elected as such otherwise than as a candidate set up by any political party or, as the case may be, be deemed to be a nominated member of the House.

4045.question: What does the Constitution (Fiftysecond Amendment) Act, 1985 state about a person who is already a member of a House at the commencement of the Act, particularly in regards to their political affiliation?
4045.answer: According to the Constitution (Fiftysecond Amendment) Act, 1985, if a person is a member of a House at the commencement of the Act and was a member of a political party immediately before such commencement, they are deemed to have been elected as a member of the House as a candidate set up by that political party. If they were not affiliated with any political party, they are deemed to be an elected member of the House who has been elected as such otherwise than as a candidate set up by any political party or, as the case may be, deemed to be a nominated member of the House.

4046.question: When does disqualification on ground of defection not apply according to paragraph 4?
4046.answer: A member of a House shall not be disqualified under subparagraph (1) of paragraph 2 where his original political party merges with another political party and he claims that he and any other members of his original political party have become members of such other political party or, as the case may be, of a new political party formed by such merger; or have not accepted the merger and opted to function as a separate group.

4047.question: What is the scenario in which a member of a House is not disqualified under subparagraph (1) of paragraph 2 when his original political party merges with another political party?
4047.answer: Disqualification on ground of defection does not apply when his original political party merges with another political party and he claims that he and any other members of his original political party have become members of such other political party or, as the case may be, of a new political party formed by such merger; or have not accepted the merger and opted to function as a separate group, according to paragraph 4.

4048.question: What is considered as the political party of a member whose original party has merged with another party?
4048.answer: From the time of such merger, such other political party or new political party or group, as the case may be, shall be deemed to be the political party to which he belongs for the purposes of sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph 2 and to be his original political party for the purposes of this sub-paragraph.

4049.question: What happens to the political party of a member when their original party merges with another party?
4049.answer: From the time of such merger, such other political party or new political party or group, as the case may be, shall be deemed to be the political party to which he belongs for the purposes of sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph 2 and to be his original political party for the purposes of this sub-paragraph.

4050.question: When is the merger of the original political party of a member of a House deemed to have taken place?
4050.answer: The merger of the original political party of a member of a House shall be deemed to have taken place if, and only if, no.

4051.question: Is it true that the merger of the original political party of a member of a House is deemed to have taken place under any circumstance?
4051.answer: No, the merger is only deemed to have taken place if certain conditions are met.

4052.question: What is the exception to disqualification under this Schedule?
4052.answer: A person who has been elected to the office of the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker of the House of the People or the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States or the Chairman or the Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council of a State or the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of a State, shall not be disqualified under this Schedule, if he voluntarily gives up the membership of the political party to which he belonged immediately before such election and does not, so long as he continues to hold such office thereafter, rejoin that political party or become a member of another political party; or if he, having given up by reason of his election to such office his membership of the political party to which he belonged immediately before such election, rejoins such political party after he ceases to hold such office.

4053.question: Who is not disqualified under this Schedule even if they voluntarily give up the membership of the political party they belonged to immediately before their election or if they rejoin that political party after they cease to hold office?
4053.answer: A person who has been elected to the office of the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker of the House of the People or the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States or the Chairman or the Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council of a State or the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of a State is not disqualified under this Schedule.

4054.question: Who decides on questions as to disqualification on grounds of defection?
4054.answer: The question shall be referred for the decision of the Chairman or, as the case may be, the Speaker of such House and his decision shall be final.

4055.question: To whom is the question of disqualification on grounds of defection referred for a final decision?
4055.answer: The question shall be referred for the decision of the Chairman or, as the case may be, the Speaker of such House.

4056.question: What happens if a question arises whether the Chairman or the Speaker of a House has become subject to disqualification?
4056.answer: The question shall be referred for the decision of such member of the House as the House may elect in this behalf and his decision shall be final.

4057.question: To whom is the question referred for a decision if a question arises about the Chairman or the Speaker of a House being subject to disqualification, and whose decision is deemed final?
4057.answer: The question shall be referred for the decision of such member of the House as the House may elect in this behalf and his decision shall be final.

4058.question: How are the proceedings in relation to any question as to disqualification of a member of a House under this Schedule deemed?
4058.answer: All proceedings under sub-paragraph (1) of this paragraph in relation to any question as to disqualification of a member of a House under this Schedule shall be deemed to be proceedings in Parliament within the meaning of article 122 or, as the case may be, proceedings in the Legislature.

4059.question: What are all proceedings under sub-paragraph (1) of this paragraph in relation to any question as to disqualification of a member of a House under this Schedule deemed as?
4059.answer: They are deemed to be proceedings in Parliament within the meaning of article 122 or, as the case may be, proceedings in the Legislature.

4068.question: When should the rules made by the Chairman or the Speaker of a House be laid before the House?
4068.answer: The rules made by the Chairman or the Speaker of a House should be laid as soon as may be after they are made before the House for a total period of thirty days which may be comprised in one session or in two or more successive sessions.

4069.question: What is the time period within which the rules made by the Chairman or the Speaker of a House need to be presented before the House?
4069.answer: The rules should be laid as soon as may be after they are made, for a total period of thirty days which may be comprised in one session or in two or more successive sessions.

4070.question: What happens to the rules after the expiry of thirty days?
4070.answer: Upon the expiry of the said period of thirty days, unless they are sooner approved with or without modifications or disapproved by the House, they shall take effect on such approval in the form in which they were laid or in such modified form, as the case may be. If they are disapproved, they shall be of no effect.

4071.question: What occurs if the rules are not approved, with or without modifications, or disapproved by the House within a thirty day period?
4071.answer: Upon the expiry of the said period of thirty days, unless they are sooner approved with or without modifications or disapproved by the House, they shall take effect on such approval in the form in which they were laid or in such modified form, as the case may be. If they are disapproved, they shall be of no effect.

4072.question: What can the Chairman or the Speaker of a House do according to the constitution?
4072.answer: The Chairman or the Speaker of a House may, without prejudice to the provisions of article 105 or, as the case may be, article 194, and to any other power which he may have under this Constitution direct that any wilful contravention by any person of the rules made under this paragraph may be dealt with in the same manner as a breach of privilege of the House.

4073.question: What does the Constitution say the Chairman or the Speaker of a House can do in the event of a wilful contravention by any person of the rules?
4073.answer: The Chairman or the Speaker of a House may, without prejudice to the provisions of article 105 or, as the case may be, article 194, and to any other power which he may have under this Constitution direct that the contravention may be dealt with in the same manner as a breach of privilege of the House.

4241.answer: It means that the person has not been previously convicted by a court for the same offence.

4242.question: What is the procedure after receiving the application under sub-section (1)?
4242.answer: After receiving the application under sub-section (1), the Court shall issue notice to the Public Prosecutor or the complainant of the case, and to the accused to appear on the date fixed for the case.

4243.question: Who does the Court issue notice to after receiving the application under sub-section (1)?
4243.answer: After receiving the application under sub-section (1), the Court issues notice to the Public Prosecutor or the complainant of the case, and to the accused.

4244.question: What happens when the Public Prosecutor, the complainant, and the accused appear on the date fixed under sub-section (3)?

4245.question: What does the court do when the Public Prosecutor, the complainant, and the accused appear on the date fixed under sub-section (3)?
4245.answer: The Court shall examine the accused in camera, where the other party in the case shall not be present, to satisfy itself that the accused has filed the application voluntarily.

4246.question: What happens if the court is satisfied that the application has been filed by the accused voluntarily?
4246.answer: If the court is satisfied that the application has been filed by the accused voluntarily, it shall provide time to the Public Prosecutor or the complainant of the case, and the accused to work out a mutually satisfactory disposition of the case.

4247.question: Who does the court provide time to if it is satisfied that the application has been filed voluntarily by the accused?
4247.answer: If the court is satisfied that the application has been filed by the accused voluntarily, it provides time to the Public Prosecutor or the complainant of the case, and the accused to work out a mutually satisfactory disposition of the case.

4248.question: What happens if the Court finds that the application has been filed involuntarily by the accused or he has previously been convicted for the same offence?
4248.answer: The Court shall proceed further in accordance with the provisions of this Code from the stage such application has been filed under sub-section (1).

4249.question: What will the Court do if it finds that the application was filed involuntarily by the accused or he has been previously convicted for the same offence, under sub-section (1)?
4249.answer: The Court shall proceed further in accordance with the provisions of this Code from the stage such application has been filed.

4250.question: What does section 265C state about mutually satisfactory disposition?
4250.answer: In working out a mutually satisfactory disposition under clause (a) of sub-section (4) of section 265B, the Court shall follow a specific procedure. This includes issuing notice to the Public Prosecutor, the police officer who has investigated the case, the accused and the victim of the case to participate in the meeting to work out a satisfactory disposition of the case.

4251.question: Who are the parties that the court should issue a notice to when working out a mutually satisfactory disposition under clause (a) of sub-section (4) of section 265B?
4251.answer: The court should issue a notice to the Public Prosecutor, the police officer who has investigated the case, the accused and the victim of the case.

4252.question: Who does the Court issue notice to for working out a mutually satisfactory disposition in a case instituted on a police report?
4252.answer: The Court issues notice to the Public Prosecutor, the police officer who has investigated the case, the accused and the victim of the case.

4253.question: In a case instituted on a police report, to whom does the Court issue notice to for working out a mutually satisfactory disposition?
4253.answer: The Court issues notice to the Public Prosecutor, the police officer who has investigated the case, the accused and the victim of the case.

4254.answer: The duty of the Court is to ensure that the entire process is completed voluntarily by the parties participating in the meeting.

4255.question: What is the Court supposed to ensure during the process of working out a satisfactory disposition of the case?
4255.answer: The Court's duty is to ensure that the entire process is completed voluntarily by the parties participating in the meeting.

4256.question: Can the accused participate in the meeting with his pleader?
4256.answer: Yes, if he so desires, the accused can participate in the meeting with his pleader, if any, engaged in the case.

4257.question: If an accused desires, can he participate in the meeting with his pleader engaged in the case?
4257.answer: Yes, the accused can participate in the meeting with his pleader if he so desires.

4258.question: What does the Court do in a case instituted otherwise than on police report?
4258.answer: The Court will issue notice to the accused and the victim of the case to participate in a meeting to work out a satisfactory disposition of the case.

4259.question: Who does the Court issue notice to in a case that is instituted otherwise than on a police report, and what is the purpose of this meeting?
4259.answer: The Court issues notice to the accused and the victim of the case to participate in a meeting to work out a satisfactory disposition of the case.

4260.question: Can the victim of the case participate in the meeting with his pleader?

4263.question: Who signs the report of a satisfactory disposition of a case that has been worked out in a meeting under section 265C?
4263.answer: The report is signed by the presiding officer of the Court and all other persons who participated in the meeting.

4264.answer: The Court records such observation and proceeds further in accordance with the provisions of this Code from the stage the application under sub-section (1) of section 265B has been filed in such case.

4265.question: What does the Court do if no satisfactory disposition is reached in a meeting under section 265C?
4265.answer: The Court records such observation and proceeds further in accordance with the provisions of this Code from the stage the application under sub-section (1) of section 265B has been filed in such case.

4266.question: How does the court dispose of a case where a satisfactory disposition has been worked out under section 265D?
4266.answer: The Court awards the compensation to the victim in accordance with the disposition under section 265D and hears the parties on the quantum of the punishment, releasing of the accused on probation of good conduct or after admonition under section 360.

4267.question: What does the court do after a disposition under section 265D is worked out and what section is invoked for releasing the accused on probation of good conduct or after admonition?
4267.answer: The Court awards the compensation to the victim in accordance with the disposition under section 265D and hears the parties on the quantum of the punishment, releasing of the accused on probation of good conduct or after admonition under section 360.

4268.question: What is the Probation of Offenders Act?
4268.answer: The Probation of Offenders Act is a law that was enacted in 1958. It allows for the accused to be released on probation under certain circumstances.

4269.question: When was the Probation of Offenders Act enacted and what does it allow?
4269.answer: The Probation of Offenders Act was enacted in 1958 and it allows for the accused to be released on probation under certain circumstances.

4270.question: What does the court do after hearing the parties under clause (a)?
4270.answer: After hearing the parties under clause (a), if the Court is of the view that section 360 or the provisions of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 or any other law for the time being in force are attracted in the case of the accused, it may release the accused on probation or provide the benefit of any such law, as the case may be.

4271.question: What happens if the Court, after hearing the parties under clause (a), decides that section 360 or the provisions of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 or any other law for the time being in force are attracted in the case of the accused?
4271.answer: The Court may release the accused on probation or provide the benefit of any such law, as the case may be.

4272.question: What happens if after hearing the parties under clause (b), the Court finds that minimum punishment has been provided under the law for the offence committed by the accused?
4272.answer: If the Court finds that minimum punishment has been provided under the law for the offence committed by the accused, it may sentence the accused to half of such minimum punishment.

4273.question: What may the court do if it finds that the minimum punishment has been provided under the law for the offence committed by the accused after hearing the parties under clause (b)?
4273.answer: The court may sentence the accused to half of such minimum punishment.

4275.question: What might the court do if it determines that the offence committed by the accused doesn't fall under clause (b) or clause (c)?
4275.answer: It may sentence the accused as per the appropriate laws.

4276.question: What does section 265F state about the delivery of judgement in court?
4276.answer: The Court shall deliver its judgment in terms of section 265E in the open Court and the same shall be signed by the presiding officer of the Court.

4277.question: Who should sign the court's judgment delivered in the open Court according to section 265E?
4277.answer: The presiding officer of the Court should sign the judgment.

4278.question: What does section 265G state about the finality of the judgement?
4278.answer: The judgment delivered by the Court under section 265G shall be final and no appeal (except the special leave petition under article 136 and writ petition under articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution) shall lie in any Court against such judgment.

4279.question: Which articles of the Constitution does section 265G allow for special leave petition and writ petition against the final judgment?
4279.answer: Section 265G allows for the special leave petition under article 136 and writ petition under articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution against the final judgment.

4280.question: What powers does the court have in plea bargaining according to section 265H?
4280.answer: A Court shall have, for the purposes of discharging its functions under this Chapter, all the powers vested in respect of bail, trial of offences and other matters relating to the disposal of a case in such Court under this Code.

4281.question: What functions does section 265H allow a court to discharge in relation to bail, trial of offences and other matters relating to the disposal of a case?
4281.answer: Section 265H gives the court all the powers vested in respect of bail, trial of offences and other matters relating to the disposal of a case for the purposes of discharging its functions.

4282.question: What does section 265-I state about the period of detention undergone by the accused?
4282.answer: The provisions of section 428 shall apply, meaning the period of detention undergone by the accused should be set off against the sentence of imprisonment.

4283.question: Which section is applied for setting off the period of detention undergone by the accused against the sentence of imprisonment as per section 265-I?
4283.answer: The provisions of section 428 are applied.

4284.question: What is the function of the period of detention undergone by the accused?
4284.answer: The period of detention undergone by the accused is set off against the sentence of imprisonment imposed under this Chapter, in the same manner as they apply in respect of the imprisonment under other provisions of this Code.

4285.question: How is the period of detention undergone by the accused applied in respect to the sentence of imprisonment?
4285.answer: The period of detention undergone by the accused is set off against the sentence of imprisonment imposed under this Chapter, in the same manner as they apply in respect of the imprisonment under other provisions of this Code.

4286.question: What is the significance of the provisions of this Chapter according to 265J?
4286.answer: The provisions of this Chapter have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other provisions of this Code and nothing in such other provisions shall be construed to constrain the meaning of any provision of this Chapter.

4287.question: What is the effect of the provisions of this Chapter according to 265J, even if they are inconsistent with other provisions of this Code?
4287.answer: The provisions of this Chapter have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other provisions of this Code and nothing in such other provisions shall be construed to constrain the meaning of any provision of this Chapter.

4288.question: How is the term 'Public Prosecutor' defined in this Chapter?
4288.answer: For the purposes of this Chapter, the expression 'Public Prosecutor' has the meaning assigned to it under clause (u) of section 2 and includes an Assistant Public Prosecutor appointed under section 25.

4289.question: What does the expression 'Public Prosecutor' include and where is it defined in this Chapter?
4289.answer: The expression 'Public Prosecutor' includes an Assistant Public Prosecutor appointed under section 25 and is defined under clause (u) of section 2 in this Chapter.

4290.question: What is the purpose of the statements of the accused according to 265K?
4290.answer: The statements or facts stated by an accused in an application for plea bargaining filed under section 265B shall not be used for any other purpose except for the purposes of plea bargaining.

4291.question: Can the statements or facts stated by an accused in an application for plea bargaining under section 265B be used for any other purposes besides plea bargaining?
4291.answer: No, the statements or facts stated by an accused in an application for plea bargaining filed under section 265B shall not be used for any other purpose except for the purposes of plea bargaining.

4292.question: Who does this Chapter not apply to?

4294.answer: Detained includes detained under any law providing for preventive detention.

4295.question: Under what law does the term 'detained' in this chapter refer to?
4295.answer: The term 'detained' in this chapter refers to being detained under any law providing for preventive detention.

4296.question: What does 'prison' include in this Chapter?
4296.answer: Prison includes any place which has been declared by the State Government, by general or special order, to be a subsidiary jail; any reformatory, Borstal institution or institution of a like nature.

4297.question: What types of institutions are included in the term 'prison' as per this Chapter?
4297.answer: Any place declared by the State Government to be a subsidiary jail, any reformatory, Borstal institution or institution of a like nature are included in the term 'prison'.

4298.question: When can a Criminal Court require the attendance of a prisoner?
4298.answer: Whenever, in the course of an inquiry, trial or proceeding under this Code, it appears to a Criminal Court that a person confined or detained in a prison should be brought before the Court for answering to a charge of an offence, or for the purpose of any proceedings against him.

4299.question: Under what circumstances should a person confined or detained in a prison be brought before the Court according to the Criminal Court?
4299.answer: A person confined or detained in a prison should be brought before the Court when, in the course of an inquiry, trial or proceeding under this Code, it appears to the Criminal Court that the person should answer to a charge of an offence, or for the purpose of any proceedings against him.

4300.question: What can the Court order the officer in charge of the prison to do?
4300.answer: The Court can order the officer in charge of the prison to produce such person before the Court for the purpose of such proceeding or, as the case may be, for giving evidence.

4301.question: What can the Court do if it wants a person to be produced before it for a proceeding or for giving evidence?
4301.answer: The Court can order the officer in charge of the prison to produce such person before the Court.

4302.question: What is required for an order made by a Magistrate of the second class to be acted upon?
4302.answer: It shall not be forwarded to, or acted upon by, the officer in charge of the prison unless it is countersigned by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, to whom such Magistrate is subordinate.

4303.question: Who needs to countersign an order made by a Magistrate of the second class for it to be forwarded to or acted upon by the officer in charge of the prison?
4303.answer: The Chief Judicial Magistrate, to whom such Magistrate is subordinate, needs to countersign the order.

4304.question: What should accompany every order submitted for countersigning under sub-section (2)?
4304.answer: Every order submitted for countersigning under sub-section (2) shall be accompanied by a statement of the facts which, in the opinion of the Magistrate, render the order necessary.

4305.question: What must accompany every order submitted for countersigning under sub-section (2) in the opinion of the Magistrate?
4305.answer: A statement of the facts which render the order necessary must accompany every order submitted for countersigning under sub-section (2).

4306.question: What can the Chief Judicial Magistrate do after considering the statement accompanying the order?
4306.answer: The Chief Judicial Magistrate to whom it is submitted may, after considering such statement, decline to countersign the order.

4307.question: What may the Chief Judicial Magistrate do after considering the statement submitted along with the order?
4307.answer: The Chief Judicial Magistrate may decline to countersign the order.

4308.question: What can the State Government direct according to the sub-section (1)?
4308.answer: The State Government can direct that any person or class of persons shall not be removed from the prison in which he or they may be confined or detained.

4309.question: Who can the State Government order to not be removed from the prison they are confined or detained in according to sub-section (1)?
4309.answer: The State Government can order that any person or class of persons shall not be removed from the prison in which he or they may be confined or detained.

4310.question: What happens when the State Government's order is in force?
4310.answer: So long as the order remains in force, no order made under section 267, whether before or after the order of the State Government, shall have effect in respect of such person or class of persons.

4311.question: What is the effect of an order made under section 267 when the State Government's order is in force?
4311.answer: No order made under section 267, whether before or after the order of the State Government, shall have effect in respect of such person or class of persons.

4312.question: What should the State Government consider before making an order under sub-section (1)?
4312.answer: Before making an order, the State Government shall have regard to the nature of the offence for which the person has been ordered to be confined, the likelihood of disturbance of public order if the person is allowed to be removed from the prison, and the public interest.

4313.question: What factors does the State Government take into account when deciding whether to remove a person from prison under sub-section (1)?
4313.answer: The State Government considers the nature of the offence for which the person has been ordered to be confined, the likelihood of disturbance of public order if the person is allowed to be removed from the prison, and the public interest.

4314.question: What is the role of the officer in charge of the prison in certain contingencies according to section 269?
4314.answer: The officer in charge of the prison should abstain from carrying out order in certain contingencies.

4315.question: What should the officer in charge of the prison do in certain contingencies according to section 269?
4315.answer: The officer in charge of the prison should abstain from carrying out order in certain contingencies.

4316.question: What are the conditions under which an officer in charge of a prison should abstain from carrying out the Court's order under section 267?
4316.answer: The officer in charge of the prison should abstain from carrying out the Court's order if the person: (a) is by reason of sickness or infirmity unfit to be removed from the prison; (b) is under committal for trial or under remand pending trial or pending a preliminary investigation; (c) is in custody for a period which would expire before the expiration of the time required for complying with the order and for taking him back to the prison in which he is confined or detained; (d) is a person to whom an order made by the State Government under section 268 applies.

4317.question: When should the officer in charge of a prison abstain from carrying out the Court's order if: (a) the person is sick or infirm and unfit to be removed from the prison; (b) the person is under committal for trial or under remand pending trial or pending a preliminary investigation; (c) the person is in custody for a period which would expire before the expiration of the time required for complying with the order and for taking him back to the prison in which he is confined or detained; (d) the person is someone to whom an order made by the State Government under section 268 applies?
4317.answer: These conditions fall under section 267, which states that an officer in charge of a prison should abstain from carrying out the Court's order under these circumstances.

4318.question: What should the officer in charge of the prison do if he abstains from carrying out the Court's order?
4318.answer: If the officer in charge of the prison abstains from carrying out the Court's order, he should send to the Court a statement of reasons for so abstaining.

4319.question: What should the officer in charge of the prison do if he decides not to carry out the Court's order?
4319.answer: He should send to the Court a statement of reasons for his decision to abstain.

4320.question: Is there an exception to the officer in charge of the prison abstaining from carrying out the Court's order?
4320.answer: Yes, where the attendance of such person is required for giving evidence at a place not more than twenty-five kilometres distance from the prison, the officer in charge of the prison shall not so abstain for the reason mentioned in clause (b).

4321.question: Under what circumstances can the officer in charge of a prison carry out the Court's order despite normally abstaining?
4321.answer: The officer in charge of the prison can carry out the Court's order when the attendance of such person is required for giving evidence at a place not more than twenty-five kilometres distance from the prison.

4322.question: What is the responsibility of the officer in charge of the prison according to section 269?
4322.answer: The officer in charge of the prison shall cause the person named in the order to be taken to the Court in which his attendance is required, so as to be present there at the time mentioned in the order, and shall cause him to be kept in custody in or near the Court until he has been examined or until the Court authorises him to be taken back to the prison in which he was confined or detained.

4323.question: According to section 269, what are the duties of the prison officer after a court order has been issued for a detained individual's attendance?
4323.answer: The officer in charge of the prison shall cause the person named in the order to be taken to the Court in which his attendance is required, so as to be present there at the time mentioned in the order, and shall cause him to be kept in custody in or near the Court until he has been examined or until the Court authorises him to be taken back to the prison in which he was confined or detained.

4324.question: What is the power given to the Court under section 284?
4324.answer: The Court has the power to issue a commission for the examination, as a witness, of any person confined or detained in a prison.

4325.question: Under which section does the Court have the power to issue a commission for the examination, as a witness, of any person confined or detained in a prison?
4325.answer: The Court has this power under section 284.

4326.question: What happens after the Court issues a commission for the examination of a person in prison?
4326.answer: The provisions of Part B of Chapter XXIII shall apply in relation to the examination on commission of any such person in the prison.

4327.question: What applies in relation to the examination on commission of any such person in the prison after the Court issues a commission for the examination of a person in prison?
4327.answer: The provisions of Part B of Chapter XXIII apply.

4328.question: When can the person named in the order be taken back to the prison?
4328.answer: The person named in the order can be taken back to the prison once he has been examined or when the Court authorises him to be taken back.

4329.question: What needs to happen before the person named in the order can be taken back to prison?
4329.answer: The person named in the order can be taken back to the prison once he has been examined or when the Court authorises him to be taken back.
